title: docs(examples): add Ubuntu desktop sandbox example and integration guide
body:
## Summary

Adds a runnable Ubuntu desktop example plus the matching English and Chinese integration guides, so a full Ubuntu 22.04 GNOME desktop can be opened in the browser from a Cube sandbox. This is useful for GUI automation, screenshot-based testing, and agent-driven desktop tasks that need a real display.

- `examples/ubuntu-desktop/Dockerfile`: builds on `cubesandbox-base` and adds dummy Xorg, `ubuntu-session`/GNOME, x11vnc and noVNC. An `APT_MIRROR` build arg defaults to a fast mirror and can be emptied to use the upstream archive.
- `examples/ubuntu-desktop/start-desktop.sh`: brings up Xorg (with an Xvfb fallback), system dbus, `systemd-logind`, the Ubuntu GNOME session, x11vnc and noVNC, then stays in the foreground so the container stops cleanly.
- `examples/ubuntu-desktop/run-local.sh` and `docker-compose.yml`: verify the image on local Docker before pushing it as a template.
- `examples/ubuntu-desktop/README.md` / `README_zh.md`: usage for both the local and Cube flows.
- `docs`: English and Chinese guides, VitePress nav entries, and rows in the examples tables.

## Design notes

- The display is a 1280x720 dummy framebuffer; software rendering (`llvmpipe`) keeps x11vnc affordable without a GPU.
- GNOME needs a session bus, system dbus, and `logind`, none of which systemd provides inside the sandbox, so the startup script provides them itself.
- noVNC listens on `6080`. The guide points the template probe at that port so a sandbox is only reported ready once the desktop actually serves.
- Inside the sandbox the desktop runs on `DISPLAY=:0`, which is what SDK-driven screenshots and window queries use.

## How to verify

1. `cd examples/ubuntu-desktop && ./run-local.sh` builds the image, waits for noVNC, then prints the X display dimensions and the envd health status.
2. Open the printed noVNC URL to reach the desktop.
3. For Cube, run the `tpl create-from-image` command from the guide, then `Sandbox.create(template="ubuntu-desktop")` and open `sb.get_host(6080)`.

## Notes

- The example image creates an unprivileged `user` account with passwordless sudo inside the sandbox, matching the assumption that the sandbox itself is the security boundary.
- x11vnc runs without a VNC password because noVNC sits in front of it on the same sandbox.

title: Cubelet restart/upgrade hangs while loading existing shims when a stale shim is unresponsiv
body:
## Summary

Cubelet remains an `active` systemd service but never binds `:9998`, `:9999`, or `:9966` after restart/upgrade when an unresponsive `containerd-shim-cube-rs` process is left behind. Startup blocks inside `LoadExistingShims -> makeConnection -> ttrpc.NewClient`, and the configured `io.containerd.timeout.shim.load = "5s"` does not cover that connection path.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `v0.7.0` / `d0081641c59822e4e5653b7462e914410b81910a`
- Host OS and kernel version: Kylin Linux, `6.6.0-32.18.v2505.ky11.x86_64`
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): <!-- attach output -->
- Deployment mode: cluster, one control node plus one compute node
- Relevant component: Cubelet

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a sandbox and leave it in a `paused`/tombstone state, or otherwise make its `containerd-shim-cube-rs` process unresponsive.
2. Stop Cubelet or run an upgrade:
```bash
sudo systemctl stop cube-sandbox-cubelet.service
sudo systemctl start cube-sandbox-cubelet.service

```

title: refactor(dev-env): reduce to VM create, boot, and login
body:
## Summary

Slims `dev-env/` down to its core purpose: create an OpenCloudOS 9 VM, boot it, and log in. The automatic in-guest provisioning steps are removed, so the VM comes up clean and developers install whatever they need themselves.

It also clarifies the intended scope: `dev-env` targets local Linux workstations. If you already have a cloud server, the PVM deployment path in the quickstart is the right route instead.

## Changes

- **`prepare_image.sh` to `create_vm.sh`**: downloads the qcow2 image, boots the VM, grows the root filesystem on first boot, applies SELinux policy, then shuts down cleanly.
- **Removed automatic provisioning**: the auto-boot flag, the autostart service, PATH and login-banner setup, and the web asset sync, along with the helper scripts that backed them.
- **Removed `sync_to_vm.sh` and `copy_logs.sh`**: plain `scp` / `rsync` over the forwarded SSH port covers both use cases and is now documented instead.
- **`run_vm.sh`**: forwards SSH plus an optional `EXTRA_FORWARDS` list. Entries are validated, and invalid ones abort before QEMU starts.
- **Dropped the ripgrep dependency**: the scripts now only require stock tools.
- **Docs rewritten**: `dev-env/README*.md` and the dev environment guide lead with the create/boot/login flow, point cloud host users at the PVM deployment, and move reference material into appendices.

## Verification

- `bash -n` on all shell scripts.
- Full end-to-end `create_vm.sh` run: enlarged root filesystem, SELinux permissive, clean shutdown.
- Default boot exposes only the SSH forward; `EXTRA_FORWARDS` adds the requested ports.
- `scp` in both directions, recursive directory copy, `rsync`, and `sudo install` all work over the forwarded port.
- Invalid `EXTRA_FORWARDS` values abort before QEMU starts.
- Docs build passes (`npm run docs:build` under `docs/`) along with the crawler discovery check.
- The end-to-end run was repeated with a restricted `PATH` to confirm no ripgrep dependency.

## Notes

`dev-env/cube-autostart.sh`, `dev-env/sync_to_vm.sh`, and `dev-env/copy_logs.sh` are gone. Anyone who relied on them should use the documented `scp` / `rsync` flow.

title: fix(cubelet): always allow configured DNS resolvers
body:
## Summary

Cubelet's existing `shouldAppendDNSAllowOut` guard is intentionally preserved. It prevents a sandbox that only uses IP/CIDR targets (and has no domain/L7 host rule) from gaining resolver access that its policy does not require.

The fix adds one narrowly-scoped exception: when the effective guest resolver is a private, link-local, or loopback IPv4 address (for example GKE kube-dns `10.204.0.10`), Cubelet automatically admits that resolver /32 even for an otherwise IP-only policy. Public resolvers remain governed by the original `shouldAppendDNSAllowOut` condition. The update path applies the same rule so resolver access is not lost when user policy is replaced.

This reuses the existing CubeVS UDP NAT, DNS learning, and reverse-NAT paths without changing CubeVS or exposing resolver configuration beyond the existing guest dns_config. IPv6 remains unsupported by the current IPv4 dataplane and is skipped with the existing warning.

## Evidence

- STG GKE `kube-dns` ClusterIP `10.204.0.10` was unreachable with the stock policy.
- The same sandbox succeeded in DNS and TLS when created with `network.allow_out=["10.204.0.10/32"]`.
- DNS resolution for `ai-gateway.stg.alva.xyz`, `api.openai.com`, and `google.com`, plus TLS 1.3 to the internal gateway, all succeeded; total E2E time was 1.068s and cleanup succeeded.
- This confirms the missing behavior is resolver policy admission, not GKE Service routing or CubeVS UDP NAT.

## Compatibility and security

- Explicit user `allow_out`, `deny_out`, and L7 rules are unchanged.
- Domain/L7 policies retain the upstream behavior and may admit their configured public resolver as before.
- For IP-only policies, only private/link-local/loopback resolver CIDRs are auto-added; a mixed private+public resolver list does not auto-add the public resolver.
- Resolver entries are deduplicated and only IPv4 `/32` values are added.
- The v0.6.0 policy map is CIDR-only, so the resolver exception currently grants the resolver IP at L3/L4 (all ports). A future port-aware policy map can narrow it to UDP/TCP port 53.

## Validation

- Added regression tests for domain/L7 policies, private resolver admission, mixed private+public resolvers, public resolver preservation, update-path refolding, and nil config handling.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Full package execution is delegated to the Linux GitHub CI runners; local macOS execution is blocked by Linux-only netlink/eBPF bindings.

title: ci(code-review): review large pull requests instead of failing on the diff API
body:
## Motivation

The prefetch step in `.github/workflows/code-review.yml` gets the diff with `gh pr diff`, which goes through the REST API. That endpoint refuses any PR above 20 000 diff lines:

```
could not find pull request diff: HTTP 406: Sorry, the diff exceeded the maximum number of lines (20000)
PullRequest.diff too_large
```

Because the step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, it exits 1 and takes the whole `review` job down with it: **a large PR is never reviewed at all**, and the 2 MB truncation further down the step cannot help, because the API fails before any diff exists.

That is the current state of the in-flight `cube-envd` PRs:

| PR | size | `review` job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #1610 | +23 513/−175, 102 files | **failed** in 11 s — HTTP 406 (run 34839063386) |
| #1723 | +28 511/−206, 104 files | **failed** in 9 s — HTTP 406 (run 34825313948) |
| #1729 | +33 572/−130, 166 files | **failed** in 13 s — HTTP 406 (run 34798433009) |
| #1730 | +10 223/−193, 48 files | passed in 7m11s — same workflow, just under the limit |

Only the size differs; #1730 shows the workflow itself is fine below 20 000 lines.

## What this changes

`.github/workflows/code-review.yml` only (+88/−1), all inside the *Prefetch PR review inputs* step:

1. keep `gh pr diff` as the normal path;
2. when it fails, rebuild the diff from git objects: fetch `refs/pull/N/head` and the merge base (`--depth=1 --no-tags`, objects only — nothing is checked out, so the trusted workspace stays clean), read the PR's file list from the files endpoint as one JSON object per entry (`per_page=100` in the query string, since `gh api -F` would switch the request to POST), and `git diff` restricted to exactly those paths;
3. include `previous_filename`, so renames keep both sides instead of turning into whole-file additions, and project the entries down to `filename` + `previous_filename` so the endpoint does not also stream back every file's `patch` — 921 KB → 7.6 KB on #1723, which is the payload this fallback exists to avoid;
4. write the pathspecs NUL-delimited (`jq -j` + `mapfile -d ''`) and prefixed with `:(top,literal)`, so a filename containing a newline cannot split into two paths and no filename is read as a glob. The entry count is then exact, which is what the 3000-entry check compares against;
5. resolve the merge base from the **live** base SHA read from the API, not the event payload's frozen `base.sha`: a re-run replays the payload, so a stale base would put back the artifacts described below;
6. refuse to install an **empty** rebuild. `git diff` exits 0 with no output when nothing matched, and the file list is read one API call before the head is resolved, so a push landing in between ends up here — previously the run would have installed an empty `pr.diff` and reviewed it behind a green check;
7. flag a file list that reaches the files endpoint's 3000-entry cap, in the rebuilt diff and in `review-input/TRUNCATED`, so a partial list is never presented as the whole change. The check defaults to the cap when the count cannot be read, because a test that cannot be evaluated only makes its `if` false — it does not abort under `set -e` — so an unknown count has to warn rather than pass silently.

`review-input/pr.diff.err` is now removed on both paths instead of being left behind as an empty file on the happy path.

## Why the merge base, not the base tip

The base tip at event time is not the fork point, so a two-dot diff against it also replays the base branch's own commits as if the PR had reverted them. Measured on #1723's head `56162df1`:

| | files | diff lines | deletions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| merge base | 104 | 29 805 | 183 |
| base tip | 104 | 30 000 | 258 |

The extra 195 lines are `docs/guide/tutorials/bring-your-own-image.md` (+99) and its `docs/zh` translation (+96): deletions the PR never made, which would otherwise be handed to the reviewer as the PR's own changes.

## Testing

- **The motivating PR, end to end, real `gh` and `git`.** Running the final step body against #1723 in a depth-1 clone: `gh pr diff` returns the 406 above, the fallback runs, and the step exits 0 with a 1 206 943-byte diff over 104 files — **byte-identical** to the same diff built by hand.
- **Parity with the old path.** Rebuilding #1739's diff the same way and diffing it against `gh pr diff 1739` is byte-identical apart from git's abbreviated `index` hashes (10 hex digits from the API, 7 in a shallow clone).
- **`git fetch --depth=1 origin <merge-base sha>` works on GitHub**, so the merge base can be fetched as a raw object rather than by ref.
- **`:(top,literal)` is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** On a probe containing `a*b.txt`, `c[1].txt`, `d e.txt` and `:colon.txt`, the bare form silently drops one of the four files; the literal form matches all four.
- **Newlines survive.** A stubbed file list with `we\nird.txt` plus a rename from `old\nname.txt` produces exactly 4 API entries → 4 pathspec arguments, with the embedded newline intact inside a single argument (the previous `mapfile` version split it into 6).
- **Page size.** The endpoint returns 30 entries per page by default and 100 with `?per_page=100`, verified against the live API; `-F per_page=100` alone returns `404 Not Found` because `gh api` switches to POST when parameters are added.
- **The 3000-entry branch** is exercised with stubs: 3 and 2999 entries produce no marker, 3000 produces the marker and the warning, and combined with a >2 MB diff both notices survive in the file. With `grep` stubbed to fail, the count is unknown and the marker is still written (the default-to-cap path).
- **The empty-rebuild guard**: a stub whose `git diff` prints nothing exits 1 with `refusing to review nothing`, and no `pr.diff` is installed.
- `yaml.safe_load` and `bash -n` on the step body both pass.

## Risk

- This is a `pull_request_target` workflow, and the change still never executes PR code: objects are fetched, nothing is checked out, `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` keeps attributes/config from pulling in external diff or textconv helpers, and `:(top,literal)` keeps filenames from being read as globs. Tree-to-tree attributes are read from the trusted working tree, so a PR-supplied `.gitattributes` does not apply either.
- No production code, config, or on-disk format is touched.
- Changes to this workflow only take effect after merge, so this PR's own `review` run still executes the old step.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` maps `/.github/workflows/` to @tinklone.

## Follow-ups

- `pr_head` is not compared against the `headRefOid` in `meta.json`, so a push landing between the two API calls would produce a diff of a revision the metadata does not describe. (The empty-rebuild guard above now catches the case where that mismatch also empties the diff.)
- The compare call used to resolve the merge base still downloads up to 300 files' worth of patches to read one SHA, since that endpoint has no field selection. Bounded by the API, noted for the record.
- The fallback's `git fetch` is unauthenticated (`persist-credentials: false`, and git ignores `GH_TOKEN`), so it depends on the repository staying public — it would fail loudly, not silently, if that changed.

DCO: the commit carries `Signed-off-by`.

title: test(cubelet): drop the vacuous and flaky Test_HashCode
body:
Follow-up to #1422. Supersedes #1423 (same defect, different approach: remove the test instead of rewriting it).

## Motivation

`Test_HashCode` in `Cubelet/pkg/utils/strings_test.go` has never asserted anything about `HashCode`, and the one assertion that can fire is a wall-clock budget:

- `cases := make([]string, 0, size)` has length 0, so `for i := 0; i < len(cases); i++` runs zero times. No input is ever generated, both loops over `cases` are empty, and the test passes in 0.00s with **zero subtests**.
- The only live assertion is `useTime > 1000000` — 10000 hashes within 1 ms. A hard millisecond budget in a unit test is inherently flaky on a loaded or emulated runner, which is how it surfaced:

  ```
  --- FAIL: Test_HashCode
      strings_test.go:43: use too much time, use 1 ms, each use 126 ns
  ```

  The reported per-hash figure is meaningless, because `useTime` measures only `make(map[string]uint32, size)` on an empty loop — nothing was hashed.
- Even if the inputs were generated, the comparison is a tautology: `HashCode` is `crc32.ChecksumIEEE`, a pure function, so hashing the same string twice always matches. Any deterministic-but-wrong implementation, including one that returns a constant, would pass.

`HashCode` has no callers in the tree outside this test:

```
$ git grep -n "HashCode" master -- '*.go'
Cubelet/pkg/utils/strings.go:54:func HashCode(dimension string) uint32 {
Cubelet/pkg/utils/strings_test.go:19:func Test_HashCode(t *testing.T) {
Cubelet/pkg/utils/strings_test.go:29:		code := HashCode(c)
Cubelet/pkg/utils/strings_test.go:34:			code := HashCode(c)
```

There is also no indirect reference (no reflection, plugin, or function registry), so nothing depends on the function today.

## What this changes

`Cubelet/pkg/utils/strings_test.go`:

- Remove `Test_HashCode`.
- Remove the imports it was the only user of: `math/rand`, `strconv`, `time`.

31 deletions, one file, no production code touched. The remaining tests in the file (`TestString2Slice`, `TestDecode`, `TestInterfaceToString`, `TestReadAtMost`, `TestMaxCommonPrefix`) are unchanged.

I deliberately did not rewrite the test instead (which is what #1423 did). With no callers there is no property worth pinning: a golden-CRC32 assertion would only freeze dead code, and the stability assertion cannot be made to fail. If `HashCode` ever gains a caller, the value contract should be asserted at that call site.

## Testing

```
$ gofmt -l pkg/utils/strings_test.go
(clean)

$ go test ./pkg/utils/ -run 'TestString2Slice|TestDecode|TestInterfaceToString|TestReadAtMost|TestMaxCommonPrefix' -count=1
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/Cubelet/pkg/utils  0.007s
```

`go vet ./pkg/utils/` reports only the pre-existing `reflect.SliceHeader` misuse at `strings.go:38` (see #1432), unrelated to this change.

Environment-specific footnote: in a plain container without a visible PID 1, `go test ./pkg/utils/` also reports `TestProcessExists` failing (`process_test.go:20` asserts `ProcessExists(ctx, 1)`). That fails identically on current `master` in the same environment and is unrelated to this change.

## Risk / rollout

None to production. Test-only deletion; no API, behaviour, config, or on-disk format changes.

DCO: the commit carries `Signed-off-by`.

title: test(cubelet): stop the volume attach tests from racing on their stub script
body:
## Summary

`TestAttachPassesPrivateDataFlag` and `TestAttachPassesEmptyPrivateDataFlag`
in `Cubelet/plugins/volume/binary` both call `t.Parallel()` and each writes an
executable shell stub it immediately execs. When one test forks while the
other's stub is still open for writing, the child inherits the write
descriptor and `execve` fails with `ETXTBSY`:

    --- FAIL: TestAttachPassesEmptyPrivateDataFlag
        driver_test.go:93: Attach: binary volume plugin "cos" attach: exit error:
        fork/exec /tmp/.../wrapper.sh: text file busy

This is the flake that intermittently reddens the `Test Cubelet` unit-test job
for unrelated PRs.

## Changes

- Drop `t.Parallel()` from the two tests so they run serially within the
  package, with a comment explaining why they must not become parallel again.

## Why

No source change is needed: with the two tests serialized, `os.WriteFile`
closes the stub before `exec`, so no concurrent fork can inherit the write
descriptor. This mirrors the CubeMaster twin cleanup in 5135a40d
(`CubeMaster/pkg/volume/plugin/binary/driver_test.go`).

## Testing

- Parent tree (with `t.Parallel()`): reproduced the flake — 3 failures / 100 runs.
- This change: `go test ./plugins/volume/binary/ -count=200` and
  `-race -count=100` both pass with 0 failures.
- `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.

title: feat(s3lvol): hot upgrade — sandbox I/O pauses instead of breaking
body:
## The problem

Upgrading the s3lvol target process currently goes through a "planned stop": `nvme disconnect`
first, then unload the lvstore. Both steps remove the block device from the host, so a running
sandbox immediately sees I/O errors (`vda` reports I/O errors, ext4 goes read-only). Upgrading
therefore means interrupting the workload.

In short: **an upgrade today is an outage.**

## The goal

When the target is upgraded, sandbox I/O should **stall for a moment and then continue in
place**, and the host should still see **the same `/dev/nvmeXnY`** — the block device is never
deleted or recreated.

## Approach: make the upgrade a controlled crash recovery

No disconnect, no unload. The sequence is:

1. **Online**: `flush` (push everything acknowledged to S3) + `checkpoint` (snapshot the chunk
   map, truncate the journal)
2. Record a layout snapshot, then **SIGKILL** the target outright (a crash, not a graceful stop)
3. The replacement rebuilds **exactly the same NQN / (subsys, nsid) / UUID layout**
4. The host's nvme_tcp reconnects on its own to the same device, and I/O resumes

This reuses the recovery logic that **crash self-healing** already uses (`Restart=on-failure`
takes this path); it is not a new mechanism.

## What is in this PR

### New

| Item | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/rcow_hot_stop.sh` | The hot stop: online flush + checkpoint + layout snapshot + SIGKILL + residue cleanup. Deliberately does **not** disconnect, unload, or touch `active_lvols` |
| `rcow_get_build_info` RPC + `s3lvol_tgt --print-build-info` | **Version gate**: compares on-disk format versions, the RPC API version, the subsystem/NQN prefix and so on between the running and the candidate binary *before* anything is swapped. Incompatible sides are refused; there is no in-place conversion |
| `rcow_active_bdev_batch` RPC | Restores a batch of volumes in a single round-trip. One `rcow_active_bdev` per volume is one process startup per volume, all inside the pause window |

### Fixes

1. **Namespaces were lost after a hot start** (the critical one)

   Replay answered from a registry entry as if it meant "this process has already exposed it",
   so every volume came back as `already_active` and the real attach was skipped — after the
   restart the namespace count was 0 and the host removed the gendisks.

   Fixed by separating **"recorded"** (the file says what a restart should restore) from
   **"already attached by this process"**; only the latter may answer `already_active`.

2. **`rcow_flush_lvstore` hung indefinitely under write load**

   The 30 s deadline check sat *after* two early returns (`in_flight > 0` and
   `super_sync_active`), and `kick` refills `in_flight` before checking — so as long as writes
   keep arriving the deadline is never reached and the callback never fires. The deadline is
   now read *before* those gates and carried in a separate `drain_expired` flag; once set, no
   new round starts and only the uploads already in flight are waited for.

   This also removes a side effect: the old timeout path set the flusher `stopping` permanently,
   so a `--dry-run` — which must be side-effect free — silently stopped the uploads of a live
   volume.

3. **Hot start deadlocked on a host-wide `sync`**

   The `sync` inside `rcow_replay_registry()` goes through `sync_bdevs()`, which waits for
   writeback on **every** block device; the sandbox's nvme_tcp device is mid-reconnect, so its
   writeback cannot complete — and the listeners that would let the controller reconnect are
   added *after* that step. Observed: a 9-minute deadlock, until the kernel deleted the
   controllers and I/O turned from "paused" into "failed".

   Fixed by `fsync`-ing only the one file (and its directory entry) that actually has to survive.

### Control plane

`cubecow` gains `rpc_connect_budget_ms` (default 60 s): during the hot-upgrade window the socket
is unlinked, so **a connect failure is the expected case, not an error**. Only connection
establishment is retried (100 ms doubling, 2 s ceiling); once connected, a JSON-RPC error
response is an answer and returns immediately — retrying a real error would only turn a fast,
correct failure into a slow one. There is deliberately no watchdog that deactivates volumes or
marks the node NotReady: a control-plane outage must not become a data-plane action.

### Other

- `--keep-connected` on `rcow_stop.sh` is now **refused**: it reads as "leave the host
  connected" but still unloads the lvstore, which hands the host a namespace-removal AEN — a
  silent hot-removal, worse than the plain stop it was meant to avoid.
- `cube-s3lvol-stop.sh` / `cube-sandbox-s3lvol.service`: the stop script's three branches, and
  the rationale for `KillMode=process` (`control-group` would let systemd's post-ExecStop sweep
  reach a target that a stop script deliberately left running).

### Follow-ups from review

- **The target is now identified by its RPC socket as well as its binary name**, and a
  hot-restart marker that names a live target survives a failed identity check instead of being
  discarded. The strict path comparison was the one check that cannot hold during an upgrade --
  the candidate has already moved into place -- so a marker could be consumed and thrown away,
  dropping the stop into the full-teardown branch that this PR exists to avoid. Only a marker
  that is stale by construction (another boot, or malformed) is now removed outright.
- **`rpc_connect_budget_ms` bounds the whole call, queueing included.** It used to start its
  clock after acquiring the connection mutex, which the retry loop holds across its sleeps, so
  concurrent callers each got a fresh allowance and the last one waited about N x the configured
  budget.
- **`connect_backoff` clamps the shift amount** rather than relying on `checked_shl`, which
  rejects only a shift past the bit width: at two values it returned a zero-length sleep instead
  of the ceiling.
- **The build stamps are evaluated once per build**, not once per translation unit, so the three
  `git` calls no longer re-run for every compile and objects cannot be stamped differently if
  the tree goes dirty part-way through.
- **CI now exercises the Rust half.** The crate's own tests are run by `cubecow-test-native`, and
  `cubecow/**` triggers `unit-test-check` (which owns them) instead of `cube-s3lvol-test`, whose
  job never reads the crate.

## Testing

### Unit / regression

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `s3_flush_test`, new case `[10]`: under load a drain must report a timeout rather than hang | **102 passed / 0 failed** (the same case was **100 passed / 2 failed** before the fix — the old code hung and never called back) |
| `run_control_test.sh`, new case `[7b]`: activating a "recorded but not exposed by this process" volume must not answer `already_active`, and must really create the namespace at the recorded position | failed at the first step before the fix |
| `cubecow`, new `connect_backoff` unit test: the backoff doubles and holds at a 2 s ceiling | passes |

### On a real machine, with a real workload

On a machine running this build, fio runs inside a sandbox (**4k randrw 70/30, direct,
iodepth 4, 900 s runtime**, data on the s3lvol volume) while the target is hot-upgraded **in the
same time window**.

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| Business I/O does not error | fio `error=0`, ran the **full 900 s**; **zero I/O errors** in the sandbox's dmesg, no ext4 errors |
| Same block device | **`diskseq` and `uuid` unchanged for all 18 nvme device nodes** — no gendisk was ever deleted |
| Layout restored exactly | `rcow_verify_active --expect` **rc=0** (same subsystem, nsid and device) |
| Controllers reconnect in place | **all 32 back**; `new ctrl`=0, `removing namespace`=0 |
| Sandbox survives | alive throughout, fio never broke, finished after the upgrade |

**Performance impact**:

| | mean | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| read | 0.46 ms | 2.87 ms | 435 ms |
| write | 0.62 ms | 2.87 ms | 39.9 s |

- **A p99 of 2.87 ms** means performance **outside** the window is identical to normal — no
  regression.
- **The 39.9 s write maximum** is the one I/O that happened to straddle the window. Its latency
  **equals the length of the pause window itself**: the completion-latency log shows a single
  **39.93 s gap** in which no I/O completed, spanning exactly from the SIGKILL to the
  replacement reporting ready. It **waited; it did not fail** — which is the semantics this work
  is about.

The **≈40 s pause window** breaks down as follows (each row is verifiable in the host logs):

| Time | What |
|---|---|
| 8 s | SIGKILL + systemd restarting the target |
| 5 s | creating 32 subsystems, the WAL bdev, the S3 namespace |
| **30 s** | **the target attaching the lvstore itself (blobstore metadata load + journal/WAL replay)** ← dominant |
| 2 s | restoring volumes and adding listeners |

> The dominant part is the target's own attach cost, which is **not in this PR's code**. It is
> the one place worth optimizing, and the lever for shortening the window later.

## Compatibility and risks

- **Version gate**: `super_version / wal_version / ckpt_version / journal_op_max / num_subsys /
  ns_per_subsys / nqn_prefix` must match on both sides, otherwise the upgrade is **refused**;
  there is no in-place conversion.
- **The journal has no version field**, so `journal_op_max` is what guards it: a log written by
  a newer build is indistinguishable from a torn tail to an older reader, and replay **stops
  there by design** — which would be a silent truncation. The gate is the mitigation.
- **The hard ceiling on the pause** is the kernel's `ctrl_loss_tmo`; past it the kernel deletes
  the controllers and I/O turns from "paused" into "failed". This build connects with
  `reconnect_delay=1` / `ctrl_loss_tmo=1800` (30 minutes); every controller must be checked
  before an upgrade.

## Not included yet

- **The production orchestration script is not landed**, so one-click upgrades still take the
  planned (disconnect) path. This PR delivers the mechanism, reachable by hand via
  `rcow_hot_stop.sh`.
- Cross-SPDK layout compatibility has no end-to-end verification.
- The `TimeoutStopSec` edge (a stop taking longer than 600 s) has not been stressed.

title: feat: add GAUGE perf metrics and replace --enable-ivshmem
body:
Add host-side performance collection for sandboxes. The guest kernel module writes counters into a shared-memory device; the host maps that same region and reads them. The device has to exist in the template snapshot, so collection is opted in at template build with --enable-metric.

Drop the unused open-source --enable-ivshmem /
cube.master.enable_ivshmem path. The old demo ivshmem helpers now implement GAUGE only: CubeMaster, CubeShim, CubeAPI, and the Python SDK expose a single switch (--enable-metric / enableMetric / cube.master.perf.metric). A VM still has one ivshmem slot, so the two flags could never coexist.

How to collect metrics:

1. Build the template with --enable-metric:

   cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \ --image <sandbox-code:latest> \ --writable-layer-size 1G \ --expose-port 49999 --expose-port 49983 \ --probe 49999 \ --enable-metric

2. After the sandbox is running, insmod cube_gauge.ko in the guest.

3. On the host, read the sandbox gauge.shmem with open-cube-gauge-sdk:

   CGO_ENABLED=1 go run ./demo <sid>

title: Open Issues and Pull Requests Related to envd in CubeSandbox
body:
## Overview

- **Direct or core envd issues: 4**
- **Substantively related SDK, runtime, or image issues: 3**
- **Architecture and lifecycle boundary issues: 3**
- **Core `cube-envd` implementation pull requests: 5**, with substantial overlap among several proposals
- **Other pull requests that directly fix or deliver envd capabilities: 6**
- **Boundary-related pull requests: 1**

The most important workstream is [Issue #1227](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1227), which proposes a CubeSandbox-maintained in-guest data-plane daemon. At least five open pull requests currently pursue this goal. [Pull Request #1723](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1723) explicitly declares that it closes #1227. These pull requests are **competing or overlapping implementations** and should not be treated as independent changes that can simply be merged one after another.

## Open Issues

### 1. Direct or Core envd Issues

| Issue | Category | Summary | Relationships and Current Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1227 — Introduce a CubeSandbox-maintained minimal envd implementation](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1227) | In-house implementation / ownership | Proposes replacing the upstream Go envd with a repository-maintained Rust `cube-envd`, covering readiness checks, `/init`, commands, files, and compatibility testing. The goal is to remove CubeSandbox's dependence on the E2B upstream implementation roadmap and release cadence. | [#1723](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1723) explicitly declares `Closes #1227`. Other pull requests addressing the same topic are [#1610](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1610), [#1729](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1729), [#1730](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1730), and the sparsely described [#1728](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1728). The earlier #1311 is closed. |
| [#1233 — Should template envs be visible to `commands.run` / PTY?](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1233) | Environment variable semantics | When envd starts commands or PTYs, it uses variables injected through `/init` but does not inherit the complete OS or template environment. The issue discusses whether template, create-time, and call-level environment variables should be merged and how precedence should work. | No open pull request. Comments lean toward the current behavior matching E2B, but the product contract or documentation still needs clarification. |
| [#934 — E2B SDK 2.26+/2.29 `commands.run` silently hangs against envd 0.5.11](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/934) | SDK / protocol compatibility | Concerns command streaming, ineffective timeouts, and proxy `Host` routing. The original hang can no longer be reproduced with newer envd releases, but questions remain about the supported SDK range and client routing contract. | No open pull request. Pull request #1187, which documents compatible versions, has been merged, but the issue remains open. |
| [#1404 — Go SDK Watcher response body is subject to concurrent double-close](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1404) | Go SDK / stream lifecycle | The natural termination and explicit close paths of `Watcher` in `sdk/go/envd.go` can execute concurrently and close the HTTP response body more than once. | Fix pull request [#1405](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1405) explicitly declares `Fixes #1404`. |

### 2. Substantively Related SDK, Runtime, or Image Issues

| Issue | Category | Summary | Relationships and Current Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1126 — Python SDK filesystem user isolation and command dependency](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1126) | Python SDK / user isolation | The Python SDK needs to propagate `username` to envd filesystem RPCs, remove the optional E2B Protobuf dependency, and handle missing home directories or working directories for non-root users. | [#1261](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1261) implements SDK-side changes and records the remaining envd gap, but it is not configured to close the issue automatically. |
| [#1570 — Node SDK `files.read` ignores format and always UTF-8-decodes](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1570) | Multi-language SDKs / binary files | SDKs treat envd file responses as UTF-8 text, breaking `bytes`, `blob`, and `stream` formats as well as binary content. The primary defect is client-side. | [#1571](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1571) fixes the Node, Python, and Go SDKs and declares `Fixes #1570`. |
| [#565 — Create-time envs are not fully propagated to sandbox runtime execution](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/565) | Environment variables / code interpreter | Propagation from CubeAPI to envd `/init` has been fixed, but `sandbox-code`'s `run_code` still does not read envd `/envs`. Consequently, `commands.run` and `run_code` can observe different environments in the same sandbox. | The envd-backed command path was fixed by merged pull request #566. The remaining image/runtime portion is addressed by [#1323](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1323), which declares `Fixes #565`. |

### 3. Architecture and Lifecycle Boundary Issues

These items genuinely involve envd, but envd is not the sole or primary implementation boundary of the current problem.

| Issue | Category | Summary | Relationships and Current Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1294 — Support deferred configuration updates for paused sandboxes before resume](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1294) | Pause/resume / configuration refresh | Proposes updating environment variables and volumes while a sandbox is paused and applying them before resume. The environment portion needs a defined mechanism for refreshing in-guest services and specifying visibility to subsequent envd commands and PTYs. | No pull request. This is a potential envd integration requirement rather than an existing envd defect. |
| [#1308 — Add in-sandbox lifecycle hooks for pause and resume](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1308) | Lifecycle orchestration | A `postResume` hook must wait until the guest and envd are ready. The proposed implementation is driven by Cubelet through containerd exec or HTTP and deliberately avoids modifying the external envd. | [#1315](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1315) declares that it resolves this issue. |
| [#1338 — Why retain container semantics inside a microVM sandbox?](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/1338) | Long-term architecture | The architecture discussion identifies envd as the user-facing Process and Filesystem API boundary and considers which preparation logic might move into envd if the container layer were removed. | No pull request. This is not a specific envd functional defect. |

## Open Pull Requests

### 1. Core `cube-envd` Implementations: Competing or Overlapping Proposals

| Pull Request | Positioning and Scope | Status at Search Time | Relationship to Other Proposals |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1723 — CubeSandbox-maintained in-guest data-plane daemon](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1723) | A full Rust implementation covering REST, Process, Filesystem, PTY, file watching, authentication, and cgroups. It includes a black-box conformance harness, SDK end-to-end tests, and performance data. The base image switches to Rust by default while retaining `/usr/bin/envd-go` and the `ENVD_BIN`/`ENVD_IMPL` rollback paths. | Not a draft; `BLOCKED`; explicitly declares `Closes #1227`. | Has the broadest scope and most extensive validation material. It overlaps heavily with #1610, #1729, and #1730. |
| [#1610 — Introduce in-repo Rust cube-envd and replace upstream Go envd](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1610) | Integrates the Rust envd with builds, base images, CI, releases, documentation, and SDK compatibility tests. It intends to replace the upstream Go envd by default and supports static musl builds for amd64 and arm64. | Not a draft; `BLOCKED`; some dual-architecture image validation remains incomplete. | Like #1723 and #1730, it follows a “Rust by default, Go available for rollback” direction and is a competing implementation. |
| [#1729 — Add optional Rust sandbox daemon](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1729) | A comparatively complete Rust implementation that **keeps Go as the default**. Users explicitly build a Rust base image and switch through new templates and sandboxes. It includes component, image, real-platform, arm64 QEMU, and performance validation. | Not a draft; `BLOCKED`. | Narrows the original “replace the default” goal of #1227 and represents a more conservative competing proposal. |
| [#1730 — CubeSandbox-maintained in-guest data-plane daemon](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1730) | A Rust implementation covering health/init/envs/status/files, Process, Filesystem, file watching, and PTY. The base image uses Rust by default while retaining the upstream Go Dockerfile and an `ENVD_IMPL` rollback option, with CI integration. | Not a draft; `UNKNOWN`; its description says publishing currently covers only linux/amd64. | Overlaps heavily with #1723 and #1610, but describes a smaller feature and validation scope. |
| [#1728 — Feat/cube envd](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1728) | Its title and branch point to `cube-envd`, but the pull request body only says “The First PR,” so its compatibility scope, integration approach, and validation cannot be determined from the description. | Not a draft; `DIRTY`. | Likely another implementation of the same proposal. More information from the diff or the author is needed before comparison. |

#### Main Decision Points Across the Core Proposals

1. **Default replacement or optional trial:** #1723, #1610, and #1730 propose placing Rust on the default path; #1729 keeps Go as the default.
2. **Rollback mechanism:** #1723 retains the Go binary and supports both runtime and build-time switching; #1730 also retains a Go build path; #1729 switches through separate images and templates without automatic or in-place rollback.
3. **Protocol coverage and strength of evidence:** #1723 claims the complete RPC surface and provides 122 black-box scenarios, SDK end-to-end tests, real guest/cgroup tests, and performance data. The other proposals use different coverage and validation criteria, so a common acceptance matrix should be established before merging.
4. **Multi-architecture publishing:** Every proposal mentions amd64 and arm64, but their actual native validation, QEMU validation, and image publishing coverage differ.
5. **Avoiding duplicate merges:** These pull requests modify many of the same components, Dockerfiles, CI workflows, SDKs, and documentation. A primary implementation should be selected first, after which missing capabilities or tests can be taken from the other proposals.

### 2. Other Pull Requests That Directly Fix or Deliver envd Capabilities

| Pull Request | Category | Summary | Related Issue / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1405 — Prevent concurrent double-close on Watcher response body](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1405) | Go SDK | Uses a single `sync.Once`-guarded close path to eliminate duplicate or concurrent closes between natural Watcher termination and explicit shutdown, and adds stress tests. | `Fixes #1404`. |
| [#1261 — Add user isolation support to the Python SDK](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1261) | Python SDK / user isolation | Propagates the execution user through command and filesystem APIs, removes command execution's dependency on the optional E2B client, and expands dual-backend SDK compatibility tests. It also documents the envd limitation for per-user filesystem operations. | Corresponds to #1126 but does not close it automatically. Further envd server work remains. |
| [#1571 — Honor E2B `files.read` formats across Node, Python, and Go](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1571) | Multi-language SDKs / file reads | Provides correct text, byte, blob, and stream read semantics for Node, Python, and Go, preventing binary content from being corrupted by UTF-8 decoding. | `Fixes #1570`. |
| [#1323 — Add a derived `sandbox-code` image with `run_code` environment inheritance](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1323) | Example image / environment variables | The derived `sandbox-code` image reads create-time environment variables from envd `/envs` and provides restoration and cleanup semantics for per-call `run_code` environment overlays. | `Fixes #565`; this is an opt-in example and does not modify the default image. |
| [#1671 — Preserve diagnostics for custom-image envd smoke tests](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1671) | BYOI documentation / diagnostics | Revises the English and Chinese bring-your-own-image tutorials so logs are not lost through `--rm` after startup failures. It adds envd health and version probes, timeouts, state checks, and failure investigation steps. | A direct documentation-level envd operations improvement with no corresponding issue. |
| [#1578 — Improve code-sandbox quickstart for local development and create-time envs](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1578) | Example / environment variable workaround | Adds a remote data-plane sidecar to the quickstart and reapplies create-time environment variables in cubebox/VNC templates to work around environment loss after entrypoint startup. | Related to environment propagation, but it is an example-side workaround and does not resolve the envd contract itself. |

### 3. Lifecycle Boundary Pull Request

| Pull Request | Category | Summary | Related Issue / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1315 — Add in-sandbox lifecycle hooks for pause/resume](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1315) | Cubelet / lifecycle | Adds `prePause` and `postResume` exec or HTTP hooks. `:49983/health` can be used to wait for envd readiness, but Cubelet drives the mechanism and envd is not modified. | Declares that it resolves #1308. This is adjacent to envd rather than an envd implementation change. |

## Dependency and Clustering Map

```text
#1227 CubeSandbox-maintained cube-envd
├── #1723  Full Rust default implementation + Go rollback (explicitly closes #1227)
├── #1610  Rust default implementation + build/release/SDK tests
├── #1729  Optional Rust implementation; Go remains the default
├── #1730  Rust default implementation + Go rollback path
└── #1728  Same topic, but insufficient description

#1404 Go Watcher double-close ─────────── #1405
#1126 Python SDK user isolation ───────── #1261 (envd server gap remains)
#1570 files.read binary formats ───────── #1571
#565 Create-time environment propagation
├── #566 (merged): CubeAPI → envd /init → commands.run
└── #1323 (open): envd /envs → sandbox-code run_code
#1308 Pause/resume hooks ───────────────── #1315 (driven by Cubelet; no envd change)
```

## Suggested Order of Work

1. **Converge on an implementation for #1227 first:** Select a primary proposal from #1723/#1610/#1729/#1730/#1728, focusing on default-switch policy, rollback, protocol conformance, real-platform validation, and multi-architecture publishing.
2. **Merge independent, well-scoped SDK fixes:** Address #1405 and #1571 first, then #1261, with an explicit follow-up item for its envd server gap.
3. **Define the environment variable contract:** Handle #1233, #565/#1323, and #1294 together, documenting the source, precedence, persistence, and post-pause/resume behavior of template, create-time, and call-level environment variables.
4. **Retain explicit version compatibility documentation:** Even after an in-house envd lands, the SDK/envd/proxy compatibility matrix highlighted by #934 must remain a testable, publishable contract rather than relying on the fact that the original failure is currently unreproducible.
5. **Review boundary work separately from the core implementation:** #1315, #1671, and #1578 can be reviewed independently and need not block the in-house envd workstream, but they should not count toward completion of core protocol compatibility.

title: perf(hypervisor): move pause VM teardown off the pause critical path
body:
## Summary

`vm_pause_to_snapshot` runs `vm_pause` + `vm_snapshot` + `vm_delete` serially inside the RPC, so the pause client waits ~100 ms for VM destruction — vcpu thread joins, KVM device close (including `synchronize_srcu` in irqfd shutdown), and `munmap` of the entire guest memory — **after the snapshot is already durably written**. The pause contract is fulfilled once `vm_snapshot` returns.

This PR moves the teardown into a background thread and pushes its `JoinHandle` onto `Vmm::threads`, which `control_loop` already joins on exit — so the shim's exit path still waits for full resource cleanup. The teardown thread writes `exit_evt` when done so the control loop wakes up and joins even if `shutdown()` errors before signalling the vcpus.

Two accompanying changes required by the move:

- **shim**: drop the wait for the `VmShutdown` notification after pause-to-snapshot. It now fires from the background teardown, and writing `metadata.json` does not depend on the VM being gone.
- **vsock muxer**: unlink a stale host socket file before `UnixListener::bind`. A previous shim instance for the same sandbox ID may leave its file behind; bind fails on an existing path, so drop a stale file first (live listeners keep working via their fd).

## Performance

aarch64, 384-core host, 2C2G template, 250 samples per data point (5 rounds × 50 at c50; 5 rounds at c1), zero retries, baseline re-anchored before and after:

| | baseline | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| pause c1 req_avg (ms) | 165.9 | **86.5 (-47.9%)** |
| pause c50 req_avg (ms) | 399.1 | **323.9 (-18.8%)** |
| pause c50 wall_avg (ms) | 574.5 | 510.4 |

Single-guest VMM pause window: ~131 ms → ~25-30 ms (teardown fully off the critical path). Phase timings are logged as `pause phases: pause=… snapshot=…` for reproduction.

## Testing done

- [x] `cargo build --release` (CubeShim workspace, aarch64)
- [x] Concurrent pause bench at c1 and c50 (250 / 5 samples), zero retries, baseline re-anchored before and after

Signed-off-by: lzh <740203701@qq.com>

title: feat(cube-envd): add optional Rust sandbox daemon
body:
## Summary

新增由 CubeSandbox 自主维护的 Rust cube-envd，在 sandbox 内提供健康检查、命令执行、PTY 和文件操作等数据面能力，并接入现有基础镜像构建与模板创建流程。

当前 CubeSandbox 默认使用上游 Go envd。本 PR 提供从本仓库源码构建的 Rust 替代实现，便于后续按项目需求维护和扩展，同时保持现有 SDK 的核心调用方式。

**本次保留 Go 默认，Rust 由用户自行构建并显式选择。** 因此，本 PR 调整了原需求中“默认使用 Rust”的交付范围；Rust 构建不依赖编译上游 Go envd，原有 Go 构建入口及其上游依赖继续保留。

## Design

沿用 envd 的 HTTP 与 Process/Filesystem RPC 接口，将协议适配与 Linux 进程、文件系统操作分开：

- `server` 负责启动、就绪状态、关键任务监督和关闭；`transport` 负责路由、认证、CORS、协议编解码与错误响应。
- `process` 管理命令、PTY、输入输出、信号、超时和退出状态。
- `filesystem` 提供元数据、目录操作和监听，文件内容通过 HTTP `/files` 上传、下载，并支持文件拼接。
- `init`、`runtime` 和 `guest` 处理初始化、环境变量、执行用户、元数据、日志、指标、TCP 转发及空闲连接。
- 镜像复用共享 entrypoint，监督 daemon 与可选应用进程；daemon 退出后停止应用和容器，避免应用仍存活却无法提供 sandbox 数据面服务。

实现使用仓库统一的 Rust 工具链和锁定依赖。平台集成复用现有模板、代理和 SDK 流程，没有为验收增加平台生产测试接口。

## Build and Integration

从仓库根目录使用以下入口：

| 入口 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `make -C cube-envd build` | 本机开发构建 |
| `make cube-envd TARGET_ARCH=amd64` | 导出 Rust 静态二进制 |
| `make cube-base-rust TARGET_ARCH=amd64` | 显式构建 Rust 基础镜像 |
| `make cube-base TARGET_ARCH=amd64` | 保留原 Go 基础镜像构建 |

镜像和静态二进制目标也支持 `TARGET_ARCH=arm64`。已有 example 可通过基础镜像参数选择 Rust，再经现有模板流程创建 sandbox。

切换实现通过选择镜像并创建新模板、新 sandbox 完成；不会迁移已有 sandbox 的运行状态，也不会在 Rust daemon 失败时自动切换为 Go。构建命令生成本地产物，不代表已有公开发布的 Rust 镜像。

## Compatibility

协议实现参照 `e2b-dev/infra@2026.16`，核心功能通过 CubeSandbox Python SDK 0.7.0 在本地平台验证：

- 健康检查及运行中 daemon 身份确认。
- 命令执行：stdout/stderr、非零退出、环境变量、默认 root、显式执行用户和超时。
- 文件读写：UTF-8、空文件、覆盖截断、缺失文件、SDK 与命令双向读写，以及二进制写入后通过命令核对。
- Rust 镜像创建新模板、达到 READY、SDK 创建 sandbox，并完成命令和文件操作。

组件测试进一步覆盖 Process/PTY、Filesystem 元数据和目录监听、HTTP 文件传输、认证及协议错误行为。兼容结论限于已实现的接口和已执行的测试，不代表所有 E2B SDK 版本及上游功能均已验证。

## Known Differences and Limitations

- Rust 分别报告产品版本和 envd 兼容版本；Go/Rust 的版本字符串不同，不能据此推断完整功能等价。
- cgroup v2 初始化失败时，Rust 记录警告并使用 no-op manager，与 Go 的初始化降级方式一致。子进程继承已有 cgroup，不施加 envd 额外分组；成功启用分组后的归组错误仍拒绝对应进程。平台与 VM 的既有隔离保持独立。
- 二进制文件写入已验证，但通过命令核对字节不代表 SDK 已支持二进制 read。
- 真实平台验收覆盖原生 amd64、Cloud Hypervisor 和 guest cgroup v1。arm64 镜像使用全系统 QEMU 验证，不等同于原生 arm64 平台验收。
- 原生 arm64 组件及平台、Firecracker 平台和远端 GitHub Actions 尚未完成运行验证。ignored、skip 和未运行项不计通过。
- 本 PR 聚焦功能交付，不提供性能对比结论或性能优势承诺。

## Test plan

| 验证范围 | 实际结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 真实平台完整链路 | Rust/Go 各通过一条：镜像 → 新模板 READY → SDK 创建 sandbox → daemon 身份与 health 204 → 命令及文件操作 → 清理 |
| 独立平台场景 | health/identity、commands、files 在 Rust/Go 上分别通过，共六次独立运行 |
| amd64 Rust 组件检查 | fmt、Clippy、build、check 完成；184 项 Rust 测试通过，3 项 VM 夹具 ignored |
| 内嵌 Python 与 guest 服务场景 | 6 项 Python 场景通过；guest 服务 9 项通过、1 项 IPv6 skip；属于同次组件 CI，不与 Rust 数量累加 |
| SDK E2E 框架自身测试 | 122 项通过，与真实平台场景分别统计 |
| amd64 镜像测试 | Rust/Go 分别 18/18 通过 |
| QEMU arm64 镜像测试 | Rust 18/18 通过；Go 原轮 7 项 image 测试通过，11 项 supervisor 中有 1 项失败 |
| supervisor 夹具修复后复验 | amd64 和 QEMU arm64 分别 11/11 通过；不是 Go arm64 全套镜像测试重跑 |

Go arm64 原轮失败来自测试 worker 读取尚未写完的退出码文件；夹具改为原子发布后完成上述复验。报告保留原失败与修复后结果。

组件验证使用源码只读挂载、私有 cgroup 和移除 SYS_TIME 的隔离环境。后续文档整理仅进行了静态命令、链接和示例检查，没有将历史功能测试描述为文档提交后重新执行的结果。受测构建身份与验证边界见功能验收报告。

## Performance

通过现有 SDK/CubeProxy 路径，在原生 amd64 平台进行五组独立 sandbox
对比，并发为 1，每个实现、每个场景共 500 个正式样本，操作错误为 0。

| 场景 | Rust 修复前 median ms | Rust 修复后 median ms | Go median ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 短命令 | 47.892 | 14.348 | 16.026 |
| 4 KiB 读取 | 44.093 | 1.813 | 1.451 |
| 4 KiB 写入 | 2.404 | 1.475 | 1.319 |
| 4 MiB 读取 | 58.065 | 26.965 | 33.636 |
| 4 MiB 写入 | 32.144 | 31.493 | 12.764 |

入站连接启用 TCP_NODELAY 后，短命令、小文件读写及大文件读取的 median 在全部五组中均较修复前改善。本轮 Rust 短命令和大文件读取快于 Go，小文件操作总体仍落后 Go；大文件写入仍约为 Go 延迟的 2.47 倍。

以上为暖缓存、固定内容下的 SDK 端到端测量，不代表所有场景或生产性能。逐组 median/p95、根因证据、资源与并发检查见 [详细性能报告](cube-envd/doc/performance_zh.md)。

## Documentation

本 PR 提供中英文文档，覆盖架构、源码组织、自行构建、模板接入、API 和功能验收：

- `cube-envd/README.md` / `README_zh.md`：组件概览、架构图、目录职责和构建测试入口。
- `cube-envd/doc/usage.md` / `usage_zh.md`：模板创建、SDK 配置及命令和文件示例。
- `cube-envd/doc/cube-envd-api.md` / `cube-envd-api_zh.md`：HTTP、Process、Filesystem、认证和流式协议。
- `cube-envd/doc/validation.md` / `validation_zh.md`：功能结果、兼容边界和复跑入口。
- `cube-envd/doc/validation/functional-excerpts.md`：脱敏功能测试日志摘录。

title: fix(network,lifecycle): per-request MTU, cross-node lease renewal, sweeper grace
body:
# Fix three sandbox lifecycle issues: per-request MTU, cross-node lease renewal, sweeper-after-resume race

Addresses #1673, #1690, #1692, #1683.

Includes a follow-up commit addressing feedback from the
in-house PR review bot (lease-renewer stop-on-resume gap, pool
tap MTU re-write, mtu_interface default-clobber fix, per-call
MTU resolution consolidation).

## Summary

Three independent fixes in the sandbox provisioning and lifecycle stack:

1. **#1673** — Guest MTU is no longer hardcoded to 1500. Operators can
   configure a runtime default via `mvm_mtu` or have the runtime
   mirror a host link's live MTU via `mtu_interface` (typically the
   Kubernetes parent bridge `cbr0`). Required for overlay networks
   whose transport MTU is below the Ethernet default.

2. **#1690 / #1692** — Cross-node resume no longer races the S3 lease
   reaper. The source Cubelet keeps the paused snapshot's export
   alive via a process-local lease renewer until Resume / Destroy /
   a Pause failure explicitly stops it.

3. **#1683** — The auto-pause sweeper no longer immediately re-pauses
   a freshly-resumed sandbox. A new `ResumeGrace` window (default 60 s)
   exempts resumed sandboxes from the idle check, gated on a
   `ResumedAtMs` timestamp the resumer stamps on success.

## Changes by area

### Cubelet — network runtime (Task 2 / #1673)

* `Cubelet/network/runtime/config.go` — new `MTUInterface` config
  field, `DefaultGuestMTU` constant (1500), `EffectiveMTU()` resolver
  in three tiers (per-request → `MvmMtu` → live host-link MTU →
  default), `resolveMTUOnce()` helper for the single-shot
  EnsureNetwork path.
* `Cubelet/network/runtime/controller.go` — `acquireTap` now takes an
  MTU; the pool-hit branch calls `ensureTapMTU` so a pooled tap
  whose previous owner had a different MTU is re-MTU'd.
  `actualInterfaces` takes a pre-resolved MTU rather than calling
  `EffectiveMTU()` independently (transient netlink errors can
  no longer desync host TAP and guest eth0). cube-dev / cube-router
  use `EffectiveMTU()`.
* `Cubelet/network/runtime/{tap_lifecycle,startup_recover,tap_cleaner}.go` —
  every tap create / restore site now calls `EffectiveMTU()`
  instead of `cfg.MvmMtu` directly (no more `LinkSetMTU(tap, 0)`
  when `mtu_interface` mode is active and `mvm_mtu` is unset).
* `Cubelet/network/types/network.go` — new `NetRequest.MTU` field
  (omitempty, backward compatible). Plumbed through the
  EnsureNetwork path; the host TAP and the guest eth0 share the
  resolved value via a single `resolveMTUOnce` call so a transient
  netlink error cannot desync them. (`NetRequest.MTU` is set by
  the caller's `cube.master.net` annotation today; wiring it
  from a Master API is a follow-up.)
* `Cubelet/network/plugin_shim.go` — `buildEnsureNetworkRequestFromIntent`
  resolves the requested MTU in three tiers matching the runtime.
* `Cubelet/network/plugin_tap.go` — new `MTUInterface` TOML field,
  plumbed into the runtime Config. The MvmMtu assignment is now
  conditional so an unset `mvm_mtu` in TOML no longer clobbers
  the runtime default with zero.

No Rust changes — `CubeShim/shim/src/sandbox/net.rs` already passes
`Mtu` from `ShimNetReq` straight through to the guest kernel.

### Cubelet — pause lease renewer (Task 3 / #1690, #1692)

* `Cubelet/storage/lease_renewer.go` (new) — `Renewer` type with
  per-snapID renewal goroutines (30 s interval, lazy-init
  singleton on `localStorage`).
* `Cubelet/storage/lease_renewer.go` — `Unregister` is deterministic:
  the per-call context in `renew` derives from `entry.cancel`,
  so closing it aborts the in-flight `UploadSnapshot` immediately
  rather than racing a 5 s wall-clock against a 60 s per-call
  timeout. Aborted-by-Unregister errors log at debug so the
  normal log filter no longer shows the path-out as a failure.
* `Cubelet/storage/local.go` — `RegisterPauseLease` /
  `UnregisterPauseLease` / `ActivePauseLeases` accessors.
* `Cubelet/services/cubebox/pause_cow.go` — Register on Pause
  success when remote UUIDs were returned. Unregister when
  `destroyLiveAfterPause` fails (the snapshot stays on disk but
  Master will not drive a Resume).
* `Cubelet/services/cubebox/service.go` — Unregister on Destroy
  immediately before `bestEffortCleanupPauseSnapshot` runs.
  Unregister on Resume (Create-from-pause) when the resume-side
  cubebox is still findable in the manager.

### cube-lifecycle-manager — sweeper race (Task 4 / #1683)

* `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/registry/registry.go` — new
  `Entry.ResumedAtMs` field, new `Registry.MarkResumed()` setter.
* `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/config/config.go` — new
  `Config.ResumeGrace` field, default 60 s, env var
  `CUBE_LCM_RESUME_GRACE`.
* `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/sweeper/sweeper.go` — new gate in
  `sweepOnce`; new `Options.ResumeGrace`.
* `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/resumer/resumer.go` — stamp
  `ResumedAtMs` after success-bookkeeping writes.
* `cube-lifecycle-manager/cmd/cube-lifecycle-manager/main.go` — wire
  `cfg.ResumeGrace` into the sweeper Options.

## Tests

* `Cubelet/network/runtime/config_test.go` (new) — locks the
  `EffectiveMTU` resolution order, the live-link branch on Linux,
  and `resolveMTUOnce`.
* `Cubelet/storage/lease_renewer_test.go` (new) — covers
  idempotent registration, XFS / unknown-backend no-ops,
  per-snapID concurrent uniqueness, and the new
  deterministic Unregister path (returns within 2 s even
  mid-tick).
* `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/registry/registry_resumed_test.go`
  (new) — covers `MarkResumed` forward-only semantics and Upsert
  preservation.
* `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/sweeper/sweeper_test.go` — three
  new tests for the `ResumeGrace` gate (in-window skip,
  post-window act, zero-grace disable).

Verified locally on macOS via cross-compiled Go test binaries:
`cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/{registry,sweeper,resumer,config}`
all pass (no regressions, 30 + new cases). Rust build is
Linux-only — full test run belongs in the project's
`cube-sandbox-builder:ubuntu2004` Docker CI.

## Risk / compatibility

* **MTU change is additive.** Existing deployments that left
  `mvm_mtu` at 1500 see no change. Setting `mtu_interface = "cbr0"`
  is opt-in.
* **Lease renewer is idempotent and bounded.** A Renewer goroutine
  re-exports via `UploadSnapshot` every 30 s with a 60 s per-call
  timeout; Pause retries and process restart are safe. Unregister
  is deterministic — closing `entry.cancel` aborts the in-flight
  call instead of racing a wall-clock timeout.
* **ResumeGrace defaults to 60 s.** Set `CUBE_LCM_RESUME_GRACE=0`
  to disable the gate entirely (legacy behaviour). Operationally
  silent — a sandbox paused because it was genuinely idle for > 60 s
  after resume still pauses normally.
