title: fix(cubemaster): classify postgres alias errors by sqlstate
body:
## Summary

Fix intermittent PostgreSQL CI failures when publishing template status with an alias.

## Root Cause

`isDuplicateAliasError` detected PostgreSQL duplicate key errors by searching arbitrary error text for `23505` or `unique_constraint`.

When a wrapped PostgreSQL `22001` error included a template ID containing `23505`, it was incorrectly classified as a duplicate alias error. The fallback path then suppressed the expected alias claim warning.

## Changes

- Classify MySQL duplicate aliases using structured error code `1062`.
- Classify PostgreSQL duplicate aliases using `pgconn.PgError.Code == "23505"`.
- Classify PostgreSQL deadlocks using SQLSTATE `40P01` and `55P03`.
- Preserve wrapped error handling through `errors.As`.
- Add regression tests for:
  - Wrapped PostgreSQL `22001` errors with template IDs containing `23505`.
  - Direct and wrapped PostgreSQL `23505` errors.
  - MySQL `1062` and non-duplicate errors.
  - Misleading error text containing `23505` or `unique_constraint`.

## Validation

- Templatecenter classification unit tests passed.
- PostgreSQL Docker test `TestAliasStorePostgreSQL` passed.
- Verified alias claim failure returns the warning, leaves the template in `READY`, and invalidates query caches.
- Changes are limited to CubeMaster error classification logic and tests.

title: feat(cube-envd): CubeSandbox-maintained in-guest data-plane daemon
body:
**Closes:** #1227 --- ## Summary This PR replaces the upstream Go `envd` in the base image with `cube-envd`, a CubeSandbox-maintained Rust implementation of the same in-guest data plane, behavior-matched fixture-by-fixture against a recorded Go envd 0.5.13 baseline. The Go binary is still built and shipped as `/usr/bin/envd-go`, so rollback is a single environment variable at sandbox startup and needs no image rebuild. | | | |---|---| | Change set | `cube-envd/` implementation, conformance harness, image integration, and SDK compatibility changes | | Build | Rust 1.89, static musl binary; Go 0.5.13 retained for rollback | | New test asset | `tests/e2e/envd_conformance/` — black-box conformance harness | | Default changed | `docker/Dockerfile.cube-base` now installs cube-envd as `/usr/bin/envd` | | Rollback | `ENVD_BIN=/usr/bin/envd-go`, or rebuild with `--build-arg ENVD_IMPL=go` | Everything lands behind the existing `ENVD_BIN` switch that `docker/cube-entrypoint.sh` already reads, so the guest contract (`envd -port 49983 -isnotfc` on `:49983`) is unchanged. ## Motivation envd runs inside every sandbox and is the compatibility boundary between the E2B SDKs and the CubeSandbox runtime. Consuming it from `e2b-dev/infra` means the implementation roadmap, fix cadence, and release schedule are owned elsewhere, and the shipped binary carries integration paths CubeSandbox never exercises: Firecracker MMDS polling, Hyperloop configuration, and NFS volume initialization. Issue #1227 laid out the proposal, the Rust-vs-Go reasoning, and the conditions for adopting cube-envd on the default path. This PR delivers the full implementation rather than the MVP subset #1227 scoped as a first milestone, so it closes that issue rather than reporting against it: declared conformance differences are explicit and allowlisted, SDK end-to-end covers command and file behavior, a template built with cube-envd creates a usable sandbox, performance measurements are published per workload, and the `ENVD_BIN` rollback to Go envd is verified. The merged performance work is deliberately reported per workload instead of collapsed into one headline. Rust has lower idle RSS and faster direct startup; the optimized command/PTY spawn paths and process-output path compare well with Go in their measured shapes; `/files` remains workload-dependent, with near-parity single-stream behavior and a remaining advantage for Go's `sendfile` path once high-concurrency downloads become CPU-bound. Rust is not adopted on the promise of a universal benchmark win; the numbers are published here so they can be checked. ## Scope This is a full envd implementation, not an MVP subset. Every RPC the E2B envd service declares is implemented and conformance-tested, including the parts issue #1227 originally deferred: PTY, interactive stdin, the whole watch family, and cgroup-specific behavior. `cube-envd/src/app/routes.rs` is the complete list — 8 of 8 `process.Process` RPCs, 9 of 9 `filesystem.Filesystem` RPCs, and the REST surface used by the platform. **In scope and implemented.** - REST: `GET /health` (204), `POST /init` (envVars merge, optional accessToken, timestamp gate), `GET /envs`, `GET /metrics`, `GET/POST /files` (octet-stream + multipart, relative paths, ownership, Go errno vocabulary). - `process.Process`: `Start`, `Connect`, `List`, `SendSignal`, `SendInput`, `StreamInput`, `CloseStdin`, `Update` — including PTY allocation with window resize and CRLF line discipline, pipe and PTY stdin, injected input, and `CloseStdin` EOF. - `filesystem.Filesystem`: `Stat`, `ListDir`, `MakeDir`, `Move`, `Remove`, `WatchDir`, `CreateWatcher`, `GetWatcherEvents`, `RemoveWatcher` — including the streaming watch family and pull watchers. - CLI: Go `flag`-compatible parsing for `-port`, `-isnotfc`, `-version`, `-commit`, and `-h`. - Auth: `Authorization: Basic base64(":")` / `username` query, `/etc/passwd` resolution, privilege drop, and `X-Access-Token` gating. - Guest integration: cgroup v2 per-command leaf placement, OOM attribution, process-group cleanup, and a deployment-reachable cgroup memory cap. **Residual protocol gaps.** These are explicit rather than silent: | Gap | Behavior | Why | |---|---|---| | `/files/compose` | HTTP 501 | The endpoint stays in the route table so callers get an explicit 501 rather than a misleading 404. | | gzip download encoding | Serves identity only; refuses unacceptable identity with upstream-compatible 406 behavior | gzip is applied by CubeProxy rather than the daemon. | | Multi-range `GET /files` | Serves the whole file with 200 instead of upstream's `206 multipart/byteranges` | A multipart range writer is not implemented; single-range and conditional requests are implemented. | | `HEAD /files` | Axum serves 200 with the GET headers, while upstream has no HEAD route and returns 405 | Framework-level route behavior; recorded as a declared conformance difference. | | Connect binary-protobuf codec | Rejected up front with a stable `unimplemented` naming the JSON codec | Every known client in this repository and the official E2B Python/JS SDKs uses the JSON codec. | `/files` signature verification is **not** a gap: cube-envd implements the endpoint surface upstream exposes, and upstream's signing path is not part of the SDK-observable contract this daemon reproduces. An earlier draft of this PR description listed it as unimplemented; that was incorrect, and it is not in the code or the conformance suite. Unrecognized **input shapes** on implemented RPCs — an empty process selector, a `StreamInput` event with zero or multiple arms, or an empty `ProcessInput` oneof — answer `unimplemented` with upstream-compatible text. That is alignment with Go envd's default branch, not a missing feature, and unit tests pin the behavior. Nothing is signalled, attached to, or otherwise side-effected on those paths. ## Design `cube-envd/` is organized as a contract index and a dependency graph: a path states what is promised, an edge states who may call whom. Six layers, one allowed direction. ```mermaid graph TD app["app/
HTTP surface + startup wiring
routes · handlers · lifecycle · metrics
cli · pool · middleware"] fs["filesystem/
Stat · ListDir · MakeDir · Move · Remove
download · upload · watch
http/ — ranges · preconditions · httpdate"] proc["process/
Start · Connect · List · SendSignal
SendInput · StreamInput · CloseStdin · Update
supervisor · table · engine · cgroup"] plat["platform/
config · identity · lock"] proto["protocol/
frames · stream · error · keepalive · timeout"] compat["compat/
vocab — Go errno text table"] app --> fs app --> proc app --> plat fs --> plat fs --> proto fs --> compat proc --> plat proc --> proto proc --> compat plat --> proto plat --> compat proto --> compat fs -. "never" .-> proc proc -. "never" .-> fs fs -. "never" .-> app proc -. "never" .-> app plat -. "never" .-> app proto -. "never" .-> plat compat -. "never" .-> proto classDef allowed fill:#1f6feb22,stroke:#1f6feb,stroke-width:2px classDef sibling fill:#8957e522,stroke:#8957e5,stroke-width:2px class app,plat,proto,compat allowed class fs,proc sibling ``` Solid edges are the allowed direction; dotted edges are the ones the layer rule forbids. `filesystem/` and `process/` are siblings and never reference each other, and nothing below `app/` reaches back into it. This is enforced, not merely intended: `cube-envd/tests/layer_rule.rs` reads `src/` and fails the test suite on a forbidden module path, so an inverted edge cannot land while `cargo test`, `clippy`, and `fmt` stay green. | Layer | Responsibility | |---|---| | `app/` | HTTP surface and startup wiring: `routes.rs`, `handlers.rs`, `lifecycle.rs`, `metrics.rs`, Go-flag-compatible `cli.rs`, blocking-thread `pool.rs`, `middleware/{cors,legacy}.rs` | | `filesystem/` | Filesystem domain; `http/` owns content disposition, encoding, HTTP date, preconditions, and ranges; `watch/` owns inotify, tree, and watch pumping | | `process/` | Process domain; command lifecycle, output fan-out, PTY, cgroup, supervision, table, and engine | | `platform/` | Host-facing services shared by both domains: config, identity, user/group lookup, path anchoring, and locking | | `protocol/` | Connect wire layer: envelope codec, error model, keepalive, timeout, and stream primitives | | `compat/` | Go compatibility vocabulary and stable error text | `spec/` holds the protocol snapshots the `wire.rs` files mirror — the upstream OpenAPI document plus `filesystem.proto` and `process.proto` copied from `e2b-dev/infra@2026.16`. It is a conformance reference, not a build input. Notably, `/init` semantics were re-derived from the upstream source rather than assumed. An **equal** timestamp is accepted (`utils.AtomicMax.SetToGreater` only rejects strictly older values), and the timestamp gate runs **before** token validation, so a stale-timestamp `/init` returns 204 rather than 401. `/init` is also on the upstream auth allowlist: it does not check `X-Access-Token`, and token semantics come entirely from the request body. ## Integration and rollback `docker/Dockerfile.cube-base` compiles both implementations in parallel stages and selects one. The build context changes from `docker/` to the repository root because `cube-envd/` must be inside it. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph build["Build time — docker/Dockerfile.cube-base, context = repo root"] direction TB src_go["e2b-dev/infra@ENVD_REF
pin: 2026.16"] src_rust["cube-envd/
this repo"] subgraph b1["Stage 1a"] go_b["envd-go-builder
Go builder"] end subgraph b2["Stage 1b"] cube_b["envd-cube-builder
Rust 1.89 + musl-tools"] end src_go --> go_b src_rust --> cube_b go_b --> go_bin["/out/envd
Go binary"] cube_b --> cube_bin["/out/envd
musl static"] go_bin --> sel{"envd-default
ENVD_IMPL"} cube_bin --> sel end subgraph img["Runtime image — Ubuntu 22.04"] direction LR e1["/usr/bin/envd
selected impl"] e2["/usr/bin/envd-go
always present"] e3["/etc/cubesandbox-envd-impl
cube | go"] end sel -->|"ENVD_IMPL=cube (default)"| e1 sel -->|"ENVD_IMPL=go"| e1 sel --> e3 e1 --> entry["cube-entrypoint.sh
envd -port 49983 -isnotfc"] e2 -. "rollback target — ENVD_BIN" .-> entry ``` Rollback is available at both runtime and build time: ```mermaid flowchart LR start{"cube-envd is
the live data plane"} --> q1{"rollback scope?"} q1 -->|"one deployment,
image, or test template"| r1["set
ENVD_BIN=/usr/bin/envd-go"] q1 -->|"whole image,
at build time"| r2["docker build
--build-arg ENVD_IMPL=go"] q1 -->|"verify side by side"| r3["run the two conformance
containers, one per impl"] r1 --> out["previous Go envd behavior restored"] r2 --> out r3 --> out ``` Installing cube-envd as the literal `/usr/bin/envd` rather than only selecting it through `ENVD_BIN` matters because Cubelet version collection executes `envd --version`. `.dockerignore` admits `cube-envd/` while still excluding `cube-envd/target/`. CI triggers include `cube-envd/**`, the component matrix runs Rust tests/clippy, and `CUBE_ENVD_COMMIT` is threaded from the source revision into the image so `envd -commit` reports the build's source commit. ## SDK changes The Rust daemon reports richer termination information than upstream's EndEvent. This is a **CubeSandbox extension**. `signal`, `oomKilled`, and `killedBy` are additive and optional, so clients that ignore them keep the previous behavior. | SDK | Change | |---|---| | Go | `CommandResult` gains `Signal *int`, `OOMKilled bool`, `KilledBy string`; `PtyHandle` gains matching accessors | | Python | `CommandResult` gains `signal`, `oom_killed`, `killed_by`; `PtyHandle` gains matching properties | | Node | `CommandResult` gains optional `signal`, `oomKilled`, `killedBy`; `PtyHandle` gains matching getters | Two behavioral corrections ride along: 1. **Python `Commands.run` always uses the in-house Connect-JSON decoder.** It previously preferred the generated E2B client when the optional `e2b` package happened to be installed, which dropped the termination extension and made behavior depend on the user's environment. 2. **Go `Pty.Connect` no longer sends `Connect-Timeout-Ms`.** Attachments are long-lived, so a client-side idle timeout must not become a hard server-side deadline. ## Verification Historical functional evidence is recorded under `tests/e2e/envd_conformance/`; the conformance README contains the commands. Performance is reported below from the merged optimization work, with each workload kept separate. ### Protocol conformance Two containers from the same image, one running each implementation, are compared message by message. Normalization removes volatile values, header case, and transfer framing. Declared differences are allowlisted with reasons. The current allowlist contains six declared differences: - `rest_files_gzip_accept` — upstream supports gzip; cube-envd serves identity only. - `rest_files_compose_probe` — upstream implements `/files/compose`; cube-envd returns 501. - `fs_bad_json` — parser-specific JSON error wording; status/error class still match. - `rest_init_timestamp_out_of_range` — upstream `UnixNano()` wraps and treats the request as stale; cube-envd rejects the caller input with 400. - `rest_files_range_multi` — upstream returns `206 multipart/byteranges`; cube-envd serves the whole file with 200. - `rest_files_head` — upstream has no HEAD route and returns 405; Axum supplies HEAD with 200 and the GET headers. A fixture that starts matching must be removed from the allowlist; otherwise a future regression could be silently downgraded from FAIL to DECLARED-DIFF. ### Unit tests At the current performance-integrated head, the latest recorded test run is **347 passed / 2 ignored**. `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. The ignored tests require privileges / a writable cgroup v2 environment that normal CI does not provide. The suite includes guards for the layer rule, poison-recovering locks, `ProcHandle` process-table indirection, constant-time access-token comparison, byte-exact Go error text, output-bus backpressure, download resource budgets, and the process-wide read-buffer pool. ### SDK end-to-end The latest recorded candidate-binary SDK run contains **21 checks, PTY included**, against a real sandbox. It covers readiness, command round trips, stdout/stderr and terminal events, stdin/PTY paths, exit status, env/user/cwd handling, timeout behavior, and text/binary file operations. ### Performance — current merged measurements The old `3c326264` direct/CubeProxy table and its temporary runners applied only to that pinned revision and are no longer used as the current performance conclusion. The sections below report the merged optimization paths separately. Topologies differ; absolute numbers from one subsection must not be mixed with another. #### Command spawn path — [chaojixinren/CubeSandbox#25](https://github.com/chaojixinren/CubeSandbox/pull/25) The fork-free path uses `clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK|SIGCHLD)` while keeping the same child-side credential, cwd, process-group, and cgroup setup. | Measurement | Go | cube-envd | |---|---:|---:| | Start → `/health`, P50 | 5.45 ms | **1.55 ms** | | First command after readiness | 3.94 ms | **3.43 ms** | | Idle RSS | 15.00 MiB | **2.98 MiB** | | Command latency, C=64 | 86.32 ms | **77.63 ms** | | Command throughput, C=64 | 732 rps | **804 rps** | | Failed requests | 0 | 0 | This is a command-spawn measurement, not a file-transfer or full CubeProxy result. #### PTY spawn path — [chaojixinren/CubeSandbox#27](https://github.com/chaojixinren/CubeSandbox/pull/27) The PTY path now uses the same fork-free spawn engine instead of maintaining a second `fork`-based path. With 2 vCPU and 2,000 PTY sessions at C=64, repeated for five rounds: | Measurement | Go | cube-envd | |---|---:|---:| | Session throughput | 684 rps | **798 rps** | | minor faults / command | **1.25** | 6.97 | | sys ms / command | 0.290 | **0.260** | The throughput result measures session creation. Existing-session PTY input/output round trips do not spawn a process and remain around parity with Go. #### Process output and slow-consumer behavior — [chaojixinren/CubeSandbox#28](https://github.com/chaojixinren/CubeSandbox/pull/28) PR #28 replaced the two bounded broadcast rings with an explicit per-process `OutputBus`. A slow live consumer now applies backpressure instead of making the daemon truncate the stream. A subscriber that is actually blocked and makes no progress for 300 seconds is evicted independently; idle subscribers are not evicted, and a reserved terminal slot guarantees that `End` still fits after data. | Process-stream check | Go 0.5.11 | cube-envd | |---|---:|---:| | 32 MiB stream, median of five | 81.2 MB/s | **128.6 MB/s** | | Delivery | complete | complete | | PTY keystroke round trip, median | 0.44 ms | **0.34 ms** | | PTY keystroke round trip, P95 | 4.00 ms | **0.56 ms** | For a 200 MiB process stream inside the guest, cube-envd delivered all **209,715,200 bytes** with a matching SHA-256 in **1.50–1.74 s**, while the daemon peaked at **2.1 MB RSS**. The Go run completed the wire transfer in **3.8–7.0 s**, but left roughly **1.0–1.5 GB** resident in the 1.9 GB guest, leaving about 139 MB available and causing a normal client to fail while writing what it received. A three-subscriber 200 MiB run (fast, ~10 MB/s, and one subscriber that does not read) delivered the full 200 MiB with matching SHA-256 to both progressing subscribers; only the stalled subscription was evicted after the 300-second window. Attachments are bounded at 8 per process and 64 per envd. #### `/files` data plane — [chaojixinren/CubeSandbox#29](https://github.com/chaojixinren/CubeSandbox/pull/29) + [#34](https://github.com/chaojixinren/CubeSandbox/pull/34) PR #29 moved large downloads to body-sized pooled/prefetched reads, added `TCP_NODELAY`, and introduced explicit thread, memory, and concurrency budgets. PR #34 then moved free read buffers into one process-wide `ReadPool`, eliminating most per-request page-fault churn at high concurrency. Single-stream, in-guest PVM measurement: | 200 MiB body | Median | vs Go | |---|---:|---:| | Go | **0.040 s** | 1.00x | | cube-envd | 0.041 s | 1.03x | Small-body keep-alive latency in the same guest: | 4 KiB body | Median | |---|---:| | Go | **0.11 ms** | | cube-envd | 0.27 ms | Latest high-concurrency read-pool result, 2 vCPU guest, in-guest C client, 32 concurrent 4 MiB downloads: | 4 MiB × 32 | Go 0.5.x | cube-envd | |---|---:|---:| | Throughput | 4855–6244 MiB/s | **3867–4133 MiB/s** | | daemon CPU | **0.01 ms/MiB** | 0.20–0.23 ms/MiB | | minor faults | **0.1 / MiB** | 1.6 / MiB | | peak RSS | **6 MiB** | 20–21 MiB | The shared pool makes cube-envd roughly **4.7–6.7× faster** than its per-body-pool predecessor in this shape and brings it to about **65–85% of Go**. Go still wins at this concurrency because `sendfile` avoids the two userspace copies that remain in the Rust path. The pool is bounded rather than free. It starts empty at about **2.5 MiB idle RSS**, retains at most 32 MiB at the default configuration, and measured about **19.5 MiB settled RSS** after repeated 32×4 MiB bursts and **22.7 MiB** after one 200 MiB body. Go stayed around 6.1–7.2 MiB because its `sendfile` path does not retain userspace read buffers. Stalled clients are bounded separately from the free-buffer cache. With 200 stalled large downloads, the configured global cap serves **128** and rejects **72 with 503**; held RSS remains about **277.2–277.9 MiB** across the tested buffered variants. The important property is that memory and blocking-thread use follow configured budgets instead of the number of connections a client can open. ### Sampling and limits Percentiles, throughput, and RSS are meaningful only inside the topology that produced them. Command-spawn, PTY, process-stream, and `/files` measurements use different harnesses and should not be cross-divided. Where a result is reported as a range, the range is kept instead of converting a small number of runs into a fake stable percentile. Historical measurements remain useful for regression archaeology, but they are not the current headline numbers. A new retest should record the source revision, image digest, binary hash, resource limits, client placement, and raw output together. ### cgroup and termination — real machine cgroup behavior is not exposed over RPC, so the conformance harness cannot compare it. `termination_e2e.py` covers it on an isolated Linux/QEMU guest: real main-process OOM, descendant-only OOM, timeout and user attribution, pipe and PTY placement, escaped-descendant cleanup, and fail-closed leaf allocation. The deployment-reachable cgroup memory cap is also verified on a real PVM guest: `cgroup_memory_max_e2e.py` records **25/25** checks for flag/env/derived precedence, clamping to the enclosing limit, invalid-value handling, `memory.high`, and the real `ENVD_EXTRA_ARGS` entrypoint path. ## Deliberate behavioral differences Each difference is documented in `cube-envd/README.md` and, where a fixture exists, allowlisted with a reason in `conformance.py`. - **Process-group cleanup.** cube-envd starts each command in its own process group and signals the whole group, so a timeout or `SendSignal` reaps the shell **and** its descendants. Go envd 0.5.13 signals only the direct child and can leave grandchildren behind. cube-envd preserves the normal exit/deadline contract and additionally publishes richer terminal metadata. - **Bounded watch buffers.** The pull-watch event buffer is capped at 10,000 events. Upstream accumulates without bound. At the cap, cube-envd fails the watcher through `GetWatcherEvents` rather than silently dropping or growing forever. - **Keepalive cadence.** 30 seconds rather than upstream's 90 seconds, chosen to stay below the common 60-second idle timeout in front of CubeProxy. The `Keepalive-Ping-Interval` header still tunes the cadence. - **CLI validation is stricter.** Invalid flags, positional arguments, and malformed values terminate startup with exit code 2 instead of being silently ignored. - **Out-of-range `Keepalive-Ping-Interval` degrades instead of panicking.** Upstream can panic when it feeds an invalid value into `time.NewTicker`; cube-envd falls back to 30 seconds. - **Slow output consumers are back-pressured, with bounded eviction.** Progressing subscribers are not truncated. A subscriber that is blocked and makes no progress for 300 seconds is evicted with `resource_exhausted`; the child and other subscribers continue. - **Uploads match upstream's non-atomic write.** Both upload paths stream into the target with `O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_TRUNC`. An interrupted upload leaves partial content, concurrent readers can observe growth, and a failed upload is not rolled back. ## Risk and rollback **Blast radius:** every sandbox's data plane. The mitigation is that rollback is a runtime switch, not a rebuild: `ENVD_BIN=/usr/bin/envd-go` restores the previous Go daemon for a deployment, image, or test template. `ENVD_IMPL=go` moves the same decision to image build time. **Not covered by this PR:** promoting the new default to production templates is a separate operational decision. This PR provides the compatibility, SDK, resource, and rollback evidence needed for that decision; it does not perform the rollout. **Known residual limitations:** - Multipart part filenames that are not valid UTF-8 return 400 where Go would write the file. - A non-UTF-8 basename falls back to `download` in `Content-Disposition`; the current query path is UTF-8-constrained, so this is effectively unreachable. - OOM attribution is command-leaf scoped, not PID scoped; an unrelated external SIGKILL concurrent with a descendant OOM is inherently ambiguous. - `-cmd` and `-cgroup-root` are recognized but not implemented; they warn and skip. ## Reviewer guide Suggested reading order: 1. `cube-envd/README.md` — design, compatibility scope, and the declared differences table. 2. `cube-envd/src/app/routes.rs` — the entire URL surface. 3. `cube-envd/tests/layer_rule.rs` — the architectural dependency rule. 4. `cube-envd/src/process/supervisor.rs` and `process/table.rs` — process lifecycle, `ProcHandle`, output fan-out, backpressure, and attachment limits. 5. `cube-envd/src/filesystem/http/` — conditional requests, Range handling, and HTTP file semantics. 6. `tests/e2e/envd_conformance/conformance.py` — especially `DECLARED_DIFFERENT`. 7. `docker/Dockerfile.cube-base` — the dual-build, default switch, and rollback binary.

title: ci(sync): use HTTP for the apt mirror in sync-to-cnb job
body:
## What

Switch the apt mirror rewritten into the `sync_to_cnb` job container from `https://` to `http://`.

## Why

#1720 pointed the container's apt sources at the Tencent Cloud mirror over HTTPS, but the `ubuntu:24.04` job container ships no CA bundle. `apt-get update` therefore failed every source with:

```
Certificate verification failed: The certificate is NOT trusted.
The certificate issuer is unknown. ... No system certificates
available. Try installing ca-certificates.
```

That is a deadlock: `ca-certificates` is the very package the step is trying to install, and the sources it would install from cannot be verified. The step aborted before installing anything, failing the whole job.

The sibling `sync_cn` job in `release-docker-images.yml` runs the same container on the same runner set and has always used `http://`, which is why it works. This change makes the two consistent.

## Testing

Reproduced by dispatching this workflow against `v0.7.1`: the `resolve_release_context` and `ensure_cnb_release` jobs passed, and `sync_release_assets` failed in `Install dependencies` on the certificate error above. Verified by the next run of this workflow.

title: ci(sync): use Tencent Cloud apt mirrors in sync-to-cnb job
body:
## What

Rewrite the apt sources of the `sync_to_cnb` job container to a Tencent Cloud mirror before `apt-get update`, so the job can install its dependencies.

## Why

The job runs in an `ubuntu:24.04` job container whose default apt sources point at `archive.ubuntu.com` and `security.ubuntu.com`. Those hosts are not reachable from the runner network, so `apt-get update` fails and the `Install dependencies` step never gets to install `ca-certificates` / `curl` / `gh`, failing the whole job before it can sync anything.

## How

A short shell step rewrites every apt source file in the container in place:

- `/etc/apt/sources.list`
- `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.list` (legacy one-line format)
- `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.sources` (deb822 format)

`archive`, `security` and `ports` entries are all remapped to the same mirror host, with `ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports` mapped to the ports path. `nullglob` keeps the loop safe when a given path matches nothing.

The change is scoped to this job; no other workflow or job is affected.

## Testing

The job only runs on the self-hosted runner set, so it is exercised by the next release run of this workflow.

title: fix(clm): timeout-kill paused sandboxes under on_timeout=kill
body:
## Problem

A sandbox created with `on_timeout="kill"` that gets paused — by a manual `pause()` or by any path that lands it in `paused` — was never reclaimed. The sweeper treated `paused` as a terminal state for every policy, so the entry stayed in the registry with `LastActive` frozen and the idle deadline past, and no action was ever taken. The sandbox leaked until deleted by hand.

## Root cause

`sweepOnce` gated on `isParkedSweepState`, which unconditionally returned true for `paused`. That is correct only for `on_timeout="pause"`, where `paused` is the desired outcome. It is wrong for `on_timeout="kill"`, where `paused` is not finished work.

A second issue sat in the kill path. `tryKill` used the unconditional `AcquireState(…, "killing", …)`, so it could overwrite a peer replica's in-flight `resuming` marker and strand the sandbox.

## Changes

**`internal/sweeper/sweeper.go`**
- `isParkedSweepState` becomes `skipSweepState(state, autoPause)`. Transition markers (`pausing`, `resuming`, `killing`, `killed`) are always skipped so the sweep does not pile onto an in-flight transition. `paused` is skipped only when `AutoPause` is set.
- The `switch` on `AutoPause` collapses into an early `continue` for the pause branch; the kill branch falls through. The duplicated leader check is hoisted above the branch.

**`internal/redisstream/stream.go`**
- New `AcquireKill`, the timeout-kill counterpart of `AcquireResume`. Both are CAS transitions over the same allow-set (absent or `paused`). A concurrent resume and kill are therefore mutually exclusive: whichever wins the transaction owns the transition, and neither clobbers an in-flight `resuming` / `pausing` / `running` lock.
- The shared CAS body is factored into `acquireIf`; `AcquireResume` becomes a thin wrapper.

**`internal/sweeper/iface.go`** — `stateStore` gains `AcquireKill`.

**Docs** (`docs/guide/lifecycle.md`, `docs/zh/guide/lifecycle.md`)
- State diagram now shows the `paused → terminated` path under `on_timeout=kill` and `kill()`.
- The default-behavior section notes that a manual `pause()` does **not** cancel the auto-kill: a later-paused sandbox is still destroyed once idle exceeds `timeout`.

## Tests

- `TestSweeper_KillsPausedSandboxWhenAutoPauseFalse` — table over `redis_paused`, `runtime_paused_redis_empty`, `both_paused`; asserts exactly one `Kill` with reason `timeout`, registry eviction, `killed` state, and kill stats. Covers the case where the Redis state-key TTL has expired (`StateLockTTL=60s`) and only `RuntimeState` still says paused.
- `TestSweeper_SkipsInFlightSandboxWhenAutoPauseFalse` — replaces `TestSweeper_KillSkipsAlreadyKillingSandbox`; covers `resuming` and `killing`.
- `TestRedisTransactionsProtectKillOwnership` and `TestAcquireKillAndResumeAreMutuallyExclusive` — pin the CAS semantics both ways: `AcquireKill` does not overwrite `resuming`, `AcquireResume` does not overwrite `killing`.
- `newTestClient` helper deduplicates client setup in the redisstream tests.

## Verification

```
go build ./...
go test -count=1 ./internal/sweeper/... ./internal/redisstream/...
```

Both packages pass; `gofmt` clean.

## Note for reviewers

The behavior change is deliberate and bounded: sandboxes on `on_timeout="kill"` that are paused and idle past `timeout` now get destroyed. Sandboxes that must survive should set `timeout=NEVER_TIMEOUT`, omit `timeout`, or send periodic activity — the docs call this out explicitly.

title: refactor(snapshot): drop legacy snapshot enable flag file
body:
## Summary

Remove the legacy `/data/cube-shim/snapshot` enable-flag file and the code that
wrote/read it. As a result, explicit app-snapshot restores that cannot use
snapshots now fail fast with a clear error instead of silently cold-booting.

## Background

During snapshot rollout, Cubelet wrote `/data/cube-shim/snapshot` after each
snapshot commit (`writeSnapshotFlag`), and the shim consulted it
(`enable_snapshot`) to decide whether to boot from a snapshot. Snapshots are
now the default boot path, so nothing reads this flag anymore — it is dead code.

## Change

- Remove `enable_snapshot()` and its use in `SandBox::by_snapshot()`
  (`CubeShim/shim/src/hypervisor/snapshot.rs`, `CubeShim/shim/src/sandbox/sb.rs`).
- Remove `writeSnapshotFlag()` and `SnapshotStatusPath` from Cubelet
  (`Cubelet/services/cubebox/appsnapshot.go`, `Cubelet/services/cubebox/template_ops.go`).
- With the silent fallback gone, the only remaining cases where `by_snapshot()`
  returns false (`cube.snapshot.disable` annotation, or a selinux label) now
  make `start_vm()` return an error on an explicit restore, instead of
  cold-booting into a VM that still reports `start_mode=RESTORE` and fails
  with a confusing `Invalid container id`.

## Testing

- [ ] Normal (non-restore) create still boots cleanly (snapshot path attempted first, cold-boot fallback kept).
- [ ] Explicit restore with `cube.snapshot.disable` set → clear error, no cold boot.
- [ ] Explicit restore with a selinux label set → clear error.

title: feat(cubemaster): runtime scheduler Profiles and binpack scorer
body:
## Problem
Runtime scheduler strategies are statically configured and difficult to switch safely by workload.

## Scope
- Opt-in `scheduler.profile` / `scheduler.profiles` overlay contract
- Three built-in runtime Profiles: `balanced_spread`, `template_locality_first`, `binpack_utilization`
- Bounded `binpack_score` scorer
- Deterministic Profile-to-selector-to-ranking behavior tests
- Bilingual operator docs + discoverability links

## Behavior and compatibility
- Empty / omitted `scheduler.profile` keeps the base Filter/Score **lists** and does not apply built-in overlays
- Deliberate empty-Profile Init tightenings (not a byte-for-byte master freeze):
  - listed factor/affinity scorers without `plugin_conf` fail `config.Init` (master only panicked when `resource_weights` was non-nil; omitted weights used to early-return and silently skip scoring)
  - `plugin_conf.<scorer>.weight < 0` fails `config.Init` for every registered scorer (master loaded it and could invert ranking)
- Profile support is opt-in; no built-in becomes the implicit default
- Unknown Profile names fail closed at config load
- `enable_filters` / `enable_scorers`: replace when the Profile provides a non-nil list
- `resource_weights`: merge; Profile keys override same-name base keys; unrelated base keys remain
- Same-name user Profile overrides the built-in entirely
- Legacy scorers: omit/`weight: 0` disables Select (plain `float64`). `binpack_score.weight` is `*float64`: omit → default 1; explicit `0` disables; negatives rejected
- Strict factor / unknown-name checks remain Profile-scoped; missing `plugin_conf` / negative weights are unconditional
- One-click TKE template: invalid factor `cpu_usage` → `quota_cpu_usage` (was silently ignored; now a live weight-1 term — ranking may change for that deploy path)

## Evidence
- Three A20-R3 Profile-to-ranking tests (`profile_runtime_behavior_test.go`)
- Binpack boundary / ordering / property tests (`binpackscore_test.go`)
- Local validation (CubeMaster):
  - `gofmt -l` on changed Go files: clean
  - `go test ./pkg/base/config ./pkg/selector/score ./pkg/scheduler -count=1`: pass
  - `go test ... -shuffle=on -count=10`: pass
  - `go test -race ... -count=1`: pass
  - `go vet ...`: pass
  - focused Profile ranking + binpack tests `-count=20`: pass
  - `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`: pass
- Full `make test` / `make test-race`: **environment-blocked** on this Windows host (`make` missing; `pkg/pausesnap` TempDir file-lock cleanup failures unrelated to this diff). Relevant packages above are green.

Runtime ranking tests are **in-process**, not live-cluster performance evidence.

## Limitations
- No offline simulator / `schedulerbench` (#1699)
- No `external_http_score` / sidecars / Prometheus protocol docs (#1700)
- No dynamic plugin loading, hot-reload redesign, decision trace, circuit breaker, or live performance claims

## Related work
- Historical integrated draft: #1666 (mixed Profile + ExternalHTTP + simulator; not cherry-picked wholesale)
- Related open slice: #1699 offline simulator / benchmark
- Related open slice: #1700 external HTTP scorer

body:
## Problem / Motivation

The Cube Lifecycle Manager was added to implement AutoPause/AutoResume/AutoKill features. For now, I think it's not well designed. There are races between CubeMaster and CLM. It's hard to coordinate sanbox status between CubeMaster/CubeProxy/CLM and Redis.


## Proposed Solution

Integrate CLM into CubeMaster. Let CubeMaster be the single entrypoint for sandbox status transition.

title: fix(clm): prevent stale auto-pause after resume
body:
## Problem

Ref #1683

An explicit `connect` could race with CLM auto-pause. CLM could decide that a sandbox was idle, mark it as `pausing`, and queue a pause request while CubeMaster was restoring the same sandbox. The CubeMaster lifecycle lock serialized both operations, but it did not invalidate a pause request whose idle decision became stale while waiting for the lock.

The `running` event from resume could then be skipped while CLM still observed the `pausing` transition, and the queued pause could run immediately afterwards. A successful `connect` could therefore return a sandbox that became `paused` again within milliseconds. Delayed bookkeeping and synchronization failures could also leave Redis, CLM's registry, and CubeProxy out of sync with the actual sandbox.

## Solution

- CLM includes `expected_lifecycle_state=pausing` in auto-pause requests. CubeMaster revalidates this precondition after acquiring the sandbox lifecycle lock, rejecting a pause that was superseded while queued before it reaches Cubelet.
- CubeMaster records a short-lived `running` lifecycle marker immediately after restore succeeds and before releasing the lock or publishing the event. This makes the completed resume visible to queued auto-pause work.
- CLM commits the final `pausing -> paused` transition with CAS. If resume changed the state while the pause RPC was running, CLM reconciles Redis, its in-memory registry, and CubeProxy instead of overwriting the newer `running` state.
- Failed reconciliation is retained and retried with a bounded context. CubeProxy notification retries are handled separately, do not block idle-timeout decisions or refresh activity timestamps, and resolve the latest state before sending it.
- CubeMaster reports when restore completed even if lifecycle synchronization failed. CLM can then finish running-state bookkeeping and apply the requested timeout while preserving the partial-failure error.
- The Info fallback preserves an explicit Cubelet `running` result when a completed resume leaves behind a stale READY pause binding.

title: fix(s3lvol): keep snapshot REF exports until snapshot delete
body:
## Summary
- Snapshot-backed REF exports stay valid for the snapshot lifetime: `ttl_sec` is accepted but ignored, and new manifests use `expires_at=0`. Cubelet does not need `rcow_release_export`.
- Deleting the snapshot releases remaining REF exports internally, including pre-lease registry entries. A live importer lease, local esnap reader, clone_count, decouple, or in-flight export still defers the delete.
- A missing manifest is treated as already released (drop the registry entry and finish the destroy). Export lookup prefers `snapshot_uuid` so a recreated snapshot does not inherit a stale uuid; older registries fall back to `blob_id`.
- Re-exporting the same snapshot returns the existing uuid (in flight or after DONE, including a materialised rewrite of that uuid). A later export is allowed only after that uuid is released.
- A queued decouple is removed before `decouple_start()` so a synchronous completion cannot double-free the queue node; `-EBUSY` requeues at the head. Lease grace is measured from the first miss of this absence; `deletable` uses the cached lease poll.

Fixes #1692.

## Test plan
- [x] `run_pending_delete_test.sh` (131 passed) — TTL ignored, snapshot delete releases the export, late importer still pins, pre-lease delete, missing-manifest 404
- [x] `run_selfimport_test.sh` (28 passed) — snapshot delete revokes the export; reused snapshot name does not revive it
- [x] `run_export_test.sh` (197 passed) — idle vs leased deletable, one export per snapshot, `expires_at=0`
- [x] `make check` in `CubeS3lvol/` (37/38; `run_cubecow_client_test.sh` NVMe node flake, 27/27 on retry)

title: feat(cubemaster): add external HTTP score plugin
body:
Review-only extraction from integrated Draft PR #1666, following the mentor guidance to submit smaller modules for earlier automated review. The final Topic 1 integrated submission remains #1666; this PR is not intended to replace it unless maintainers prefer independent merging.

## Scope
`external_http_score` configuration, registration, HTTP protocol validation, timeout handling, score validation, scheduler integration, circuit breaker + `failure_policy`, and focused tests. Intentionally excludes scheduler profiles, built-in binpack policy, offline benchmark, and broader production features.

## Scheduler-wide behaviors (not plugin-local)
These live in `runScoreFilter` and apply to the whole Score roster:
1. **`FailClosedError` aborts Score/create** — typed fail-closed from any scorer (today: `external_http_score` with `failure_policy: fail_closed`) short-circuits the phase and discards already-blended scores from earlier scorers. There is no canary-only scope.
2. **`Weight()` is sampled once** before each scorer's `Select` so the blended weight is not re-read mid-blend.
3. **Non-finite weights and per-node scores are refused** in the blend so they cannot poison `totalPluginWeight` / final scores / `AllSortByScore` order.

Documented in `docs/guide/cubemaster-scheduler-config.md` and the zh mirror.

## Validation
Focused Go tests for score + scheduler packages pass locally. CI remains authoritative on current master.

Related: #1666

title: fix(templatecenter): invalidate alias mutation caches on alias write
body:
## Problem

Alias transfers mutate two template definitions (the new holder and the displaced holder), but the query/runtime caches were not invalidated for both IDs after the write committed.

**Scope of the staleness** (corrected — an earlier version of this text said 6h, which conflated two different caches):

| Cache | TTL | Affects alias display? |
|-------|-----|------------------------|
| `templateInfoCache` / `templateListCache` | **1 min** (`templateQueryCacheTTL`), refreshed every **30s** | **Yes** — this is what this PR fixes |
| `templateDefinitionCache` / kind / locality | 6h (`templateCacheTTL`) | No — keyed by template ID, not alias |

After an alias transfer, list/detail reads on the **CubeMaster replica that performed the write** are invalidated immediately. Other replicas still rely on the 1-minute query cache and the 30-second refresh backstop (up to ~30–60s staleness). **Sandbox create by alias is unaffected** — `GetTemplateByAlias` always hits the DB.

Split out from #1693 per review feedback — this is an intentional v3 carry-over, independent of the tpl migrate workflow.

## Fix

- Add `invalidateTemplateAliasMutationCaches(templateID, displacedTemplateID)` which clears both the target and the displaced holder (deduping when they are the same ID).
- Call it after the alias claim/transfer transaction commits in `publishTemplateStatusWithAlias` and `setTemplateAliasLocked`.
- Report the displaced holder on the `DELETING` path of `claimTemplateAliasByJobOrderTx`: `claimTemplateAliasTx` clears by `alias_key` with **no status filter**, so a DELETING holder is mutated even though it is invisible to the status-filtered lookup. `setTemplateAliasLocked` now resolves the previous holder without the `status <> DELETING` filter, so the invalidated ID matches the rows actually written.
- Branch the transfer log on the holder status: the DELETING path never compares job order, so calling the released template a "newer template build" asserted an ordering that was never evaluated.

**Behavior change worth calling out:** with the unfiltered lookup, `SetTemplateAlias` now also acts on a DELETING holder — its CREATE/REDO `RequestJSON` alias is rewritten via `syncCreateRedoImageJobAliasTx`, where previously the holder was invisible and that step was skipped. This matches what the publish path already does (`testBuildClearsDeletingHolderJobAlias`) and is intentional. The consequence is that a malformed job payload on a DELETING holder now fails the operator's alias transfer instead of silently skipping it; we consider failing loudly the correct behavior here.

## Tests

- `cache_query_test.go`: both-IDs-cleared and same-ID dedup behavior.
- `store_alias_docker_test.go`: alias store cases (get-by-alias excludes snapshots, newer build transfers alias, older build cannot reclaim, concurrent claims converge, etc.).
- `store_alias_docker_test.go`: `SetAliasTransferFromDeletingHolderInvalidatesBothQueryCaches` — primes the query caches, transfers an alias whose current holder is `DELETING` via `SetTemplateAlias`, then asserts (a) both IDs' info/list caches are cleared and (b) the DELETING holder's `display_name` is cleared. This is the case that pins the new unfiltered lookup; the existing READY-holder transfer test passes either way.

title: [Bug Report] CubeEgress domain allow rules do not bind Host/SNI to the original destination

labels.name: area/CubeNet
labels.description: Impacts the CubeNet module and network-agent

body:
## Summary

For requests that reach CubeEgress's L7 proxy, a matching Host/SNI does not establish that the original destination IP belongs to that name. Client-side hosts or `curl --resolve` overrides can preserve the allowed name while changing the destination. I am opening this issue to discuss the intended authorization boundary and agree on an approach before proceeding with #1695, as requested in the PR review.

## Environment

- Baseline: CubeSandbox commit `62da0187` (v0.7.1-rc1).
- Relevant components: CubeEgress access policy/proxy routing; CubeVS determines which flows reach L7.
- Reproduction: isolated Docker socket fixture on LinuxKit 6.12.76, OpenResty 1.31.1.1, real DNS and HTTP/TLS backends.
- KVM/deployment mode: not used; this is not a deployed sandbox test. The patched production OpenResty 1.29.2.5 image and the complete guest/TPROXY/eBPF path have not been runtime-verified here.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an isolated fixture, configure an allow rule for `*.example.test`; proxy-side DNS resolves `allowed.example.test` only to `127.0.0.2`. Run a second backend at `127.0.0.3`.
2. Keep Host/SNI as `allowed.example.test`, but connect to `127.0.0.3` using a client-container hosts entry or these commands inside the fixture network:

```sh
curl --noproxy '*' --resolve allowed.example.test:80:127.0.0.3 http://allowed.example.test/
curl --noproxy '*' --cacert /fixture/cert.pem --resolve allowed.example.test:443:127.0.0.3 https://allowed.example.test/
```

For the HTTPS case, the unrelated backend deliberately presents a certificate valid for the allowed name and trusted by the test proxy. This demonstrates the DNS-binding gap even when upstream certificate verification succeeds; an arbitrary backend without a valid certificate is not claimed to pass HTTPS verification.

3. Separately, use an HTTPS Host-only allow rule with `Host: allowed.example.test`, SNI `blocked.example.test`, and a shared destination IP. The policy matches the first name, while nginx uses SNI for upstream TLS and rewrites upstream Host to the second name.

The reproducible harness is in #1695: `python3 CubeEgress/tests/dns_auth_integration.py --baseline-ref 62da0187`. It retains production access/audit modules and proxy locations but substitutes policy storage, static certificates, direct listeners, and backend ports.

## Expected Behavior

A domain-constrained allow should authorize the identity actually used upstream, with an explicit policy for how that identity is bound to the original destination. An unrelated destination or unauthorized Host/SNI identity change should be denied before forwarding or credential injection.

## Actual Behavior

The baseline returned 200 for all four HTTP/HTTPS × hosts/`--resolve` cases. The Host-only HTTPS identity mismatch also returned 200. The proposed implementation in #1695 returns 403 for these cases while normal requests return 200. This evidence applies to the socket fixture, not arbitrary IP reachability through CubeVS. Flows rejected before L7 remain rejected; ordinary SNAT flows are outside this check.

## Additional Context: Design Discussion

The current proposal preserves the original IP/port and checks membership against trusted proxy-side DNS, with asynchronous resolution, bounded concurrency/deadlines, validated CNAME ownership and TTL-respecting caching. HTTPS Host constraints must agree with the SNI used upstream.

Points to agree on:

- Is proxy-side DNS membership the desired authorization contract? CDN, split-DNS and rotation can give guest and proxy different valid address sets and cause false denials.
- Should the binding instead use trusted DNS results already observed by CubeVS? This would require defining provenance, expiration and access from CubeEgress.
- If the proxy selects a new resolved IP, the new destination must undergo L4/CIDR authorization again; silently replacing the original IP would bypass that boundary.
- Should HTTPS Host/SNI disagreement be rejected for all Host-constrained allow rules, including rules without credential injection?

DNS membership alone does not prove tenant ownership on shared hosting or restrict an attacker-controlled subdomain already covered by an allowed wildcard. TLS verification and destination restrictions remain necessary. #1695 is a concrete implementation for discussion, not an assumption that these semantics have already been agreed.

title: [Bug Report] PVM guest panics in gmi_sm4_init on Intel hosts with 64 logical CPUs (CPUID 0xC0000001 returns host x2APIC ID)
body:
## Summary

On Intel hosts with 64 logical CPUs (x2APIC IDs 0x00–0x3F), roughly 25% of PVM guest boots panic in `gmi_sm4_init` (the built-in Zhaoxin GMI SM4 driver, `CONFIG_CRYPTO_SM4_ZHAOXIN_GMI=y` in `deploy/pvm/configs/pvm_guest`), because `cpuid 0xC0000001` executes natively under PVM and returns host leaf-0x1F data whose EDX is the host CPU's x2APIC ID. `panic=1` reboots the guest, the VMM exits on CMOS reset, and CubeShim fails the create with `Create sandbox failed: Receive event timeout after 10000ms`.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: v0.6.0, `8721dd151971ce3c2966482bbd32904ad98f378e` (CubeShim rebuilt from that commit with only the virtio-blk duplicate-head patch)
- Guest kernel: `6.6.69-opencloudos9.cubesandbox.pvm.guest-g0de43d6b3bcd` (`PVM_KERNEL_TAG 6.6.69-1.2.cubesandbox`, config `deploy/pvm/configs/pvm_guest`)
- Host OS and kernel version: Ubuntu 24.04.4, host kernel `6.6.69-opencloudos9.cubesandbox.pvm.host-g0de43d6b3bcd`, `kvm_pvm` loaded, `CUBE_PVM_ENABLE=1`
- Host hardware: AWS EC2 `r7i.16xlarge`, Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C (Sapphire Rapids), 64 logical CPUs, CPUID max basic leaf `0x1F`, max extended leaf `0x80000008`
- Deployment mode: cluster (EKS, 3 compute nodes)
- Relevant component: guest kernel config (`deploy/pvm/configs/pvm_guest`) / PVM; surfaces in CubeShim and Cubelet

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run CubeSandbox v0.6.0 with PVM on an Intel host that exposes 64 logical CPUs (x2APIC IDs up to 0x3F). `r7i.16xlarge` reproduces; `r7i.8xlarge` (32 logical CPUs, x2APIC IDs up to 0x1F) never does.
2. Create sandboxes or build templates normally (`cubemastercli tpl create ...` on each node).
3. Roughly one in four guest boots per node fails. Over 9 template boots on one node we saw 4 failures; a sibling node failed 1 of 9; the third node 0 of 9. On a 3-node template build the whole build fails whenever any node loses the coin flip.

## Expected Behavior

The guest kernel should not probe or trust the Zhaoxin/Centaur CPUID leaf `0xC0000001` on a non-Zhaoxin CPU, and a PVM guest boot should not depend on which host CPU the vCPU thread is scheduled on.

## Actual Behavior

Guest console (from `cube-shim-req.log`), identical on every failed boot:

```
[    1.065786] GMI is unavailable on this platform.
...
[    1.267752] GMI SM4 is detected by CPUID
[    1.267971] BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffff0003ec00001
[    1.268391] #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
[    1.268724] #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
[    1.269025] PGD 0 P4D 0
[    1.269284] Oops: 0000 [#1] PREEMPT SMP PTI
[    1.269336] CPU: 0 PID: 1 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 6.6.69-opencloudos9.cubesandbox.pvm.guest-g0de43d6b3bcd #1
[    1.269657] Hardware name: Cube Hypervisor cube-hypervisor, BIOS 0
[    1.269714] RIP: 0010:gmi_sm4_init+0x83/0x250
[    1.269755] Code: 00 00 b8 01 00 00 c0 0f a2 f7 d2 83 e2 30 0f 85 87 01 00 00 48 8d 3d 04 8c 4d ff e8 97 02 96 fd 48 89 d8 48 03 05 ad 7a 57 ff <80> 78 01 06 76 7e 4c 8d 35 a0 5e d8 ff be 05 00 00
[    1.269883] RSP: 0018:ffffd20000013e00 EFLAGS: 00010286
[    1.269927] RAX: fffff0003ec00000 RBX: 0000000000000000 RCX: c0000000fffffbff
[    1.269985] RDX: 0000000000000000 RSI: 00000000fffffbff RDI: 0000000000000001
[    1.270246] FS:  0000000000000000(0000) GS:fffff0003ec00000(0000) knlGS:0000000000000000
[    1.270349] CR2: fffff0003ec00001 CR3: 0000000003414000 CR4: 00000000000506f0
[    1.270439] Call Trace:
[    1.270464]  <TASK>
[    1.270789]  ? exc_page_fault+0x153/0x160
[    1.270789]  ? pvm_exception.constprop.0+0x12/0x190
[    1.270789]  ? pvm_event+0x6b/0x80
[    1.270789]  ? pvm_kernel_exception_entry+0x4f/0x100
[    1.270789]  ? gmi_sm4_init+0x83/0x250
[    1.270789]  do_one_initcall+0x4b/0x320
[    1.270789]  do_initcalls+0xda/0x180
[    1.270789]  kernel_init_freeable+0x126/0x1e0
[    1.270789]  kernel_init+0x20/0x1c0
[    1.270789]  ret_from_fork+0x3f/0x60
[    1.270789]  </TASK>
[    1.270789] Modules linked in:
[    1.270789] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
[    1.270789] Rebooting in 1 seconds..
```

Guest command line: `root=/dev/pmem0 rootflags=dax,errors=remount-ro ro rootfstype=ext4 panic=1 no_timer_check noreplace-smp printk.devkmsg=on console=hvc0 net.ifnames=0 audit=0 LANG=C raid=noautodetect earlyprintk=ttyS0 ...`

VMM (`vmm.log`) after the panic:

```
2510 ERROR <vcpu0> devices/src/legacy/cmos.rs:68 -- Shutdown because of CMOS reset
2510 ERROR <vcpu0> vmm/src/cpu.rs:1128 -- VCPU generated error: VcpuRun(Failed to run vcpu: Unexpected exit reason on vcpu run: InternalError
2510 INFO  <vmm>   vmm/src/lib.rs:1863 -- VM exit event
10026 INFO <main>  containerd-shim ... Shutting down shim instance
```

CubeShim stats (`cube-shim-stat.log`): `LaunchVmm Ok 1ms`, `CreateVm Ok 0ms`, `BootVm Ok 29ms`, then no `Agent CreateSandbox`, and `CreatePodSandbox Err 10031ms`. Successful boots on the same node show `Agent CreateSandbox Ok 22ms` and `CreatePodSandbox Ok ~1600ms`.

Cubelet: `run container failed.failed to create shim task: Others("Other: Create sandbox failed:Receive event timeout after 10000ms")`; CubeMaster then marks the template FAILED.

## Additional Context

Observed while deploying CubeSandbox on AWS EC2 `r7i.16xlarge` (Intel Sapphire Rapids) hosts, after moving from `r7i.8xlarge` hosts that had never shown the failure.

**Why it is nondeterministic and host-size dependent.** The faulting code is:

```
mov eax, 0xC0000001 ; cpuid ; not edx ; and edx, 0x30 ; jnz skip
```

so the driver only continues into the crashing path when EDX bits 4 and 5 are both set. Leaf `0xC0000001` is the Zhaoxin/Centaur GMI feature leaf. On Intel it is out of range, and per the Intel SDM an out-of-range leaf returns the data of the highest basic leaf, here `0x1F`, whose EDX is the x2APIC ID of the executing logical CPU. Because the PVM guest runs `cpuid` natively, the value depends on which host CPU the vCPU thread is on at that instant. Measured directly on the hosts via `/dev/cpu/*/cpuid`:

| Host | Logical CPUs | x2APIC IDs | CPUs where leaf 0xC0000001 EDX has bits 4+5 set |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| r7i.8xlarge | 32 | 0x00–0x1F | 0 of 32 |
| r7i.16xlarge | 64 | 0x00–0x3F | 16 of 64 (x2APIC 0x30–0x3F) |

The 25% failure rate matches. Boots that skip the path print only `GMI is unavailable on this platform.`; boots that fail additionally print `GMI SM4 is detected by CPUID` immediately before the Oops. The driver is built in (`CONFIG_CRYPTO_SM4_ZHAOXIN_GMI=y`, also `CONFIG_CRYPTO_SM3_ZHAOXIN_GMI=y`), so it cannot be blacklisted as a module.

**Suggested fixes**

1. In the guest kernel: check `boot_cpu_data.x86_vendor` for Zhaoxin/Centaur before issuing `cpuid 0xC0000001` in the GMI SM4/SM3 init paths, or drop `CONFIG_CRYPTO_SM4_ZHAOXIN_GMI` / `CONFIG_CRYPTO_SM3_ZHAOXIN_GMI` from `deploy/pvm/configs/pvm_guest` (the guest has no Zhaoxin hardware).
2. Interim: add `initcall_blacklist=gmi_sm4_init` to the default cmdline in `CubeShim/shim/src/hypervisor/config.rs`.
3. Harden PVM: trap or sanitize out-of-range CPUID leaves so guest behavior does not vary with host CPU placement.

Any host with more than 48 logical CPUs (x2APIC IDs reaching 0x30) is exposed; hosts with 32 or fewer are safe by accident, which is why this went unnoticed.

title: Validate original destinations before domain-based egress allow
body:
CubeEgress previously matched only the presented Host/SNI before forwarding to the original destination. For traffic reaching the L7 proxy, client hosts or `curl --resolve` overrides could therefore authorize an unrelated IP. Host-only HTTPS rules could also match one Host while forwarding another SNI on a shared IP.

Bind domain-constrained allow rules to trusted proxy-side DNS A records before connecting upstream or injecting credentials. Validate answer owner/class/section and CNAME chains; require HTTPS Host constraints to agree with SNI. Preserve the original IP/port and behavior for rules without domain constraints.

Asynchronous lookups have a five-second whole-operation deadline, five-alias limit, 16 active lookups per worker, and up to 256 coalesced same-name waiters. Shared positive caching uses the shortest A/CNAME TTL with a 300-second cap and elapsed lookup time deducted; zero and sub-millisecond TTLs are not cached. Timer-owned work and independent deadline cleanup handle client disconnects and callbacks dropped under resource pressure. Cache keys distinguish resolver configurations.

## Validation

- Lua port/scheme and DNS suites, Lua bytecode compilation, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Real curl HTTP/HTTPS with container `/etc/hosts` and `--resolve` overrides: all four forged-destination cases returned 200 on baseline `62da0187`, and 403 with the fix. Normal HTTP/HTTPS requests returned 200.
- Real DNS/OpenResty/TLS fixture tests cover injection, redacted audit, Host/SNI mismatch, CNAME ownership and expiry, TTL zero, NXDOMAIN, timeouts, IP literals, and explicit deny precedence. Denied requests did not increase upstream hit counts.
- 32 overlapping TTL-zero requests used one DNS query; 32 NXDOMAIN requests also used one query. Forty distinct concurrent misses used at most 16 active names. A slow CNAME chain was denied at approximately 5.02 seconds, with subsequent recovery. Initiator disconnection, dropped timers, late callbacks, and sub-millisecond TTLs have regression coverage.

Run `make -C CubeEgress test-lua` and `make -C CubeEgress test-dns-integration`. Reproduce the baseline with `python3 CubeEgress/tests/dns_auth_integration.py --baseline-ref 62da0187`.

## Scope and limitations

The container harness uses production access/audit modules and proxy locations, but fixture policy storage, static test certificates, direct sockets instead of TPROXY, and separate backend ports. It does not verify a deployed CubeSandbox guest, CubeVS/eBPF interception, or the patched production image. Test OpenResty is 1.31.1.1; the production base is 1.29.2.5 and was not rebuilt here.

CDN/split-DNS views and rotation may reject legitimate destinations. DNS membership does not establish tenant ownership or replace private-IP policy and TLS verification. IPv4 only; positive cache is shared across workers, while in-flight coalescing is per worker. English and Chinese guides document these boundaries.

title: [S3 backend] Pause snapshot volumes stay allocated for ~1h (export TTL) after sandbox destroy/resume, and accumulate across repeated pause/resume cycles
body:
**Components:** CubeS3lvol (pending-delete / export pin), Cubelet (S3 cleanup), CubeMaster (pause lifecycle)
**Environment:** v0.7.x, all-in-one single-node deployment, S3 storage backend

## Summary

After a sandbox on the S3 backend is paused, the three temporary snapshot volumes created by that pause (`tpl-snap-<id>-memory-snap`, `tpl-snap-<id>-rootfs`, `s3-meta-snap-<id>-snap`) are **not released immediately** when the sandbox is resumed or destroyed. Their deletion is deferred until the S3 export created during that pause expires (default TTL 3600s), at which point the s3lvol background poller finally completes it. Until then, the S3 objects and lvstore clusters stay allocated.

When the same sandbox goes through several pause/resume cycles within one export TTL window, every cycle leaves one such deferred group behind, so the **peak storage usage grows linearly with the number of cycles**.

## Steps to reproduce

Scenario A — single destroy/resume:

1. Create a sandbox with the S3 backend and pause it (pause completes, snapshot export finishes).
2. Resume it (or destroy the paused sandbox directly).
3. The sandbox's own live volumes (`sb-<id>-*`) are deleted immediately, but the three pause snapshot volumes show up as pending-delete (reason=export).
4. For at least the next hour (until the export TTL expires), the S3 object count/bytes do not drop.
5. Only after the export expires (plus up to one 60s poller tick) are the three volumes actually deleted and the space reclaimed.

Scenario B — repeated pause/resume:

1. Cycle the same sandbox pause → resume → pause → resume … with intervals shorter than the export TTL.
2. Every resume's cleanup request gets parked in the pending-delete queue, so several snapshot groups coexist in the lvstore.
3. Usage ≈ (number of groups) × (size per group), until each group's export expires in turn.

## Expected behavior

Once a sandbox is resumed or destroyed, the temporary snapshots of that pause should be deleted and their storage released promptly (seconds to minutes), not deferred by an export TTL that is unrelated to the sandbox lifecycle at that point.

## Actual behavior

- The delete request is refused by s3lvol and parked in the pending-delete queue until the export TTL lapses.
- The cleanup caller (Cubelet) treats the refusal as success, so the control plane has no way to notice the delay.

## Root cause analysis

Three layers stack up:

1. **Pause snapshots and their exports share one pin lifecycle.**
   When a pause completes (S3 remote-ready), s3lvol creates a ref-layout export for each snapshot volume to enable cross-node restore. Later, the cleanup path issues `rcow_delete_lvol`, and `s3lvol_lvol_destroy` sees the snapshot is behind an export pin (`export_pin_verdict` returns LEASE: no lease object exists yet, TTL not expired), refuses the delete, and records a pending-delete intent (reason=export) in `vbdev_s3lvol_pending.c`.

2. **Cubelet has no way to release an export, and treats "busy" as success.**
   The cubecow engine does not expose a release_export call. `S3Cow.DeleteByKind` (`Cubelet/storage/s3_volume_manager.go`) treats a "device busy" refusal for a snapshot as already deleted (it logs "recording it as deleted and leaking the object"), then continues removing the local directory and catalog and returns success. From the control plane's point of view the cleanup is done, while the objects actually sit in s3lvol's pending queue.

3. **The pending queue's auto-complete condition is exactly the export TTL.**
   The pending poller (60s period) only completes the delete once the export pin turns STALE (TTL expired and the lease miss confirmed). In other words, **the lower bound of the reclaim delay is the export TTL (default 3600s, `S3LVOL_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TTL_SEC`)**.

Representative target-side log lines during a destroy/resume cleanup:

```
ERROR: lvol 'tpl-snap-<id>-memory-snap' is the snapshot behind export <uuid>,
       which another node may be reading through. Release that export, or wait
       for it to expire, before deleting this.
NOTICE: delete of 'tpl-snap-<id>-memory-snap' is pending: export
        (will complete once the blocker clears)
```

`rcow_get_pending_deletes` shows the three volumes with reason=export; `rcow_get_exports` shows the matching exports with `lease_absent=true`, `pin=lease`, `expires_at ≈ pause time + 1h`.

## Impact

- Every pause/resume or destroy of a paused sandbox leaves the temporary snapshot space allocated for up to one hour.
- Under frequent pause/resume (e.g. auto-pause scheduling), the peak storage footprint grows with the number of cycles and is not bounded.
- Cleanup reports success while the objects remain, so storage monitoring and capacity planning disagree with reality.

## Suggested fixes (for discussion)

1. **Root fix: release the export before deleting the snapshots.**
   `rcow_release_export` already exists on the s3lvol side but is not exposed or called by Cubelet/cubecow. If the pause-package cleanup (resume/destroy → `CleanupPauseSnapshot` → Cubelet `CleanupTemplate`) released the corresponding exports before deleting the snapshots, the pin would clear immediately and the pending poller would finish the delete on its next tick (≤60s), with no dependence on the TTL.
2. **Alternative: deterministic sweep of the previous pause group when the next pause starts.**
   A successful resume means the previous pause package is no longer needed; reclaiming it at the start of the next pause would bound the accumulation to one group.
3. **Semantics: stop treating "busy" as success in Cubelet.**
   `DeleteByKind` should surface export-pinned refusals (or wait for / trigger the pending completion) so the upper layer can observe the real reclaim progress instead of silently recording "deleted + leaked".

## Relevant code paths

- `CubeS3lvol/module/bdev/s3lvol/vbdev_s3lvol_lvstore.c` — `s3lvol_lvol_destroy` (refuses deletes behind an export pin)
- `CubeS3lvol/module/bdev/s3lvol/vbdev_s3lvol_pending.c` — pending-delete recording + 60s poller (`pending_lvol_deletable`)
- `CubeS3lvol/module/bdev/s3lvol/vbdev_s3lvol_exports.c` — `export_pin_verdict` / lease semantics
- `CubeS3lvol/module/bdev/s3lvol/vbdev_s3lvol.h` — `S3LVOL_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TTL_SEC = 3600`
- `Cubelet/storage/s3_volume_manager.go` — `DeleteByKind` / `isS3DeleteBusy` (busy → recorded deleted + leaked)
- `Cubelet/services/cubebox/template_ops.go` — `cleanupTemplate` (pause package cleanup entry)
- `CubeMaster/pkg/pausesnap/delete_paused.go` — destroy paused / `CleanupPauseSnapshot`

title: [Bug Report] Cross-node resume of a paused sandbox fails after the export TTL (1 h): s3lvol auto-reaps the ref export while the sandbox is still paused
body:
## Summary

A sandbox that is paused can no longer be resumed on a **different node** if the cross-node resume happens after the pause export's TTL (default **1 hour**) expires.

When a sandbox is paused, the `s3lvol` side publishes a *ref*-layout export (lease-aware, `pin=lease`) so that a later cross-node resume can import it. If nothing imports it while the sandbox stays paused, the export becomes "terminal" once its lease is confirmed absent past the TTL deadline, and the reaper removes it **automatically** — manifest deleted, registry entry cleared. From that point on, any cross-node resume attempt fails because the manifest it must import returns 404. Same-node resume keeps working because it is served from the local pause catalog / lvstore snapshot volume and never depends on the export.

## Environment

- Affected version: current `master` — the automatic reaper behavior that causes this was introduced in #1663 (the fix for #1634).
- Deployment mode: cluster (cross-node resume).
- Relevant components: CubeS3lvol (export/lease) / CubeMaster (restoreplace cross-node placement) / Cubelet (resume).

## Description / mechanism

1. Pause completes. The `s3lvol` side publishes a *ref*-layout export for the pause package (manifest under `<lvstore>/meta/exports/<uuid>.json`) with `lease_aware=true` and the default TTL `S3LVOL_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TTL_SEC = 3600` (1 h).
2. Cross-node resume depends on that export: `restoreplace.Decide` only allows a resume to leave the origin node while the pause record reports `remote_status=ready` (i.e. the export exists), and Cubelet on the destination node imports it through the export UUIDs (`remoteUUIDs`).
3. If the export expires with no lease taken (`lease_absent` — nothing imported it during the pause), `export_lease_is_terminal()` becomes true and the periodic `exports_reap` poller reaps it **automatically**: the manifest is deleted and the registry entry cleared. No explicit delete / release request is involved.
4. Any later cross-node resume reads the already-removed manifest → 404 → the resume fails. Same-node resume is unaffected: it goes through the local pause catalog + lvstore snapshot volume and does not depend on the export.

## Expected Behavior

A sandbox that is still paused should remain resumable on another node (cross-node) without being silently limited to the ~1 h export TTL. Reaching the export deadline should not invalidate a pause that is still owed to a possible cross-node recovery.

## Actual Behavior

- The effective window for cross-node resume after a pause is the export TTL (default 1 h).
- Beyond that window, only same-node resume works. Cross-node recovery for the scenarios the export exists to serve — origin node failure / removal / drift — fails with a 404 on the export manifest.

## Additional Context

- `rcow_get_exports` on a paused sandbox shows the exports with `lease_aware=true`, `lease_absent=true`, `pin=lease`, and `expires_at` = pause time + 1 h.
- Reaper logic lives in `CubeS3lvol/module/bdev/s3lvol/vbdev_s3lvol_exports.c` (`export_lease_is_terminal()` + `exports_reap()`).
- Cross-node placement decision: `CubeMaster/pkg/restoreplace/placement.go`; same-node resume path: `Cubelet/services/cubebox/pause_package.go`.
- Related upstream context: this is a follow-on of the reaper introduced by #1663 (which fixed #1634) and relates to the open cross-node resume effort in #1197.

title: fix(s3): keep pause package after Resume so Snapshot stays incremental
body:
## Summary

- After S3 Resume, Cubelet used to delete the pause catalog immediately. `CommitSandbox` only resolves a memory base from that catalog, so the next Snapshot fell through to a full 2GiB dump (same-node and cross-node).
- Resume-time `CleanupTemplate` now no-ops on S3 the same way it already does on XFS while a live sandbox still holds the pause id. The next Pause or Destroy still GCs the old package. Cross-node origin leftover (tombstone + package) is still dropped.
- Cross-node Resume never writes a local pause catalog. `prepareCommitMemoryArtifact` now clones the imported `sb-*-memory` volume (the same base Pause already uses) instead of full-dumping.

XFS Resume keep / mmap behavior is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit: `TestKeepLiveXFSPausePackage` — live sandbox keeps the package; PAUSED / forged annotation still allow delete
- [ ] Same-node S3: Create → Pause → Resume → Snapshot — memory is incremental / soft-dirty, not full; pause package dir still present until next Pause or Destroy
- [ ] Same-node S3: Resume → Pause again — second pause is incremental; previous package is cleaned
- [ ] Cross-node S3: Pause@A → Resume@B → Snapshot@B — Snapshot is incremental (own volume), not Device busy
- [ ] Destroy / DelPaused still delete the pause package

title: fix(cubelet): honor node IP when host NIC has multiple IPv4 addresses
body:
## Problem

`GetHostDevice` required the uplink NIC to have exactly one IPv4 address and
failed with `ipv4 address on %s is not unique` otherwise. Cloud hosts commonly
stack secondary/alias addresses on the primary NIC, so one-click compute nodes
failed to start (fixes #444).

## Fix

Instead of rejecting a multi-address NIC, select the primary address:

1. the first global-scope, non-secondary, non-deprecated IPv4 address;
2. fall back to the first address if no primary exists.

A NIC with zero IPv4 addresses still errors. The returned `IPMask` comes from
the selected address, so the eBPF `NodeIPMask` / on-link view stays consistent.

No change to `GetHostDevice`'s signature or the egress data path. Selecting the
correct egress device/address via policy routing is left to route-aware egress
(cube-router).

## Tests

Unit tests cover single-address regression, primary-address preference, fallback
when every address is secondary, the empty-NIC error, and an end-to-end
multi-address `GetHostDevice` case.
