title: [bug] Sandbox destroy leaks hostdir bind mounts in cubelet's private mount namespace — fills kernel 100k mounts limit, ENOSPC on create after weeks of churn
body:
### Summary

Destroying a sandbox **does not unmount the hostdir staging bind mounts** it created.
These mounts live inside cubelet's **private mount namespace**, so they are invisible
from the host root namespace and are never reclaimed. After ~5 weeks of production
traffic (~1,000 sandbox create/destroy cycles per day, 2–3 hostdir volumes each), the
namespace accumulated **99,926 leaked mounts** and hit the kernel's hard limit of
**100,000 mounts per mount namespace**. Every subsequent `create` failed with
`mount(2) ENOSPC` — while the disk was only 1% full.

### Environment

- Cube Sandbox version: **v0.6.0** (confirming from image tags: `cube-proxy:v0.6.0`,
  `cube-lifecycle-manager:v0.6.0`, `cube-egress:v0.6.0`; `cubemastercli` also reports v0.6.0)
- OS: openEuler 22.03, x86_64 bare metal, KVM
- Deployment: single node, E2B-compatible API on :3000, ~1k sandboxes/day, each sandbox
  created with 2–3 hostdir volumes (user files / skills)
- Component placement (mixed container / host-process deployment):
  - **Host processes** (systemd units): `cube-sandbox-cubelet` (`ExecStart=cubelet-start.sh`,
    `KillMode=process`), `cube-sandbox-cubemaster`, `cube-sandbox-cube-api`,
    `cube-sandbox-network-agent`, `cube-sandbox-cubeops`, plus shims
  - **Docker containers**: `cube-webui`, `cube-proxy`, `cube-lifecycle-manager`,
    `cube-egress`, `cube-proxy-coredns`, `cube-sandbox-mysql`, `cube-sandbox-redis`
  - The leak lives in the **cubelet host process's** private mount namespace
- Uptime before incident: ~5 weeks

### Symptom and error chain

All sandbox creations started failing at once:

```
# Cubelet log
prepareHostDirVolume: bind mount /data/shared/<user-data>
  -> /data/cubelet/hostdir/<sandbox-id>/rw/hostdir-N:
  mount(2) failed: No space left on device

# cubelet -> CubeMaster -> API error codes
130527 NoSpaceLeftOnDevice
130597 "no more resource"
```

Key observation: the **last successful create** (before the flood of failures) had only
`cube_rootfs_rw` in its volume list — no hostdir volume. Every failing create carried
hostdir volumes. Disk usage was 1%, inodes were fine. `df` lied; the real resource was
the **mount count inside cubelet's mount namespace**:

```
# Host root namespace — totally blind to the leak
$ cat /proc/mounts | wc -l
71

# Cubelet's private namespace — the smoking gun
$ cat /proc/<cubelet-pid>/mounts | wc -l
99999
$ grep -c hostdir /proc/<cubelet-pid>/mounts
99926
```

### Root cause

`DestroySandbox` stops the VM (via shim) but **never unmounts the staging bind mounts**
under `/data/cubelet/hostdir/<id>/rw/hostdir-*`, and the volumeLifetime GC does not
reclaim the residual directories either (GC log shows `totalUsers:0, need_delete:0`
while **42,017** residual hostdir directories existed — i.e. every sandbox ever created).

Related findings from the same incident (may deserve separate tracking):

1. **`volumeLifetime` GC is blind** — it never sees the residual hostdir directories,
   so disk-side cleanup never happens either.
2. **`KillMode=process` in the cubelet systemd unit leaves containerd-shim processes
   behind** (reparented to PID 1). Together with the nsfs pin at
   `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/cubeletmnt/mnt`, these leftover shims keep the
   polluted mount namespace alive — which is why `systemctl restart cubelet` **does not
   clear the leaked mounts**: the new cubelet process `setns()`-es back into the same
   old namespace via the pin (the pin path is hardcoded in the cubelet binary).

### Reproduction (5 minutes)

```bash
CUBELET_PID=$(pidof cubelet)  # or systemctl show -p MainPID

before=$(grep -c hostdir /proc/$CUBELET_PID/mounts)
# create one sandbox with a hostdir volume, then destroy it (SDK kill() / DELETE /sandboxes/:id)
after=$(grep -c hostdir /proc/$CUBELET_PID/mounts)

echo "before=$before after=$after"
# If after >= before, the mount leaked.
```

Long-term: run ~1k create/destroy cycles per day for a few weeks and watch
`grep -c hostdir /proc/<cubelet-pid>/mounts` grow monotonically.

### Workaround / recovery

The only way to reclaim the leaked mounts is to **destroy the entire mount namespace**
("drain" procedure):

```bash
systemctl stop cube-sandbox-cubelet          # 1. stop service
kill -9 <leftover-shim-pids>                  # 2. kill leftover shims holding the ns
lsns -t mnt | grep <ns-id>                    #    confirm no process remains in the ns
umount /usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/cubeletmnt/mnt   # 3. remove the nsfs pin
systemctl start cube-sandbox-cubelet          # 4. start; cubelet re-pins a fresh ns
```

After this, `/proc/<new-pid>/mounts` dropped from 99,999 to 73 lines, hostdir count to 0.
Note this kills all running sandboxes and bypasses the normal destroy path, so it is an
incident-recovery-only procedure. Residual directories can be cleaned with
`find /data/cubelet/hostdir -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -mmin +60 -exec rm -rf {} +`.

### Suggested fixes

1. `DestroySandbox` should `umount` every hostdir staging mount it created (ideally
   unmount **before** stopping the VM, so a failure is visible in the destroy path).
2. The volumeLifetime GC should also detect hostdir directories with no active sandbox
   and clean them, and/or expose a CLI/API to reconcile mounts vs. live sandboxes.
3. Consider `KillMode=control-group` (or explicitly kill shims) in the cubelet unit so a
   restart actually reclaims resources.

Happy to provide full logs from the incident if useful — thanks for the great project!

title: [Bug Report] s3lvol: an export whose lease is confirmed absent and whose TTL has lapsed is neither released nor stops polling, degrading into a 1 req/s 404 storm after restart
body:
## Summary

**Affected versions**: v0.7.0 (`s3lvol_git d0081641c59822e4e5653b7462e914410b81910a`, built 2026-08-28), and current `master`

**Severity**: High — a single node reliably saturates its 2 dedicated busy-poll cores, writes 200+ MB of error log in under two days, and the export registry grows without ever shrinking

**Component**: `CubeS3lvol/module/bdev/s3lvol/vbdev_s3lvol_exports.c`

Once a reference export has both (a) a lease object confirmed absent (HEAD returns 404 → `-ENOENT`) and (b) a lapsed manifest TTL, it is in a terminal state that no importer can possibly be reading. Yet at that point:

1. `lease_poller` is never unregistered. It keeps issuing a HEAD once per second against a key already known not to exist, each one leaving an aws-c-s3 ERROR line in the log.
2. The registry entry is never removed, so a restart makes `exports_parse()` load it back and re-arm the poller.

The resulting request rate is exactly `leaked_entries × 1 req/s`, grows linearly with the number of entries, and accumulates permanently across restarts.

## Reproduction

Preconditions: `enable_s3lvol: true`, snapshot backend on S3 (ours is Baidu BOS via its S3-compatible API, plaintext HTTP + path style).

1. Pause a sandbox / resume it on another node, producing a reference export. The log looks healthy at this point:

   ```
   s3_export_run_ref: Export <uuid> references 2000 object(s) holding 2097152000 byte(s)
                      of a 2147483648-byte snapshot across 1 layer(s)
   s3lvol_export_lease_start: watching lease of export <uuid> every 1199 second(s)
   ```

2. Wait out the manifest TTL (~1200 s). The importer's `/meta/exports/<uuid>.lease` does not exist (never created, or already cleaned up), so every lease check returns 404:

   ```
   [ERROR] [S3MetaRequest] - Meta request cannot recover from error 14343
           (Invalid response status from request). (response status=404)
   ```

   At this stage the interval is still 1200 s, so it is nearly invisible — **but the entry has already leaked**.

3. `systemctl restart cube-sandbox-s3lvol`. On attach:

   ```
   exports_parse: lvstore '<lvs>' still owes export <uuid> the snapshot '<name>'
                  (deadline passed; the lease decides)
   s3lvol_export_lease_start: watching lease of export <uuid> every 1 second(s)
   ```

   The poll interval goes from 1200 s to **1 s**, and the 404 storm begins.

**Is a restart a guaranteed reproducer?** Yes, deterministically, provided the registry already holds at least one such entry. The restart does not create the leak; it amplifies a silent one by a factor of 1200. The entries themselves also accumulate deterministically — see the data below.

## Observed data

Four machines across two clusters reproduced this independently, and the leaked-entry count matches the measured 404 rate exactly 1:1:

- Node A: 57 entries → ~157 req/s; 1.35M error lines and 279 MB of log in 12.5 h; both SPDK reactor cores consumed by lease checks
- Node B: 27 entries → 810 hits in 30 s = 27 req/s; 411 MB log
- Node C: 6 entries → 180 hits in 30 s = 6 req/s; 219 MB in under two days
- Node D: 3 entries → 92 hits in 30 s = 3 req/s; 115 MB

Node A also suffered a whole-machine freeze (no panic, no OOM, clean IPMI SEL, stable memory) which has not recurred since s3lvol was stopped there. We cannot establish causation (journald was not persistent, no kdump), so this is recorded as background only.

**An export is never released on its own.** Across the complete log history of two machines, the number of spontaneous `Released export` events is **0**:

- Node B: 42 exports created in total = 27 owed + 15 still live. Not one ever left the registry.
- Node A: 57 created, all 57 owed.

Consequently, operational workarounds such as "avoid deleting the snapshot inside the TTL window" do not help: the leak is established the moment the deadline passes, independent of when the snapshot is deleted.

## Root cause

The handling of 404 in `export_lease_head_done()` is itself correct:

```c
if (status == -ENOENT) {
        exp->lease_checked = true;
        exp->lease_updated_at = 0;
        exp->lease_failures = 0;
        export_lease_get_done(ctx);
        return;
}
```

`lease_checked = true` together with `lease_updated_at = 0` lets the delete path through, which matches what we observe: `rcow_get_lvstores` reports these snapshots as `deletable: "YES"` throughout. The problem is what happens after this branch.

- **The poller is never unregistered.** `-ENOENT` is terminal: the lease object does not exist and `expires_at` has passed, so there is no way for an importer to show up later (an importer must write its lease before it can read). Yet `export_lease_renew()` keeps sending a HEAD every second. The `S3LVOL_LEASE_MAX_FAILURES` backoff only covers the `status != 0 && status != -ENOENT` branch; a 404 takes the "successfully determined" path, which *resets* `lease_failures` to 0, so backoff can never engage.

- **The registry entry is never reclaimed.** The comment in `exports_parse()` states this is deliberate:

  > Deliberately *not* a filter on `expires_at`. That stamp is written once at export creation and never refreshed, while the importer renews its lease past the manifest TTL for as long as it is reading.

  That reasoning holds completely for "TTL passed but the lease is still being renewed". But "lease confirmed 404 **and** TTL passed" is a different case: with both conditions true, no importer can be reading and the entry is safe to drop. The current code does not distinguish the two,   so the entry persists forever and re-arms a 1 s poller on every attach.

As an aside: #1537 previously dropped expired entries by `expires_at` at parse time (motivated by a registry growing past `S3LVOL_MAX_EXPORTS` and bricking the lvstore's attach), and was later superseded by the lease approach above. The lease approach fixed a real correctness problem — forgetting a live importer's pin — but reintroduced the unbounded-entry resource problem, this time surfacing as a 404 storm rather than a failed attach.

One secondary factor leaves the leak unowned. Per `CubeS3lvol/README.md`, Cubelet's `S3Cow.DeleteByKind` treats a refused snapshot delete as success. The control plane therefore believes the snapshot is gone, stops tracking it, and nobody ever comes back to release the export. The logs show a large number of:

```
s3lvol_lvol_destroy: *ERROR*: lvol '<snap>' is the snapshot behind export <uuid>,
    which another node may be reading through. Release that export, or wait for
    it to expire, before deleting this.
```

On one machine 54 distinct snapshots hit this refusal, so it is the normal path rather than an edge case.

## Expected behaviour

When `lease_checked == true && lease_updated_at == 0 && now > expires_at`, the export should:

1. unregister `lease_poller` — the state is terminal, there is nothing left to check;
2. be released automatically, or at minimum be dropped from the registry in `exports_parse()` with the registry object rewritten, so it does not come back to life across restarts.

Failing that, the 404 branch should at least be subject to backoff instead of holding a constant 1 req/s.

## Current operational workaround

`rcow_release_export` clears these precisely. `export_uuid` is the only required parameter (`lvs_name` is not needed):

```sh
python3 scripts/s3lvol_rpc.py rcow_release_export '{"export_uuid":"<uuid>"}'
```

Each call deletes exactly one S3 object (the manifest) and leaves the local lvol untouched: after release, `export_status` flips from `DONE` to `NONE` and the lvol count is unchanged. After running it over 84 entries, the 404 rate dropped to exactly zero, and a restart confirmed the registry rewrite with `0 export(s) in the registry`.

Two things worth flagging for anyone hitting this:

- **`s3lvol_rpc.py --retry-pending` does not solve this.** It only acts on snapshots with `delete_pending == true && deletable == YES`, whereas the snapshots behind these leaked exports are invariably `delete_pending: false`. Using it here would instead delete a different set of snapshots that an operator is supposed to judge individually.
- **The uuid of an owed export is only obtainable from the log.** `rpc_get_methods` exposes no equivalent of `rcow_get_exports` (only the import-side `rcow_get_imports`), and `rcow_get_lvstores` yields `export_status` but not the uuid. The sole source is the `still owes export <uuid> the snapshot '<name>'` line emitted by `exports_parse()` at attach. An RPC to query the export registry would make this far easier to operate.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox v0.7.0 (in-place upgrade from v0.6.0)
- CubeS3lvol v0.7.0, `s3lvol_git d0081641c59822e4e5653b7462e914410b81910a`, built 2026-08-28
- SPDK `d64c4fa89233397460e2e4ff55a1c69b8e498598`, `spdk_target_arch: haswell`, aws-c-s3 v0.8.7
- Object store: Baidu BOS via its S3-compatible API, `path_style = true`, `no_tls = true` (plaintext HTTP)
- s3lvol started with `-m 0x3`: 2 reactors pinned to 2 dedicated cores

title: fix(one-click): honor ONE_CLICK_ENABLE_S3LVOL enable/disable on upgrade
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1622: the s3lvol on/off switch set through the one-click installer was unreliable during an `install.sh` upgrade. Two causes: the three-way `.env` merge only treats a value as an explicit override when it differs from the `env.example` default (the `cp env.example .env` safeguard), so flipping the switch back to its default `0` could never be expressed; and on upgrade the merged old-runtime env is sourced after `.env`, clobbering both `VAR=x ./install.sh` and `.env`-provided values. Stopping also raced the bundled MinIO.

## Changes

- **`lib/common.sh`** — new generic installer-toggle mechanism: `ONE_CLICK_TOGGLE_KEYS` (currently `ONE_CLICK_ENABLE_S3LVOL`, `CUBE_PVM_ENABLE`), `snapshot_one_click_toggles` (captures this-run intent from the process environment and the bundle `.env` before any file is sourced — presence counts as explicit, even when the value equals the `env.example` default) and `apply_one_click_toggles` (re-applies it after the upgrade merge, alongside the existing `apply_cli_overrides` pattern). The final value is persisted by the existing `upsert_env_kv`; the env merge itself stays fully generic — the per-key special case from the first revision is gone.
- **`install.sh`** — wires the two mechanism calls; stops the s3lvol unit before the role-target/glob stop so it can flush to MinIO while the S3 endpoint is still up; clears a leftover failed state via `reset-failed` on disable.
- **`CUBE_PVM_ENABLE`** had the same bug and now rides the same mechanism: a `.env` carrying `CUBE_PVM_ENABLE=0` actually disables it on upgrade (previously the old runtime `1` was silently kept).
- **`systemd/cube-sandbox-s3lvol.service`** — declare `After=network-online.target cube-sandbox-minio.service` so it starts after and stops before the bundled MinIO. No `Requires=`: compute nodes do not ship MinIO.
- **Tests** — merge contract coverage in `tests/test_env_merge.sh` (a default-valued `.env` key is not explicit in the merge), a new `tests/test_toggle_inputs.sh` for the snapshot/apply matrix, and install-mode / unit-dependency assertions.
- **Docs** — one-click README (EN/ZH) enable/disable guidance updated: no more hand-editing `.one-click.env`; avoid a full `cp env.example .env` before upgrade, which resets the toggles to their defaults; `CUBE_PVM_ENABLE` follows the same rule.

## Upgrade note

After this change, disabling s3lvol on an upgrade is done with `ONE_CLICK_ENABLE_S3LVOL=0 ./install.sh` (or by putting only that key in the bundle `.env` and re-running `install.sh`). The same applies to `CUBE_PVM_ENABLE`.

title: [Feature] Template center split: control flow / data flow separation with build execution on compute instances (0.7.1)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Summary

Split the template lifecycle out of CubeMaster by re-dividing responsibilities along **control flow vs. data flow**:

- **CubeMaster — control flow**: cluster scheduling, node management, quotas, and API routing/forwarding. Template-related API requests are received by CubeMaster and forwarded to the template center, so callers see no change.
- **Template center — data flow**: template metadata, build-job orchestration, replica and snapshot lifecycle, and artifact storage / distribution / reclamation. It takes no part in scheduling decisions.
- **Compute instances — build execution**: heavy I/O work (image pull, ext4 creation) moves down to compute instances instead of being centralized on the Master.

## Motivation

Template capabilities are currently all embedded in CubeMaster, which creates three structural problems:

1. **Build I/O is centralized on the Master**: image pulls, unpacking, and ext4 creation all run locally on the Master. Build jobs consume large amounts of CPU, disk, and bandwidth; at peak times they slow down scheduling decisions, and Master restarts interrupt in-flight builds.
2. **Artifacts live on the Master's local disk**: a single point of failure, plus an egress bandwidth bottleneck when every compute node pulls multi-GB ext4 files from the Master.
3. **Oversized failure domain**: a Master failure or rolling upgrade disrupts both scheduling and templates at the same time.

After the split: the control flow stays lightweight and stable, the data flow scales independently, and build execution scales out with compute capacity.

## Functional scope

### 1. Independently deployable template center (data flow)

- Owns template creation (from-image / commit), build-job orchestration, replica distribution, snapshot lifecycle, and artifact reclamation
- Independently deployable, scalable, and releasable
- Single-node deployments may still run a combined topology by default; the split is a topology option, not a mandate

### 2. Build execution moved down to compute instances

- The Master no longer performs image pulls or ext4 creation, and its deployment artifact no longer ships the build toolchain
- The template center selects a host instance based on resources and spec requirements, and dispatches build jobs to it
- Observable builds: progress reporting, log collection, failure retry
- If the host instance fails, the build can be retried on another instance without affecting the control plane or existing templates

### 3. Artifact object storage (MinIO / S3)

- Configurable storage backend: local disk (default, current behavior) or S3-compatible object storage
- Compute instances upload/download directly against object storage; the Master no longer proxies artifact traffic
- Content verification (sha256) is preserved on download
- Lifecycle reclamation covers objects in storage, including deletion retries and orphan-object cleanup
- Credentials are injected via environment variables / Secrets only, never plaintext in config files

### 4. CubeMaster control-flow convergence + routing/forwarding

- CubeMaster converges to scheduling, node registration/heartbeat, and quota management
- Template-related API requests are received by CubeMaster and routed to the template center; the external API is unchanged
- Template locality information needed by scheduling is synced via the service interface with a local cache fallback, avoiding a remote call on every scheduling decision
- When the template center is down, sandbox creation from existing READY templates is unaffected; only new builds/rebuilds fail

## Compatibility

- External API unchanged; callers are unaware (requests are forwarded by CubeMaster)
- During rolling upgrades, mixed old/new compute instances can build and download normally
- No plaintext credentials in config files; legacy config keys emit a deprecation warning for one release

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Template builds produce no image-pull / ext4-creation I/O on CubeMaster (builds execute observably on host instances)
- [ ] When a host instance fails, the build is retried on another instance without leaving dirty artifacts
- [ ] With 10 nodes concurrently creating sandboxes from the same template, Master egress bandwidth is no longer the bottleneck (compared to pre-split)
- [ ] After an object-storage restart, build / download / reclamation recover end-to-end
- [ ] With the template center down, sandbox creation from existing READY templates is unaffected
- [ ] Rolling upgrade 0.7.0 → 0.7.1 completes with zero interruption to existing templates and sandboxes

## Suggested milestones

| Phase | Content | Exit criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phase 1 | Object-storage backend for artifacts + known fixes (artifact ID uniqueness, #1591 path unification, PENDING timeout) | full workflow passes on both storage backends |
| Phase 2 | Standalone template center deployment (build location unchanged, compatible form) | standalone and combined topologies are functionally equivalent |
| Phase 3 | Build execution moved to instances + CubeMaster convergence and routing | all acceptance criteria pass |

## Related

- bug: #1591 (cbri path configuration unification)
- This issue consolidates #1613 / #1614 / #1628 (and supersedes #1629)

title: [Feature] 模板中心独立拆分：管控流与数据流分离，构建执行下沉计算实例（0.7.1）
body:
## 概述

将模板生命周期能力从 CubeMaster 拆分，按「管控流 / 数据流」重新划分职责：

- **CubeMaster —— 管控流**：集群调度、节点管理、配额，以及对外 API 的路由转发（模板类请求统一由 CubeMaster 接收并转发给模板中心，调用方无感知）
- **模板中心 —— 数据流**：模板元数据、构建任务编排、副本与快照生命周期、artifact 的存储 / 分发 / 回收，不参与调度决策
- **计算实例 —— 承载模板构建执行**：镜像拉取、ext4 制作等重 I/O 工作下沉到计算实例执行，不再集中在 Master

## 背景与动机

当前模板能力全部内嵌在 CubeMaster，三个结构性问题：

1. **构建重 I/O 集中在 Master**：拉镜像、解包、制作 ext4 都在 Master 本地执行。构建任务消耗大量 CPU / 磁盘 / 带宽，高峰期直接拖慢调度决策；Master 升级重启也会中断进行中的构建。
2. **artifact 存 Master 本地盘**：单点故障 + 所有计算节点向 Master 拉取数 GB ext4 的出口带宽瓶颈。
3. **故障域过大**：Master 的故障或滚动升级同时影响调度与模板两条线。

拆分后：管控流轻量稳定，数据流独立扩展，构建执行随计算资源水平扩容。

## 目标架构

```
  调用方
    │  ① 模板类 API（建模板 / 查状态 / 删除）
    ▼
┌──────────────────────────┐
│ CubeMaster（管控流）       │──── ② 路由转发 ────┐
│ · 调度 / 节点管理 / 配额   │                    │
│ · locality 缓存兜底        │◄─── ③ locality 同步 ┐│
└──────────────────────────┘                    ││
    │ ④ 调度选节点（创建沙箱）                     ▼▼
    ▼                              ┌──────────────────────────┐
┌──────────────────────────┐       │ 模板中心（数据流）          │
│ 计算实例（承载构建执行）     │◄── ⑤ 下发构建任务 ─ │ · 模板元数据 / 构建编排     │
│ · 拉取镜像 / 制作 ext4     │       │ · 副本 / 快照生命周期      │
│ · 上传 artifact ───────────┼──┐    │ · artifact 回收           │
│ · 拉取 artifact 启动沙箱 ◄──┼──┤    └──────────────────────────┘
└──────────────────────────┘  │  ▼
                              │  ┌──────────────────────────┐
                              └─►│ MinIO / S3（artifact 存储）│
                                 └──────────────────────────┘
```

## 功能范围

### 1. 模板中心独立部署（数据流）

- 承担模板创建（from-image / commit）、构建任务编排、副本分发、快照生命周期、artifact 回收
- 可独立部署、独立扩缩容、独立发布
- 单节点部署默认仍可合并部署，拆分是部署拓扑选项而非强制

### 2. 构建执行下沉到计算实例

- Master 不再执行镜像拉取与 ext4 制作，部署物不再附带构建工具链
- 模板中心按资源与规格要求选择承载实例下发构建任务
- 构建过程可观测：进度回报、日志采集、失败重试
- 承载实例故障可换机重建，不影响控制面与存量模板

### 3. artifact 对象存储（MinIO / S3）

- 存储后端可配置：本地磁盘（默认，保持现状）或 S3 兼容对象存储
- 计算实例与对象存储直连上传 / 下载，Master 不再中转 artifact 流量
- 下载保留内容校验（sha256）
- 生命周期回收覆盖对象存储数据，含失败重试与孤儿对象清理
- 访问凭证仅通过环境变量 / Secret 注入，不落配置文件明文

### 4. CubeMaster 管控流收敛 + 路由转发

- CubeMaster 收敛为调度、节点注册与心跳、配额管理
- 模板类 API 由 CubeMaster 统一接收并路由转发到模板中心，对外接口不变
- 调度所需的模板 locality 信息经接口同步并本地缓存兜底，避免每次调度发起远程调用
- 模板中心宕机时，基于存量 READY 模板创建沙箱不受影响（仅新建 / 重建模板失败）

## 兼容性

- 对外 API 保持不变，调用方无感知（由 CubeMaster 路由转发）
- 滚动升级期间，新旧版本计算节点混合执行构建与下载均正常
- 访问凭证不落明文配置；旧配置项保留一个版本的废弃警告

## 验收标准

- [ ] 模板构建全程不在 CubeMaster 上产生镜像拉取 / ext4 制作 I/O（构建在承载实例执行，可观测）
- [ ] 承载实例故障时构建可换机重试，不产生脏 artifact
- [ ] 10 节点并发基于同一模板创建沙箱，Master 出口带宽不再成为瓶颈（对比拆分前）
- [ ] 对象存储重启后，构建 / 下载 / 回收全链路恢复
- [ ] 模板中心宕机时，存量 READY 模板创建沙箱不受影响
- [ ] 0.7.0 → 0.7.1 滚动升级，存量模板与沙箱零中断

## 里程碑建议

| 阶段 | 内容 | 出口标准 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 阶段 1 | artifact 对象存储后端 + 已知修复合入（artifact ID 唯一化、#1591 路径统一、PENDING 超时） | 双存储后端全链路通过 |
| 阶段 2 | 模板中心独立部署（构建位置不变的兼容形态） | 独立 / 合并两种拓扑功能等价 |
| 阶段 3 | 构建执行下沉实例 + CubeMaster 收敛与路由转发 | 全部验收标准通过 |

## 关联

- bug：#1591（cbri 路径配置统一）
- 本 issue 由 #1613 / #1614 / #1628 合并而成

将模板中心从 CubeMaster 中拆分出来，成为可独立部署、独立扩缩容、独立发布的服务。

## 背景与动机

模板构建是重 I/O 操作（拉取镜像、解包、制作 ext4、上传分发），与调度逻辑同进程部署会互相争抢资源：一次大规模模板构建可能拖慢调度决策，调度面的升级重启也会中断进行中的构建任务。拆分后两个服务可独立演进、独立容错。

## 功能范围

- 模板中心独立承担：模板创建（from-image / commit）、构建任务管理、副本分发、快照生命周期、artifact 构建与回收
- CubeMaster 保留：调度、节点注册与心跳、配额管理
- 调度侧通过服务接口查询模板副本的节点分布（locality），并带本地缓存兜底，避免每次调度都发起远程调用

## 兼容性

- 对外 API 保持不变，调用方无感知
- 单节点部署默认仍可合并部署，拆分是可选的部署拓扑而非强制

## 验收标准

- [ ] 模板中心独立部署后，模板构建、删除、重建功能与原单体完全等价
- [ ] 模板中心宕机时，基于存量 READY 模板创建沙箱不受影响（仅新建/重建模板失败）
- [ ] 滚动升级期间调度与模板构建互不阻塞

title: feat(scheduler): add extensible plugin system
body:
## Summary

Split out from #1619 to fit the auto-review time budget; #1619 remains as the overall design overview. This change originates from fork PR shsaihdsaiudh/CubeSandbox#1 (author @JunWang666, `Signed-off-by` preserved on the commit; original authorship trailer `Autonomously-by: Codex:GPT-5.6` kept).

Add an extensible scheduler plugin system:

- **Explicit plugin registry** (`pkg/selector/plugin`): factory args per plugin instance, fail-fast on unknown plugins, errors instead of panics; Selector interfaces unchanged.
- **Two out-of-tree plugin kinds**: CEL expressions (`plugin/expr`, via `google/cel-go`) and gRPC plugins (`plugin/grpcplugin`) speaking the versioned, batch-oriented `SchedulerPlugin` API (Handshake / SyncSnapshot / Filter / Score; per-request calls carry only a snapshot version, request context and candidate IDs).
- **Named profiles** (`pkg/scheduler/profile`): per-plugin args + named Profiles with a legacy translator mapping the existing config onto the default profile.
- **Builtins migrated onto the same mechanism**: new `node_safety` filter, `template_locality` converted to a builtin plugin.
- **Proto** lives at `pkgs/proto/services/schedulerplugin/v1` following the unified proto module layout (#1600); generated code regenerated with the pinned toolchain (protoc-gen-go v1.36.11 / protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.6.1).
- Docs: `docs/guide/scheduler-plugin.md` (en + zh), runnable example under `CubeMaster/examples/scheduler-plugin/`.

## Test plan

- `cd pkgs/proto && go build ./... && go test ./...` — passing.
- `cd CubeMaster && go build ./...` — passing.
- `cd CubeMaster && go test ./pkg/selector/... ./pkg/scheduler/... ./pkg/base/config/... ./pkg/base/node/...` — passing (all 12 test-bearing packages ok, incl. new `selector/plugin`, `plugin/expr`, `plugin/grpcplugin`, `scheduler/profile`).

body:
## Summary

Split out from #1619 to fit the auto-review time budget; #1619 remains as the overall design overview.

Add an in-process scheduling simulator for offline scheduler evaluation:

- **`cmd/schedsim` + `pkg/scheduler/sim`**: drives the real `scheduler.Select` in-process against simulated node state injected via localcache exported APIs (no DB/Redis, `localcache.Init` not called).
- **Virtual-clock event loop** (create + expiry events) replays a cube-bench trace file; per-request `Select` latency measured with the real wall clock.
- **Time-weighted cluster metrics**: cpu/mem allocation rate, load CV, Jain index, fragmentation ratio, herding top-1 share, template hit rate, plus success rate and Select latency percentiles; multi-round aggregation for reproducibility (`priority_select_num > 1` is time-seeded, documented in `cmd/schedsim/README.md`).
- Ships `example.sim.yaml` with the safety valves simulation needs (large `metric_update_timeout`, deterministic top-1 pick).

## Test plan

## Summary

Split out from #1619 to fit the auto-review time budget; #1619 remains as the overall design overview.

Extend `examples/cube-bench` from a single fixed benchmark into a repeatable scheduler workload harness:

- **Pre-generated request sequences from a fixed `--seed`**: Poisson arrivals (`--rate`), uniform per-sandbox lifetimes (`--lifetime`, client-scheduled delete plus server-side timeout as a safety net), and weighted multi-template mixes (`--templates id[:weight[:cpuMillis:memMiB]]`).
- **Workload presets** matching the scheduler benchmark plan: `burst`, `template_storm`, `mixed_spec`; `--dump-trace` writes the exact sequence as a JSON trace for replay by the scheduling simulator.
- **New per-request fields** (template, scheduled/actual start, queue delay) exported in JSON; queue-delay percentiles added to the report.
- **New `compare` subcommand**: multi-seed A/B report with mean ± 95% CI, absolute/relative deltas and direction-aware improved/regressed verdicts; accepts both cube-bench exports and schedsim reports.
- Legacy mode is unchanged when no scheduling flags are given (regression-tested).

body:
## Summary

Make CubeS3lvol an explicit opt-in. Cubelet no longer probes the s3lvol RPC socket by default. The background s3 cubecow init loop starts only when `[cow.s3] enable = true`; otherwise `backend=s3` requests fail fast with `ErrS3NotConfigured` instead of blocking on `ErrS3NotReady`.

## Changes

- **`Cubelet/config/config.toml`** — ship a default-disabled `[cow.s3]` block (`enable = false`, `socket_path = /var/run/s3lvol.sock`).
- **`Cubelet/storage/plugin.go`** — add `CowS3UserConfig.Enable` and `Config.s3lvolConfigured()`.
- **`Cubelet/storage/local.go` / `s3_init.go`** — gate `startS3CowInitLoop` and `storeForBackend` on `s3lvolConfigured()`; add `ErrS3NotConfigured`.
- **`Cubelet/storage/cow_store_ops.go`** — document the updated `StoreFor` contract for S3.
- **`Cubelet/storage/s3_init_test.go`** — new/updated tests for config gating, disabled `StoreFor`, init-loop skip, and enabled init flow.
- **`cubecow/src/ffi.rs`** — remove a noisy `eprintln` in `set_last_init_error`.

## One-click deploy

- **`deploy/one-click/scripts/common/cubelet_config.sh`** — `write_cubelet_s3lvol_enable` flips `[cow.s3] enable` from `ONE_CLICK_ENABLE_S3LVOL`. It preserves a hand-written `socket_path`. If the section is missing, it inserts after `cow.log` / before `images`. If the header already exists anywhere (including after `images`), it only flips `enable` and never inserts a second table.
- **`deploy/one-click/scripts/systemd/cubelet-start.sh`** — on every cubelet start, writes `enable` from `ONE_CLICK_ENABLE_S3LVOL` (default `0`). On one-click nodes the env var is the source of truth; a hand-edited `enable = true` is overwritten on restart unless the env var is also `1`.
- **`deploy/one-click/tests/test_cubeops_addr.sh`** — covers insert-after-log, flip-existing, section-after-images (no duplicate table), ordering, and that no stale helper remains.

## How to enable

- **One-click:** set `ONE_CLICK_ENABLE_S3LVOL=1` in `.env` / `.one-click.env`, then restart cubelet (or re-run `install.sh`). Do not rely on editing `[cow.s3] enable` alone on one-click nodes.
- **Non-one-click / hand-managed toml:** set `[cow.s3] enable = true` and restart cubelet.

## Upgrade note

Nodes that previously used S3 because cubelet always probed `/var/run/s3lvol.sock` (no `[cow.s3]` block, or a block without `enable`) will have S3 disabled after this change (`Enable` defaults to false). To keep S3, set `ONE_CLICK_ENABLE_S3LVOL=1` (one-click) or `enable = true` (manual config).

title: [Feature Request] Decouple snapshot deletion from sandbox lifecycle: allow deleting snapshots still referenced by running sandboxes
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Current behavior**: deleting a snapshot that is still referenced by running sandboxes (created from it, or rolled back to it) returns `409` from `DELETE /templates/{snapshotID}`. The caller must wait for every referencing sandbox to exit and then retry.

This restriction causes four real problems:

1. **Cleanup automation dead-ends.** A snapshot occupies a full image in persistent storage. SDK "delete when done" flows, periodic cleanup, and failure-recovery logic all fail while a snapshot is still referenced. Callers must maintain their own pending-delete lists and retry as sandboxes exit, and storage stays occupied in the meantime.
2. **The error misstates the real cause.** CubeAPI flattens this class of 409 into "active operation in progress" — the user is told an operation is running when the real reason is "still referenced by running instances", sending debugging in the wrong direction.
3. **The restriction can rot into a permanent deadlock.** Runtime references have no timeout fallback: if a node goes down permanently and its sandboxes were never destroyed cleanly, the reference never releases and the snapshot can *never* be deleted — an unbounded storage leak with no escape hatch.
4. **The API exposes a dead field.** The `retain` field on snapshot resources is never written or consumed anywhere, yet appears in API responses and the DB, misleading users into thinking a retention policy is configurable.

**Key background**: the block is a deliberate control-plane tightening (#693), not a data-plane physical constraint — on the default XFS backend, deleting a snapshot's physical files is safe for running instances (rootfs is reflink-derived; the memory file is mmap'ed and fd-held). The only real physical dependency across the whole chain is the S3 backend "same-node template start" path, where an instance's memory directly uses the snapshot's lvol.

## Proposed Solution

Change deletion semantics from "synchronous physical delete, rejected while referenced" to "**retire immediately + reclaim later**":

**1. DELETE takes effect immediately (logical delete).** As long as the snapshot is not CREATING / DELETING / in another active job, DELETE returns success synchronously; duplicate deletes and deleting an already-deleted snapshot are idempotent successes. After deletion the snapshot disappears from list/get immediately, can no longer be used to create new sandboxes, and rollback to it returns 404.

**2. Running sandboxes are unaffected.** Sandboxes already created from the snapshot keep running normally; no storage backend (XFS / S3) may crash an instance or corrupt data.

**3. Physical storage is reclaimed automatically.** Physical files are cleaned up by the system after the last referencing sandbox exits, with no user involvement; failed cleanups must be retried automatically and must not get stuck in an intermediate state.

**4. Reclamation is bounded (nothing may linger forever).** Orphan references — where the referencing sandbox no longer exists or its node is permanently gone — are treated as stale after a TTL (24h suggested), after which physical cleanup must eventually happen. No snapshot may enter an undeletable state.

**5. Downgrades are well-defined.** If a surviving sandbox takes a later snapshot and its incremental lineage has been broken, it automatically falls back to a full snapshot (existing behavior preserved).

**6. Error semantics are honest.** Genuine "operation in progress" (CREATING / DELETING / active job) still returns 409; deleted / nonexistent returns 404; "referenced by running instances" is no longer a reason for DELETE to fail.

**7. Remove the dead field.** Drop the unused `retain` field from the API and DB (including a DB migration).

### Acceptance criteria

- Create sandbox A from snapshot S → delete S succeeds immediately → A keeps running normally and can be destroyed; S's physical storage is reclaimed after A exits.
- After deleting S: list no longer contains S, get returns 404, creating from S returns 404, rolling back to S returns 404, a repeated DELETE is an idempotent success.
- Simulated node loss: after a referencing sandbox is unreachable past the TTL, S still completes physical reclamation.
- On the S3 backend, a sandbox started same-node from a snapshot keeps running without crashing after its source snapshot is deleted.

## Alternatives Considered

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Simply lift the guard** (regress to #360's warn-and-proceed) | Minimal change, but on the S3 same-node template-start path it is equivalent to yanking the memory disk out of a running instance — unacceptable |
| **`force=true` hard-delete parameter** | Fine as an ops escape hatch, but the default path still fails the "safe + automatable" bar; only additive |
| **Two-phase delete** (logical delete immediately, physical delete once references drop to zero) ✅ | Inherently safe on both backends; on XFS even an immediate physical delete would only reclaim space after instances exit, so deferring costs almost no extra disk |

## Additional Context

- **History**: the delete guard was relaxed to "warn and proceed" in a89fb00c, and #360 kept that semantics when the snapshot engine landed; #693 reintroduced the hard block when the runtime-reference table was added. "Reject while referenced" is thus a recent control-plane choice, not how it has always been.
- **Prior art in this repo**: an ext4 OS-image artifact referenced by a running sandbox is rejected with Conflict and later reclaimed by GC once references drop to zero — the snapshot system can align with this same "deferred physical delete" semantics.
- **Docs**: on landing, the snapshot best-practices section of the user docs (EN/ZH) must be updated to describe the new decoupled semantics.

title: feat(cubemaster): support deleting snapshots while sandboxes are running
body:
### Background

Close #1621 

`DELETE /cube/snapshot/{id}` used to fail with a conflict while any sandbox still held a runtime reference to the snapshot, so a snapshot could only be deleted after every consuming sandbox was destroyed. A long-lived sandbox therefore pinned snapshots indefinitely, and callers had no way to express "delete it as soon as nothing needs it".

This PR decouples logical deletion from physical reclamation with a **tombstone-based two-phase delete**: the logical delete always succeeds, and physical cleanup runs once the last runtime reference is gone.

### Design

1. **Logical retire (tombstone).** When active runtime refs remain, `DeleteSnapshot` marks the row `DELETED` and returns a synthetic `READY` job, keeping the API surface synchronous and idempotent (a repeated DELETE re-returns READY). A tombstoned snapshot disappears from List/Get and rejects new sandbox creates, rollbacks, and restore-source lookups.
2. **Physical finalize.** When the last runtime ref detaches (sandbox destroy hook), the existing snapshot-delete job runs asynchronously to clean replicas and metadata. The periodic snapshot reconciler retries lost finalizations and expires orphan refs — a ref is only expired when the sandbox is gone from master **and** it has been unobserved beyond a 24 h TTL, so a transient cache miss cannot drop a live ref.
3. **In-flight create safety.** A sandbox whose create bound just before the tombstone still records its runtime ref, so cleanup waits for it. Ready-replica validation is skipped only for that already-bound case.
4. **Failure semantics.** A physical-delete failure returns the row to `DELETED` (retryable by the reconciler or a repeated DELETE) instead of `FAILED`; replica-presence failures now use a compare-and-set update so they never overwrite a concurrent tombstone; a row stuck in `DELETING` past the operation timeout returns to `DELETED` for retry.

### Other changes

- **CubeAPI routing:** `has_snapshot` routes `snap-*` ids to the snapshot delete path by identity rather than row visibility, so a tombstoned snapshot keeps being deleted idempotently instead of falling through to template deletion.
- **`DeleteTemplate` delegation:** deleting a template id that is actually a snapshot row now delegates to `DeleteSnapshot`, so both delete paths behave identically.
- **Schema cleanup:** drop the `retain` column from `t_cube_snapshot` and `t_cube_template_definition` — it was never written or consumed by control-plane logic. Goose migrations for MySQL and Postgres, guarded by the usual migration advisory locks; the Down migration restores the column.

### Testing

- New `snapshot_tombstone_test.go` (18 cases) covering tombstone visibility (List / Get / template kind / template info / request), rejection of new use (create / rollback / restore source), ref-count gating of physical cleanup, orphan-ref expiry requiring both a missing sandbox and TTL, fail-closed sandbox lookups, and tombstone-preserving failure paths.
- Updated existing tests for the `DeleteSnapshot` tombstone path, runtime-ref registration for in-flight creates, reconciler drain, replica-presence compare-and-set, and CubeAPI `snap-*` identity routing.
- Migration schema assertions updated: `retain` must be absent at head schema for both MySQL and Postgres.

### Compatibility / upgrade notes

- `DELETED` is a new snapshot status; all pre-existing statuses keep their previous handling. When no runtime refs remain, the delete path is unchanged and still fully synchronous.
- The `retain` column drop is safe for the control plane (never read or written); the Down migration restores the column if a rollback is ever needed.

title: feat(cubemaster): add extensible scheduler plugin system and scheduling-quality evaluation
body:
## Summary

This draft adds two complementary pieces to CubeMaster scheduling, developed on top of each other:

1. **Scheduling-quality evaluation framework** — Prometheus metrics for the scheduling pipeline (`scheduler_attempts_total`, `scheduler_duration_seconds`, `scheduler_decisions_total`, `scheduler_reschedules_total`, `sandbox_create_*`, cluster gauges), a seeded workload generator + A/B compare report in `examples/cube-bench`, and `cmd/schedsim`, an in-process simulator that replays cube-bench traces through the real `scheduler.Select` over a simulated node fleet and reports packing/fragmentation/balance/locality metrics.
2. **Extensible scheduler plugin system** (merged from fork PR shsaihdsaiudh/CubeSandbox#1) — an explicit plugin registry replacing the reflect-based maps, named strategy **profiles** with per-plugin config and failure policies, three picker modes (`random`/`spread`/`highest`), CEL expression plugins, and external gRPC plugins, with legacy config translated to an equivalent `default` profile so existing behavior is unchanged.

The merge also resolves the `TODO(profile-router)` in the scheduler metrics: all scheduler/sandbox-create Prometheus series are now stamped with the profile that actually routed the request.

Design background: see `SCHEDULER_PLUGIN_DESIGN.md` and `SCHEDULER_CODE_READING_GUIDE.md` on the branch root.

## Changes

- `ab2ddfd7` feat(cubemaster): add scheduler Prometheus metrics
- `4967c66c` feat(cube-bench): add seeded workload generator and A/B compare report
- `675bb864` feat(cubemaster): add schedsim scheduling simulator
- `de1a7af3`/`be808e09` docs(scheduler): evaluation and plugin design
- `4209e1f7` feat(scheduler): add extensible plugin system (from shsaihdsaiudh/CubeSandbox#1)
- `c45dda12` feat(scheduler): merge extensible plugin system from PR #1
- `a8c8b415` feat(cubemaster): wire profile labels into scheduler metrics and add schedsim compare mode (`--compare name=config.yaml,...` renders a markdown A/B report across scheduler configs)

## Test plan

- [x] `go test` green for `pkg/scheduler/...`, `pkg/selector/...`, `pkg/base/...`, `pkg/service/sandbox/...`, `pkg/server`, `pkg/localcache`, `cmd/schedsim`, and the `examples/cube-bench` module

title: fix(shim): restore RPC log forward after template create

## Summary
- Keep passfd compiled in but opt-in (`cube.use_passfd_io=true` plus nonempty stdout/stderr). Default sandboxes use the original RPC log forwarder again, which is what template restore needs after #728.
- Shim creates `/data/cubelet/log/<sandbox-id>/stdout|stderr` and removes that directory on binary delete (`delete_shim` / `clean_sandbox_resource`), so a crashed shim does not leak files.

[Feature] MinIO/S3 object storage backend for template artifacts (0.7.1 M3)
body:
## 概述

支持将模板 rootfs artifact（ext4）存储到 S3 兼容对象存储（MinIO），计算节点直接从对象存储下载，替代当前的「Master 本地盘存储 + 所有节点向 Master 拉取」模式。

## 背景与动机

当前 artifact 存放在 CubeMaster 本地磁盘，存在两个硬伤：

1. **单点**：Master 磁盘故障或空间耗尽会影响整个集群的模板分发
2. **带宽瓶颈**：N 个计算节点并发创建沙箱时，所有节点都向 Master 拉取数 GB 的 ext4，Master 出口带宽成为瓶颈

引入对象存储后，artifact 上传一次、各节点直连对象存储下载，存储可靠性和分发带宽都水平扩展，也为跨机快照共享存储打底。

## 功能范围

- 存储后端可配置：本地磁盘（默认，保持现状）或 S3 兼容对象存储（MinIO/S3）
- 构建完成后 artifact 上传对象存储，节点下载仍带内容校验（sha256）
- 生命周期回收同步覆盖对象存储中的数据，含失败重试与孤儿对象清理
- 访问凭证仅通过环境变量/Secret 注入，不落配置文件明文
- 滚动升级兼容：新旧版本计算节点在升级期间都能正常下载

## 验收标准

- [ ] 配置对象存储后端后，模板构建、下载、回收全链路正常，MinIO 重启后可恢复
- [ ] 10 节点并发基于同一模板创建沙箱，Master 出口带宽不再成为瓶颈（对比本地模式）
- [ ] 滚动升级期间新旧节点混合下载均正常

title: [Feature] Full CubeMaster split: converge to pure control plane (0.7.1 M2)
body:
## 概述

在模板中心独立拆分（M1）的基础上完成收尾，使 CubeMaster 彻底不再承担模板构建与分发的 I/O 工作，收敛为纯粹的调度 + 节点元数据控制面。

## 背景与动机

CubeMaster 当前同时承载调度决策和模板构建 I/O，职责过重：构建任务消耗大量磁盘和 CPU，进程镜像还要附带镜像拉取工具链。彻底拆分后，CubeMaster 进程更轻、更稳定，控制面与重 I/O 工作负载实现故障隔离。

## 功能范围

- 模板构建所需的镜像拉取、ext4 制作、artifact 工作目录全部移出 CubeMaster
- 进程边界明确：
  - CubeMaster：调度、节点注册与心跳、配额
  - 模板中心：模板 / artifact / 快照全生命周期
  - 既有独立组件（API 网关、运维、生命周期管理、代理、控制台）保持不变
- 配置项按服务归属迁移，旧配置保留一个版本的废弃警告，平滑过渡

## 验收标准

- [ ] CubeMaster 部署物不再包含镜像拉取与 ext4 构建依赖
- [ ] 模板中心宕机时，基于存量 READY 模板创建沙箱不受影响
- [ ] 旧配置项启动时给出废弃警告，功能正常

title: feat(cube-envd): introduce in-repo Rust cube-envd and replace upstream Go envd
body:
## 概述

本 PR 新增仓库自研的 Rust E2B 兼容 guest daemon `cube-envd`，并把它接入构建、基础镜像、CI、发布、文档与一致性对照链路。`cubesandbox-base` 默认使用仓库内编译的 `cube-envd`；上游 Go envd 仍随镜像一起发布，可在**运行期**一键回滚。

同时新增一套**基线对照套件**：在同一个镜像内，对 `cube-envd` 与固定的 Go envd（`e2b-dev/infra@2026.16`，envd 0.5.13）逐场景采集并 diff；每一处有意差异连同理由写入 `declared_differences.toml`，渲染进 README 并由 CI 校验。

## 目的

- 消除对 `e2b-dev/infra` 固定 tag 及外部 clone 的构建依赖
- envd 的版本与 commit 随 CubeSandbox 仓库确定性产生
- 复用仓库现有 Rust 工具链，支持 linux/amd64、linux/arm64 musl 静态构建
- 把"与上游的差异"从口头声明变成**可测量、可门禁**的清单

## 变更内容

### 新组件：`cube-envd`

- **进程**：`Start` / `Connect` / `List` / `Update` / `SendInput` / `StreamInput` / `SendSignal` / `CloseStdin`，含真实 PTY（初始窗口尺寸、Ctrl+D 语义）
- **文件系统**：`Stat` / `ListDir` / `MakeDir` / `Move` / `Remove` / `WatchDir`
- **HTTP 面**：`/health`、`/init`、`/envs`、`/files`（上传/下载；Range 与条件请求属已声明差异）
- Connect-JSON 线协议、错误码，以及与 connect-go `DiscardUnknown` 一致的未知字段处理
- 版本的唯一事实源是 `src/version.rs` 的 semver 常量（不再从 tag/sha 派生），`-version` / `-commit` 供 Cubelet / CubeMaster 采集
- 静态 musl 二进制约 6.9 MiB

### 协议兼容性与差异声明

- `tests/e2e/cube_envd/conformance/`：同一镜像内的两个二进制（`/usr/bin/envd` 与 `/usr/bin/envd-go`）逐场景对照，另提供活体模式（经 CubeProxy 在两个真实沙箱上对比）
- `declared_differences.toml` 记录每处有意差异及依据；`conformance.py render-docs` 渲染进 `cube-envd/README.md`，`check-docs` 在 CI 校验，避免"声明"与"实测"脱节
- **声明范围之外**的三个面（`/files/compose`、`/metrics`、CreateWatcher 系列）显式返回 501 + Connect `unimplemented` 错误体，而不是让路由缺失导致 404

### 本轮修复的实质缺陷（对照评审意见）

- **`StreamInput` 响应未装帧**：它是客户端流式 RPC，响应此前按一元裸 JSON 返回（`application/json` + `{}`）。connect-go 客户端会因流式响应 content-type 校验失败而直接报错（`invalid content-type: "application/json"; expecting "application/connect+json"`），而 e2b 的 `processC.StreamInput(ctx)` 正是这种客户端。现已按"数据信封 + end-stream 信封"返回
- **基础镜像版本校验恒真**：校验值与被校验值来自同一个环境变量，永远相等；且 `ARG` 默认值会把手工构建的镜像钉死在旧版本。现已让二进制只认源码常量，`ARG` 仅用于镜像 label 并与之交叉校验
- **`setpriv` 路径写死**：非 root 用户执行会走 `/usr/bin/setpriv`，而 Alpine 的 util-linux 装在 `/bin/setpriv`，装了包也仍然失败。现改为固定候选路径探测（并排除 busybox 的同名 applet），失败时给出可定位错误

### 构建与镜像

- 根 `Makefile` 新增 `cube-envd` / `cube-envd-test` / `cube-envd-lint` / `cube-envd-proto-doc-check`；构建 `cubemaster` 时自动编译并内嵌到 `cubemastercli`
- `docker/Dockerfile.cube-base` 同时产出两个实现：`ENVD_IMPL=cube|go` 决定谁被安装为 `/usr/bin/envd`（构建期），`/usr/bin/envd-go` 恒定存在，`ENVD_BIN=/usr/bin/envd-go` 可在运行期回滚、无需重建镜像
- `.dockerignore` 放行 `cube-envd/` 并排除 `cube-envd/target`
- `docker/Dockerfile.builder` 增加 envd 使用的 Rust toolchain（含 clippy/rustfmt）与 protoc-gen-doc

### CI 门禁

- **build-check**：`cube-envd` 在 amd64/arm64 双架构构建；`src/generated` 漂移门禁；clippy（`-D warnings`）门禁；生成式协议文档漂移门禁
- **unit-test-check**：`cube-envd-test`（以 root 在 builder 容器内运行 —— 集成测试需要 passwd 条目来构造 Authorization 头，而 GitHub runner 的 uid 在镜像里没有该条目，会让用例 panic）
- **新增 `cube-envd-conformance.yml`**：跑基线对照、校验差异表与 README 一致、上传结果 artifact
- fmt-check 覆盖 Rust 源码

### 测试

- `cube-envd/tests/`：CLI、HTTP 面、Connect 帧、进程/PTY/输入/信号、文件系统、上传、watch、认证与路径解析、优雅关闭
- `tests/layer_rule.rs`：断言模块依赖方向（`pub(crate)` 对同级模块一律可见，越界引用只有该用例能挡；注意 `cargo test --lib --bins` 会静默跳过它）
- SDK 兼容 command cases 不再依赖镜像内 Python；signal 用例改由 capability 门禁，而不是 backend 条件分支 + 宽松断言
- one-click 单元运行器纳入 `cube-envd-test`

### 文档

- `cube-envd/README.md` 与 `README_zh.md` 逐节对齐，新增：`Why`（自研动机）、`Design`（层契约与依赖方向、注释目录树、以及"必须带 `tests` 目标运行"的运维提醒）、`Integration notes`（entrypoint 契约；为什么安装路径必须是字面的 `/usr/bin/envd`；keepalive 节奏与 LB 空闲超时的关系）
- `cube-envd/doc/cube-envd-api.md`：生成式协议参考，新增漂移门禁
- `docker/README.md`：两个实现的选择方式、按模板覆盖 `env` 的陷阱
- 中英文 `bring-your-own-image` 教程：envd 来源与镜像 tag、`-isnotfc` 是 no-op、非 root 用户需要 util-linux 的 `setpriv`
- 全部 `.rs` 与自研 `.proto` 补齐版权/SPDX 头

## 验证

**已在真实部署上验收**（CubeSandbox v0.6.0，宿主 `100.64.0.34`；镜像 `127.0.0.1:5000/cube-envd-accept:20260914` = 本分支 cube-envd 0.1.0 + `/usr/bin/envd-go` 回滚二进制，模板 `tpl-c7a6aada633b48f79425d95f` 与 `tpl-5b10b52198304d698ea9c3f8`）：

- [x] 建模板 → READY；起沙箱经 CubeProxy 探活 `/health` **204**、`/envs` 含 `E2B_SANDBOX=false`
- [x] **活体 e2e**（仓库自带 `tests/e2e/cube_envd/raw_proxy_e2e.py`，经 CubeProxy 的原始 Connect-JSON 全链路）→ **PASS**：覆盖代理访问控制、`/init`+`/envs`、命令流/退出码/stderr、输入、信号、超时、重连、PTY、文件系统读写/移动/删除/符号链接/WatchDir、协议错误、日志、`envd -version`
- [x] **SDK 兼容 e2e**（cubesandbox 后端，SDK 0.7.0）：`-m "smoke or p0"` → 22 passed / 6 failed；6 个失败全在 `cases/run_code`（HTTP 502，基础镜像不含 Jupyter 内核，属模板能力问题而非 daemon），换 code-interpreter 模板单跑 → 6 passed
- [x] **活体双沙箱对拍**（`run_live.py`：部署里两个模板各起一个私有沙箱，经 CubeProxy 采集）：`EQUAL 26 / DECLARED-DIFF 7 / UNDECLARED-DIFF 0 / DECLARED-BUT-EQUAL 0` → **PASS（--strict）**
- [x] 模板级 `ENVD_BIN` 回滚实证：`/metrics` 在默认模板 **501**（cube-envd）/ 回滚模板 **200**（Go envd），两者同在一个镜像里

**本地与容器内实测：**

- [x] 容器模式对照（同一镜像两个容器，`--user root`）：`EQUAL 26 / DECLARED-DIFF 9 / UNDECLARED-DIFF 0 / DECLARED-BUT-EQUAL 0` → PASS（--strict）
- [x] `make -C cube-envd lint`（`cargo fmt --check` + `clippy -D warnings`）
- [x] `make -C cube-envd test` 全绿（含 `layer_rule`；`blocking_strategy` 为 `--ignored` 的手工用例）
- [x] `make -C cube-envd proto-gen-check` / `proto-doc-check`（builder 容器内；镜像带 protoc-gen-doc）
- [x] `StreamInput` 修复：真实二进制返回 `application/connect+json` + 数据信封 + end-stream 信封；把 handler 改回旧实现后新断言确实失败
- [x] 基础镜像版本校验：不带 `--build-arg` 时二进制自报源码常量；传入不匹配的 `--build-arg` 时构建失败且不产镜像
- [x] `setpriv` 解析：Alpine 默认（仅 busybox applet）给出可定位错误；`apk add util-linux` 后返回 200

**待 CI：**

- [ ] base 镜像 **arm64** 构建与 smoke —— 目前的验收镜像为 amd64（本地无 arm runner），由 CI 的原生 `ubuntu-24.04-arm` 覆盖
- [ ] 各 CI 门禁首跑（fork PR 的 workflow 需维护者批准）

## 备注

- 安装后的命令名仍保持 `/usr/bin/envd`，SDK 无需改动
- 原 `workflow_dispatch` 的 `envd_ref` 上游版本输入已移除
- 差异清单里每条"与基线不同"都必须带理由；对照套件不覆盖的面（如 per-command cgroup）只作为文档条目说明，不计入差异表
- 差异声明表由脚本生成（正文为中文）；模块 README 为中英双语且逐节对齐

title: cubelet plugin init failure when gateway ARP cache is not yet populated
body: Breaking Change Notice: Error message format for GetGatewayMacAddr has been updated to include retry and probe error context. Consumers matching on the exact error string may be affected. fix #1608 During Kubernetes cubenode Cubelet plugin initialization, plugin fails to load with: failed to get internal plugin: gateway mac for ens3 via 192.168.0.1 not found Image Manually pinging the gateway prior to initialization resolves the issue, confirming that ARP cache population is the missing prerequisite. Image GetGatewayMacAddr reads the kernel neighbor table exactly once. At early boot the gateway's ARP entry may not exist yet (or is in NUD_INCOMPLETE state), so the lookup fails immediately with no recovery mechanism. This is a timing-dependent issue — it does not reproduce on every boot. Root Cause GetHostDevice → GetGatewayMacAddr performs a single NeighList call. If no usable neighbor entry (REACHABLE / STALE / DELAY / PROBE / PERMANENT) is found for the gateway IP, it returns an error. There is no ARP trigger or retry logic. Fix Modified GetGatewayMacAddr in Cubelet/network/runtime/systemnet/device.go to: Fast path — first attempt reads the neighbor table as before; if the entry exists, return immediately (no behavior change for the common case). Retry with ARP trigger — on cache miss, retry up to 5 times with 200ms backoff. Each retry calls triggerARPResolution which uses a two-layer approach: Layer 1: NeighSet(NUD_PROBE) — precisely targets the gateway on the correct interface index, causes the kernel to send an ARP Request. Side-effect-free but only works when a neighbor entry already exists. Layer 2: UDP probe fallback — sends a small UDP packet to the gateway, forcing the kernel to create a neighbor entry and issue an ARP request. This handles the case where no entry exists yet (the exact scenario during node init). Files Changed Cubelet/network/runtime/systemnet/device.go — added retry loop, triggerARPResolution, extracted lookupGatewayMac helper Cubelet/network/runtime/systemnet/device_test.go — added tests for lookupGatewayMac and the retry-on-cache-miss path
