title: fix(cubeops): support configurable Redis database selection
body:
## Motivation

When CubeMaster is configured to read node metrics from a non-zero Redis logical database, CubeOps still writes those metrics to DB 0 when it uses split Redis settings. CubeMaster therefore cannot see the metrics, causing scheduler metric updates to time out.

The same mismatch affects Sentinel connections because CubeOps does not select the configured logical database after discovering the Redis master.

## What Changed

* Add `redis_db` YAML and `REDIS_DB` environment configuration to CubeOps, defaulting to database `0`.
* Use the configured database for split standalone Redis connections.
* Use the configured database for Sentinel master connections.
* Treat `REDIS_URL` as the complete, highest-priority Redis connection configuration, including its database path, without combining it with Sentinel or split settings.
* Add focused coverage for Redis connection source priority, Sentinel master database selection, and YAML/environment precedence.
* Update CubeOps documentation.

## Validation

* `go test ./... -count=1` passed for CubeOps.
* CubeOps binaries built successfully.
* `REDIS_URL` priority and Sentinel database selection tests passed for 20 consecutive runs.
* Runtime Redis selection validation confirmed that a metric written with database `7` is readable from DB 7 and absent from DB 0.

## Scope

This PR is intentionally limited to CubeOps logical Redis database selection. It does not change the Helm chart or CubeMaster.

The chart already supports additional CubeOps environment variables through `cubeOps.env`, so Kubernetes installations can set `REDIS_DB` without adding a Chart-level `redis_db` value. CubeMaster continues using its existing `conf.yaml` Redis database configuration.

title: CubeEgress: Cap inject secrets at 2048 bytes and grow policy_store
body:
64 KiB secrets overflow nginx's default 8k header buffers and fill the 16m store. Align the cap with e2b (maxNetworkRuleHeaderValueLen=2048) in CubeAPI and the SDKs, drop the CubeEgress runtime size check, and size policy_store for 1000 sandboxes × 10 inject rules.

Closes #1428 and #1449.

title: fix(chart): rewrite imageRegistry only for official Cube TCR hosts
body:
## Summary

`global.imageRegistry` previously rewrote the leading registry host of every Cube-owned image, so a single override could accidentally rewrite images explicitly pointed at a private or third-party host. This change restricts the rewrite to the official Cube TCR hosts (`cube-sandbox-int` / `cube-sandbox-cn`), leaving any other declared repository untouched.

## Changes

- `cube.cubeImage` now rewrites the host only when the current repository starts with an official Cube TCR host, via the new `cube.officialImageRegistries` helper.
- Added `deploy/kubernetes/chart/scripts/test-cube-image-registry-guard.sh`, which renders the chart with `helm template` across chart defaults, `values-cn.yaml`, partial private overrides, full-mirror `global.imageRegistry`, and mixed configurations.
- Updated chart docs (`README.md`, `values.yaml`, `values-cn.yaml`, `runtime-values.example.yaml`) to describe the new behavior.

## How to verify

```sh
./deploy/kubernetes/chart/scripts/test-cube-image-registry-guard.sh
```

All assertions pass:

- chart defaults stay on the int TCR host
- `values-cn.yaml` moves official images to the cn TCR host
- private per-image repositories are never rewritten
- full-mirror `imageRegistry` still rewrites official defaults

title: fix(chart): use stable labels for redis PVC volumeClaimTemplates
body:
## Summary

Fixes the redis StatefulSet upgrade failure. The `cube.labels` helper renders version-dependent labels (`helm.sh/chart`, `app.kubernetes.io/version`). These labels are inherited by the PVCs created by the redis StatefulSet `volumeClaimTemplates`. On `helm upgrade`, a chart or app version bump changes the PVC labels, so the StatefulSet controller can no longer adopt the existing volumes and the upgrade fails.

## Changes

- Replace `cube.labels` in the redis `volumeClaimTemplates` metadata with a stable label set (`app.kubernetes.io/name`, `app.kubernetes.io/instance`, `app.kubernetes.io/component`) so existing PVCs remain matched across upgrades.

## How to verify

- `helm template` renders stable, version-independent labels on the PVC.
- Subsequent `helm upgrade` runs reuse the existing PVCs instead of recreating them.

title: CLM: Drop leftover sidecar comments and simplify subscriber retry
body:
CubeProxy-sidecar is gone; comments in cube-lifecycle-manager still named the old sidecar. Call the current process Cube Lifecycle Manager (CLM). Keep the cube-proxy-sidecar consumer group and CubeProxy /_sidecar_resume location so the wire protocol does not need a lock-step rename.

Retry Pub/Sub setup with time.Sleep instead of NewTimer so a cancelled context cannot leave an undrained timer.

title: fix(terraform): query cube-ops nodes via CLB and fix jq syntax
body:
Node verification/template creation was skipped ("Registered healthy nodes: 0") because:
1. The node query exec'd into the cube-ops pod to curl localhost, but the alpine runtime image ships no curl, so nodes_json held the exec error text and jq fell back to 0. Now curl cube-ops' CLB from the jumpserver .
2. The jq filters used wrong shapes.

title: fix(ci): run pkgs/proto's own unit tests in CI
body:
## Summary

`pkgs/proto` is a standalone Go module imported by CubeMaster, Cubelet and the cos/rpc example via a `replace` directive. `go test ./...` in an importing module never compiles or runs a dependency's `_test.go` files, so the credential-masking and address-normalization unit tests shipped with `pkgs/proto` were only exercised locally and silently skipped by CI.

## Changes

- Add a `proto-test` make target (host-run, like `cubedb-test`) that runs `go vet ./... && go test ./...` inside the `pkgs/proto` module.
- Wire a `proto` component into `unit-test-check`: `pkgs/proto/*` changes now re-run the module's own tests alongside the consumer test sets, and `workflow_dispatch` gains a `proto` option.
- Fix a `go vet` copylocks warning in `SafePrintImageSpec`: copy the proto message via `proto.Clone` instead of copying the struct by value (a proto message embeds `protoimpl.MessageState`, a `sync.Mutex`).

## Testing

- `make proto-test` passes: go vet is clean and all pkgs/proto tests pass, including the `TestSafePrintImageSpec*` and grpctarget `TestNormalize` / `TestParseListen` cases.
- Simulated the workflow select logic: a `pkgs/proto/*` change now yields a `Proto (amd64)` / `Proto (arm64)` matrix entry with `make=proto-test`.

title: refactor(proto): unify gRPC protos into shared pkgs/proto module
body:
## Summary

Introduce `pkgs/proto`, a single shared Go module that becomes the sole
source of truth for the CubeMaster ↔ Cubelet gRPC contracts, and migrate
every consumer onto it. This removes the duplicated proto trees that
historically lived under `CubeMaster/api` and `Cubelet/api` and had to be
kept in sync by hand (git history shows 12 protocol changes, each touching
two copies).

Related: #1354, #1023.

## What changed

- **New `pkgs/proto` module**: 6 proto groups (`cubebox` / `errorcode` /
  `images` / `snapshot` / `volumeplugin` / `types`) with checked-in
  generated `.pb.go`, the `volumeplugin/grpctarget` address-normalization
  helper, and a `protoc-gen-doc` API reference (`doc/api.md`).
- **Migration**: all consumers (CubeMaster, Cubelet,
  cube-lifecycle-manager, volume plugins, the cos/rpc example) now import
  the module via a `replace` directive. CubeMaster no longer replaces the
  whole Cubelet module just to reach the proto imports.
- **Safety hardening**:
  - `Cubelet/pkg/critypes`: nil-guarded CRI conversion helpers plus
    table-driven tests (previously exported from `Cubelet/api/types/v1`).
  - `SafePrintImageSpec` now masks registry credentials
    (token/username annotations) before specs are logged.
  - Fixed `cos/rpc` `isMountPoint`: an existing directory that is not a
    mount point is reported as "not mounted" instead of an error.
- **CI & tooling**: `pkgs/proto/*` changes trigger the real consumers'
  test sets (CubeMaster, cubelet, volume-cos-rpc); a new
  `volume-cos-rpc` component and a `make cube-volume-cos-rpc-test` target
  were added; docs updated for the new layout.

## Wire compatibility

Non-negotiable identifiers — proto package names, message names, field
numbers and full gRPC service method names — are unchanged. Only file
locations, `go_package` paths and import paths moved, so old and new
components can still interoperate on the wire.

## Testing

- Unit tests: updated consumer packages pass (CubeMaster, Cubelet,
  cos/rpc), including the new critypes / grpctarget / images-utils tests.
- CI: unit-test-check now covers `pkgs/proto` changes via its consumers.
- **E2E**: full `tests/e2e/sdk_compat` suite passed against a live
  one-click deployment (all-in-one control node) running this branch's
  build — **229 passed, 16 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed**. The 16 skips
  are documented opt-in gates (platform lifecycle, key auth, L7 HTTPS CA
  trust, external-resolver connectivity); the xfail is the known
  host-mount symlink TOCTOU case.

## Diff stat

284 files changed, +5,641 / −17,015 (net ≈ −11k lines, mostly duplicated
generated code).

title: [Feature Request] Support snapshots for sandboxes with volumes and host mounts

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem / Motivation

CubeSandbox currently rejects `create_snapshot()` / `CommitSandbox` when a sandbox uses `host-mount`, `host_dir`, `plugin_volume`, host-path-backed mounts, or some shared `sandbox_path` mounts. This prevents sandboxes using persistent datasets, shared workspaces, model caches, or output directories from using snapshots, rollback, or clone.

Pause/Resume already preserves mount configuration, reattaches or rebinds external storage, and reconnects virtiofs during restore. The ordinary snapshot path should reuse these capabilities.

The feature must distinguish VM state from external data: a VM snapshot contains memory, device state, rootfs, and mount configuration, but it should not implicitly copy host-path or external-volume contents. Without a provider-level point-in-time snapshot, restore sees the volume's current contents rather than its contents at VM snapshot creation time.

## Proposed Solution

### 1. External-reference snapshots

Initially support an **external reference** mode:

- Persist the volume identity, driver, access mode, mount destination, read-only flag, and restore constraints.
- Do not copy arbitrary host-path contents into the VM snapshot package.
- Reattach or rebind every required volume before VM memory restore.
- Fail restore before VM startup if any dependency is unavailable.

A future **provider snapshot** mode can extend the Volume Plugin interface with create, restore, and delete snapshot operations. This mode is required for point-in-time volume consistency.

### 2. Host mounts remain origin-node-only

- Allow ordinary snapshot creation after validating and persisting the mount specification.
- Mark the snapshot as origin-node-only.
- Set `PinToOrigin` for both Pause/Resume and create-from-snapshot placement.
- Before restore, verify that each source path exists, has the expected type, and is allowed by the host-mount policy.
- Preserve read-only behavior and deterministic parent-before-child ordering for nested mounts.

An identical path string on another node does not guarantee identical storage, so raw host paths must not be treated as cross-node portable.

### 3. Plugin volumes may be portable

Cross-node restore should be allowed only when the VM snapshot is cross-node capable, the target has the required driver and configuration, every volume is portable to that node, and all Attach operations succeed before the hypervisor starts. Placement must include volume topology and driver availability.

### 4. Lifecycle and dependency tracking

- Record every external volume required by a snapshot.
- Acquire runtime references during restore and release them during destroy.
- Roll back successful attaches and reference-count changes after a partial failure.
- Store stable secret references rather than credentials or short-lived tokens.

### 5. Clone, rollback, and consistency

- Read-only volumes may be shared by clones.
- Rollback must verify that the current volume set is compatible with the snapshot.
- External-reference rollback restores VM/rootfs state but keeps external data at its current state.
- Provider snapshots should use a documented quiesce sequence: flush or freeze guest filesystems, freeze the VM, snapshot volumes and VM state, then thaw and resume.

The documented guarantee must distinguish reference-only, crash, filesystem, and application consistency. Open files, FUSE handles, locks, `mmap`, in-flight writes, and virtiofs daemon reconnection require dedicated tests.

### 6. Security and API behavior

Host-path handling should protect against symlink escape, time-of-check/time-of-use replacement, mount type changes, UID/GID or ACL differences, xattr behavior, and SELinux labeling differences.

Snapshot APIs should expose the external-volume mode, portability, origin pinning, and volume dependencies. Unsupported combinations should fail during validation rather than later in the Cubelet commit path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Sandboxes with read-only or writable host mounts can create and restore snapshots on the origin node.
- Create-from-snapshot and Pause/Resume both pin raw host mounts to the origin node.
- Restore fails before VM startup when a required path or volume is unavailable.
- A portable plugin volume can be reattached on a compatible target during S3 cross-node restore.
- A node-local plugin volume prevents cross-node placement.
- Nested and multiple mounts retain their expected order and permissions.
- Read-write volumes cannot fan out unless multi-attach is supported and explicitly requested.
- Secrets and short-lived credentials are not copied into snapshot metadata.
- API and documentation clearly state the consistency and sharing semantics.

## Test Plan

- Same-node snapshot, restore, and rollback with read-only, writable, nested, missing, and unauthorized host mounts.
- Cross-node restore with portable and node-local plugin volumes, including missing drivers and partial Attach failures.
- Clone tests for read-only sharing, rejected RW fan-out, and explicit multi-attach.
- Consistency tests covering open files, locks, `mmap`, concurrent writes, and virtiofs/plugin restarts.
- Lifecycle tests covering volume deletion, snapshot deletion, timeouts, process restarts, and reference counts.
- Security tests covering symlink replacement, UID/GID, ACL, xattr, SELinux, and secret leakage.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Copy every host mount into the VM snapshot:** provides isolation but duplicates potentially large datasets and turns host mounts into an implicit backup system. It may be offered later as an explicit mode.
- **Continue rejecting external volumes:** safe, but blocks common persistent-workspace use cases despite existing Pause/Resume reattach support.
- **Allow cross-node restore based only on an identical path:** unsafe because the path may refer to different storage or permissions.
- **Always share RW volumes between clones:** simple, but violates clone isolation.

## Additional Context

The existing implementation already provides persisted sandbox specs, Pause package mount metadata, Volume Plugin Attach/Detach and reference counting, per-sandbox host bind staging, RO/RW virtiofs channels, deterministic nested-mount ordering, virtiofs reconnection during memory restore, and S3 cross-node snapshot import.

The main missing pieces are ordinary snapshot admission, explicit external-data semantics, FromSnap origin pinning, volume-aware placement, snapshot-to-volume dependency tracking, consistency coordination, and end-to-end coverage.

Recommended delivery order:

1. Same-node external-reference snapshots.
2. Snapshot-volume dependency tracking and lifecycle safety.
3. Capability-gated cross-node plugin volumes.
4. Provider point-in-time snapshots and coordinated consistency.

title: [Bug Report] [v0.7.0] stdout/stderr files are not created for restored Sandbox, causing `cubecli logs` to fail

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Impacts the cube-agent which runs in the guest VM

body:
## Summary In CubeSandbox v0.7.0, `stdout` and `stderr` files are not created for a Sandbox restored from a template snapshot, causing `cubecli logs` to fail with `log file not found`. ## Environment - CubeSandbox version / commit: v0.7.0 - Host OS and kernel version: Not collected yet - KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): Not collected yet - Deployment mode: single-node - Relevant component: CubeShim / agent (init log forwarding) Additional version information from the affected Sandbox: CubeShim: /data/cubelet/root/component_versions/cube-shim/v0.7.0/bin/containerd-shim-cube-rs CubeShim SHA256: 4bda796396250a6d59bbd2224e15c4ebbd0489a71c6b1b71e4beb071febfb7e1 CubeAgent: /data/cubelet/root/component_versions/cube-agent/v0.7.0/cube-agent.ext4 Guest image: /data/cubelet/root/component_versions/cube-image/guest-image-260820-1/cube-guest-image-cpu.img ## Steps to Reproduce Deploy CubeSandbox v0.7.0 and create a template. Create a Sandbox from the template snapshot and confirm that the Sandbox is running: cubemastercli ls --all Example: sandbox_id status host_id 0450f26b34424c0ba7f408ed3be89cea running 10.0.64.172 Run: cubecli logs 0450f26b34424c0ba7f408ed3be89cea Enter the Cubelet mount namespace and inspect the Sandbox runtime directory: nsenter -t $(pidof cubelet) -m -- bash ls -lah \ /data/cubelet/state/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default/0450f26b34424c0ba7f408ed3be89cea/ ## Expected Behavior The Sandbox init log forwarding should start after the Sandbox is started. The following files should be created in the runtime directory: /data/cubelet/state/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default//stdout /data/cubelet/state/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default//stderr cubecli logs should be able to read the Sandbox init process logs. In v0.6.0, the same scenario starts log forwarding successfully, with CubeShim logs similar to: start request, id:, execid: starting log forwarding for container: stdout:stdout stderr:stderr start req finish forward init log stderr start forward init log stdout start ## Actual Behavior The Sandbox itself is created successfully and remains in the running state, but cubecli logs fails: cubecli run fail: log file not found: /data/cubelet/state/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default/0450f26b34424c0ba7f408ed3be89cea/stdout (sandbox may not exist or log forwarding may not be enabled) The runtime directory exists, but neither stdout nor stderr is created: address bootstrap.json config.json log rootfs/ shim-binary-path shim.pid vmm.pid work CubeShim logs show that the VM, agent, and Sandbox start successfully: snapshot restore init using snapshot_base:... start vm start agent is ready receive create sandbox create sandbox!, add storage:0ms start sandbox finish at:28 passfd streams ready for create, id:0450f26b34424c0ba7f408ed3be89cea, stdin_port:0, stdout_port:0, stderr_port:0 [cube-strace]recv create container create container by restore start container finish at:52 create req finish start request, id:0450f26b34424c0ba7f408ed3be89cea, execid: start req finish, id:0450f26b34424c0ba7f408ed3be89cea, execid:, cost_ms:0 wait process start However, for this Sandbox, the following log-forwarding messages never appear: starting log forwarding for container: forward init log stderr start forward init log stdout start ## Additional Context

I compared this behavior with a CubeSandbox v0.6.0 environment.

In v0.6.0, a Sandbox created by restoring from a template snapshot successfully starts init log forwarding:

start request, id:b00c14f1a1a74635a880c625b9340d73, execid:
starting log forwarding for container:b00c14f1a1a74635a880c625b9340d73 stdout:stdout stderr:stderr
start req finish
forward init log stderr start
forward init log stdout start

The runtime directory contains both:

stderr
stdout

and cubecli logs works normally.

Another observation is that log forwarding is not completely broken in the v0.7.0 environment.

During template creation in the same v0.7.0 environment, CubeShim still logs:

starting log forwarding for container:tpl-...
forward init log stderr start
forward init log stdout start

and template logs are written successfully.

Therefore, the issue appears to be specific to the normal Sandbox restored from a template snapshot rather than the entire log-forwarding mechanism.

Comparison:

Item | v0.6.0 | v0.7.0 -- | -- | -- Sandbox running | Yes | Yes Agent ready | Yes | Yes Restored from template snapshot | Yes | Yes starting log forwarding for Sandbox | Yes | No forward init log stdout/stderr start | Yes | No Runtime stdout / stderr created | Yes | No cubecli logs | Works | log file not found Template log forwarding | Works | Works

title: fix(cubelog): accept case-insensitive log levels
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1593
Accept case-insensitive log levels and ignore leading/trailing whitespace.

## Root cause

CubeMaster configurations use values such as `level: "info"`.
CubeMaster passes this value to `StringToLevel`, which previously matched only exact uppercase strings, causing valid lowercase values to fall back to `DEBUG`.

## Changes

- Normalize input with `strings.TrimSpace` and `strings.ToUpper`.
- Add contract coverage for uppercase, lowercase, mixed-case, whitespace-padded, unknown, and empty values.
- Keep the existing `DEBUG` fallback behavior.
- No configuration templates were modified.

## Tests

- CubeLog tests passed.
- CubeMaster tests passed in the builder environment.



Issue #1289 is already fixed and is outside this PR.
Issue #1470 is outside this PR scope.

title: fix(cubeopscli): report build-injected version instead of hardcoded 0.1.0
body:
## Summary

`cubeopscli --version` printed a hardcoded `0.1.0`, and `cubeopscli version`
failed with `No help topic for 'version'`, because no build path injected the
canonical `CUBE_VERSION` / `CUBE_COMMIT` / `CUBE_BUILD_TIME` triplet into
`CubeOps/internal/version`.

This change fixes both the code and every build path, mirroring the existing
`cubemastercli` pattern.

## Changes

### Code
- Add `VersionString(binaryName)` to `CubeOps/internal/version` (keeps
  `ShowVersion()`, which logging depends on).
- `cubeopscli` now consumes the injected version: `app.Version` comes from
  `version.ShowVersion()`, a `cli.VersionPrinter` prints the unified string,
  and a new `version` subcommand is registered.
- `cubeopscli version` prints the full version string by default
  (e.g. `cubeopscli v0.7.0 (<commit>) built at <timestamp>`) and bare semver
  with `--versiononly`, which is script-friendly.

### Build
- The top-level `make cubeops` target now delegates to the CubeOps Makefile
  build (`APPS=cubeops cubeopscli`; `BUILD_FLAGS` owns the version injection),
  matching the `cubemaster` / `cubelet` pattern.
- The one-click builder builds `cubeopscli` inside `track_cubeops` with the
  shared ldflags.
- `build-release-bundle.sh` passes the CubeOps version package to the binary
  helper.
- The `cubemastercli` Docker image `builder-ops` stage declares the version
  build args and injects them like `builder-master`.

### Tests and docs
- End-to-end tests for `--version` and the `version` subcommand.
- Documented the `cubeopscli version` commands in the CLI tools guide
  (English and Chinese).

## Verification

- `make cubeops` and the one-click packaging both produce binaries that report
  the injected version; a plain `go build` without ldflags falls back to
  `0.0.0-dev (unknown) built at unknown`.

title: refactor(cubemaster): consolidate CPU/mem overcommit into Cubelet
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1565

## Motivation

When sandboxes are created concurrently in batches, CubeMaster admits far more sandboxes onto a node than the configured overcommit ratios should permit (issue #1565). One of the root causes is that CPU/mem overcommit is applied **twice**, so the effective overcommit is much larger than what an operator configures:

- **Cubelet** bakes a hardcoded overcommit factor into the node-reported quota when deriving it from host hardware   (CPU ×2, Mem ×1.25).
- **CubeMaster** then multiplies that already-inflated value by its own
  `overcommit_ratio` (default CPU ×3, Mem ×2).

The compounded default becomes **6× CPU / 2.5× memory** instead of the 3× / 2× the operator expects, so the scheduler admits roughly twice the intended number of sandboxes onto a node.

Overcommit is fundamentally a per-node decision — it depends on the node's hardware, workload, and local policy — so it belongs at the node agent (Cubelet), not in the centralized scheduler. Consolidating it in one place also removes the double-application footgun and leaves room for future Cubelet-side resource reservation.

  ## What this PR does

Remove CPU/mem overcommit from CubeMaster entirely. The scheduler now treats the Cubelet-reported `quota_cpu` / `quota_mem_mb` as the final schedulable capacity, since that value already carries Cubelet's overcommit factor.

- `CubeMaster/pkg/base/config/config.go`: remove the `OvercommitRatio` / `OvercommitRatioByType` fields, the `OvercommitRatioConf` type, the `GetEffectiveOvercommitRatio` / `sanitized` / `isValidRatio` / `EffectiveQuotaCpu` / `EffectiveQuotaMem` / `floatToInt64Clamped` helpers, the default ratio constants, and the default-value injection in `preHandleScheduler`. `EffectiveAllocated` (the `ignore_redis_allocation` path) is kept untouched.
- `CubeMaster/pkg/selector/filter/cpufilter.go`, `memfilter.go`: compute `quotaCpuFree` / `quotaMemFree` directly from the node-reported `QuotaCpu` / `QuotaMem` instead of the overcommit-adjusted effective quota.
- `CubeMaster/pkg/selector/score/utils.go`, `realtimescore.go`: score against `n.QuotaCpu` / `n.QuotaMem` directly.
- `CubeMaster/pkg/base/config/config_test.go`: drop the overcommit and `floatToInt64Clamped` tests; keep and rename the `EffectiveAllocated` and ignore-defaults coverage; drop the now-unused `math` import.
- `CubeMaster/conf.yaml`: remove the `overcommit_ratio` / `overcommit_ratio_conf` block.
- `docs/guide/cubemaster-scheduler-config.md` (+ zh): remove the overcommit field reference, clarify that the reported quota already carries Cubelet's overcommit, and drop stale overcommit guidance in the multi-node deploy guide.

  ## Notes

- Cubelet is intentionally untouched; its existing quota-derivation overcommit strategy is preserved as the single source of overcommit.
- Existing deployments with a stale `overcommit_ratio` key in `cubemaster.yaml` are unaffected: the YAML loader ignores unknown fields, so the stale key is silently dropped rather than failing startup. Operators can safely remove it from their config.

title: feat(cube-lifecycle-manager): add webhook event delivery
body: Summary Adds webhook event delivery to cube-lifecycle-manager (CLM). CLM now pushes sandbox lifecycle events (sandbox.created, sandbox.deleted, sandbox.paused, sandbox.resumed, sandbox.timeout.updated) to external HTTP endpoints, so the auto-pause/auto-resume coordinator can feed real-time lifecycle notifications into alerting and automation systems. The wire protocol (payload shape + X-Cube-Signature-256 HMAC-SHA256 signing) is identical to CubeAPI's webhook emitter, so a receiver built for one works for the other unchanged. Closes https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/642. What's included Core delivery (internal/webhook/) - New webhook package: an independent consumer of the lifecycle Redis stream using its own consumer group (cube-webhook-delivery), separate from the main reconciliation group — so delivery is async and never blocks sandbox create/destroy. - Durable (at-least-once): events are acknowledged only after delivery; a CLM crash cannot lose them. Receivers deduplicate on the stable event_id (= the Redis stream entry ID). - HMAC-SHA256 signing: X-Cube-Signature-256: sha256= over the raw request body. - Bounded retry: plain for-loop exponential backoff (default 3 attempts, then ack+drop). - Crash recovery: startup ReadPending (reclaims the whole group pending list) + a periodic XAUTOCLAIM safety net for entries stuck in pending (dead peer replica, failed ack). - Context enrichment: a meta cache so sandbox.deleted/state events carry template_id even though their stream entries have no payload. Config (internal/config, env vars) - CUBE_LCM_WEBHOOK_URLS (comma-separated targets, empty = disabled) - CUBE_LCM_WEBHOOK_EVENTS (filter, * = all) - CUBE_LCM_WEBHOOK_SECRET (optional signing secret) - CUBE_LCM_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT / CUBE_LCM_WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES (tuning) Runtime management (internal/httpapi) - Authenticated REST API: GET/POST /admin/webhooks, PUT/DELETE /admin/webhooks/{id}, GET /admin/webhooks/stats — gated by X-Cube-Admin-Token. Example & docs - examples/webhook-receiver/ — runnable zero-dependency receiver (Python 3.10+, stdlib only) with optional signature verification. - docs/guide/integrations/webhook.md + docs/zh/guide/integrations/webhook.md — configuration, payload schema, signature verification (Python/Go/curl), delivery semantics, and WeCom-bot / generic HTTP alerting references. Architecture ``` CubeMaster ──XADD──► lifecycle events stream (Redis, durable) │ ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐ │ group: cube-proxy-sidecar │ group: cube-webhook-delivery │ (main reconciliation, │ (webhook delivery, NEW) │ unchanged) │ │ │ read → build event → deliver │ │ (HMAC + retry) → ack only after delivery ``` Because each consumer group receives the full stream independently, webhook delivery is durable, non-blocking, and never interferes with the main reconciliation loop. Verification 1. cd cube-lifecycle-manager && go test ./... — all green (incl. -race on webhook/redisstream). 2. Cross-compile for the target: CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o bin/cube-lifecycle-manager ./cmd/cube-lifecycle-manager 3. Run CLM with CUBE_LCM_WEBHOOK_URLS + CUBE_LCM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, run the example receiver, then trigger a sandbox create/pause/resume/delete and confirm events arrive with a valid signature. Screenshots 1. Example webhook receiver printing delivered events 2. CLM startup logs showing webhook delivery enabled 3. REST admin API (add/list endpoints) 4. CURL signature-verification test --- Files changed: 24 files, +3382 / -8. Highlights: - cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/webhook/ (new package: manager, client, event, config, iface + tests) - cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/redisstream/stream.go (ReadPending, ReclaimStale) - cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/httpapi/server.go (/admin/webhooks + auth) - cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/config/config.go (webhook env vars) - examples/webhook-receiver/, docs/guide/integrations/webhook.md + zh

title: [Bug Report] CubeMaster silently downgrades shipped log level "info" to DEBUG
body:
## Summary

CubeMaster's shipped configuration files all use lowercase `level: "info"`, but `CubeLog.StringToLevel` matches only uppercase names and falls back to `DEBUG` for anything else. Every default deployment therefore runs at DEBUG instead of INFO, which writes request signature material to disk, enables caller reporting, and inflates request-log volume.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `9270cabfc048f25b8ce411895b2dc5443956a6b0`
- Host OS and kernel version: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS, Linux `6.6.69-opencloudos9.cubesandbox.pvm.host-gb85200d80fa2`
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): `/lib/modules/6.6.69-opencloudos9.cubesandbox.pvm.host-gb85200d80fa2/kernel/arch/x86/kvm/kvm.ko`, `intree: Y`, vermagic matches the running kernel
- Deployment mode: affects **all shipped modes** — single-node, Kubernetes chart, and Terraform
- Relevant component: CubeMaster (parsing defect in `pkgs/CubeLog`)
- Build/test environment: builder image `cube-sandbox-cubemaster-builder:ubuntu2004`, Go `1.25.7`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out `9270cabf` and use any shipped CubeMaster configuration unchanged, e.g. `configs/single-node/cubemaster.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   log:
     module: "cubemaster"
     path: "/data/log/CubeMaster"
     file_size: 100
     file_num: 10
     level: "info"
   ```

2. Start CubeMaster so that `log.Init()` runs.
3. Observe that `log.IsDebug()` is true and that DEBUG-only request logging is emitted.

The parse chain can be verified in isolation with the probe under **Test Report** below.

## Expected Behavior

The shipped lowercase value `info` should resolve to the `INFO` level.

Log levels should be accepted case-insensitively, or unsupported values should be rejected with a clear configuration error. They should not silently fall back to `DEBUG`.

## Actual Behavior

The YAML decoder preserves the value verbatim — `Conf.UnmarshalYAML` in `CubeMaster/pkg/base/log/types.go` only reconciles snake_case/camelCase *key* spellings and never normalizes the value. It is then passed straight through:

- `CubeMaster/pkg/base/log/log.go:23` — `CubeLog.SetLevel(CubeLog.StringToLevel(conf.Level))` at startup
- `CubeMaster/pkg/base/log/log.go:64` — the same conversion during configuration hot reload

`CubeLog.StringToLevel` (`pkgs/CubeLog/logger.go:146-159`) matches only uppercase:

```go
switch level {
case "DEBUG":
    return DEBUG
case "INFO":
    return INFO
case "WARN":
    return WARN
case "ERROR":
    return ERROR
case "FATAL":
    return FATAL
default:
    return DEBUG
}
```

so `StringToLevel("info") == DEBUG`.

This has three consequences.

**1. Request signature material is written to disk.** `CubeMaster/pkg/service/httpservice/middleware/middleware.go:86` serializes the full `auth.SignatureParams` struct, which includes the signature and nonce:

```go
if log.IsDebug() {
    log.G(ctx).Debugf("http_request_comming: %v", utils.InterfaceToString(sgnp))
}
```

`auth.SignatureParams` (`CubeMaster/pkg/base/auth/auth.go:21-29`) carries `cube_nonce` and `cube_signature`.

Separately, `CubeMaster/pkg/service/httpservice/middleware/gin_middleware.go:55` dumps the request once DEBUG is on:

```go
var dump []byte
if log.IsDebug() {
    dump, _ = httputil.DumpRequest(c.Request, config.GetConfig().Common.DebugDumpHttpBody)
}
```

logged at `gin_middleware.go:82` as `http_request_coming`. Since `debug_dump_http_body` (`CubeMaster/pkg/base/config/config.go:64`) is not set in any shipped config, it defaults to `false`, so the body is not dumped — but all request headers are, and the auth parameters are read from headers.

**2. Caller reporting is enabled.** `CubeMaster/pkg/base/log/log.go:26-28` gates on the resulting level:

```go
if IsDebug() {
    CubeLog.SetReportCaller(true)
}
```

adding a `runtime.Caller` stack walk per log line.

**3. Request log volume grows well beyond what INFO would produce**, since both middleware paths log per request.

## Test Report

Probe added temporarily at `CubeMaster/pkg/base/log/zz_probe_test.go` (removed after the run), reading each shipped config and reporting the resolved level:

```go
package log

import (
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"testing"

	"github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/pkgs/CubeLog"
	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

type probeRoot struct {
	Log Conf `yaml:"log"`
}

var levelName = map[CubeLog.LogLevel]string{
	CubeLog.DEBUG: "DEBUG", CubeLog.INFO: "INFO", CubeLog.WARN: "WARN",
	CubeLog.ERROR: "ERROR", CubeLog.FATAL: "FATAL",
}

func report(t *testing.T, file, raw string) {
	t.Helper()
	lvl := CubeLog.StringToLevel(raw)
	CubeLog.SetLevel(lvl)
	t.Logf("%-56s level=%-8q -> %-5s  IsDebug()=%v", file, raw, levelName[lvl], IsDebug())
}

func TestProbeShippedLevels(t *testing.T) {
	for _, f := range []string{
		"../../../conf.yaml",
		"../../../../configs/single-node/cubemaster.yaml",
	} {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(f)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", f, err)
		}
		var root probeRoot
		if err := yaml.Unmarshal(b, &root); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("parse %s: %v", f, err)
		}
		report(t, f, root.Log.Level)
	}

	// Helm template and HCL are not plain YAML; extract the literal.
	re := regexp.MustCompile(`level\s*[:=]\s*"([^"]+)"`)
	for _, f := range []string{
		"../../../../deploy/kubernetes/chart/files/cube-master/conf.yaml",
		"../../../../deploy/one-click/terraform/tencentcloud/tke-addons.tf",
	} {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(f)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", f, err)
		}
		m := re.FindSubmatch(b)
		if m == nil {
			t.Fatalf("no level literal in %s", f)
		}
		report(t, f, string(m[1]))
	}
}

func TestProbeCaseVariants(t *testing.T) {
	for _, in := range []string{"info", "Info", "INFO", " INFO ", "warn", "typo"} {
		t.Logf("StringToLevel(%-8q) = %s", in, levelName[CubeLog.StringToLevel(in)])
	}
}
```

Output:

```text
=== RUN   TestProbeShippedLevels
    ../../../conf.yaml                                       level="info"   -> DEBUG  IsDebug()=true
    ../../../../configs/single-node/cubemaster.yaml          level="info"   -> DEBUG  IsDebug()=true
    ../../../../deploy/kubernetes/chart/files/cube-master/conf.yaml level="info" -> DEBUG  IsDebug()=true
    ../../../../deploy/one-click/terraform/tencentcloud/tke-addons.tf level="info" -> DEBUG  IsDebug()=true
--- PASS: TestProbeShippedLevels (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestProbeCaseVariants
    StringToLevel("info"  ) = DEBUG
    StringToLevel("Info"  ) = DEBUG
    StringToLevel("INFO"  ) = INFO
    StringToLevel(" INFO ") = DEBUG
    StringToLevel("warn"  ) = DEBUG
    StringToLevel("typo"  ) = DEBUG
--- PASS: TestProbeCaseVariants (0.00s)
PASS
```

The existing `pkgs/CubeLog` suite passes unchanged:

```text
go test ./... -count=1
ok  	github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/pkgs/CubeLog	0.014s
```

It passes because `TestSetLevelGetLevelAndStringToLevel` (`pkgs/CubeLog/contract_test.go:55-75`) asserts only the five uppercase spellings plus `"unknown"` — the lowercase case that every shipped config actually uses is not covered, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Additional Context

All four shipped configurations use the lowercase spelling at `9270cabf`:

- `CubeMaster/conf.yaml:21`
- `configs/single-node/cubemaster.yaml:23`
- `deploy/kubernetes/chart/files/cube-master/conf.yaml:20`
- `deploy/one-click/terraform/tencentcloud/tke-addons.tf:283` (`level = "info"`)

**Interaction with #1470.** Editing a running deployment's config from `info` to `INFO` does not take effect, because the hot-reload guard at `CubeMaster/pkg/base/hotswap/file.go:94` compares case-insensitively:

```go
if len(o.backupOldCfg) == len(new) && bytes.EqualFold(o.backupOldCfg, new) {
```

`bytes.EqualFold` treats `info` and `INFO` as equal, so the reload is skipped. Working around this bug therefore requires a process restart, not a config reload. Tracked separately as #1470.

**Relationship to #1289.** #1289 covered a separate `file_size` / `file_num` key mismatch affecting log rotation and is closed. This report is limited to log-level parsing; the two together could compound into unbounded log growth on older releases.

## Suggested Fix

Normalize before matching in `StringToLevel`:

```go
switch strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(level)) {
```

and extend `TestSetLevelGetLevelAndStringToLevel` to cover `info`, `Info`, `INFO`, `" INFO "`, and an invalid value.

**Open question, worth deciding separately:** the `default: return DEBUG` fallback means any typo in the level name silently enables the most verbose setting, including credential-bearing request logs. A safer default would be `INFO`, or an explicit startup error on an unrecognized value. That is a behavior change and probably belongs in its own PR rather than being folded into the case-insensitivity fix.

title: cubelet: cbri image_base_path does not drive pmem artifact paths (ext4 download & sandbox PmemFile stay on hardcoded cubetool_base_dir)
body:
## Summary

Configuring the cbri plugin section in `Cubelet/config/config.toml`:

```toml
[plugins."io.cubelet.cbri.v1.cubebox"]
  image_base_path    = "/data/cubebox_os_image"
  kernel_base_path   = "/data/cubebox_os_image"
  snapshot_base_path = "/data/cube-snapshot"
```

only redirects paths resolved by the **cubeboxcbri plugin itself**. The pmem path family (`pmem.GetRawImageFilePath` / `pmem.GetPmemBasePath`) is driven by a **separate** config item `cubetool_base_dir` (hardcoded default `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox`), so:

- ext4 artifact **downloads** still land on the system disk
- the **sandbox PmemFile** (the path mounted into the build/runtime container, visible as overlay2 lowerdir) still resolves to the old absolute path

The cbri section is therefore only partially effective — one concept, two independent configs.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox 0.7.0, single-node (non-K8s, systemd one-click deployment)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Append the cbri section above to `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/Cubelet/config/config.toml`
2. `systemctl restart cube-sandbox-cubelet.service`
3. Build a template from image (`POST /templates`), then create a sandbox from it
4. Observe:

| What | Where it lands | Driven by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| kernel `.vm` sync, snapshot writes | `/data/...` ✅ | cbri `image_base_path`/`snapshot_base_path` |
| ext4 artifact download | `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/cubebox_os_image/<artifactID>/` ❌ | pmem (cubetool_base_dir) |
| sandbox pmem backing file | same hardcoded old path ❌ | pmem (cubetool_base_dir) |

Verify on node:

```bash
find /usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/cubebox_os_image/ -name '*.ext4'   # present = bug
find /data/cubebox_os_image/ -name '*.ext4'                            # empty
journalctl -u cube-sandbox-cubelet.service | grep -iE 'pmem|cubebox_os_image'
```

## Root cause

Two independent path systems that never consult each other:

| | cbri plugin (configurable) | images service / pmem (hardcoded default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config | `[plugins."io.cubelet.cbri.v1.cubebox"]` | `[plugins."io.cubelet.internal.v1.images"]` `cubetool_base_dir` |
| Default | `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox` (BasePath) | `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox` |
| Code | `Cubelet/plugins/cbri/cubeboxcbri/cubebox.go:54-71` | `Cubelet/services/images/local.go:79-81,125` → `pmem.Init()` |

pmem consumers (all bypass the cbri config):

- `Cubelet/pkg/container/pmem/pmem.go:35-37` — `GetPmemBasePath` = `<cubetool_base_dir>/<instanceType>_os_image`
- `Cubelet/internal/cube/server/images/ext4image/utils.go:46` — ext4 existence check + download target
- `Cubelet/internal/cube/server/images/ext4image/destroy.go:65` — artifact destroy
- `Cubelet/services/cubebox/cube_container_create.go:598` — `mountsConfig.PmemFile` at sandbox creation

## Why the symlink workaround breaks upgrades

Since PR #538 (2026-06-18, `--mode upgrade`), the one-click installer wipes the install root and refuses to proceed when it contains a top-level symlink:

```
ERROR: refusing to wipe install root: contains top-level symlink (/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/cubebox_os_image); move it away and retry
```

(`_assert_no_top_level_symlinks`, `deploy/one-click/lib/common.sh:904-912` — a deliberate safety guard with test coverage, not a runtime restriction.)

So today operators must use `mount --bind` instead, and remember to `umount` before every upgrade (rm -rf on a mountpoint fails) — fragile.

## Proposed fix

Make the cbri section the single source of truth: register `image_base_path` into the pmem package at plugin init, and let `GetPmemBasePath` prefer the registered value.

```go
// Cubelet/pkg/container/pmem/pmem.go
var instanceBasePaths sync.Map // instanceType -> full os_image dir

func SetInstanceBasePath(instanceType, basePath string) {
    if instanceType == "" || basePath == "" { return }
    instanceBasePaths.Store(instanceType, basePath)
}

func GetPmemBasePath(instanceType string) string {
    if v, ok := instanceBasePaths.Load(instanceType); ok { return v.(string) }
    return filepath.Join(baseDirPath, instanceType+"_os_image")
}

// Cubelet/plugins/cbri/cubeboxcbri/cubebox.go — InitFn
pmem.SetInstanceBasePath(config.instanceType, config.ImageBasePath)
```

- Lookup happens at call time, so plugin init order does not matter
- All pmem consumers (download/destroy/PmemFile) follow the cbri config automatically
- Shared kernel (`GetSharedKernelFilePath`) stays on `cubetool_base_dir`, staged assets unaffected
- Fully backward compatible when unconfigured

## Workaround until fixed

```bash
mount --bind /data/cubebox_os_image /usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/cubebox_os_image
mount --bind /data/cube-snapshot    /usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/cube-snapshot
# persist via /etc/fstab; umount before each one-click upgrade, re-mount after
```

title: [Bug Report] v0.7.0 legacy recovery leaves port mappings on an old TAP ifindex

labels.name: area/CubeNet
labels.description: Impacts the CubeNet module and network-agent

body:
## Summary

After upgrading from v0.6.0 to v0.7.0, Cubelet legacy network recovery can leave CubeVS port mappings pinned to an old TAP ifindex. If the live TAP has the same name and IP but a new ifindex, subsequent sandbox creation fails with a host-port conflict against the stale old ifindex.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: v0.7.0
- Previous version: v0.6.0
- Host OS and kernel version: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, `6.6.69-cube.pvm.host.005.x-gb85200d80fa2`
- KVM info: functional PVM/KVM deployment; exact module version is not exported by `modinfo -F version kvm`
- Deployment mode: one-click, single-node
- Relevant component: Cubelet embedded network runtime / CubeNet CubeVS

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On v0.6.0, retain a legacy network-agent state record containing a TAP identity, an old `TapIfIndex`, and a port mapping.
2. Keep the pinned CubeVS port-map entry in bpffs, then recreate or restore the TAP with the same name and sandbox IP but a different live ifindex.
3. Upgrade to v0.7.0 and start Cubelet so `startup_recover.go` migrates the legacy record.
4. Create a sandbox that receives the same host port.

The relevant recovery path appears to be:

- `restoreLegacyActiveTap` clones the legacy record and immediately replaces `state.TapIfIndex` with the current live TAP index.
- `reconcilePortMappingsForTap` calls `DeletePortMappingsByIfindex` only for the current index.
- The pinned remote mapping still belongs to the old index, so it is not deleted.
- `AddPortMapping` then rejects the same host port because it is still owned by the old index.

Source locations:

- https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/v0.7.0/Cubelet/network/runtime/startup_recover.go#L509-L567
- https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/v0.7.0/Cubelet/network/runtime/tap_lifecycle.go#L281-L301
- https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/v0.7.0/CubeNet/cubevs/port.go#L17-L75

The current migration test uses the same ifindex for the persisted state and recovered TAP, so the reindexed-TAP case is not covered:

- https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/v0.7.0/Cubelet/network/runtime/startup_recover_test.go#L497-L565

## Expected Behavior

Legacy recovery should safely remove stale port mappings owned by the old TAP lifecycle before installing mappings for the current TAP ifindex. It must preserve mappings owned by an unrelated live TAP if the numeric ifindex has been reused.

## Actual Behavior

Sandbox creation repeatedly failed with errors equivalent to:

```text
network runtime EnsureNetwork failed: host port 20063 already maps to ifindex/listen_port 290/8080, cannot map to 6624/8080
```

At incident time:

- CubeAPI reported zero sandboxes.
- Cubelet reported no active Cubeboxes.
- `remote_port_mapping` and `local_port_mapping` each contained 6000 entries.
- None of the mapping ifindexes existed in the current host network-device inventory.
- Startup logs contained 6000 `network runtime replace cubevs tap` events from legacy recovery.

A controlled host reboot cleared the pinned maps. A full create, HTTP health check, delete, and asynchronous cleanup test then passed, and all four relevant CubeVS maps returned to zero entries. This isolates the failure to orphaned pinned network state rather than scheduler capacity, disk, template, or CubeAPI health.

## Suggested Fix

- Preserve both the persisted old ifindex and current live ifindex during legacy migration.
- Reconcile stale mappings for the old lifecycle only after proving that the old ifindex/tuple is absent or unowned; fail closed if ownership is ambiguous.
- Reconcile the current ifindex before adding desired mappings.
- Add a startup GC for port-map entries whose ifindex has no live TAP and no durable owner.
- Add regression tests where persisted `TapIfIndex != liveTap.Index`, including a case where the old numeric ifindex has been reused by an unrelated live device.

## Additional Context

Related design work already identifies stale port mapping residue as a recovery concern:

- https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/953
- https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1285

No exact public issue for this old-ifindex/new-ifindex migration case was found before filing.

title: [Bug Report] build: Dockerfile.builder fails on Ubuntu 20.04 due to upstream llvm.sh check failure

labels.name: area/CI
labels.description: Continuous Integration testing issue or flake

body:
## Summary

When CI runs on pull requests where published GHCR builder images (`ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-builder:ubuntu2004`) cannot be pulled anonymously or when building `docker/Dockerfile.builder` locally, the build fails during LLVM 14 installation:

```
+ wget -O /tmp/llvm.sh https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh
+ bash /tmp/llvm.sh 14
[error] Distribution 'ubuntu' in version '20.04' is not supported by this script.
```

This causes `docker build` to fail in the `Resolve builder image` step of `.github/workflows/unit-test-check.yml`, failing subsequent unit test jobs.

## Root Cause Analysis

In `docker/Dockerfile.builder`:

```dockerfile
# Line 189-192
wget -O /tmp/llvm.sh "${script_url}"; bash /tmp/llvm.sh "$@"; rm -f /tmp/llvm.sh;
```

The upstream `https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh` script recently added a URL pre-check (`check_url "${BASE_URL}/${CODENAME}/"`). Since `https://apt.llvm.org/focal/` returns 404 on HEAD requests, `llvm.sh` errors out with `Distribution 'ubuntu' in version '20.04' is not supported by this script`, even though the focal apt repository `http://apt.llvm.org/focal/ llvm-toolchain-focal-14 main` remains fully functional.

## Proposed Fix

1. In `docker/Dockerfile.builder`, replace the remote `llvm.sh` execution with direct configuration of the `llvm-toolchain-focal-14` APT source into `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm-14.list`.
2. Support `LLVM_MIRROR_BASE` if provided.
3. Install `clang-14`, `llvm-14`, and toolchain packages directly with `apt-get install`.

## Claim Statement

I have verified the root cause and have a tested Dockerfile fix prepared. Please assign this to me, I will submit a PR shortly.

title: fix(grpcconn): match full and prefixed keys in CloseWorkerConn
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1584

In `CubeMaster/pkg/cubelet/grpcconn/worker_conn.go`, `GetWorkerConn` stores connection pools under `ua + "+" + addr`. However, `CloseWorkerConn(addr)` previously performed a direct lookup with the bare `addr` string (`connPool.cache.Load(addr)`).

Because the keys did not match, `CloseWorkerConn` was a silent no-op. Calls from `node_cache` (`node_cache.go:220/240`) upon node down / deletion failed to immediately close active gRPC connections for the removed node.

## Changes

1. Updated `CloseWorkerConn(addr string)` to scan `connPool.cache` using `Range` and match entries where `key == addr` or `strings.HasSuffix(key, "+"+addr)`.
2. Delete matched keys from `connPool.cache` and close the corresponding connection pools (`Pool.Close()`).
3. Added `if connPool == nil { return }` nil guard.
4. Added comprehensive unit tests in `CubeMaster/pkg/cubelet/grpcconn/worker_conn_test.go` covering matching, nil-pool handling, and uninitialized pool errors (100% target function test coverage).

## Verification

- `go test -v -cover ./pkg/cubelet/grpcconn/...` passes cleanly.
- `gofmt -w` verified.

title: [Bug Report] cubelet/grpcconn: CloseWorkerConn fails to match cached pool due to key prefix mismatch
body:
## Summary

In `CubeMaster/pkg/cubelet/grpcconn/worker_conn.go`, `GetWorkerConn` stores connection pools in `connPool.cache` (`sync.Map`) with a prefixed key composed of the caller's User-Agent and the worker address (`ua + "+" + addr`). However, `CloseWorkerConn(addr)` performs a lookup using the bare `addr` string without the `ua + "+"` prefix.

Because the lookup key never matches any cached pool, `CloseWorkerConn` is completely ineffective (a silent no-op). When nodes are deleted or marked down (e.g. in `CubeMaster/pkg/localcache/node_cache.go:220/240`), the active gRPC connections associated with the removed node are never closed immediately and linger until the background expiry cleanup sweep (`checkWorkerConn`).

## Root Cause Analysis

In `CubeMaster/pkg/cubelet/grpcconn/worker_conn.go`:

```go
func GetWorkerConn(ctx context.Context, addr string) (grpcpool.Conn, error) {
	key := constants.GetUA(ctx) + "+" + addr
	cp, ok := connPool.cache.Load(key)
    ...
	cp, ok = connPool.cache.LoadOrStore(key, newPool)
    ...
}

func CloseWorkerConn(addr string) {
	cp, ok := connPool.cache.Load(addr) // ❌ Never matches "ua+addr" key
	if ok && cp != nil {
		connPool.cache.Delete(addr)
		_ = cp.(grpcpool.Pool).Close()
	}
}
```

When `CloseWorkerConn` is invoked by `node_cache` upon node teardown:
1. `connPool.cache.Load(addr)` always returns `ok == false` because all entries are keyed with `ua + "+" + addr`.
2. The stale pool remains in `connPool.cache`, maintaining open connections to deleted nodes.

## Proposed Fix

1. In `CloseWorkerConn(addr string)`, scan `connPool.cache` using `Range` and match entries where the key equals `addr` or has suffix `"+" + addr`.
2. Delete matched keys from `connPool.cache` and close the corresponding connection pools.
3. Add `if connPool == nil { return }` nil-guard.
4. Add comprehensive unit tests in `CubeMaster/pkg/cubelet/grpcconn/worker_conn_test.go` covering `GetWorkerConn`, `CloseWorkerConn` matching, and nil-pool handling.

## Claim Statement

I have verified this issue and prepared the fix along with unit tests. Please assign this to me, I will submit a PR shortly.

title: fix(hotswap): use bytes.Equal and handle yaml.Marshal error in reload
body:
Fixes #1470

## Summary
FileOperator.reload compared marshalled config with bytes.EqualFold, so any edit that only changes ASCII letter case was treated as "no change" and never applied. The yaml.Marshal error on the same line was also unchecked (staticcheck SA4006).

Repro:
- log level INFO -> info => reload() returns false (silently ignored)
- host Foo.internal -> foo.internal => same
- genuine content change => true (control)
- length differs => true (control)

Root cause: CubeMaster/pkg/base/hotswap/file.go:94 and identical Cubelet/pkg/hotswap/file.go:94

```
new, err := yaml.Marshal(config)
if len(o.backupOldCfg) == len(new) && bytes.EqualFold(o.backupOldCfg, new) { return false }
```

EqualFold is Unicode case-folding, not byte identity. Error from Marshal never checked -- on failure new is nil, so backupOldCfg is wiped to nil and notify still fires.

## Fix
- Check yaml.Marshal error, log via o.Errorf and return false
- Use bytes.Equal for exact comparison (handles length internally)
- Apply to both copies (CubeMaster and Cubelet -- they are vendored copies)

Mirrors Init() at 71-74 which already checks the marshal error.

## How tested
- git diff shows 10 insertions, 2 deletions across 2 files.
- Manual inspection: bytes.Equal is exact, case-sensitive; error path logs and aborts.
- No other files use EqualFold for config comparison (grep -r EqualFold confirms only these two).

title: fix(images): gate cubelog probe behind consumer images
body:
## What this PR does

`ensure_source_tree()` in `deploy/kubernetes/images/build-cube-images.sh` always probed the cubelog module via `cubelog_module_at_ref` when `SOURCE_REF` is set. That probe fails when `SOURCE_REF` predates both `pkgs/CubeLog` and the legacy `cubelog` module (for example when building from an older release tag).

Only `cube-master`, `cubemastercli`, `cubelet` and `cube-ops` actually consume cubelog. This change gates the probe behind those images, mirroring how the CubeOps export is already gated, so older release tags can still build `cube-api`, `cube-proxy`, `cube-webui`, `cube-egress` and `cube-lifecycle-manager`.

## Why it matters

Follows up on the cubelog relocation (#1574) and unblocks building older release tags for images that never exported cubelog.

## Testing notes

- Building only `cube-api` from a `SOURCE_REF` that predates `pkgs/CubeLog` no longer runs the cubelog probe and should succeed.
- Building `cube-master` from the same `SOURCE_REF` still fails with the existing clear error message, since cubelog is a hard requirement there.

title: docs(integrations): add LangGraph integration guide
body:
## Summary

Adds a LangGraph integration guide (English and Chinese) and two runnable examples under `examples/langgraph-integration/` that demonstrate running an explicit LangGraph `StateGraph` agent — a `coder → reviewer` graph with a conditional retry edge — whose code-execution node invokes Python inside a Cube Sandbox MicroVM through the official `cubesandbox` SDK. A single MicroVM is shared across every node via a `run_python` closure, and LangGraph checkpointing is wired to Cube's `pause()` / `connect()` lifecycle so a run can be snapshotted and resumed on the same MicroVM.

本 PR 新增 LangGraph 集成指南（中英双语）与 `examples/langgraph-integration/` 下两个可运行示例，演示运行一个显式的 LangGraph `StateGraph` agent——`coder → reviewer` 图带条件重试边，其代码执行节点通过官方 `cubesandbox` SDK 在 Cube Sandbox MicroVM 内执行 Python。单个 MicroVM 通过 `run_python` 闭包在全部图节点间共享，LangGraph 的 checkpoint 机制与 Cube 的 `pause()` / `connect()` 生命周期对接，使一次运行可被快照并在同一 MicroVM 上恢复。

## Why

The existing LangChain guide only covers the high-level `create_agent` helper, which hides the graph topology and retry policy behind a black box. Real agents need explicit control over the node structure, the review loop, and where code actually executes — the three things `create_agent` abstracts away.

现有 LangChain 指南只覆盖高层 `create_agent` 封装，把图拓扑与重试策略隐藏在黑盒之后。而真实的 agent 需要对节点结构、审查循环以及代码实际执行的位置拥有显式控制——这正是 `create_agent` 抽象掉的三件事。

This PR fills that gap with an explicit-graph counterpart:

- **Explicit node and edge control** — a `coder → reviewer` graph with a conditional retry edge (`route_after_review`), so the attempt cap and retry predicate can be tuned directly.
- **Code execution isolated in a MicroVM** — each code-execution node runs Python in a Cube Sandbox MicroVM via the `cubesandbox` SDK, giving the agent a disposable, reproducible runtime instead of the host process.
- **Checkpointing mapped to the sandbox lifecycle** — the LangGraph checkpointer is keyed by `sandbox_id` and mapped to Cube's `pause()` / `connect()`, so a graph run survives a MicroVM snapshot and resumes with its `/workspace` filesystem intact — a scenario the existing guide does not cover.

本 PR 以显式图版本填补这一空白：

- **显式节点与边控制**——`coder → reviewer` 图带条件重试边（`route_after_review`），尝试次数上限与重试判定可直接调优。
- **代码执行隔离在 MicroVM 内**——每个代码执行节点通过 `cubesandbox` SDK 在 Cube Sandbox MicroVM 内运行 Python，为 agent 提供一次性、可复现的运行环境，而非宿主机进程。
- **Checkpoint 与沙箱生命周期对接**——LangGraph 的 checkpointer 以 `sandbox_id` 为键并映射到 Cube 的 `pause()` / `connect()`，使一次图运行能在 MicroVM 快照后存活，并以完整的 `/workspace` 文件系统恢复——这是现有指南未覆盖的场景。

## What changed

**Docs**
- `docs/guide/integrations/langgraph.md` — 英文指南（new）
- `docs/zh/guide/integrations/langgraph.md` — 中文指南（new）
- `docs/guide/integrations/index.md` / `docs/zh/guide/integrations/index.md` — 注册文章
- `docs/.vitepress/config.mjs` — 注册导航

**Runnable examples**（`examples/langgraph-integration/`，new）
- `langgraph_agent_demo.py` — 单 MicroVM 的 generate → execute → review → retry 循环
- `langgraph_checkpoint_demo.py` — 通过 checkpointer 跨 `pause()` / `connect()` 恢复
- `Dockerfile` — 含 pandas/numpy/matplotlib/scikit-learn 的模板镜像
- `requirements.txt` — `langgraph>=1,<2`、`langchain-openai>=1.0`、`cubesandbox>=0.6.0`
- `.env.example` / `.gitignore` / `README.md` / `README_zh.md` / `sales.csv`

## Two demos at a glance

| Demo | Purpose / 作用 |
|---|---|

title: fix(sdk): honour e2b files.read formats across Node/Python/Go
body:
## Summary

`files.read` in the CubeSandbox SDKs always treated the response as text, so the e2b-compatible binary formats were missing or ignored. Binary payloads (e.g. PNG `0x89`) were corrupted on the Node/Python UTF-8 text paths.

This PR aligns all three official SDKs with the e2b surface:

| SDK | Surface |
| --- | --- |
| **Node** | `format: 'text' \| 'bytes' \| 'blob' \| 'stream'` |
| **Python** | `format="text" \| "bytes" \| "stream"` → `str` / `bytearray` / `Iterator[bytes]` |
| **Go** | `Read` (text) + `ReadBytes` + `ReadStream` (e2b has no Go SDK; these are the idiomatic equivalents) |

Also mirrors e2b's empty `content-length: 0` short-circuit where applicable.

Fixes #1570

## Test plan

- [x] `cd sdk/node && npm test -- --run` (221 passed)
- [x] `cd sdk/go && go test ./...`
- [x] `cd sdk/python && pytest tests/test_sandbox.py -k read_` (7 passed, via container)
- [ ] Reviewer: optional live check — write a PNG into a sandbox and read it back with the binary API unaltered

title: Node SDK files.read ignores format and always UTF-8-decodes (breaks e2b-compatible bytes/blob/stream)
body:
## Summary

The Node SDK's `Filesystem.read` always calls `resp.text()` and returns a `string`. Callers that pass the e2b-compatible `format: 'bytes' | 'blob' | 'stream'` option are silently ignored, so binary files are corrupted before the application sees them.

This breaks drop-in / e2b-surface compatibility for any consumer that already writes:

```ts
const bytes = await sandbox.files.read(path, { format: 'bytes' })
```

## Measured

Against a live sandbox, a 4-byte PNG magic (`89 50 4E 47`) read through the current Node SDK arrives as a UTF-8 string whose bytes are `EF BF BD 50 4E 47` (the leading `0x89` became the U+FFFD replacement character). Length grows; the file is no longer a PNG.

The official e2b Node SDK returns an unaltered `Uint8Array` for the same call.

## Expected (e2b surface)

| `options.format` | Return type |
| --- | --- |
| omitted / `text` (default) | `string` |
| `bytes` | `Uint8Array` |
| `blob` | `Blob` |
| `stream` | `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` |

## Environment

- CubeSandbox ≥ 0.7.0
- `@cubesandbox/sdk` Node package from `sdk/node` (still unpublished to npm; consumed as a build artifact)

## Why this matters

Deployments that speak CubeSandbox through the e2b-shaped client (and HamsterHQ in particular) serve panel image/binary downloads through `files.read({ format: 'bytes' })`. The docker/e2b simulation path works; the Cube path does not, for the same source line.

## Proposed fix

Honour `format` in `sdk/node/src/filesystem.ts` the same way e2b does (including the empty `content-length: 0` short-circuit). Unit tests covering `text` / `bytes` / `blob` / `stream` will land with the PR.

Happy to send the PR.

title: [Bug Report] One-click / cubetoolbox upgrade silently drops third-party VolumePlugins (binary + volume_plugins registration)
body:
## Summary

**中文摘要：** 一键安装树（`/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/.../plugin/`）以及同树下的 `conf.yaml` / `config.toml` 在平台升级时会被覆盖或重置。官方示例与文档把第三方 VolumePlugin 引导安装到该目录，导致升级后第三方 driver 静默消失，所有依赖该 volume 的 sandbox 创建失败（例如 `unknown driver: juicefs`），租户持久卷不可用。协议本身允许 `binary_path` 指向任意绝对路径，但文档未警示「装进 toolbox 会被升级清掉」，也未给出升级安全的安装布局与配置保留策略。

Upgrading CubeSandbox (one-click / cubetoolbox package replace) can **silently remove third-party VolumePlugins** that were installed under the documented `CubeMaster/plugin/` and `Cubelet/plugin/` paths, and can also **reset `volume_plugins` registration** in `conf.yaml` / `config.toml` that live in the same tree.

After upgrade, create/attach with a custom `driver` fails with errors such as `unknown driver: <name>` / `no plugin registered for driver "<name>"`, while tenant data on the backend (object store + metadata DB) may still be intact. This is an **upgrade footgun**, not a plugin protocol bug: the framework already allows arbitrary `binary_path`, but docs and examples steer operators into a path that the installer owns and replaces.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: observed when upgrading to **v0.7.0-amd64** (from a prior 0.6.x one-click install)
- Host OS: Linux (amd64), bare-metal / VM with one-click `cubetoolbox` layout
- Deployment mode: single-node (CubeMaster + Cubelet under `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/`)
- Relevant component: CubeMaster, Cubelet, Volume Plugin registration / packaging
- Custom driver: third-party JuiceFS VolumePlugin (binary type), previously registered and working

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install CubeSandbox via the one-click / cubetoolbox layout.
2. Follow the same install pattern as the official COS/S3 examples: place a **third-party** VolumePlugin binary (and its credential/config file) under:
   - `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/CubeMaster/plugin/<driver>`
   - `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/Cubelet/plugin/<driver>`
3. Register it in CubeMaster `conf.yaml` and Cubelet `config.toml` `volume_plugins` with matching `name` / `binary_path` (as in [docs/guide/volume-plugin.md](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/master/docs/guide/volume-plugin.md#registration-and-configuration) and [examples/volume/cos](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/volume/cos) / [examples/volume/s3](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/volume/s3)).
4. Confirm volumes create/attach with that `driver` succeed.
5. Upgrade the platform by replacing / reinstalling the cubetoolbox package (e.g. to `v0.7.0-amd64`).
6. Attempt to create a sandbox (or volume) that still uses the custom `driver`.

## Expected Behavior

Either:

1. **Upgrade preserves** third-party plugin binaries, credential files, and `volume_plugins` entries that are not part of the shipped tree; **or**
2. Documentation and install guides **explicitly warn** that `.../cubetoolbox/*/plugin/` is owned by the installer and will be reset, and recommend an **upgrade-safe layout** (absolute `binary_path` outside cubetoolbox + how to re-apply / merge `volume_plugins` after upgrade); **or**
3. Packaging provides a supported **drop-in / overlay** location for third-party plugins and config fragments that upgrades do not wipe (similar to distro `conf.d` patterns).

The existing rolling-upgrade notes in the Volume Plugin guide cover Master/Cubelet version skew for Volume features, but not this packaging hazard:

> Volume requires both CubeMaster and Cubelet to be on a release that supports the Volume Plugin. During a rolling upgrade: …

## Actual Behavior

After the upgrade:

1. `CubeMaster/plugin/` and `Cubelet/plugin/` contained only the **bundled** drivers again (e.g. `s3` / `cos`); the third-party binary and its config file were gone.
2. `volume_plugins` in `conf.yaml` / `config.toml` no longer listed the custom driver (or only the default bundled entries remained).
3. CubeMaster returned errors such as:

```text
CubeMaster returned error code 130400: unknown driver: juicefs
```

Cubelet-side equivalent when registration was missing:

```text
no plugin registered for driver "juicefs"
```

4. Existing tenant volume **data** (JuiceFS metadata DB + object store blocks) was still present; the failure was **registration / packaging**, not data loss. Production impact: every sandbox create that depended on that volume driver failed until operators manually reinstalled the plugin and re-registered + restarted CubeMaster/Cubelet.

## Why this is easy to hit

- Official examples install into `$PREFIX/CubeMaster/plugin/` and `$PREFIX/Cubelet/plugin/` (see COS/S3 READMEs; Dockerfile also `COPY`/`install` bundled plugins into that tree).
- The development guide points operators at that layout: *“one-click packages the binary under `CubeMaster/plugin/` and `Cubelet/plugin/`”*.
- Registration docs correctly allow `binary_path: <binary_path>` as a placeholder (any absolute path), and guideline that credentials layout is **not** mandated by the framework — but neither the guide nor the examples call out that **putting third-party assets inside cubetoolbox couples them to the upgrade wipe**.
- Operators following the examples therefore install into the one place the next upgrade is most likely to replace.

## Suggested improvements

### Docs (high value, low risk)

1. Add an **“Upgrade-safe installation”** subsection to [docs/guide/volume-plugin.md](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/master/docs/guide/volume-plugin.md) (and zh mirror):
   - Prefer installing third-party binaries + credential files **outside** `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/` (e.g. `/opt/<org>/<plugin>/`).
   - Point `binary_path` / `socket_path` at that stable absolute path.
   - State clearly that `cubetoolbox/*/plugin/` is for **shipped** plugins and may be replaced on upgrade.
   - Document a post-upgrade checklist: verify `volume_plugins` still contains custom drivers; re-merge config if the installer rewrote `conf.yaml` / `config.toml`; restart CubeMaster/Cubelet.
2. Update COS/S3 example READMEs to distinguish **bundled path** vs **recommended path for third-party plugins**.

### Packaging / product (stronger fix)

1. Preserve or merge `volume_plugins` entries across upgrades (or ship `conf.d`-style drop-ins for custom drivers).
2. Optionally provide a dedicated third-party plugin directory that upgrades never empty (e.g. `/etc/cubesandbox/volume-plugins/` or `/var/lib/cubesandbox/plugins/`), scanned in addition to the bundled tree.
3. Emit a clear startup warning if a previously-used `driver` appears in volume records but is missing from current registration (fail loudly at upgrade time, not on the first tenant create).

## Additional Context

- Hard constraint that **does** belong under platform paths remains: Attach `host_path` must stay under `volume_plugin_base_dir` (default `/data/cube-shared/volume`). That is unrelated to where the **plugin binary** lives.
- Workaround we used operationally: reinstall binary + conf, re-add `volume_plugins` on both Master and Cubelet, restart both services. Longer-term: move binary/conf outside cubetoolbox and keep only a small registration snippet to re-apply after upgrades.
- Happy to help review doc wording or a proposed drop-in layout if maintainers want one.

## Related docs / examples

- [docs/guide/volume-plugin.md](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/master/docs/guide/volume-plugin.md) — Registration; rolling upgrade note
- [examples/volume/cos](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/volume/cos)
- [examples/volume/s3](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/volume/s3)

title: docs(README): fix pypi badge
[Bug Report] Overcommit ratios not enforced under concurrent creation — node can be massively over-scheduled
body:
## Summary

Under concurrent batch creation, cubemaster admits far more sandboxes onto a node than its configured overcommit ratio should allow, because scheduling decisions are made against a stale, 1s-polled resource snapshot. This is compounded by cubelet applying its own default overcommit factor on top of whatever ratio is configured on cubemaster, and by the fact that cubelet's creation path never re-checks local resources before booting a VM — so nothing catches the over-allocation until the node is already oversubscribed, risking OOM on pre-existing sandboxes.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `master` branch (as of this report)
- Deployment mode: single-node
- Relevant component: CubeMaster, Cubelet

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Provision a node with 64 vCPU / 128GB memory, sandbox spec 2 vCPU / 2.0GB, overcommit ratios left at default (`cpu_ratio: 3`, `mem_ratio: 2`).
2. Run `./cube-bench -c 10 -n 300 -w 3 -mode create-only` against it (10 concurrency, 300 create requests).
3. Observe how many requests succeed vs. the theoretical ceiling.

## Expected Behavior

With the compounded default overcommit (cubelet's own default factor — CPU ×2, memory ×1.25 — multiplied by cubemaster's `overcommit_ratio` of CPU ×3, memory ×2), the node's true ceiling is **160 sandboxes** (memory-bound: `128GB × 1.25 × 2 ÷ 2.0GB`). Requests beyond that should be rejected with `no more resource`.

## Actual Behavior

286 / 300 requests succeeded — well beyond the 160 ceiling. Only 14 were rejected:

```
HTTP 500: {"code":500,"message":"CubeMaster returned error code 130597: no more resource"}
```

Bench summary: Completed 286/300, Errors 14, QPS 75.0, Avg Create 136ms, Elapsed 3.9s.

**Root causes, with code references:**

1. **Scheduler reads a stale snapshot.** `cpuFilter.Select`/`memFilter.Select` (`CubeMaster/pkg/selector/filter/{cpufilter,memfilter}.go`) each run a quota check and a physical-load check, but both read from the same `inList[i]` node object, refreshed only every ~1s from Redis. Concurrent requests within that window all see the same pre-allocation numbers and all pass the filter independently.

2. **Cubelet's default overcommit compounds with cubemaster's.** In `Cubelet/pkg/cubelet/node_status.go`, `resolveHostQuotaCPUMilli`/`resolveHostQuotaMemMB` apply a default factor (CPU ×2, mem ×1.25) to the node's *reported* quota when `hostCfg.Quota.Cpu/Mem` isn't explicitly set. Cubemaster's `EffectiveQuotaCpu`/`EffectiveQuotaMem` (`CubeMaster/pkg/base/config/config.go`) then multiplies that already-inflated value by its own `overcommit_ratio` — so the effective overcommit an operator gets by default is 6× CPU / 2.5× memory, not the 3×/2× implied by `overcommit_ratio` alone.

3. **No local admission check in the cubelet creation path.** `checkResource` (check.go:152) only validates request format, the cgroup step only computes quota (not physical usage), and `prepare_resource`/`create_vm`/`boot_vm` (sb.rs:750, 918-919) never check local `/proc/meminfo` before booting. Over-allocation is only ever caught if/when cloud-hypervisor's mmap allocation itself fails — and under Linux memory overcommit + demand paging, freshly-created sandboxes that haven't written their full declared memory yet don't trigger that failure at all, so the over-allocation stays invisible until multiple sandboxes become active simultaneously, at which point the node can hit real OOM and take down pre-existing sandboxes.

## Additional Context

Two design questions worth discussing:

- Would the community consider a K8s-style `requests`/`limits` split (with QoS tiers) instead of a single ratio scaling the whole node, so overcommit risk lands on lower-priority sandboxes rather than uniformly?
- Would it make sense for cubelet to add a local admission check (similar to kubelet's) that re-validates actual available resources right before `create_vm`/`boot_vm`, as a last line of defense against stale scheduling decisions?

Happy to help test or discuss further.

title: [Bug Report] CubeOps fails to connect to MySQL when password contains URL-reserved characters

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

body:
CubeSandbox 0.6.0

**Description**

When CubeOps is configured through the Helm Chart using the standard `mysql.*` values, it receives the expected environment variables:

```text
CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_HOST=<external-mysql-host>
CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PORT=13307
CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_USER=<user>
CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PASSWORD=<password>
CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_DB=<database>
```

However, CubeOps may still fail during startup with:

```text
failed to initialize database, got error dial tcp [::1]:3306: connect: connection refused
```

This happens when the MySQL password contains URL-reserved characters, such as `#`, `?`, `/`, or an invalid `%` escape sequence.

**Root cause**

CubeOps builds an internal MySQL URL from the individual environment variables using string interpolation:

```go
fmt.Sprintf("mysql://%s:%s@%s:%d/%s",
    c.MySQLUser,
    c.MySQLPassword,
    c.MySQLHost,
    c.MySQLPortOrDefault(),
    c.MySQLDB,
)
```

The password is inserted without URL escaping. CubeOps subsequently parses this generated URL using `url.Parse()`.

If the password contains URL-reserved characters, parsing may fail or produce an empty host. The parsing error is silently ignored, and the code falls back to MySQL’s default port `3306`. This results in an address equivalent to `:3306`, which is normalized by the DAO layer to `localhost:3306`, producing the observed `[::1]:3306` connection attempt.

**Expected behavior**

CubeOps should connect using the configured `CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_HOST` and `CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PORT`, regardless of valid MySQL password characters.

A malformed `DATABASE_URL` should fail fast with a clear configuration error instead of silently falling back to `localhost:3306`.

**Suggested fix**

For the individual `CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_*` configuration path, build `dao.Config` directly instead of constructing and reparsing a URL.

Alternatively, construct the URL safely using `url.UserPassword()` and `net.JoinHostPort()`, and return an error if URL parsing fails or if host/user/database is empty after parsing.

**Affected code**

- `CubeOps/internal/config/config.go`
  - `buildMySQLURL()`
  - `parseDatabaseURL()`
  - `Config.DaoConfig()`
- `CubeDB/dao/dao.go`
  - `normalizeAddr()` masks the configuration error by converting `:3306` to `localhost:3306`.

When enabled, cube-node runs on the host network namespace so sandbox network devices survive cube-node Pod recreation. The `dnsPolicy` switches to `ClusterFirstWithHostNet` to keep in-cluster DNS working from the host network namespace.

## Trade-offs

- cube-node loses its CNI-assigned Pod identity — Kubernetes NetworkPolicy can no longer govern sandbox traffic.
- cubelet ports (9998/9999/9966) bind directly on the host.

## Changes

- `deploy/kubernetes/chart/templates/node-daemonset.yaml`: add `hostNetwork` field and conditional `dnsPolicy`.
- `deploy/kubernetes/chart/values.yaml`: add `cubeNode.hostNetwork` config with usage notes.

## Behavior

Default behavior is unchanged (`hostNetwork: false`, `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst`).

title: fix(cubelet): name sandbox TAPs after IPv4 and reject oversize names

The z+IPv4 scheme produced 16-byte names (e.g. z192.168.195.183). vishvananda/netlink LinkAdd copies into ifr_name[:15] and truncates silently, so create could succeed while later open/query used a different string than the kernel device.

New creates use the dotted IPv4. Recover still accepts leftover z-prefixed names when the decoded address is in the configured sandbox CIDR. Create fails before LinkAdd if the name is >= IFNAMSIZ.
