title: fix(sdk): do not send a non-positive Connect-Timeout-Ms for a command
body:
Fixes #1484.

## What

`commands.run` forwarded `timeoutMs` to envd as `Connect-Timeout-Ms` without checking that it was
positive. envd reads that header as a hard wall-clock deadline, so a zero or negative one has
already passed: the request is never answered, and the caller waits until its HTTP client gives up
on headers and reports a transport error that says nothing about the cause.

Both non-positive values arrive in ordinary use:

- **`0`** is how the `e2b` SDK spells "no deadline", so it comes with exactly the port the README's
  drop-in compatibility invites.
- **`NEVER_TIMEOUT`** is how this SDK spells it, and its value is `-1` — a constant meaning "does
  not time out" whose effect was that nothing ever returned.

## Why this is a slip rather than a design choice

The same guard is already correct everywhere else it appears:

| | `commands` | `pty` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node | `if (idleMs !== undefined)` ← fixed here | `if (options.timeoutMs !== undefined && options.timeoutMs > 0)` |
| Python | `if timeout is not None:` ← fixed here | `if timeout is not None and timeout > 0:` |
| Go | `if timeout <= 0 { return }` | same helper |

## What is not changed

`Sandbox.create`'s own `timeout` field. `0` and `NEVER_TIMEOUT` are meaningful to CubeAPI there,
and `test_create_sends_explicit_zero_timeout` / `test_create_sends_never_timeout` still pass
unchanged.

## Tests

Node and Python both gain two cases: no `Connect-Timeout-Ms` header for `0` or `NEVER_TIMEOUT`, and
a header that is still sent for a positive value. Both new cases fail against the previous
behaviour — reverting the one-line guard turns them red and leaves the rest green.

```
node    216 passed | 2 skipped   tsc --noEmit clean
python  257 passed | 4 skipped
```

## Measured

Against a running sandbox, before the fix:

```
timeoutMs: 0              → fetch failed / UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
timeoutMs: NEVER_TIMEOUT  → fetch failed / UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
timeoutMs: 30000          → { stdout: "hi\n", exitCode: 0 }   ~22 ms
omitted                   → { stdout: "hi\n", exitCode: 0 }   ~21 ms
```

title: [Bug Report] commands.run forwards a non-positive timeoutMs to envd, hanging every command (Node & Python)

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update python code

body:
## Summary

`commands.run` forwards `timeoutMs` to envd as `Connect-Timeout-Ms` without checking that it is
positive. A non-positive value therefore reaches envd as an already-expired deadline, envd never
answers, and the call fails with a transport-level headers timeout rather than with anything that
says what happened.

Two values reach it that way in ordinary use:

- **`0`**, which is how the official `e2b` SDK spells "no deadline". Code ported under the
  "drop-in E2B SDK compatibility" claim passes it.
- **`NEVER_TIMEOUT`**, which this SDK exports itself. Its value is `-1`, and it is forwarded
  verbatim.

The same SDKs already get this right for a pty, and the Go SDK gets it right for both — so this
is one guard missing in one place, in two of the three clients.

| SDK | `commands` guard | `pty` guard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node | `if (idleMs !== undefined)` — `src/commands.ts:241` | `if (options.timeoutMs !== undefined && options.timeoutMs > 0)` — `src/pty.ts:315` |
| Python | `if timeout is not None:` — `cubesandbox/_commands.py:149` | `if timeout is not None and timeout > 0:` — `cubesandbox/_pty.py:232` |
| Go | `if timeout <= 0 { return }` — `envd.go:240` | same helper |

## Environment

- CubeSandbox commit: `981ccda4` (master)
- SDK: `@cubesandbox/sdk` 0.3.0, built from `sdk/node`
- Node.js 24
- Relevant component: SDK (Node, Python)

## Steps to Reproduce

Against any running sandbox:

```js
import { Sandbox, NEVER_TIMEOUT } from "@cubesandbox/sdk"

const sb = await Sandbox.connect(sandboxId)

await sb.commands.run("echo hi", { user: "root", timeoutMs: 0 })              // hangs
await sb.commands.run("echo hi", { user: "root", timeoutMs: NEVER_TIMEOUT })  // hangs
await sb.commands.run("echo hi", { user: "root", timeoutMs: 30000 })          // fine
await sb.commands.run("echo hi", { user: "root" })                            // fine
```

## Expected Behavior

A non-positive `timeoutMs` means "no deadline" and no `Connect-Timeout-Ms` header is sent — which
is what `pty` in the same SDK does, and what the Go SDK does for both.

`NEVER_TIMEOUT` in particular should never produce a hang: it is the constant this SDK exports for
saying that a thing does not time out.

## Actual Behavior

```
timeoutMs: 0              → fetch failed / UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
timeoutMs: NEVER_TIMEOUT  → fetch failed / UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
timeoutMs: 30000          → { stdout: "hi\n", stderr: "", exitCode: 0 }   ~22 ms
omitted                   → { stdout: "hi\n", stderr: "", exitCode: 0 }   ~21 ms
```

The failure surfaces as a transport error from the HTTP client, so nothing in it points at the
header that caused it.

## Impact

Every command in every sandbox hangs for the lifetime of the client's headers timeout. For an
application that runs a command per request, that is the whole application — and because the error
is a generic `fetch failed`, it reads as a network or proxy fault rather than as an argument.

`0` is the value E2B's SDK documents for "no timeout", so this is reachable by exactly the port the
README invites.

## Suggested Fix

Match `pty` in the same file's neighbour:

```diff
-    if (idleMs !== undefined) {
+    if (idleMs !== undefined && idleMs > 0) {
       headers["Connect-Timeout-Ms"] = String(Math.trunc(idleMs));
     }
```

and the equivalent in `cubesandbox/_commands.py:149`.

title: fix(cubeapi): accept E2B host-keyed network rules
body:
## Motivation

The E2B Python and npm SDKs send `network.rules` as a host-keyed map for per-host request transforms.

CubeAPI currently models this field as an ordered array, so an otherwise valid `Sandbox.create` request is rejected with:

```text
422: network.rules: invalid type: map, expected a sequence
```

This breaks E2B-compatible sandbox creation when SDK users configure network transform rules.

Fixes #1482.

## What Changed

* Accept E2B's host-keyed `network.rules` map in `SandboxNetworkConfig`.
* Convert each host key to `match.host`.
* Convert each non-empty `transform.headers` entry to `action.inject` in the existing internal egress-rule model.
* Ignore E2B no-op entries with no transform or no headers instead of creating an unintended allow-only rule.
* Reject unsupported E2B transform fields instead of silently discarding network intent CubeAPI cannot express.
* Preserve the existing array-shaped `network.rules` format for backward compatibility.
* Document both accepted wire shapes in OpenAPI and add regression coverage for map, array, no-op, schema, and complete `NewSandbox` requests.

## Validation

* Python `e2b==2.34.0` / `e2b-code-interpreter==2.8.1` created and deleted a sandbox with host-keyed `network.rules`.
* npm `e2b==2.45.0` created and deleted a sandbox with host-keyed `network.rules`.
* CubeMaster and Cubelet request payloads preserved the converted host match and injected header in the final sandbox creation request.
* Existing array-shaped rules created a sandbox successfully and remained present in the downstream request.
* Targeted CubeAPI regression tests passed, including E2B no-op handling and OpenAPI schema coverage.
* Full CubeAPI test suite passed with 126 tests.
* CubeAPI release build and generated OpenAPI export passed.

## Scope

This PR only adds CubeAPI request-shape compatibility for E2B-style `network.rules`.

It does not change network policy semantics, the internal egress-rule model, CubeMaster/Cubelet behavior, or SDK code.

title: [Bug Report] CubeAPI rejects the official E2B SDK's `network.rules` map shape, breaking drop-in SDK compatibility
body:
## Summary

The README advertises "Native E2B SDK compatibility — swap one URL env var, zero business code
changes", and the capability table marks E2B SDK compatibility as "Drop-in". That holds for
everything I exercised except one thing: `SandboxOpts.network.rules`.

The official `e2b` SDK types `rules` as a **map keyed by host**; CubeAPI deserializes it as an
**array** of `EgressRule`. So any application that passes the SDK's documented `network` option
gets an HTTP 422 at sandbox creation and cannot proceed through the SDK at all.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `abe4a4f` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: n/a
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: n/a
- Base image tag: `2026.16`
- Client: official `e2b` npm SDK `2.45.0`
- Relevant component: CubeAPI

## Steps to Reproduce

Create a sandbox through the official SDK using the `network` option exactly as documented at
https://docs.e2b.dev/sandbox/internet-access :

```js
network: {
  allowOut: ['api.example.com'],
  rules: {
    'api.example.com': [
      { transform: { headers: { 'X-Header': 'Content' } } }
    ],
  },
}
```

## Expected Behavior

The sandbox is created, since this is the shape the official SDK produces and the documented way to
express per-host egress rules.

## Actual Behavior

`POST /sandboxes` rejects the body:

```
HTTP 422
Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: network.rules: invalid type: map
```

The field is declared as a list in `CubeAPI/src/models/mod.rs`:

```rust
/// L7 egress rules, evaluated first-match-wins in list order.
#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
pub rules: Option<Vec<EgressRule>>,
```

with `EgressRule` being `{ name: String, match: EgressRuleMatch, action: EgressRuleAction }`.

## Impact

`network.rules` with `transform.headers` is E2B's documented mechanism for injecting credentials into
outbound HTTP(S) requests, so that the secret never has to be placed inside the sandbox as an
environment variable. With the shapes diverging, a caller using the official SDK's `network` option
cannot create a sandbox — the only workaround is to bypass the SDK and hand-build the request body in
CubeSandbox's own shape, which is exactly the "zero business code changes" property the README
promises.

## Scope — this is the only divergence I hit

To keep the severity honest: everything else I exercised through the official SDK worked. Sandbox
create, list and kill, plus the whole envd surface — filesystem read/write/list/rename/remove/exists,
`commands.run`, `pty.create` — 15 checks passing. `network.rules` is the single failing one.

## Suggested Fix (just a suggestion)

Accept both shapes, e.g. a `#[serde(untagged)]` enum over `Vec<EgressRule>` and
`HashMap<String, Vec<StandardRule>>`, expanding the map form into the existing internal
`Vec<EgressRule>`: each host key becomes `match: { host: <key> }` and
`action: { allow: true, inject: <from transform.headers> }`.

This would be purely additive — callers already using the array form are unaffected. CubeSandbox's
array form is strictly more expressive anyway (it can match on method/path/scheme, can deny, and
carries audit levels), so the map form is a subset that lowers cleanly into it.

title: cubelog: remove the dead requestTrace aggregation path
body:
Closes #1480.

## Motivation

`requestTrace` is never constructed anywhere in the tree, so its methods `indexKey()` and `realKey()`
have no callers, and `slice2Str()` is called only from `realKey()`. The whole block is unreachable.

It is not harmless dead weight: `go vet` reports `possible misuse of reflect.StringHeader` at
`metric.go:179`, inside `slice2Str`. Keeping unreachable unsafe-pointer code around means that warning
sits in the build output forever and any future reader has to work out whether it matters.

## What this changes

`cubelog/metric.go` — deletes 109 lines:

- `type requestTrace struct` (`:77-130`)
- `func (m *requestTrace) indexKey()` (`:128`)
- `func (m *requestTrace) realKey()` (`:142`)
- `func slice2Str(b []byte) string` (`:173`)

and drops the four imports that only that block used: `bytes`, `reflect`, `strconv`, `unsafe`. `io` and
`time` remain.

The exported `RequestTrace` type (different type, capital R) and `Trace()` are untouched — those are
the live API.

Verified nothing outside the deleted block referenced any of these identifiers:

```
$ grep -rn "requestTrace\b|slice2Str|indexKey()" --include='*.go' .   # outside cubelog/: no hits
```

`Cubelet/services/images/volumelifetime.go` has its **own** separate `slice2Str`/`realKey` which are
live and are deliberately left alone here — they belong to the unsafe-header issue.

No comment changes.

## Testing

Deletion only, so no new tests. Existing coverage confirms nothing depended on it:

```
$ cd cubelog && go build ./...
BUILD OK

$ go test -count=1 ./
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/cubelog  1.663s

$ go vet ./
(clean — the metric.go:179 reflect.StringHeader warning is gone)
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l .` — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./` — all clean.

`git diff --stat`: `cubelog/metric.go | 109 ------` , 1 file changed, 109 deletions.

## Risk / rollout

Very low — removing code with no callers and no exported surface. If the aggregation was intended to
come back, this PR is the wrong direction and it should be wired up instead; the deleted code is
recoverable from history either way.

title: [Bug Report] cubelog's requestTrace metric-aggregation path is dead code (and contains a vet-flagged unsafe misuse)
body:
## Summary

The `requestTrace` struct in `cubelog/metric.go` is never instantiated, so `indexKey()`, `realKey()`
and `slice2Str()` are all unreachable — including a `reflect.StringHeader` misuse that `go vet` reports.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: n/a
- Relevant component: cubelog

## Steps to Reproduce

```
grep -rn "requestTrace{" cubelog/          # no results: never constructed
grep -n "realKey()\|indexKey()" cubelog/   # only the definitions
cd cubelog && go vet ./                    # reports metric.go:179
```

## Expected Behavior

Either the aggregation path is wired up and used, or it is removed.

## Actual Behavior

It is orphaned. `go vet` reports a real hazard inside code that can never run:

```
metric.go:179:35: possible misuse of reflect.StringHeader
```

`staticcheck` additionally reports `reflect.SliceHeader` / `reflect.StringHeader` as deprecated since
Go 1.21 (`SA1019`).

## Additional Context

- `requestTrace` — `cubelog/metric.go:77-130`, never constructed.
- `indexKey()` — `:128`, no callers.
- `realKey()` — `:142`, no callers.
- `slice2Str()` — `:173`, called only from `realKey()`.

This looks like the other half of a partially-removed metric aggregation path: `Trace()` still computes
`region` / `tmcluster` / `version` locals and discards them (tracked separately), which is consistent
with the consumer having been deleted while the producer side was left behind.

Note `Cubelet/services/images/volumelifetime.go` has its **own** separate `slice2Str` and `realKey`,
which are live and are tracked under the unsafe-header issue. Only the cubelog copies are dead.

title: tests: fix the data races in queueworker, recov and bufferqueue
body:
Closes #1478.

## Motivation

`go test -race` fails in three packages because tests read state written by a goroutine without
synchronization. The production code is correct in all three cases; the tests are wrong.

These are part of what stands between the repo and a green `-race` gate.

## What this changes

**`queueworker/queue_test.go` — `TestQueueBlock`** (CubeMaster and Cubelet copies)

`got` becomes an `atomic.Bool`, and the test now waits on a `done` channel closed by the goroutine
instead of sleeping for a fixed second:

- removes the race on `got`
- removes the unconditional 1s sleep, so the test finishes as soon as `BPop` returns
- fails with a clear message if `BPop` never returns, instead of reporting a confusing assertion failure

**`recov/runtime_test.go` — `TestGoWithRetryWithCrash`** (CubeMaster and Cubelet copies)

`int(panicTime)` becomes `int(atomic.LoadInt32(&panicTime))`, matching the `atomic.AddInt32` that
production `HandleCrash` uses to write it.

**`bufferqueue/bufferqueue_test.go` — `TestQueueCheckTimestampPriority`** (CubeMaster only)

The watcher goroutine is given a `watcherDone` channel and the test joins it via `defer`, so `t.Logf`
can no longer run after the test function has returned.

No production code changed. No comment changes.

Per CONTRIBUTING's "one component per commit", this should land as two commits — one for CubeMaster, one
for Cubelet.

## Testing

```
CubeMaster:
  ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/base/queueworker  10.694s
  ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/base/recov         5.869s

Cubelet:
  ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/Cubelet/pkg/queueworker  12.305s
  ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/Cubelet/pkg/recov         5.478s
```

all under `-race -count=1`, where master reports `--- FAIL` plus a `WARNING: DATA RACE` for
`TestQueueBlock` and `TestGoWithRetryWithCrash`.

Module-wide `go test -race ./...` in CubeMaster:

| | races |
|---|---|
| master | 9 |
| this branch | **7** |

The remaining 7 are the `localcache` production races, which are fixed on their own branch. The two
changes together take CubeMaster to 0.

## On the bufferqueue one

I could not reproduce that race in five isolated runs of the package — it showed up only in a full
`go test -race ./...`. `bw.Workings()` is correctly `atomic.LoadInt32`, so the plausible cause is the
unjoined goroutine touching `t` after the test returned, which is a `testing` misuse regardless of
whether the detector catches it on a given run. I fixed it on those grounds rather than claiming a
verified red/green, since I would rather say so than present an unproven fix as proven.

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l` on all four packages — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `go test -race` on all four — clean.

title: [Bug Report] Test-side data races in queueworker, recov and bufferqueue make go test -race fail

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

body:
## Summary

Three tests read state written by a goroutine without synchronization, so `go test -race` reports data
races and the tests fail. The production code in all three cases is correct — these are defects in the
tests.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: n/a — unit tests
- Relevant component: CubeMaster and Cubelet (duplicated packages)

## Steps to Reproduce

```
cd CubeMaster && go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/base/queueworker/ ./pkg/base/recov/
cd Cubelet    && go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/queueworker/ ./pkg/recov/
```

## Expected Behavior

Race-clean.

## Actual Behavior

```
--- FAIL: TestQueueBlock (1.03s)
--- FAIL: TestGoWithRetryWithCrash (2.04s)
race: queueworker/queue_test.go:75 | queue_test.go:67 | queue_test.go:65
race: recov/runtime_test.go:147 vs recov/runtime.go:30 (atomic.AddInt32 in HandleCrash)
```

## Additional Context

**a. `queueworker/queue_test.go` — `TestQueueBlock`.** A plain `got := false` is written inside a
goroutine after `q.BPop()` returns and read from the test goroutine, with only a `time.Sleep` between
them. Unsynchronized, and the sleep makes it slow as well as racy.

**b. `recov/runtime_test.go` — `TestGoWithRetryWithCrash`.** `panicTime` is incremented with
`atomic.AddInt32` from the recovery handler (production `HandleCrash`, `runtime.go:30`) but read as
`int(panicTime)` — a plain, non-atomic read of an atomically-written variable.

**c. `bufferqueue/bufferqueue_test.go` — `TestQueueCheckTimestampPriority`.** The watcher goroutine
calls `t.Logf` but is never joined, so it can log after the test function has returned. This one is
timing-dependent — it appeared in a full `go test -race ./...` run but I could not reproduce it in five
isolated runs of the package.

Both CubeMaster and Cubelet carry copies of `queueworker` and `recov`, so (a) and (b) each occur twice.
`bufferqueue` exists only under CubeMaster.

title: sdk/python: use typing.List in classes that define a `list` method
body:
Closes #1476.

## Motivation

`Template`, `Sandbox`, `Volume` and `Filesystem` each define a method named `list`. Inside a class body the
name `list` binds to that method, so an annotation written `list[TemplateInfo]` in the same class refers to
the method, not the builtin. mypy reports `Function "...list" is not valid as a type` and, more importantly,
**stops type-checking those parameters** — 10 annotations across two files were effectively `Any`.

## What this changes

Replaces `list[...]` with `typing.List[...]` in the four affected modules and adds `List` to each
`from typing import ...` line:

| file | annotations rewritten |
|---|---|
| `cubesandbox/_template.py` | 11 |
| `cubesandbox/sandbox.py` | 6 |
| `cubesandbox/_volume.py` | 4 |
| `cubesandbox/_filesystem.py` | 2 |

`typing.List` is not shadowed by anything, so the annotations resolve for static analysers as well as at
runtime. The public API — including the `list` method names — is unchanged.

I fixed all four rather than only the two mypy currently flags: `_volume.py` and `_filesystem.py` have the
same construct and would start producing the same errors as soon as anything about their annotations
changed.

No comment changes.

## Correcting the original report

The issue I filed first claimed this broke `typing.get_type_hints` at runtime. **That was wrong**, and I
verified it rather than leaving it in:

```
MASTER get_type_hints(Template.build) -> OK
MASTER get_type_hints(Template.list)  -> OK
MASTER get_type_hints(Sandbox.list)   -> OK
```

All four modules use `from __future__ import annotations`, and `get_type_hints` evaluates against **module**
globals rather than the class namespace, so `list` resolves to the builtin at runtime. The defect is
static-analysis only, and the issue text has been corrected to say so. That also lowers the severity from
what I first suggested.

## Testing

The evidence is the mypy count, since the defect is a type-resolution one:

```
MASTER 'not valid as a type' count: 10
BRANCH 'not valid as a type' count:  0
```

No behavioural change, so no new tests. Existing suite and lint are unaffected:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests -q
225 passed in 0.38s

$ ruff check --select F,E9 cubesandbox
Found 2 errors.        # both pre-existing F401 on master, identical count
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `pytest` — 225 passed (`sdk-test-check`).
- `ruff` — no new findings (the two `F401` unused-import errors are present on master too and are not
  touched here).

title: [Bug Report] Classes with a `list` method shadow the builtin in their own annotations, so mypy cannot check those parameters

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update python code

body:
## Summary

Four classes in the Python SDK define a method named `list`. Inside a class body the name `list` resolves
to that method, so annotations written as `list[...]` in the same class refer to the method rather than the
builtin. mypy reports them as invalid types and silently stops checking those parameters.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: n/a — SDK
- Relevant component: sdk/python

## Steps to Reproduce

```
cd sdk/python && mypy --python-version 3.11 --ignore-missing-imports cubesandbox
```

## Expected Behavior

No `valid-type` errors; `list[...]` annotations resolve to the builtin and are type-checked.

## Actual Behavior

10 errors:

```
cubesandbox/_template.py:220: error: Function "cubesandbox._template.Template.list" is not valid as a type  [valid-type]
cubesandbox/_template.py:228: error: ... (7 total in _template.py)
cubesandbox/sandbox.py:374:   error: Function "cubesandbox.sandbox.Sandbox.list" is not valid as a type  [valid-type]
cubesandbox/sandbox.py:647:   error: ... (3 total in sandbox.py)
```

Each error means mypy could not resolve that annotation, so the parameter or return value is effectively
untyped — genuine type errors there go unreported.

## Scope

Classes defining a `list` method:

- `cubesandbox/_template.py:149` — `Template.list`
- `cubesandbox/sandbox.py:357` — `Sandbox.list`
- `cubesandbox/_volume.py:379` — `Volume.list`
- `cubesandbox/_filesystem.py:143` — `Filesystem.list`

The first two are the ones mypy currently flags; the other two have `list[...]` annotations in the same
class body and are the same latent problem.

## Note: runtime is NOT affected

Worth stating explicitly to keep the severity honest. All four modules use
`from __future__ import annotations`, and `typing.get_type_hints` evaluates annotations in **module**
globals, not the class namespace — so at runtime `list[...]` resolves to the builtin as intended:

```
get_type_hints(Template.build) -> OK
get_type_hints(Template.list)  -> OK
get_type_hints(Sandbox.list)   -> OK
```

This is a static-analysis defect, not a runtime one.

title: cubemaster: clamp the gRPC pool refcount in the stored value, not a local copy
body:
Closes #1474.

## Motivation

Both `incrRef` and `decrRef` clamped a **local** `int32` after the atomic add, so neither clamp had
any effect on `p.ref`:

```go
newRef := atomic.AddInt32(&p.ref, 1)
if newRef >= math.MaxInt32 { newRef = math.MaxInt32 }   // local only
```

`staticcheck` flags the increment side as `SA4003`. The consequential half is the decrement: a single
unbalanced `decrRef` drives the stored counter to `-1`, and from then on the
`atomic.LoadInt32(&p.ref) == 0` guard inside `decrRef` never holds again — so `deleteFrom(MaxIdle)` is
never reached and idle connections above `MaxIdle` are never reclaimed. A silent connection leak.

## What this changes

`CubeMaster/pkg/base/grpc-middleware/pool/pool.go` — both operations become compare-and-swap loops so
the bound is enforced on the stored value:

- `incrRef` saturates at `math.MaxInt32` instead of wrapping negative.
- `decrRef` stops at `0` instead of going negative, which keeps the idle-trim branch reachable.

`decrRef`'s existing idle-trim block is unchanged; it now sees a counter that can actually reach `0`.

No comment changes.

## Testing

New: `CubeMaster/pkg/base/grpc-middleware/pool/pool_refcount_test.go`

- `TestIncrRefDoesNotOverflowPastMaxInt32` — asserts the **stored** value saturates.
- `TestIncrRefIncrementsNormally` — normal path unchanged.
- `TestDecrRefDoesNotGoNegative` — repeated unbalanced releases leave the stored value at `0`.
- `TestDecrRefDecrementsNormally` — normal path unchanged.
- `TestRefCountIsBalancedUnderConcurrency` — 64 goroutines × 500 balanced incr/decr pairs end at `0`,
  which exercises the CAS retry loops.

Red/green verified — with `pool.go` reverted to master:

```
--- FAIL: TestIncrRefDoesNotOverflowPastMaxInt32
--- FAIL: TestDecrRefDoesNotGoNegative
FAIL
```

and with the fix:

```
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/base/grpc-middleware/pool  0.283s
```

Also clean under the race detector:

```
$ go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/base/grpc-middleware/pool/
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/base/grpc-middleware/pool  1.740s
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l` on the package — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `GOOS=linux go build` on the package — clean.
- `staticcheck -checks 'SA*'` — the `SA4003` finding is gone; the remaining `SA1019` hits are
  pre-existing `grpc.DialContext` / `WithInsecure` / `WithBlock` deprecations in `options.go`, not
  touched here.

title: [Bug Report] gRPC connection-pool refcount clamps are dead code; an unbalanced release permanently disables idle trimming

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

body:
## Summary

`incrRef` and `decrRef` clamp only their local copy of the refcount, never the stored value, so the
clamps have no effect. A negative stored refcount permanently disables the pool's idle-connection
trimming.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a — control-plane only
- Deployment mode: single-node / cluster
- Relevant component: CubeMaster (`pkg/base/grpc-middleware/pool`)

## Steps to Reproduce

The reachable half is `decrRef`. Any path that releases a pooled connection more times than it
acquired it drives the stored counter negative:

1. `p.decrRef()` on a pool whose `ref` is already `0`.
2. `atomic.LoadInt32(&p.ref)` is now `-1`.
3. From this point on, the `newRef == 0 && ...` branch in `decrRef` can still be entered, but the
   inner `atomic.LoadInt32(&p.ref) == 0` guard never holds again, so `deleteFrom(p.opt.MaxIdle)` is
   never called and idle connections above `MaxIdle` are never reclaimed.

## Expected Behavior

The stored refcount stays within `[0, math.MaxInt32]`, so the idle-trim path keeps working after an
unbalanced release and the counter cannot wrap.

## Actual Behavior

```go
func (p *pool) incrRef() int32 {
    newRef := atomic.AddInt32(&p.ref, 1)
    if newRef >= math.MaxInt32 {
        newRef = math.MaxInt32      // local copy only
    }
    return newRef
}
```

`newRef` is a local `int32`; assigning to it does not touch `p.ref`. `decrRef` has the same shape
with `if newRef < 0 { newRef = 0 }`.

`staticcheck` flags the increment side as `SA4003` — *"no value of type int32 is greater than
math.MaxInt32"* — i.e. the `>` half of `>=` is unreachable, and when `==` does hold the assignment is
a no-op.

## Additional Context

`CubeMaster/pkg/base/grpc-middleware/pool/pool.go:113-140`.

The overflow side needs 2^31 acquisitions and is effectively unreachable in practice; the
negative-refcount side is reachable from any double-release and its consequence (a connection leak
via disabled idle trimming) is silent.

title: cubelog: emit the Region/Cluster defaults that Trace already computes
body:
Closes #1472.

## Motivation

`Trace()` computed `region`, `tmcluster` and `version` fallbacks from the configured globals and then
never used them — `staticcheck` reports all three as `SA4006`. Because
`makeLogFieldsFromTrace` only sets `Region`/`Cluster` when the *trace struct* carries them, any caller
that omits them produced a trace line with no Region and no Cluster, even when the logger had defaults
configured.

`Version` was already defaulted inside `makeLogFieldsFromTrace` (`entry.go:213-217`), so the `version`
local was pure duplication.

## What this changes

`cubelog/metric.go` in `Trace()`:

- The computed `region` / `tmcluster` are now applied to the emitted fields.
- They are applied **only when non-empty**, which preserves the existing omit-when-empty contract —
  see below.
- The redundant `version` local is removed, since `makeLogFieldsFromTrace` already defaults it.

No comment changes.

## The omit-when-empty detail

My first attempt set the fields unconditionally, which broke `TestTraceEnds`
(`logger_test.go:92-93`). That test asserts that when neither the trace nor the globals carry a
cluster, the output must **not** contain `Cluster` — an unconditional assignment made the key present
with an empty value.

The guarded version keeps that contract: absent stays absent, configured defaults now come through.
Both halves of `TestTraceEnds` pass.

## Testing

New: `cubelog/metric_trace_test.go`

- `TestTraceEmitsConfiguredRegionAndClusterDefaults` — with globals configured and the trace fields
  empty, the emitted JSON carries the defaults.
- `TestTracePrefersExplicitRegionAndCluster` — an explicit value on the trace still wins over the
  global.

Both capture the real trace line via `SetTraceOutput` + `EnableLogMetric` and parse it as JSON, and both
restore the globals and the writer afterwards so they do not leak into other tests in the package.

Red/green verified — with `metric.go` reverted to master:

```
--- FAIL: TestTraceEmitsConfiguredRegionAndClusterDefaults
    metric_trace_test.go:49: Region = <nil>, want ap-guangzhou (the configured default)
    metric_trace_test.go:52: Cluster = <nil>, want cluster-a (the configured default)
```

and with the fix:

```
$ cd cubelog && go test -count=1 ./
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/cubelog  0.625s

$ go test -count=1 -run TestTrace ./          # the ordering that exposed the omit-when-empty issue
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/cubelog  0.164s
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l .` — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `go build ./...` — clean.
- `staticcheck -checks 'SA4006' ./` — the three `metric.go` findings are gone.

Note the package directory is `cubelog/` but the Go package is `CubeLog`; the new test file matches.

## Risk / rollout

Trace lines from callers that omit Region/Cluster will start carrying the configured values. Anything
that parses those lines and currently treats the fields as absent will now see them populated — which
is the intended behaviour, but it is a visible change in log output.

## Related, not fixed here

`cubelog/metric.go:77-180` — the `requestTrace` / `indexKey` / `realKey` / `slice2Str` block is
unreachable (never instantiated). It looks like the other half of a partially-removed metric
aggregation path, and `Trace()` computing inputs for it is probably why these locals existed. Tracked
separately.

title: [Bug Report] cubelog Trace() computes Region/Cluster defaults and then discards them
body:
## Summary

`Trace()` resolves `Region` and `Cluster` fallbacks from the configured globals, then never uses them,
so trace lines from callers that omit those fields carry no Region or Cluster at all.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: single-node / cluster
- Relevant component: cubelog (used by CubeMaster, Cubelet, CubeOps)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the logger globals: `cubelog.SetRegion("ap-guangzhou")`, `cubelog.SetCluster("cluster-a")`.
2. Emit a trace that does not set those fields explicitly — for example the volume GC trace at
   `Cubelet/services/images/volumelifetime.go:644-651`, which sets only
   Action/CalleeAction/Caller/Callee/RequestID/AppID.
3. Inspect the emitted JSON line.

## Expected Behavior

`Region` is `ap-guangzhou` and `Cluster` is `cluster-a`, from the configured defaults.

## Actual Behavior

Neither key is present. Reproduced with the fix reverted:

```
--- FAIL: TestTraceEmitsConfiguredRegionAndClusterDefaults
    metric_trace_test.go:49: Region = <nil>, want ap-guangzhou (the configured default)
    metric_trace_test.go:52: Cluster = <nil>, want cluster-a (the configured default)
```

## Additional Context

`cubelog/metric.go:189-215`:

```go
region := trace.Region
if region == "" { region = string(defaultRegion) }      // computed
tmcluster := trace.Cluster
if tmcluster == "" { tmcluster = cluster }              // computed
version := trace.Version
if version == "" { version = moduleVersion }            // computed
if enableLogMetric {
    fields := makeLogFieldsFromTrace(trace)             // uses `trace`, not the locals
    ...
}
```

All three locals are dead — `staticcheck` flags them as `SA4006` ×3.

`makeLogFieldsFromTrace` (`cubelog/entry.go:232-239`) sets Region and Cluster only when the *trace*
carries them, with no fallback to the globals. `Version` is the exception — it *is* defaulted inside
`makeLogFieldsFromTrace` at `entry.go:213-217` — so only Region and Cluster are actually lost.

This also affects the positional formatter at `entry.go:284`, which writes `fields["Region"]` into a
fixed pipe-delimited column.

title: hotswap: compare config bytes exactly and check the marshal error
body:
Closes #1470.

## Motivation

`FileOperator.reload` used `bytes.EqualFold` to decide whether the config had changed.
`EqualFold` is a case-*insensitive* comparison, so any edit that only changed ASCII letter case —
`level: INFO` → `level: info`, `host: Foo.internal` → `host: foo.internal`, `driver: MySQL` →
`driver: mysql` — was reported as "no change" and never pushed to listeners.

The `yaml.Marshal` error on the same line was also unchecked. On failure `new` is nil, so the
baseline `backupOldCfg` was wiped to nil and `notify()` still fired with the unmarshalable config.
`Init()` at `:71-74` already checks the same call, so this was an inconsistency within one file.

## What this changes

Both copies of the package — `CubeMaster/pkg/base/hotswap/file.go` and `Cubelet/pkg/hotswap/file.go`
— get the same two-line change:

```go
new, err := yaml.Marshal(config)
if err != nil {
    return false
}
if bytes.Equal(o.backupOldCfg, new) {
    return false
}
```

`bytes.Equal` replaces `EqualFold`, and the `len(...) == len(...)` pre-check goes away because
`bytes.Equal` already compares lengths first. A marshal failure now returns `false` without
corrupting the baseline or notifying listeners.

No comment changes.

Per CONTRIBUTING's "one component per commit", this should land as two commits — one for CubeMaster,
one for Cubelet — since the two packages are separate copies. The diff is identical in both.

## Testing

New: `CubeMaster/pkg/base/hotswap/file_reload_test.go` and `Cubelet/pkg/hotswap/file_reload_test.go`
(identical).

- `TestReloadDetectsCaseOnlyKeyValueChange` — `INFO` → `info` is detected.
- `TestReloadDetectsCaseOnlyHostChange` — `Foo.internal` → `foo.internal` is detected.
- `TestReloadReportsNoChangeForIdenticalConfig` — an unchanged file still reports no change, so the
  fix does not turn every watcher tick into a spurious notify.
- `TestReloadDetectsOrdinaryChange` — regression guard for the normal path.

The tests drive `reload()` directly via `NewWatcher` rather than `Init()`, so no fsnotify goroutine is
started.

Red/green verified — with `file.go` reverted to master:

```
--- FAIL: TestReloadDetectsCaseOnlyKeyValueChange
--- FAIL: TestReloadDetectsCaseOnlyHostChange
FAIL
```

and with the fix applied:

```
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/base/hotswap  0.363s
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/Cubelet/pkg/hotswap          0.512s
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l` on both packages — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `GOOS=linux go build` on both packages — clean.

## Risk / rollout

Low. The change makes reload strictly more sensitive, so the only behavioural difference is that
case-only edits now take effect — which is the intent. Listeners already had to tolerate being
notified on any change.

title: [Bug Report] Config hot-reload uses bytes.EqualFold, so case-only edits are silently ignored
body:
## Summary

`FileOperator.reload` compares the old and new marshalled config with `bytes.EqualFold`, so any edit
that only changes ASCII letter case is treated as "no change" and never applied. The
`yaml.Marshal` error on the same line is also unchecked.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a — control-plane only
- Deployment mode: single-node / cluster
- Relevant component: CubeMaster and Cubelet (identical copies of the package)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start CubeMaster (or Cubelet) with a hot-swappable YAML config containing
   `log:\n  level: INFO`.
2. Edit the file in place to `log:\n  level: info` and save.
3. The file watcher fires, but no listener is notified and the running config is unchanged.

Any case-only edit reproduces it — for example a hostname `Foo.internal` → `foo.internal`, or a
driver name `MySQL` → `mysql`.

## Expected Behavior

The edit is detected and pushed to listeners, as it would be for any other content change.

## Actual Behavior

`reload()` returns `false` and nothing happens. Reproduced against the change-detection expression:

```
config edit                  reloaded?
log level INFO -> info       false       <== edit SILENTLY IGNORED
host Foo -> foo              false       <== edit SILENTLY IGNORED
driver MySQL -> mysql        false       <== edit SILENTLY IGNORED
genuine change (control)     true
length differs (control)     true
```

## Additional Context

`CubeMaster/pkg/base/hotswap/file.go:88-100` and the identical
`Cubelet/pkg/hotswap/file.go:88-100`:

```go
new, err := yaml.Marshal(config)
if len(o.backupOldCfg) == len(new) && bytes.EqualFold(o.backupOldCfg, new) {
    return false
}
```

`bytes.EqualFold` compares under Unicode simple case-folding — it is for case-insensitive *text*
matching, not byte identity.

Second defect on the same line: the `yaml.Marshal` error is never checked (`staticcheck SA4006`). The
sibling `Init()` at `:71-74` *does* check it, so the asymmetry within the same file looks like an
oversight. On a marshal failure `new` is nil, so `o.backupOldCfg` is set to nil and
`o.notify(config)` still fires — the change-detection baseline is wiped and every subsequent reload
reports "changed".

title: sdk/node: reject arrays for transform and transform.headers
body:
Closes #1468.

## Motivation

`convertE2BTransformToInject` validated with `typeof headers !== "object"`. In JavaScript
`typeof [] === "object"`, so an array passed the guard, and `Object.entries(["a","b"])` produced
`[["0","a"],["1","b"]]` — injects whose header names are the array indices `"0"` and `"1"`, carrying real
credentials.

The Python SDK rejects the same input via `isinstance(headers, dict)`, so this was also a cross-SDK
divergence. And the server does not catch it: `validate_policy` requires only a non-empty string header
name, and `"0"` satisfies that, so the malformed policy is accepted end to end.

## What this changes

`sdk/node/src/policy.ts` — two guards gain an `Array.isArray` check:

```ts
if (typeof transform !== "object" || transform === null || Array.isArray(transform)) { ... }
if (typeof headers !== "object" || headers === null || Array.isArray(headers)) { ... }
```

Error messages are unchanged, so callers matching on them are unaffected. Strings and numbers were
already rejected; this closes the array case, and does the same for the outer `transform` for
consistency.

No comment changes.

## Testing

New: `sdk/node/test/policy-e2b-shapes.test.ts`

- rejects an array of header values (the reported case)
- rejects a string, rejects a number (regression guards for the paths that already worked)
- rejects an array `transform`
- accepts a plain header map, and accepts multiple headers in one transform with order preserved

Red/green — with `policy.ts` reverted:

```
× convertE2BPerHostRules transform.headers validation > rejects an array of header values
  Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
```

with the fix, and the whole SDK suite:

```
$ npx vitest run
Test Files  16 passed | 1 skipped (17)
     Tests  192 passed | 1 skipped (193)
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npx vitest run` — 192 passed (`sdk-test-check`).

title: [Bug Report] Node SDK accepts transform.headers as an array, injecting credentials under header names "0" and "1"

labels.name: area/CubeNet
labels.description: Impacts the CubeNet module and network-agent

body:
## Summary

The Node SDK guards `transform.headers` with `typeof headers !== "object"`, which is **true for arrays**,
so an array of secret values is accepted and turned into injects with header names `"0"`, `"1"`, …. The
Python SDK rejects the same input.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: single-node / cluster
- Relevant component: sdk/node (and CubeEgress policy validation)

## Steps to Reproduce

```ts
convertE2BPerHostRules({
  "api.example.com": [{ transform: { headers: ["sk-secret-1", "sk-secret-2"] } }],
});
```

## Expected Behavior

Rejected with `transform.headers must be an object`, as the Python SDK does.

## Actual Behavior

Accepted, producing garbage header names:

```
NODE  |headers as ARRAY|ACCEPTED|[{"header":"0","secret":"sk-secret-1"},{"header":"1","secret":"sk-secret-2"}]
PYTHON|headers as ARRAY|REJECTED|network.rules transform.headers must be a dict, got list
```

And the server does not catch it either — `validate_policy` only requires `inj.header` to be a non-empty
string, and `"0"` qualifies:

```
server validate_policy(header="0"/"1") -> ok=true err=nil
```

So the malformed policy is accepted end to end and `ngx.req.set_header("0", secret)` runs: the operator's
credential goes upstream under a meaningless header name instead of the request being rejected.

## Additional Context

- `sdk/node/src/policy.ts:126-157` — `convertE2BTransformToInject`; `typeof [] === "object"` in JS, so
  the array passes, and `Object.entries(["a","b"])` yields `[["0","a"],["1","b"]]`.
- `sdk/python/cubesandbox/_policy.py:209-243` — uses `isinstance(headers, dict)`, which rejects lists.
- `CubeEgress/lua/policy.lua:100-106` — server-side header validation is non-empty-string only.

Strings and numbers were already rejected by the Node guard; only arrays slipped through.

title: sdk: make render() previews match the data plane's single substitution
body:
Closes #1466.

## Motivation

`Inject.render()` exists to show the operator the header value that will actually be sent. The Go and
Python implementations substituted **every** `${SECRET}` occurrence, but CubeEgress substitutes only the
**first** (`access_phase.lua:171` passes `1` as `gsub`'s count limit). For a format like
`Basic ${SECRET}:${SECRET}` the preview said `Basic tok:tok` while the upstream received
`Basic tok:${SECRET}`.

## What this changes

Aligns the two outliers with the server:

- `sdk/go/policy.go` — `strings.ReplaceAll(...)` → `strings.Replace(..., 1)`
- `sdk/python/cubesandbox/_policy.py` — `fmt.replace(...)` → `fmt.replace(..., 1)`

The Node SDK already matches (JS `String.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first), and the
server is unchanged.

No comment changes.

## Why change the SDKs rather than the server

Two of the four implementations already do single substitution, and the server's explicit `1` limit plus
its "format has no ${SECRET} placeholder" warning read as a deliberate single-substitution contract.
More importantly, changing the server would alter the header value emitted for any existing policy that
repeats the placeholder — a live data-plane change. Changing a preview helper cannot break traffic.

If the maintainers would rather the contract be "replace all", the change is dropping the `1` in
`access_phase.lua:171` and reverting these two lines; the tests here document the contract either way so
the decision is visible.

## Testing

New:

- `sdk/go/policy_render_test.go` — `TestInjectRenderMatchesServerSubstitution`, table-driven over the six
  cases from the issue including the default (empty) format, a `%`-containing secret, and a format with
  no placeholder.
- `sdk/python/tests/test_policy_render.py` — the same table.

Red/green, per SDK:

```
Go, with policy.go reverted:
  --- FAIL: TestInjectRenderMatchesServerSubstitution
      policy_render_test.go:27: Render() = "Basic tok:tok", want "Basic tok:${SECRET}"
      policy_render_test.go:27: Render() = "tok-tok-tok", want "tok-${SECRET}-${SECRET}"
Go, with the fix:
  ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/sdk/go  0.820s

Python, with _policy.py reverted:
  FAILED tests/test_policy_render.py::test_render_matches_server_substitution
Python, with the fix:
  1 passed in 0.03s
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l .` in `sdk/go` — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `go build ./...` in `sdk/go` — clean.
- `sdk-test-check` covers the SDK suites; both new tests sit in the existing test locations.

## Risk / rollout

None to the data plane. The only behaviour change is that `render()` now returns the same string the
server produces. Anyone who was relying on `render()` to expand a repeated placeholder was getting a
value the server never emitted.

title: [Bug Report] SDK render() previews disagree with the data plane when the inject format repeats ${SECRET}

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update python code

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

body:
## Summary

The Go and Python SDK `render()` preview helpers substitute **every** `${SECRET}` in an inject format,
while CubeEgress (the data plane) substitutes only the **first**. An operator previewing such a format
sees a header value the sandbox's upstream will never receive.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: single-node / cluster
- Relevant component: sdk/go, sdk/python (vs CubeEgress)

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from cubesandbox import Inject
Inject(header="Authorization", secret="tok", format="Basic ${SECRET}:${SECRET}").render()
```

and compare against what CubeEgress emits for the same rule.

## Expected Behavior

`render()` shows exactly what will be sent.

## Actual Behavior

Four-way differential over the real implementations:

| format | secret | CubeEgress (data plane) | Go SDK | Python SDK | Node SDK |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `${SECRET}` | tok | `tok` | `tok` | `tok` | `tok` |
| `Bearer ${SECRET}` | tok | `Bearer tok` | `Bearer tok` | `Bearer tok` | `Bearer tok` |
| `Basic ${SECRET}:${SECRET}` | tok | `Basic tok:${SECRET}` | **`Basic tok:tok`** | **`Basic tok:tok`** | `Basic tok:${SECRET}` |
| `${SECRET}-${SECRET}-${SECRET}` | tok | `tok-${SECRET}-${SECRET}` | **`tok-tok-tok`** | **`tok-tok-tok`** | `tok-${SECRET}-${SECRET}` |
| `Bearer ${SECRET}` | `a%2Fb` | `Bearer a%2Fb` | `Bearer a%2Fb` | `Bearer a%2Fb` | `Bearer a%2Fb` |

So the operator previews a fully-substituted credential while the upstream receives one that still
contains a literal `${SECRET}` — a broken credential plus a placeholder leaked into the header.

## Additional Context

- Server: `CubeEgress/lua/access_phase.lua:171` — `string.gsub(fmt, "%${SECRET}", escaped, 1)`, note the
  `1` limit.
- Go: `sdk/go/policy.go:41` — `strings.ReplaceAll`.
- Python: `sdk/python/cubesandbox/_policy.py:71` — `str.replace` with no count.
- Node: `sdk/node/src/policy.ts:87` — `String.replace` with a string pattern, which replaces only the
  first and therefore already matches the server.

The server's `%` escaping is correct and round-trips secrets containing `%` — that part is not a bug
(see the `a%2Fb` row).

title: cubemaster: fix ceiling division in the scheduler concurrency limits
body:
Closes #1464.

## Motivation

Three limit calculations were written as `int64(math.Ceil(float64(a * b * 1.0 / c)))`. Every operand
is `int64` and the untyped constant `1.0` is representable as an integer, so it converts to `int64`
and the whole inner expression is **integer** arithmetic — it truncates. `math.Ceil` then runs on an
already-integral value and does nothing.

The `* 1.0` factors show the intent was float division and round-up. What actually happens is
round-down, so whenever the node counts do not divide evenly the cluster runs one unit below its
configured create/destroy concurrency.

## What this changes

`CubeMaster/pkg/scheduler/local.go` — convert to `float64` *before* dividing, at all three sites:

| line | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `:283` | `float64(totalLimitCreate*1.0/newHealthyNodes)` | `float64(totalLimitCreate)/float64(newHealthyNodes)` |
| `:286` | `float64(newHealthyNodes * newCreateLimitOfEveryNode * 1.0 / newMasterNodes)` | `float64(newHealthyNodes*newCreateLimitOfEveryNode) / float64(newMasterNodes)` |
| `:309` | `float64(newHealthyNodes * newLimitDesroyOfEveryNode * 1.0 / newMasterNodes)` | `float64(newHealthyNodes*newLimitDesroyOfEveryNode) / float64(newMasterNodes)` |

The numerator product stays in `int64` (it is a small count product, nowhere near overflow) and only
the division becomes floating point, which is the minimal change that makes `math.Ceil` meaningful.

No comment changes.

## Testing

New: `CubeMaster/pkg/scheduler/local_limit_math_test.go` — table tests pinning the rounding for both
shapes, including the exact cases from the issue (`10/3 → 4`, `4*5/3 → 7`) plus exact-division and
`n < divisor` cases so a future refactor cannot silently reintroduce truncation.

```
$ docker run --rm ... -w /w/CubeMaster golang:1.26 go test -short ./pkg/scheduler/...
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/scheduler         0.004s
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/scheduler/selctx  0.002s
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l ./pkg` — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `GOOS=linux go build ./...` — clean.
- `staticcheck -checks 'SA4015' ./pkg/scheduler/` — the three `local.go` findings are gone.

## Risk / rollout

Behaviour change by design: create and destroy concurrency will increase by one unit in clusters
where the division was not exact. That is the configured intent, but it does mean slightly more
in-flight work per node after this lands — worth noting if a cluster was unknowingly relying on the
lower effective limit.

`pkg/selector/score/realtimescore_test.go:40-41` has the same `math.Ceil`-on-integer pattern in a
**test**; left alone here to keep this PR single-purpose.

title: [Bug Report] Broken ceiling division silently rounds CubeMaster's create/destroy concurrency limits down
body:
## Summary

Three `math.Ceil` calls in the scheduler's concurrency-limit loop operate on integer division that
has already truncated, so the limits are rounded **down** instead of up.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a — control-plane only
- Deployment mode: cluster (any node/master count where the division is not exact)
- Relevant component: CubeMaster

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a cluster where the node counts do not divide evenly — e.g. 3 healthy nodes with a total
   create limit of 10, or 4 healthy nodes and 3 healthy masters.
2. Watch the `monitorLimit,limitCreate:<product>:<n>` / `monitorLimit,limitDestroy:<n>` warn lines
   emitted by `CubeMaster/pkg/scheduler/local.go:289` and `:311`.
3. Compare the reported value against the intended ceiling.

## Expected Behavior

The limits round up, which is what the `math.Ceil` calls and the `* 1.0` factors were written to do.
For 10 total across 3 nodes the per-node create limit should be `4`.

## Actual Behavior

The value is rounded down — `3` for that case. Reproduced with the exact expressions from those
lines:

```
local.go:283  totalLimitCreate=10 nodes=3
  as written : int64(math.Ceil(float64(a*1.0/b)))        = 3
  intended   : int64(math.Ceil(float64(a)/float64(b)))   = 4

local.go:286/309  nodes=4 perNode=5 masters=3
  as written : 6
  intended   : 7

inner expr type check: a*1.0/b with int64 operands truncates -> 3 (not 3.3333)
```

## Additional Context

All operands are `int64`. The untyped constant `1.0` is representable as an integer, so it converts
to `int64` and the entire inner expression is integer arithmetic — it truncates. Only the
already-truncated result is converted to `float64`, so `math.Ceil` is a no-op.

Affected lines in `CubeMaster/pkg/scheduler/local.go`:

- `:283` — `newCreateLimitOfEveryNode`
- `:286` — `limitCreate`, fed to `setBufferTaskConcurrent`
- `:309` — `limitDestroy`, fed to `task.SetTaskWorkerConcurrent(task.DestroySandbox, ...)`

`staticcheck` flags all three as `SA4015` — "calling math.Ceil on a converted integer is pointless".

Impact is capacity rather than correctness: whenever the division is not exact the cluster runs one
unit below its configured create/destroy concurrency, silently and permanently.

title: cubemaster: stop shadowing err when parsing container resource quantities
body:
Closes #1462.

## Motivation

`getReqResource` has a named return `err`, but the loop body used `:=` when calling
`resource.ParseQuantity`, which declares a *new* `err` scoped to the loop body. The
`err = fmt.Errorf(...)` assignments therefore wrote to that shadow and were discarded at `break`,
leaving the named return `nil`.

Consequence: a `CreateCubeSandbox` request with an unparseable `cpu` or `mem` string was admitted as
consuming `cpu=0, mem=0`. Those values flow through `checkAndGetReqResource` into
`selctx.RequestResource`, which is what the scheduler filters on — so the sandbox passed every
resource filter and could land on any node regardless of its real footprint.

The `ctr.Resources == nil` branch a few lines above uses plain `=` on the named return and worked
correctly, which is what made the bug easy to miss.

## What this changes

`CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/util.go` — the two `ParseQuantity` calls now use distinct error
variables (`cpuErr`, `memErr`) so the `fmt.Errorf` assignments land on the named return:

```go
ctncpuQuantity, cpuErr := resource.ParseQuantity(ctr.Resources.Cpu)
if cpuErr != nil {
    err = fmt.Errorf("parse container %q cpu limit: %w", ctr.Name, cpuErr)
    break
}
```

Three lines, no behaviour change on the success path, no comment changes.

## Testing

New: `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/util_resource_parse_test.go`

- `TestGetReqResourceRejectsUnparseableQuantities` — three sub-cases (bad cpu, bad mem, both); each
  asserts a non-nil error that names both the offending field and the container.
- `TestGetReqResourceSumsValidQuantities` — regression guard that valid multi-container quantities
  still sum correctly (`750m` / `512Mi`).

```
$ docker run --rm ... -w /w/CubeMaster golang:1.26 go test -short -v -run TestGetReqResource ./pkg/service/sandbox/
--- PASS: TestGetReqResourceRejectsUnparseableQuantities
--- PASS: TestGetReqResourceSumsValidQuantities
--- PASS: TestGetReqResourceRejectsCPUOverflowWhenMemIsValid        (pre-existing)
--- PASS: TestGetReqResourceRejectsCPUOverflowBeforeMemOverflow     (pre-existing)
ok  github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l ./pkg` — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `GOOS=linux go build ./...` — clean.
- `staticcheck -checks 'SA*' ./pkg/service/sandbox/` — the `SA4006` / `SA4017` findings on
  `util.go:168` and `:173` are gone.

## Pre-existing failure, unrelated to this change

Running the whole `pkg/service/sandbox` package in Linux (as `make test` does) shows one failure:

```
--- FAIL: TestValidatePauseResumeVolumesPresent
```

I confirmed this is **pre-existing on master**, not introduced here:

- passes in isolation (`-run TestValidatePauseResumeVolumesPresent`) on both master and this branch;
- fails when the full package runs, on **master** as well as this branch.

It looks like cross-test state pollution within the package. Not fixed here to keep this PR
single-purpose; worth its own issue.

(On macOS the package additionally cannot run at all — `gomonkey` cannot patch binaries on darwin —
so Linux is the only meaningful local target, matching CI.)

title: [Bug Report] Shadowed err makes CubeMaster accept malformed cpu/mem as 0/0, bypassing scheduler resource filters
body:
## Summary

`getReqResource` declares a new `err` with `:=` inside its loop, shadowing the named return, so an
unparseable `cpu` or `mem` string is accepted as `cpu=0, mem=0` instead of being rejected.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a — control-plane only
- Deployment mode: single-node / cluster
- Relevant component: CubeMaster

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a `CreateCubeSandbox` request whose container resources contain an unparseable quantity, e.g.
   `{"containers":[{"name":"c1","resources":{"cpu":"not-a-quantity","mem":"512Mi"}}]}`
2. Observe that the request is admitted rather than rejected with a parameter error.
3. The scheduler receives `Cpu=0, Mem=0` for that sandbox.

## Expected Behavior

`400`-class parameter error naming the offending container and field, as already happens for
`resources: null`.

## Actual Behavior

The request is admitted with zero resources. Reproduced against the real function:

```
unparseable cpu    cpu="not-a-quantity" mem="512Mi" -> returned err=<nil>, cpu=0 mem=0
unparseable mem    cpu="500m" mem="10 GB"           -> returned err=<nil>, cpu=0 mem=0
both bad           cpu="abc" mem="def"              -> returned err=<nil>, cpu=0 mem=0

Resources==nil -> err=request Resources nil    (this branch works)
```

Note even the valid `mem: "512Mi"` is lost, because the loop `break`s before `mem.Add`.

## Additional Context

`CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/util.go:157-182`:

```go
func getReqResource(req *types.CreateCubeSandboxReq) (cpu, mem resource.Quantity, err error) {
    for _, ctr := range req.Containers {
        if ctr.Resources == nil {
            err = ret.Err(...)                                    // plain `=` -> works
            break
        }
        ctncpuQuantity, err := resource.ParseQuantity(...)         // `:=` declares a NEW err
        if err != nil {
            err = fmt.Errorf("parse container %q cpu limit: %w", ...)  // writes the SHADOW
            break
        }
        ...
    }
    if err != nil {                                               // the OUTER err -> still nil
        return cpu, mem, err
    }
```

Impact path: the sole caller `checkAndGetReqResource` (`util.go:46-52`) feeds these values into
`selctx.RequestResource{Cpu, Mem}` — the values the scheduler uses for fit and capacity filtering.
A sandbox declared with a malformed quantity therefore passes every resource filter and can be
placed on any node regardless of its real footprint.

`staticcheck` flags both lines: `SA4006` ("this value of err is never used") and `SA4017`
("Errorf doesn't have side effects and its return value is ignored").

title: ci: run the race detector for the modules that are already race-clean
body:
Closes #1460.

## Motivation

Nothing in the repo passes `-race` to `go test`, so concurrency bugs ship undetected. Enabling it surfaces
12 races and 12 failing tests today — five of the races in production code, including a torn `interface{}`
read in `CubeMaster/pkg/base/localcache`.

## What this changes

Adds `-race` to the four modules that are **already clean**, so this can land immediately without waiting on
any fix:

| target | file |
|---|---|
| `cubelog-test` | `Makefile:356` |
| `cubedb-test` | `Makefile:360` |
| `cube-lifecycle-manager-test` | `Makefile:364` |
| Go SDK | `tests/unittest/run_sdk_test.sh:72` |

Nothing else changes — same packages, same flags otherwise.

## Deliberately staged

`cubeops-test`, `cubemaster-test` and `cubelet-pkg-test` are **not** switched on here, because they are red
today and this PR would fail CI on arrival. They should be enabled as a follow-up once the corresponding
fixes land:

| target | blocked on |
|---|---|
| `cubeops-test` | the `cachingFakeFetchOnly` map-read race in `internal/handler/store_test.go` |
| `cubemaster-test` | the five `localcache` production races, plus the `queueworker` / `recov` / `bufferqueue` test races |
| `cubelet-pkg-test` | the `queueworker` / `recov` test races |

Each of those has its own branch. Landing this PR first means the gate exists and every *new* module or
package added to these four targets is race-checked from day one.

## Testing

All four gated modules verified clean under the detector:

```
cubelog                  0  <- races + failures
CubeDB                   0
cube-lifecycle-manager   0
sdk/go                   0
```

(`go test -race -count=1 ./...` per module, counting `WARNING: DATA RACE` and `FAIL` lines.)

## Cost

`-race` typically costs 2-5x runtime and ~5-10x memory. These four are the small, fast modules — the ones
whose runtime is dominated by process startup rather than the tests themselves — so the CI impact is
minimal. The expensive modules (CubeMaster, Cubelet) are the ones deliberately left for the follow-up, which
is a good moment to measure the real cost before committing to it.

`cubelog-test` keeps `-short`, so the long-running cases stay skipped.

title: cubeegress: validate match field types, and make rule_matches fail closed
body:
Closes #1458.

## Motivation

`validate_policy` verified that `rule.match` is a table and stopped there. `rule_matches` then called
`string.upper` on each `match.method` entry and `string.lower` on `match.scheme`, so a policy the admin API
had accepted produced an uncaught Lua error inside `access_by_lua_block` — nginx 500 for every request from
that sandbox, with nothing pointing at the policy as the cause.

## What this changes

Two layers, because either alone leaves a gap.

**1. `CubeEgress/lua/policy.lua` — reject malformed policies at install time.** `validate_policy` now
requires `match.sni` / `match.host` / `match.path` / `match.scheme` to be strings when present, and
`match.method` to be an array of strings. Errors name the rule index and the field, matching the existing
message style. An empty `match = {}` is still allowed, as documented.

**2. `CubeEgress/lua/access_phase.lua` — make `rule_matches` fail closed.** A non-string `method` entry is
skipped rather than passed to `string.upper`, and a non-string `scheme` returns no-match rather than being
passed to `string.lower`. This matters because a policy can reach the shared dict without going through
`validate_policy` (bootstrap load, or anything written directly), and the data plane should deny rather than
500 in that case.

No comment changes.

## Testing

**Install-time validation** — all 11 cases behave as intended, where master accepted 8 of them:

```
                                   this branch          master
match.method = [ {} ]              rejected             accepted
match.method = [ 1 ]               rejected             accepted
match.method = "GET"               rejected             accepted
match.scheme = {}                  rejected             accepted
match.scheme = 80                  rejected             accepted
match.host   = {}                  rejected             accepted
match.path   = {}                  rejected             accepted
match.sni    = 12345               rejected             accepted
match.method = {} (empty object)   accepted             accepted
match = {} (empty, allowed)        accepted             accepted
valid full match                   accepted             accepted
```

with messages like `rules[1].match.method[1] must be a string`.

**Request-path hardening** — driving the real `rule_matches` via its exported `_rule_matches` hook:

```
                     master                               this branch
method = [ {} ]      LUA ERROR -> nginx 500               returned false (deny)
scheme = {}          LUA ERROR -> nginx 500               returned false (deny)
method = [ 1 ]       returned false                       returned false
scheme = 80          returned false                       returned false
host/path/sni bad    returned false                       returned false
                     LUA ERRORS: 2                        NO LUA ERRORS
```

**Matching semantics unchanged** — the same harness checks the normal cases, and the credential-injection
harness from the HTTP-inject issue is re-run as a regression check:

```
valid match (should be true)      -> true
non-matching method (false)       -> false
empty match (matches anything)    -> true

1. HTTPS, Host==SNI (legit)              allow=true  injected=sk-live-REAL-OPERATOR-CREDENTIAL
2. HTTPS, Host!=SNI (G4 blocks)          allow=true  injected=<none>
3. HTTP, spoofed Host -> attacker dst_ip allow=true  injected=sk-live-REAL-OPERATOR-CREDENTIAL
```

Case 3 is the separate plaintext-injection issue, tracked on its own branch — unchanged here, and shown so it
is clear this PR did not alter it.

CI gates: the Lua files are not covered by `fmt-check` (no Lua formatter configured) or by
`unit-test-check`. Verification is via LuaJIT against the real modules, as above.

## Risk / rollout

A `PUT` that previously returned `200` for a malformed rule now returns `400`. Any control-plane component
pushing such a rule would start seeing failures — but those rules were producing 500s on the data plane
anyway, so surfacing the error at install time is strictly better.

title: [Bug Report] CubeEgress accepts wrong-typed match.method / match.scheme, then returns nginx 500 for every request from that sandbox

labels.name: area/CubeNet
labels.description: Impacts the CubeNet module and network-agent

body:
## Summary

`validate_policy` checks that `rule.match` is a table but never checks the types of the fields inside it.
`rule_matches` then calls `string.upper` / `string.lower` on them, so a policy the admin API accepted causes
an uncaught Lua error at request time and nginx returns 500.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: `5960c56` (master)
- Host OS and kernel version: any
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): n/a
- Deployment mode: single-node / cluster
- Relevant component: CubeEgress

## Steps to Reproduce

```
curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:9091/admin/v1/policies/169.254.68.6 -d '{
  "policy_id": "p1",
  "rules": [{"id": "r1", "match": {"method": [{}]}, "action": {"allow": true}}]
}'
```

The API returns `200 {"ok":true}`. Every subsequent request from that sandbox returns 500.

## Expected Behavior

The `PUT` is rejected with a 400 naming the offending field.

## Actual Behavior

The policy is stored, and at request time:

```
match.method = [ {} ]   LUA ERROR -> nginx 500: bad argument #1 to 'upper' (string expected, got table)
match.scheme = {}       LUA ERROR -> nginx 500: bad argument #1 to 'lower' (string expected, got table)
```

Only these two shapes error; the other wrong-typed fields happen to fail closed to 403:

```
match.method = [ 1 ]    returned false (deny)
match.scheme = 80       returned false (deny)
match.host   = {}       returned false (deny)
match.path   = {}       returned false (deny)
match.sni    = 12345    returned false (deny)
```

## Additional Context

- `CubeEgress/lua/policy.lua:82-84` — `validate_policy` stops at "match is a table"; the comment says
  "empty {} allowed", and the field types are never checked.
- `CubeEgress/lua/access_phase.lua:139` — `string.upper(mm)` over `m.method`.
- `CubeEgress/lua/access_phase.lua:147` — `string.lower(m.scheme)`.

It fails **closed** — no traffic is allowed through — so this is availability and diagnosability rather than
a policy bypass. The operator sees 500s with no indication that the policy they installed is malformed.

title: cubemaster: log score-plugin failures instead of silently skipping them
body:
Closes #1456.

## Motivation

`runScoreFilter` swallowed score-plugin errors with a bare `continue`. A plugin failing on every call
looked exactly like a disabled one, and because `totalPluginWeight` only accumulates for plugins that
returned results, a persistently failing plugin silently drops out of the weighted average and skews
placement — with nothing in the log to explain it.

The filter stage already reports its failures (`schedule.go:127`), so this was an inconsistency
between the two stages.

## What this changes

`CubeMaster/pkg/scheduler/schedule.go` — one line added to the existing error branch:

```go
if tmpResult, err := f.Select(selCtx); err != nil {
    log.G(selCtx.Ctx).Warnf("runScoreFilter_skipped, selector: %s, err: %v", f.ID(), err)
    continue
} else {
```

`f.ID()` is part of the `score.Selector` interface (`pkg/selector/score/init.go:21`), so the plugin is
named in the log. The message shape follows the existing `runFilter_failed` convention. Warn level
matches `runFilter`.

Scoring behaviour is unchanged — this is observability only.

No comment changes.

## Testing

No new test: the change adds a log line inside an existing branch and alters no logic, so there is no
new behaviour to pin. Existing coverage for the scoring path continues to pass.

```
$ docker run --rm ... -w /w/CubeMaster golang:1.26 go test -short ./pkg/scheduler/... ./pkg/selector/...
ok  .../pkg/scheduler          ok  .../pkg/scheduler/selctx
ok  .../pkg/selector/filter    ok  .../pkg/selector/score
```

CI gates checked locally:

- `gofmt -l ./pkg/scheduler` — clean (`fmt-check`).
- `GOOS=linux go build ./pkg/scheduler/` — clean.

## Related, not fixed here

`parallelRunFilters` discards the context returned by `errgroup.WithContext`
(`schedule.go:139`), so filter goroutines never observe cancellation when a sibling fails. Left out to
keep this PR to one concern; tracked with the scheduler filter-intersection issue.

```go

} else {
```
