title: [Bug Report] AgentHub CreateInstance falls back to a hardcoded template identifier "wecom-ds-openclaw" that nothing provisions
body:
## Summary

`AgentHubService.CreateInstance` falls back to the hardcoded template identifier `"wecom-ds-openclaw"` when the caller omits `templateId`, but nothing in this repository ever provisions a template under that identifier — so on a self-hosted install, creating an agent without an explicit `templateId` always fails with an opaque `130404`.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: installed `v0.6.0-amd64`; defect verified present on `master` @ `9f1d914a`
- Host OS and kernel version: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, `Linux 5.15.0-168-generic x86_64`
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): `/lib/modules/5.15.0-168-generic/kernel/arch/x86/kvm/kvm.ko`
- Deployment mode: single-node (one-click `control`, all-in-one)
- Relevant component: CubeOps (AgentHub)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install single-node CubeSandbox and confirm no AgentHub template is registered yet:

   ```console
   $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://<host>:<cubeops>/api/v1/agenthub/templates
   []
   ```

2. Create an agent without an explicit `templateId` — exactly what the Dashboard's AgentHub "create" dialog sends when its template selector has nothing to select (`templateId: L || void 0`):

   ```console
   $ curl -X POST http://<host>:<cubeops>/api/v1/agenthub/instances \
       -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
       --data-raw '{"name":"demo","engine":"openclaw","persistenceMode":"shared_files"}'
   ```

## Expected Behavior

Either the request succeeds against a sensible default template, or it fails with an actionable message telling the operator that no agent template is registered and how to register one.

## Actual Behavior

```
failed to create sandbox: cubemaster error 130404: failed to resolve template identifier "wecom-ds-openclaw": template not found
```

The error names an identifier the caller never supplied and cannot act on.

The fallback is `CubeOps/internal/service/agenthub.go:441` on `master`:

```go
} else {
    if req.TemplateID != "" {
        rootfsSourceID = req.TemplateID
    } else {
        rootfsSourceID = "wecom-ds-openclaw"
    }
}
```

`"wecom-ds-openclaw"` is a bare literal — not a constant, not configurable, not looked up. `rootfsSourceID` is handed straight to CubeMaster, whose `ResolveTemplateIdentifier` passes through `tpl-`/`snap-` prefixed ids and otherwise resolves via `GetTemplateByAlias` (`CubeMaster/pkg/templatecenter/store.go:956`, used at `:990`). So the fallback can only ever resolve on an install where somebody has claimed exactly that template alias.

Nothing in the tree does that. `"wecom-ds-openclaw"` occurs in three places, all of which *assume* it already exists:

| Location | What it does |
|---|---|
| `CubeOps/internal/service/agenthub.go:441` | the fallback above |
| `docs/guide/digital-assistant.md:17` (and `docs/zh/…`) | "A custom template must be built from the same … image as `wecom-ds-openclaw`" |
| `CubeAPI/scripts/test-cube-api.sh:26` | `TEMPLATE_ID="${TEMPLATE_ID:-wecom-ds-openclaw}"` |

There is no seed, no migration, and no install step that creates it. The Dashboard's own template-market flow does not either: it builds the template via `POST /templates` (which returns a generated `tpl-*` and claims no alias) and then registers that `tpl-*` id into AgentHub. On our install both market templates came back with `"aliases": []`:

```json
{"templateID":"tpl-428c48e7…","imageInfo":"…/demo/lightweight-openclaw-deepseek-wecom:latest@sha256:…","status":"READY","aliases":[]}
{"templateID":"tpl-6a7e6252…","imageInfo":"…/demo/aio-sandbox-envd-openclaw:latest@sha256:…","status":"READY","aliases":[]}
```

It looks like a name from an internal environment that leaked into the default path, the docs, and a test script.

Worth noting: `t_agenthub_template` already carries a `recommended` flag (`CubeOps/internal/store/agenthub.go:441`), and the Dashboard sets `recommended: true` on every market registration — but `CreateInstance` never consults it. Selecting the recommended registered template is the behaviour the schema already anticipates.

## Additional Context

Secondary observation on how an install ends up with zero registered templates while cube templates exist: in the Dashboard's Store flow, "build template" and "register into AgentHub" are two client-side steps — the page builds the template, polls `GET /templates` on a `setInterval` until `READY`, and only then issues `POST /agenthub/templates/market`. The interval is cleared on unmount. The market images are 2.6 GB (`openclaw-lite`) and 6.35 GB (`openclaw-aio`), so navigating away during the pull leaves the template `READY` on CubeMaster and absent from AgentHub, with no server-side reconciliation. That is exactly the state we hit. Re-clicking the entry on the Store page recovers it, but nothing tells the operator that is what is needed — the failure surfaces later, in the create dialog, as the `130404` above.

Happy to send a PR: resolve the default from the registered AgentHub templates (recommended first, most recent otherwise), keep the literal as a last resort so any environment that does have that alias is unaffected, and turn the resulting not-found into an actionable `400` when the unprovisioned fallback was the one that was used.

title: [Feature Request] Route auto-resume through CubeAPI for policy and quota enforcement
body:
## Background

We are designing an external Policy Gateway to enforce per-tenant limits, initially:

- Maximum total sandboxes
- Maximum running sandboxes

Create and user-initiated resume requests can be admitted through CubeAPI. However, the current auto-resume path is:

CubeProxy -> cube-lifecycle-manager -> CubeMaster

This bypasses CubeAPI and any policy or quota checks implemented there. As a result, a paused sandbox may auto-resume even when the tenant has already reached its running-sandbox limit. Reconciliation can correct the counter afterward, but cannot prevent the quota violation.

## Proposal

Route auto-resume through an internal CubeAPI endpoint:

CubeProxy -> cube-lifecycle-manager -> CubeAPI -> Policy Gateway -> CubeMaster

The lifecycle manager would continue to own resume locking and request coalescing. CubeAPI would perform policy admission before calling CubeMaster, then commit or release the quota reservation based on the result.

This keeps CubeMaster unaware of tenants and quotas.

## Questions

1. Does the community agree that auto-resume should pass through CubeAPI?
2. Would making the lifecycle manager depend on CubeAPI introduce any concerns?
3. Would a policy admission hook inside the lifecycle manager be preferable?

title: feat(examples): add derived sandbox-code image with run_code env inheritance
body:
## Motivation

PR #566 made sandbox create-time environment variables available to envd-backed command execution, so `commands.run` now observes create-time environment variables correctly.

However, `run_code` still behaves differently. The bundled lightweight code interpreter does not load create-time values from envd, so code executed through `run_code` cannot see environment variables that were provided when the sandbox was created.

This means `commands.run` and `run_code` can observe different environments in the same sandbox. That is surprising for users who configure API keys, feature flags, or runtime settings at sandbox creation time.

This PR adds a derived `sandbox-code` example image that lets the lightweight code interpreter inherit sandbox create-time environment variables, while keeping per-call `run_code` environment overrides temporary and scoped to a single execution.

The per-call lifecycle follows [e2b-dev/code-interpreter#141](https://github.com/e2b-dev/code-interpreter/pull/141): inject environment values into the user execution, clean them up in a background execution, and make the next request wait for cleanup.

Fixes #565.
Follow-up to #566.

## What Changed

* Added `examples/run-code-env-inheritance/`, a derived image based on the official `sandbox-code` image.
* Replaced only `/opt/lightweight-code-interpreter/server.py` in the derived image.
* Loaded create-time environment variables from envd once per Jupyter kernel and applied environment setup in a separate background execution before unchanged user code.
* Marked sandbox-level values as applied only after environment setup succeeds, so a compilation failure in the first user cell does not suppress later initialization.
* Preserved per-call override behavior by applying `env` and `env_vars` after create-time values.
* Snapshotted prior kernel values for per-call keys, restored existing values after execution, removed only previously absent keys, and made the next execution wait for cleanup.
* Rolled back the per-call snapshot immediately when background environment setup fails, while leaving sandbox initialization retryable on the next execution.
* Disabled Jupyter history storage for silent setup and cleanup executions.
* Made the envd fetch timeout configurable through `ENVD_TIMEOUT`, while preserving fail-fast HTTP 502 behavior for unavailable or invalid `/envs` responses.
* Added focused interpreter tests for envd loading, caching, precedence, prior-value restoration, first-cell compilation failures, cleanup, retry behavior, and invalid envd responses.
* Extended shared SDK compatibility adapters with optional per-call `run_code` environment support.
* Added shared E2E cases for both E2B and CubeSandbox backends, covering temporary per-call restoration and first-cell syntax failures. They are disabled by default and skip before sandbox creation unless `SDK_E2E_RUN_CODE_ENV_INHERITANCE=true` is explicitly set for a compatible template.
* Updated English and Chinese SDK compatibility documentation and example instructions, including registry-backed and one-click local-image template creation paths.

## Validation

* Derived-image interpreter tests: 14 passed.
* Default SDK compatibility behavior without the opt-in flag: 4 skipped before sandbox creation.
* Opt-in SDK compatibility E2E through E2B and CubeSandbox: 4 passed.
* Built the derived image, created a template, and verified:

  * create-time environment inheritance
  * temporary per-call override precedence
  * restoration of sandbox-level and kernel-defined values after per-call overrides
  * cleanup that tolerates user code deleting a per-call key
  * sandbox environment initialization before a failing first user cell
  * rollback and retry after background environment setup failure

## Scope

This PR adds an opt-in derived `sandbox-code` example image and shared compatibility coverage.

The replacement server is based on the lightweight code interpreter already bundled in the official `sandbox-code` image. Existing execution, context, restart, and timeout behavior is intentionally preserved; this example changes only sandbox environment loading and the per-call environment overlay lifecycle.

It does not modify the default `sandbox-code` image or any existing templates. Users who want this behavior need to build the derived image and create a template from it.

Create-time environment variables are read once per Jupyter kernel. This PR does not add generic environment refresh behavior. Per-call `run_code` values remain temporary overlays for a single execution.

The derived interpreter requires envd's `/envs` endpoint and fails with HTTP 502 when that dependency is unavailable or returns an invalid payload; it does not fall back to the stock interpreter behavior.

The shared environment-inheritance E2E case is disabled by default and skips before sandbox creation unless `SDK_E2E_RUN_CODE_ENV_INHERITANCE=true` is explicitly set for a compatible template.

title: feat(pause): cubecow pause/resume with shim exit and volume/host-mount support
body:
## Summary

- Unify Pause/Resume on the **cubecow CoW** path: pause snapshots use the same local CoW layout/catalog as user snapshots (no separate pausevm bypass).
- After Pause succeeds, the **shim must exit**; Resume recreates the sandbox from the pause snap (same sandboxID) instead of keeping a live paused process.
- Keep **plugin volumes** and **host-mount** working across Pause/Resume: Detach on Pause / Attach on Resume with aligned Master↔node refcounts; on pause resume reconnect virtiofs devices without remount/`exec.mount` when guest binds already exist; reject Resume if pause-detached volumes were deleted meanwhile.
- Destroy **never** resumes a paused sandbox (CoW pause already exited the shim). Pause post-cleanup uses `cube.pause.keep_tombstone` (replaces `cube.pause.skip_auto_resume`).
- Restore create-time **network policy** on Resume (egress `CubeNetworkConfig` + CubeProxy route refresh) and cover it in `sdk_compat` pause/resume network cases.

## Test plan

- [x] CubeMaster UT: `pausesnap`, `volume/refcount`, `sandbox` resume-pause validation, `sandboxlock`
- [x] Cubelet UT: CoW store helpers / pause cow / Destroy lifecycle (no resume-before-delete)

title: fix(cubenet): resolve direct on-link neighbors via ARP
body:
## Motivation

In direct egress mode, CubeVS sends outbound traffic to the node gateway MAC.

This works for off-link destinations, but on-link traffic then depends on the gateway forwarding the packet back through the same interface. On networks without that hairpin behavior, same-subnet destinations are unreachable.

## What Changed

- Pass the node's primary IPv4 mask to CubeVS to identify on-link destinations in direct mode.
- Add an LRU IP-to-MAC map for direct on-link neighbors.
- Try `bpf_fib_lookup` first. If the kernel has no neighbor, replace the packet with an ARP request and keep a pending map entry.
- Learn ARP replies only for IPs already present in the map.
- Once the MAC is learned, rewrite later packets with that MAC and send them out the node NIC.
- Keep the existing gateway-MAC path for off-link direct egress and route-aware egress.
- Keep the `from_world` dispatch path inlined so Linux 5.4 can load the DNS tail call.

A cache miss consumes the triggering packet (it becomes the ARP request). A later revalidation probe does the same. No userspace resolver or host iptables/sysctl setup is required.

## Validation

- Ran `go test -count=1 ./...` and `go vet ./...` in `CubeNet/cubevs`.
- Ran `go test -count=1 ./network/runtime/systemnet ./network/runtime` and `go vet ./network/runtime/...` in `Cubelet`.
- Tested on Ubuntu 20.04.6 with Linux `5.4.0-216-generic` on arm64:
  - Generated the CubeVS BPF objects with Go 1.24.8 and clang 14.
  - Loaded all generated BPF programs successfully.
  - Attached `from_cube` and `from_world` and confirmed that both were JIT-compiled.
  - Verified the datapath in isolated network namespaces using veth pairs:
    - On a cold neighbor miss, the first ICMP packet was converted into an ARP request.
    - The ARP reply populated the neighbor map, and the second ICMP packet succeeded.
    - On-link UDP and TCP traffic passed.
    - Packet capture showed on-link traffic using the peer MAC.
    - Off-link traffic continued to use the configured gateway MAC.

## Scope

This change only affects IPv4 on-link traffic in direct egress mode.

Off-link direct egress and route-aware egress keep their existing behavior.

Fixes #1209

Signed-off-by: jay3cx <137191587@qq.com>

title: [Bug Report] one-click install has no preflight for required kernel modules (dummy / sch_ingress / cls_bpf) or inotify limits — failures surface as unrelated runtime errors
body:
## Summary

`deploy/one-click/install.sh` has a fairly thorough preflight (glibc, cgroup v2 `cpu` controller, `/dev/kvm`, memory, XFS on `/data/cubelet`, docker + a list of shell utilities), but it **does not check the kernel modules and sysctl limits that `network-agent` and `CubeMaster` hard-require**. On a host where those happen to be absent, the install completes "successfully" and then the services fail one after another with errors that do not point at the cause.

We hit three of these back-to-back bringing up v0.6.0 on a fresh host, and each cost real debugging time because the error text is unrelated to the actual missing dependency.

## The three gaps

### 1. `dummy` module — `network-agent` panics with `operation not supported`

`network-agent` creates its gateway interface `cube-dev` as a `dummy` link. Without the module:

```
panic: operation not supported
  main.main() /workspace/network-agent/cmd/network-agent/main.go:139
```

strace shows what it actually was:

```
RTM_NEWLINK  IFLA_IFNAME="cube-dev"
             IFLA_LINKINFO -> IFLA_INFO_KIND="dummy"
  -> error = -EOPNOTSUPP
```

`modprobe dummy` fixes it. Note `deploy/one-click/lib/common.sh:1679` already refers to "cubesandbox's own dummy gateway (constant name `cube-dev`)", so the dependency is known to the code — it just is not ensured at install time.

### 2. `sch_ingress` / `cls_bpf` — `tcnl.Qdisc.Add failed`, with a misleading ifindex

Next failure:

```
network-agent init failed: tcnl.Qdisc.Add failed:
  netlink receive: no such file or directory, ifindex: 2014235
```

The `ifindex: 2014235` in that message is a red herring and cost us the most time — our host has been up long enough for the kernel ifindex counter to reach ~2M (heavy container churn), so the large value looked like the obvious suspect. It is not. Reproducing by hand makes the real cause immediate:

```
# ip link add cubetest0 type dummy
# tc qdisc add dev cubetest0 clsact
Error: Specified qdisc kind is unknown.
```

`clsact` simply is not available — `sch_ingress` is not loaded, and `request_module` autoloading did not kick in for the netlink path. Aligning the module set with a known-good host required:

```
modprobe sch_ingress cls_bpf cls_flower act_csum act_pedit
```

ENOENT from `RTM_NEWQDISC` means "no such qdisc kind module", but the error surfaced to the operator reads as if a *device* were missing, and it helpfully prints an ifindex to reinforce that reading.

### 3. `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` — CubeMaster reports `too many open files`

```
cube-sandbox-cubemaster.service: config init fail: too many open files
cube-sandbox-cubemaster.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
```

This is not a file-descriptor problem — `fs.file-max` was effectively unlimited, `fs.nr_open` 1048576, and only ~72k fds were in use. It is inotify instance exhaustion:

```
fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 128      # kernel default
root's inotify instances       = 128      # exactly at the cap
```

`inotify_init()` returns `EMFILE`, which Go surfaces as "too many open files". Any reasonably busy host (ours runs a few dozen containers plus a kubelet) sits at the default 128 cap long before CubeSandbox is installed. Raising it to 8192 fixed it instantly.

## Suggestion

A preflight block in the same place as the existing checks would have turned three separate debugging sessions into one clear error message. Something like:

- **required modules**: `dummy`, `sch_ingress`, `cls_bpf` — `modprobe` them (or fail with an explicit message naming the module and why it is needed). `cls_flower` / `act_csum` / `act_pedit` are also in the loaded set on our working host; worth confirming which of those are genuinely required vs. incidental.
- **sysctl**: warn (or raise) when `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` is at the 128 default, since CubeMaster cannot start once a host's root user has consumed them.
- **persistence**: on success, drop `/etc/modules-load.d/` and `/etc/sysctl.d/` entries so a reboot does not silently undo it. We had to add these by hand.

Independently of the preflight, the `tcnl.Qdisc.Add` error would be much easier to act on if it did not print `ifindex` for what is actually a missing-qdisc-kind condition — or if it distinguished "no such device" from "no such qdisc kind", both of which arrive as ENOENT.

## Environment

- **Version:** v0.6.0 (`release_version=v0.6.0-amd64`, `git_commit=8721dd151971ce3c2966482bbd32904ad98f378e`)
- **Deployment:** one-click, `ONE_CLICK_DEPLOY_ROLE=control`, single-node all-in-one
- **Host:** Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15.0-168-generic, Intel, `kvm_intel` with `nested=Y`, glibc 2.35
- **Notes:** host also runs an unrelated container workload and a kubelet, which is why the inotify cap was already saturated and why the ifindex counter was large. A quiet, dedicated host would likely hit gaps 1 and 2 but not 3.

All three were straightforward to fix once identified — the ask here is purely about surfacing them at install time instead of as three unrelated-looking runtime failures. Happy to send a PR adding the preflight if that shape is agreeable.

title: perf/fix(network): cut policy apply latency and harden TAP create under density
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to the network-agent → Cubelet embed refactor (#1285). This PR tightens create-path latency when network policy is enabled, and hardens TAP allocation under high-concurrency density load.
- **CubeVS policy hot path:** cache HashOfMaps inner maps and avoid per-call outer `Lookup`s that trigger `synchronize_rcu` (tens of ms). Delete policy maps on TAP destroy, and limit the DNS reaper to live ifindices so create latency with policy stays near the no-policy baseline.
- **TAP create under density:** retry dump-style netlink reads on `ErrDumpInterrupted` / `EINTR`, and stop doing a full `LinkList` on every pool-miss create — `cleanupConflictingTap` only needs a by-name lookup. This stops `EnsureNetwork` failing with "results may be incomplete or inconsistent" under concurrent create pressure.
- **Cleanup:** remove an unused Cubelet helper left over from the above changes.
- **cube-bench:** extend network-policy / warmup coverage so the latency and density paths are easier to exercise in CI/local benches.

title: feat(components): keep multiple component versions on disk for stable restore
body:
## Problem Every time CubeSandbox upgrades node components (shim, kernel, guest image, agent), it **overwrites** the files under `/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/` in place. This creates a problem: after an upgrade, **existing sandboxes and templates** that try to restore end up using the new component version — which may have changed behavior or no longer match. An upgrade silently breaks previously stable instances. ## What this PR does In one sentence: **don't delete old versions on upgrade, so existing sandboxes/templates always use the component version they were created with.** Three steps: 1. **Keep a copy on install**: when installing a component, first copy it into the `component_versions/` multi-version directory, then update the live toolbox. Old versions are not overwritten. 2. **Record on create**: when creating a sandbox or making a template, record "which version was used this time" (only the version string, not the path). 3. **Resolve by record on restore**: later, on recreate / restore, look up the file in `component_versions/` using the recorded version string. If not found, fail hard — **never silently fall back to the current latest version**. ## On-disk layout ``` /usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/ ← current (replaced on upgrade) cube-shim/ cube-kernel-scf/ cube-image/ cube-agent/ /data/cubelet/root/component_versions/ ← multi-version inventory (old versions kept) cube-shim/v0.6.0-test1/bin/containerd-shim-cube-rs cube-shim/v0.6.0-test2/bin/containerd-shim-cube-rs cube-image/v0.6.0-test1/cube-guest-image-cpu.img cube-agent/v0.6.0-test1/cube-agent.ext4 cube-kernel-scf/sha256-5df9ab5d8f8c/ ← kernel named by file content vmlinux-bm vmlinux -> vmlinux-bm variant (bm or pvm) version (sha256:5df9ab5d8f8c...) ``` For shim / image / agent, the directory name is just the version string (e.g. `v0.6.0-test1`). Kernel is special: a single release tag may include both `vmlinux-bm` and `vmlinux-pvm`, which have different bytes. If we used the version string as the directory name, replacing the kernel would overwrite the old directory. So kernel directories are named by the **first 12 hex chars of the file's sha256** — if the content changes, the directory name changes, so they never collide. ## Overall flow ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph install [Install / upgrade node] Pkg["Package / component image"] Inv["component_versions
multi-version inventory"] Live["cubetoolbox
current"] Pkg -->|"① write to inventory first"| Inv Pkg -->|"② then update current"| Live end subgraph create [Create sandbox / make template] CreateOp["Create / make template"] Coll["Collector reads live version"] CB[("CubeBox
records version string")] CreateOp --> Coll Live -.->|"Collector reads"| Coll Coll --> CB end subgraph restore [Restore sandbox / Recreate] RestoreOp["Recreate / Restore"] Ens["Ensure: look up inventory by version"] Shim["Launch shim at that path"] Fail["Error → Master reschedules"] RestoreOp --> CB CB --> Ens Ens --> Inv Ens -->|"found"| Shim Ens -->|"not found"| Fail end ``` ## Create sandbox in detail ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Master participant Cubelet participant Disk as component_versions Master->>Cubelet: Create sandbox (optional version annotations) alt request or template already has version Cubelet->>Cubelet: use annotation / template version else no version (first create) Cubelet->>Cubelet: Collector reads current live toolbox version end Cubelet->>Cubelet: write version string to CubeBox.ComponentVersions Cubelet->>Disk: Ensure(name, version) → check directory exists alt directory exists Disk-->>Cubelet: return absolute path Cubelet->>Cubelet: write annotations for Shim (kernel/image path) Cubelet->>Cubelet: launch container with that shim path else directory missing Disk-->>Cubelet: error: component version missing Note over Cubelet: no fallback to live toolbox Cubelet-->>Master: create fails, Master reschedules to a node with that version end ``` Key design: **we store version strings, not paths.** This means changing nodes or paths doesn't matter — as long as the new node has the same version directory under `component_versions/`, it finds the same files. ## What happens after an upgrade ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before [Before upgrade] S1["Sandbox A: created with v0.6.0-test1"] T1["Template T: created with v0.6.0-test1"] end subgraph upgrade [Upgrade to v0.6.0-test2] NewInv["component_versions has both versions"] NewLive["live toolbox now test2"] end subgraph after [After upgrade] S1R["Sandbox A restores → still uses test1 dir"] NewS["New sandbox B → uses test2 dir"] end S1 --> NewInv T1 --> NewInv NewInv --> S1R NewInv --> NewS ``` After upgrade: - Sandbox A restores using its recorded `v0.6.0-test1` — still the old files - New sandbox B uses the current live version `v0.6.0-test2` - Both sandboxes coexist on the same node, unaffected by each other ## Components covered | Component | Inventory directory | Files | |-----------|-------------------|-------| | cube-shim | `cube-shim//` | `bin/containerd-shim-cube-rs`, `bin/cube-runtime` | | kernel | `cube-kernel-scf/sha256-<12>/` | `vmlinux` (symlink), `vmlinux-bm`/`vmlinux-pvm` | | guest image | `cube-image//` | `cube-guest-image-cpu.img` | | agent | `cube-agent//` | `cube-agent.ext4` | ## What this PR does NOT do - **No cross-node distribution**: will not automatically sync a version to other nodes - **No remote download**: if a version is missing locally, will not pull from object storage - **No fallback**: missing version fails immediately; Master reschedules to a node that has it - How historical versions arrive on a node is up to the user/operator to sync manually ## Testing ### Automated tests (passing) - Cubelet unit tests: path / version key / Ensure / Capture / collector - one-click shell tests: `test_sync_kernel_inventory.sh`, `test_kernel_content_version.sh` - K8s shell test: `test-stage-kernel-select.sh` (inventory write, kernel dual-variant, digest-less JSON rewrite) ### Real-machine tests (one-click, 2026-08-10) Single-node one-click environment, two package versions to validate the main flow: | Scenario | Result | Notes | |----------|--------|-------| | Install version A → create template → run code | Pass | Annotation paths point to inventory A | | **After upgrade to B, create from old template** | **Pass** | Still uses A's inventory path, no drift to B | | **Hide A's shim inventory dir, then create** | **Pass** | Reports `component version missing`, no silent live fallback | | **Redo old template, create new sandbox** | **Pass** | Uses B's inventory; coexists with running A sandbox | | **Pause(A) → upgrade B → Resume** | **Partial** | Paths frozen on A at pause time; Resume failed with tap `Device or resource busy` (network device issue, not wrong multi-version path) | Follow-up packages with content-addressed kernel inventory (`v0.6.0-test3` / `test4`) were installed on the same host with create smoke test: confirmed `component_versions/cube-kernel-scf/sha256-*/` layout and sandbox kernel annotation pointing at that inventory path.

title: feat(cubelet): add in-sandbox lifecycle hooks for pause/resume
body:
## What & Why

Resolves #1308.

CubeSandbox 可以 pause（持久化 VM 内存）/ resume（恢复内存），且覆盖手动与自动（空闲超时暂停、活动到达自动恢复）两条路径。但这两次转换对沙箱内应用是**透明的**——内存被整体冷冻/解冻，应用收不到任何信号。这会撕裂应用状态：

- 暂停时内存里的脏数据、写一半的文件、半截事务、活跃的外部连接被一起冷冻；
- 恢复后，沙箱被立即报告 ready，但数据库连接可能已超时失效、缓存与外部世界已不一致、凭证已过期——客户端撞上一堆难排查的随机错误。

异步 Webhook（#642）只能事后**通知**，不能**协调或阻塞**转换；应用自己在 SDK 调用前处理则覆盖不了**自动**暂停/恢复。本 PR 增加**可选的、可在沙箱内执行**的 `prePause` / `postResume` 生命周期钩子。

## 设计

- **执行点**：手动与自动两条路径的请求最终都汇聚到 Cubelet 的 `UpdateWithPause` / `UpdateWithResume`，因此钩子插在这里即可一次性覆盖所有路径。
- **驱动方**：`envd`（`:49983`）来自外部项目 `e2b-dev/infra`，无法在本仓库修改，故钩子一律由 **Cubelet 驱动**：`exec`（复用 `collectEnvdVersion` 的 `task.Exec` 路径）或 `http`（复用 `NewRequestForHTTPGetAction`）。
- **失败策略** `ABORT`（默认）/ `IGNORE`：
  - `prePause` + ABORT 失败 → 不暂停，回滚 `PausingAt`，沙箱保持 running（可逆）。
  - `postResume` + ABORT 失败 → VM 已恢复（不可逆），返回错误但保留 running（K8s PostStart 语义）。
- **上下文**：操作 ID（`RequestID`）+ 阶段经 HTTP 头 / exec 环境变量传给钩子，便于幂等。
- **销毁路径跳过钩子**（`resumeOptions.skipHooks`）：5s 预算且沙箱即将销毁，跑 postResume 既浪费又会吞掉 ABORT。
- **向后兼容**：钩子为空时路径与改动前逐字节一致；配置了 `pre_pause` 时暂停会抑制旧的 fire-and-forget `doPreStop`（避免重复执行，销毁时仍触发）。

## 改动概览

- **proto**（Cubelet + CubeMaster 两份副本，字段号一致；protoc 28.3 重新生成）：`ExecAction` / `LifecycleHookHandler` / `HookFailurePolicy` / `LifecycleHook` / `LifecycleHooks`，`ContainerConfig.lifecycle_hooks = 22`。
- **Cubelet** `services/cubebox/lifecycle_hooks.go`（新增）：`runLifecycleHook` 派发 exec/http；装配进 `UpdateWithPause`（prePause）/ `resumeLocked`（postResume）。
- **Cubelet** `local.go`：`makeContainerConfigToSave` 保留 `LifecycleHooks`（此前逐字段拷贝时被丢弃，端到端测试发现并修复）。
- **CubeMaster**（模板级配置搬运）：`types.go` 镜像结构、`util.go` 的 `handleLifecycleHooks` 转换、`cubeboxutil.go` 无条件拷贝（**不**进 `WhitelistReqTag`——白名单语义是反的）。

## 验证

- 单元测试：Cubelet `services/cubebox` 全套（新增 `lifecycle_hooks_test.go` 覆盖 exec/http/策略/超时/no-op + doPreStop 抑制）、CubeMaster 转换测试（新增 `TestHandleLifecycleHooks`），均通过。
- 端到端（一键式部署，真实 CubeAPI）：注入钩子配置后实测——prePause `/bin/false`(ABORT) **阻止**暂停且沙箱保持 running；`/bin/true` 放行；HTTP `:49983/health` 放行；IGNORE 策略照常放行；无钩子模板 create→pause→resume→kill 无回归。

## 配置示例（模板级 container config）

```json
"lifecycle_hooks": {
  "pre_pause":   { "handler": { "exec": { "command": ["/app/flush"] } }, "timeout_ms": 5000, "failure_policy": "ABORT" },
  "post_resume": { "handler": { "http_get": { "port": 49983, "path": "/health" } }, "timeout_ms": 5000, "failure_policy": "IGNORE" }
}
```

## 范围

本 PR 实现 pause/resume 两个钩子点。机制可扩展，后续可按同样方式挂 `preSnapshot` / `postSnapshot` / `preTerminate`。create-request / SDK 覆盖、修改外部 `envd` 不在本 PR 范围。

---
设计文档与对抗性评审记录见 worktree 内 `docs/plans/issue-1308-lifecycle-hooks.md`（未纳入本提交）。

title: fix(cubemaster): stop reporting node cache size as error
body:
## Motivation

CubeMaster periodically reconciles node metadata into its local cache. After each reconciliation, it unconditionally logs the cache size at ERROR level, even when synchronization succeeds and all cached nodes are healthy.

This creates a recurring false error signal and makes real synchronization failures harder to distinguish from normal cache refreshes.

## Current Behavior

For example, a v0.6.0 CubeMaster emitted a log with the following relevant fields after a successful refresh:

```json
{"Version":"v0.6.0","LogLevel":"ERROR","CodeLine":"localcache/node_cache.go:106","LogContent":"loop_all,size:1"}
```

`CodeLine` points to the node-cache refresh path, while `size:1` is only the number of nodes in the local cache. Neither field indicates a synchronization failure, but ERROR-level alerting treats the message like one on every refresh interval.

## What Changed

* Include the node-cache size in the existing DEBUG snapshot.
* Stop emitting an unconditional ERROR after successful reconciliation.
* Preserve ERROR logging for actual metadata synchronization failures.

## Validation

* `go test ./pkg/localcache -count=1` passed
* CubeMaster built and ran successfully with this change.
* Three consecutive node metadata refresh cycles completed with the expected results:

  * Cached node state remained healthy.
  * Cache size appeared in the DEBUG snapshot.
  * No cache-size ERROR log was emitted.

## Scope

This PR only corrects the severity of the periodic node-cache size message.

It does not change metadata synchronization, cache contents, node health evaluation, scheduling, or refresh intervals.

title: docs(agents): flag unusual PR file changes
body:
## Motivation

This PR follows the suggestion accepted by @lkml-likexu during the review of #1304: improve the Claude auto-review guidance so unexpected files such as the `1.md` removed in #1043 or the 42 MB `CubeOps/bin/cubeops` build binary committed in #984 can be noticed before merge.

Unusual files can still be valid when intentional, so the reviewer should report the file facts and ask for justification rather than assume they must be removed.

## What Changed

- Require the CubeSandbox project reviewer to inspect the complete changed-file inventory before focusing on the rendered text diff.
- Review added, modified, renamed, and deleted paths for unrelated, misplaced, generated, transient, machine-local, tool-produced, or unexplained opaque files.
- Treat paths, extensions, diff metadata, size, and content-type indicators as supporting evidence rather than definitive proof of type or intent.
- State when the complete inventory or supporting evidence is unavailable instead of asserting that the check passed.
- Ask the author to remove unintended files or explain why intentional files belong in the pull request.

## Validation

- Verified that the auto-review context supplies a complete changed-file inventory and that the guidance fails explicitly when another review context does not.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Confirmed that the final diff only updates `.claude/agents/cube-project-reviewer.md`.

## Scope

This PR only updates the CubeSandbox project-reviewer guidance. It does not add a deterministic workflow, change repository checks, or block intentional files.

title: feat(cube-envd): CubeSandbox-maintained envd implementation in Rust
body:
Closes #1227 ## TL;DR CubeSandbox-maintained Rust rewrite of the in-guest envd data plane, wire-compatible with the Go envd from `e2b-dev/infra@2026.16`: **40/40 conformance scenarios pass byte-for-byte** (9 further differences declared with reasons), **19/19 SDK E2E** on a live deployment. The base image now installs it as `/usr/bin/envd` by default; Go envd stays at `/usr/bin/envd-go` — rollback is one env var (`ENVD_BIN`), no rebuild. Same contract, ~1/7 the memory (2.3 vs 16.1 MiB), ~1/3 the cold start (13 vs 39 ms). PTY / stdin / watch are deferred behind SDK version feature-gates and answer with stable `unimplemented` errors. ## Acceptance criteria from #1227 - [x] **Conformance cases pass.** Go envd 0.5.13 behavior recorded first (49 scenarios, wire-byte level, covering success / error / timeout / cancellation / disconnect), then cube-envd replayed against the same set: **40 PASS / 0 FAIL / 9 declared differences**. Every allowlisted difference carries a written reason (`tests/e2e/envd_conformance/conformance.py::DECLARED_DIFFERENT`). - [x] **SDK E2E against the Go baseline.** Python SDK through CubeProxy on a live deployment: stdout/stderr split, event order, exit codes, env injection, user switching, cwd, large output, enforced timeouts, text/binary file round-trips — 19/19 (`e2e_sdk.py`). - [x] **Template built with cube-envd creates a usable sandbox.** `tpl create-from-image` reaches READY (#312 readiness contract: `:49983/health` → 204); all SDK scenarios ran inside that sandbox. - [x] **Test scenarios documented.** `RESULTS.md`: health/readiness, command execution, file I/O, rollback smoke; reproduction steps in `tests/e2e/envd_conformance/README.md`. - [x] **Measurements published** (same host, same image, `perf.py`): | Metric | Go envd 0.5.13 | cube-envd 0.1.0 | |---|---|---| | Steady-state RSS | 16.1 MiB | 2.3 MiB (−85%) | | Cold start → /health 204 (mean of 10) | 39 ms | 13 ms (−66%) | | `echo hi` latency P50 / P95 (100 runs) | 6.3 / 8.3 ms | 4.3 / 5.6 ms (−32% / −33%) | | Static binary size | 10.5 MB | 2.6 MB (−75%) | - [x] **`ENVD_BIN` rollback verified.** Go-envd template (`ENVD_BIN=/usr/bin/envd-go`) passed command + file smoke; no image rebuild needed. ## Scope Covered: `/health`, `/init` (envVars subset + accessToken), `/envs`, `/metrics`, `/files` upload/download, `process.Process` Start (Connect JSON streaming, keepalive on quiet streams, `Connect-Timeout-Ms`, disconnect semantics) / List / SendSignal, `filesystem.Filesystem` Stat / ListDir / MakeDir / Move / Remove, CLI + auth compatible with `cube-entrypoint.sh`. Deferred per the MVP boundary — each returns a documented, stable, protocol-appropriate error (verified by an 11-input probe suite: no panic, no silent success, no partial execution): | Deferred surface | SDK entry point affected | |---|---| | PTY (`Start.pty`, `Update`) | `sandbox.pty.*` (interactive terminal) | | stdin (`Start.stdin`, `SendInput`, `StreamInput`, `CloseStdin`) | writing to a running process's stdin | | `Process/Connect` | `commands.connect()` (reattach to a running process) | | watch family (`WatchDir`, `CreateWatcher`, `GetWatcherEvents`, `RemoveWatcher`) | `files.watch_dir()` | | `/files/compose`, gzip download encoding, binary proto codec | no known SDK consumer | These are safe to defer because the SDKs feature-gate them on the reported envd version: cube-envd reports 0.1.0, which keeps the gates closed. The corollary is a hard ordering constraint for post-MVP work — moving to a higher / upstream-aligned version number requires implementing the watch family (and PTY for the pty gates) first, otherwise SDKs would start calling surfaces that answer `unimplemented`. None of the upstream E2B-runtime paths (MMDS polling, Hyperloop, NFS/volume init) exist in cube-envd. Known behavioral differences are enumerated with reasons in `cube-envd/README.md`; each can be reverted to bug-for-bug Go behavior individually. ## Build & CI - `docker/Dockerfile.cube-base`: cube-envd build stage, installed as `/usr/bin/envd` (default; `--build-arg ENVD_IMPL=go` flips back); build context moves to the repo root. Installing as the literal `/usr/bin/envd` keeps Cubelet version collection (#641/#650) working unchanged. - `unit-test-check.yml` runs `make cube-envd-test` (44 unit tests + `clippy -D warnings`) on cube-envd changes; the base-image workflow smoke test verifies both binaries. - Guest contract unchanged: `cube-entrypoint.sh` still starts `${ENVD_BIN:-/usr/bin/envd} -port 49983 -isnotfc`. ## Follow-ups (separate PRs) 1. Wire the dual-binary conformance run into CI as a scheduled job (the suite is committed and reproducible; the two-container run is not yet a CI gate). 2. Run the #1187 pinned SDK matrix against a cube-envd template. ## Architecture Module map (matches the routing in `server.rs`): ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph clients["Callers"] SDK["E2B SDKs (Python/JS/Go)
via CubeProxy"] CTRL["Control plane

main.rs"] CTRL --> L subgraph daemon["cube-envd (tokio, 2 workers)"] L --> R["server.rs — axum Router
+ CatchPanicLayer (panic → 500, daemon survives)"] R --> REST["rest/
/health /init /envs /metrics /files"] R --> PROC["services/process.rs
Start (streaming) · List · SendSignal"] R --> FS["services/filesystem.rs
Stat · ListDir · MakeDir · Move · Remove"] R --> UNIMPL["out-of-MVP surfaces
PTY / stdin / watch / compose / Connect

Basic auth / username query
→ /etc/passwd /etc/group"] PROC --> AUTH FS --> AUTH REST --> ST["state.rs — AppState
env vars (/init merge)
access token (constant-time compare)
process table (handle-keyed, pid-reuse safe)"] PROC --> ST PROC --> CODEC["connect.rs
envelope codec / EndStream frames
64 MiB cap / Connect-Timeout-Ms"] FS --> CODEC PROC --> EX["exec.rs
spawn + privilege drop + process group + output pump"] end EX -->|"fork + pre_exec:
setpgid(0,0) → setgroups/setgid/setuid → chdir"| CHILD["child process
own process group (pgid = pid)"] AUTH --> PASSWD[("/etc/passwd
/etc/group")] REST --> DISK[("sandbox filesystem")] FS --> DISK ``` `Start` streaming sequence — three stream endings (normal exit / timeout / client disconnect): ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as SDK client participant H as server.rs
process_start participant S as services/process.rs
start / drive_stream participant E as exec.rs participant P as child (own process group) participant T as state.rs process table C->>H: POST /process.Process/Start
application/connect+json, single envelope H->>H: codec check → token check → decode envelope (≤64 MiB) H->>H: resolve user (Basic auth → /etc/passwd) · Connect-Timeout-Ms → deadline H->>S: start(state, req, user, deadline) S->>S: reject pty / stdin=true (unimplemented), empty cmd (invalid_argument) S->>E: merged env (defaults, then /init, then request — later wins) + resolve_cwd (invalid → invalid_argument) E->>P: spawn · pre_exec: setpgid(0,0) → setgroups → setgid → setuid → chdir Note over E,P: chdir AFTER the privilege drop:
a dir the target user cannot enter fails with EACCES S->>T: insert_process → monotonic handle (not pid-keyed) S-->>C: HTTP 200, frame event.start (pid) loop output pump (one task per pipe, 32 KiB chunks) P->>E: pipe data E->>S: base64 chunk S-->>C: frame event.data (stdout / stderr) end alt normal exit P->>E: exit status (pipes drained first — End never precedes Data) S-->>C: frame event.end + EndStream ok else Connect-Timeout-Ms expires S->>E: kill_process_group(−pid, SIGKILL) — reaps grandchildren too S-->>C: EndStream error deadline_exceeded (no end event) Note over S,P: keeps draining until the child is reaped else client disconnects Note over S,P: sends are ignored — child keeps running,
still visible to List until natural exit end S->>T: remove_process(handle) — pid reuse cannot evict another entry ```

The builder image ships no npm, so the web fmt step in the `fmt` target used to fall through to a SKIP when `make fmt` was routed through `builder-run`. This change splits the two:

title: feat(control-plane): Expose node isolation in CubeOps/WebUI and converge multi-replica CubeMaster state near-real-time via Redis Stream
body:
# feat(control-plane): Expose node isolation in CubeOps/WebUI and converge multi-replica CubeMaster state near-real-time via Redis Stream

## TL;DR

| Dimension | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Isolation entry points | Only `cubemastercli` + CubeMaster HTTP (port 8089) | **4 entry points**: WebUI node detail · CubeOps `PUT/DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{id}/isolation` · CubeMaster HTTP · `cubemastercli` |
| API response fields | Isolation state not exposed | Every `nodeView` carries an extra `schedulingDisabled: boolean` |
| Multi-replica consistency | Relies on `nodemeta` periodic DB reload (typical 60s wait window) | DB remains the source of truth; a new Redis Stream `cube:v1:shared:master:control:events` broadcasts events → every replica's in-memory view converges within **seconds**; DB reload is demoted to a safety net |
| Unisolate | Same as above — CLI / HTTP only | WebUI row menu + CubeOps `DELETE` also supported |
| Documented entry points | Docs cover only 2 | Bilingual docs cover all 4; the 60s wait window is clarified as the "in-flight create-RPC window", not cache lag |

Type: 🚀 Feature (new functionality)
Components touched: CubeMaster control plane · CubeOps backend · Web frontend · bilingual docs

---

## 🎯 Background & Motivation

Node isolation (scheduling cordon / uncordon) is a routine operations action:

- **Block scheduling before upgrades**: prevent new sandboxes from landing on a node that is about to go under maintenance.
- **Stop the bleed on a sick node**: when a node has hardware / network issues, drive its scheduling traffic to zero quickly for diagnosis.
- **Batch maintenance (e.g., K8s node-pool upgrade)**: keep the node draining existing sandboxes but stop accepting new ones.

Previously this action was only available via `cubemastercli` or CubeMaster HTTP, which made the ops mental load heavier. Worse, in **multi-CubeMaster-replica deployments**, the scheduling view between a new replica or different replicas was kept in sync only by `nodemeta.loopReload` (a periodic refresh, by default every tens of seconds) — meaning operators had to wait a whole window before another replica "saw" an isolation take effect.

This PR closes both gaps in one go:

1. **Lift isolation into WebUI / CubeOps** so zero-CLI operations can complete it.
2. **Add a Redis Stream control-plane channel** so multi-replica in-memory scheduling views converge within **seconds** after a DB write; MySQL remains the single source of truth, with periodic reload covering any missed events.

---

## 🏗️ Architecture at a Glance

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Clients["Client Entry Points"]
        WebUI["WebUI (Nodes / NodeDetail)"]
        CubeOps["CubeOps REST"]
        CMHTTP["CubeMaster HTTP :8089"]
        CLI["cubemastercli"]
    end

    subgraph CM["CubeMaster Replica (any peer)"]
        direction TB
        OpsH["CubeOps handler writeIsolation"]
        Client["cubemaster.Client PUT/DELETE /internal/meta/nodes/{id}/isolation"]
        MetaSvc["meta.writeIsolation"]
        SetNode["nodemeta.SetNodeSchedulingDisabled"]
        LocalCache["local snapshot + syncLocalcache"]
        Pub["controlevents.Publisher.PublishNodeIsolation (best-effort)"]
        subgraph Peers["Other CubeMaster Replicas"]
            direction TB
            ReplA["consumer.Run — Replica A"]
            ReplB["consumer.Run — Replica B"]
            ReplC["consumer.Run — Replica C"]
        end
        Apply["nodemeta.ApplySchedulingDisabledLocal"]
    end

    DB[("MySQL node_meta (source of truth)")]
    Stream[("Redis Stream cube:v1:shared:master:control:events")]

    WebUI --> OpsH
    CubeOps --> OpsH
    CMHTTP --> MetaSvc
    CLI --> MetaSvc
    OpsH --> Client
    Client --> MetaSvc
    MetaSvc --> SetNode
    SetNode --> DB
    SetNode --> LocalCache
    SetNode -.best-effort.-> Pub
    DB -.loopReload safety net.-> SetNode
    Pub -->|XADD MAXLEN ~10000| Stream
    Stream -.XREAD $ BLOCK 5s broadcast.-> ReplA
    Stream -.XREAD $ BLOCK 5s broadcast.-> ReplB
    Stream -.XREAD $ BLOCK 5s broadcast.-> ReplC
    ReplA --> Apply
    ReplB --> Apply
    ReplC --> Apply
    Apply --> LocalCache

    classDef db fill:#fde,stroke:#c33,color:#000
    classDef stream fill:#def,stroke:#37c,color:#000
    classDef peer fill:#efe,stroke:#393,color:#000
    classDef critical fill:#fee,stroke:#e33,color:#000
    class DB db
    class Stream stream
    class ReplA,ReplB,ReplC peer
    class Pub critical
```

> DB reload is the safety net: if the stream is trimmed by MAXLEN, a replica misses an event, or Redis flaps, the next `loopReload` still pulls the correct `SchedulingDisabled` from MySQL.

---

## 📦 Changes

### A. CubeMaster control plane

A new `controlevents` package (publisher / consumer / schema / apply / init + tests) is responsible for broadcasting "node isolation" events to every CubeMaster replica via a Redis Stream: once the local replica finishes its DB write it publishes best-effort; other replicas consume via `XREAD $ BLOCK` and callback into `nodemeta` to mutate their local view and localcache; missed events are covered by DB reload. At startup the package issues PING / TYPE against Redis — any failure is fatal.

`nodemeta/isolation.go` appends a best-effort event publish at the tail of the existing DB-write function; a symmetric "local apply" function (no DB write) is added for consumer callbacks; the two paths are mutually exclusive via `lockNodeLabels`.

`main.go` inserts `controlevents.Init` into the `coreInit` order, after `nodemeta` and before `scheduler`, as a fatal dependency — Redis unavailable ⇒ CubeMaster refuses to start.

`rediskey` gains a `MasterControlEvents()` constructor, yielding `cube:v1:shared:master:control:events` (Stream, `shared` scope, `XADD MAXLEN ~ 10000`).

### B. CubeOps backend

Two new REST endpoints, `PUT/DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeID}/isolation`, are added. The handler is a thin pass-through to CubeMaster's existing isolate / unisolate REST; the response is the updated full `nodeView`, now including a `schedulingDisabled` field. The `nodeView` struct, the `CubeMasterClient` interface, and `cubemaster.Client` all gain the corresponding methods (including a PUT helper), and `CubeOps/README.md` gets two extra lines. Both endpoints have no request body and are idempotent.

On the test side, `cluster_test.go` has its list assertion rewritten and three new cases (isolate / unisolate / 404) added; `fake_cm_*` get their stubs. CubeOps has **no direct coupling** to the new `controlevents` package — it merely wraps the existing CubeMaster REST into two client methods; stream broadcasting happens entirely inside CubeMaster.

### C. Web frontend

A generic `IsolateConfirmDialog` (Portal, reused by the list page and the detail page) is introduced, exposing `open` / `onClose` / `onConfirm` / `pending` / `error` props and an error-formatting helper.

The list page `Nodes.tsx` adds a ⋯ menu at the top-right of every node card: when not isolated, the menu shows a destructive "Isolate" item (opens the global dialog); when isolated, it shows an "Unisolate" item (submits directly); the card title displays an "Isolated" badge driven by `schedulingDisabled`; the bottom conditions use the unified readable text and colour scheme.

The detail page `NodeDetail.tsx` adds an isolate / unisolate button to the Header before the heartbeat time. The icon switches with state (`ShieldOff` / `ShieldCheck`); isolate goes through the confirm dialog, unisolate submits directly; the title carries the same "Isolated" badge; on success, a toast fires and both the current-node and the list caches are invalidated; errors are rendered as a red banner at the top of the page.

The API client gains `isolate` / `unisolate`; the schema gains the `schedulingDisabled` field; `utils.ts` gains formatting and colour helpers for condition badges (reused by the list and the detail-page `ConditionRow`). Bilingual locales are extended with isolation-related copy (12 keys in the detail page + 1 key in the list page).

### D. Docs

The bilingual `node-isolation.md` extends the entry-point list from 2 to 4 (WebUI · CubeOps · CubeMaster HTTP · `cubemastercli`), adds a "DB + Stream" mechanism section and a "Multi-replica CubeMaster" scope note, and clarifies the 60s wait window as the in-flight create-RPC pipeline window rather than a cache delay.

The bilingual `redis-key-spec.md` registers the new Stream key, its field contract, and the `MAXLEN ~ 10000` TTL policy. EN and ZH are fully aligned — no single-side updates.

title: [Feature Request] Add in-sandbox lifecycle hooks for pause and resume
body:
## Problem / Motivation

Agent runtimes may need to flush in-memory state, drain active work, sync files or volumes before pause, and reconnect or validate state after resume.

CubeSandbox supports manual and automatic pause/resume, but it does not expose user-defined hooks inside those lifecycle transitions. The asynchronous Webhook proposal in #642 is useful for notifications, but cannot coordinate or block a transition.

## Proposed Solution

Add optional in-sandbox lifecycle hooks, initially:

- `prePause`: run before the VM state is persisted.
- `postResume`: run after the guest and envd are available, but before the sandbox is reported ready.

Support `exec` and in-sandbox HTTP handlers. Each hook should have a bounded timeout and a failure policy such as `Abort` or `Ignore`.

Hooks should cover both manual and automatic pause/resume paths. Pass an idempotent operation ID and lifecycle context, and expose the hook result through sandbox status or lifecycle events.

The same mechanism could later support `preSnapshot`, `postSnapshot`, and `preTerminate`.

## Alternatives Considered

Applications can call their own hooks before invoking the SDK, but this does not cover automatic pause/resume and cannot make hook execution part of the platform state transition.

Asynchronous Webhooks are suitable for notifications, but they cannot prepare or validate in-sandbox state before a transition completes.

## Additional Context

- OpenKruise Agents lifecycle hook proposal: https://github.com/openkruise/agents/issues/743
- Related CubeSandbox asynchronous Webhook proposal: #642

title: build(one-click): parallelize release bundle build
body:
Run the component compiles as bounded-concurrency tracks and overlap the WebUI npm build with the guest-image build, so a full one-click bundle no longer serializes every step. Concurrency auto-caps from CPU count and available memory, overridable via ONE_CLICK_BUILD_JOBS:

\# time deploy/one-click/build-release-bundle-builder.sh
Baseline:
  1st run: 7m15.818s
  2nd run: 6m33.720s
  3rd run: 6m36.016s
After \# running 7 build tracks with up to 7 concurrent:
  1st run: 3m54.011s
  2nd run: 1m54.838s
  3rd run: 1m56.891s

Each track's output is captured to a per-track log and always replayed on completion, so compiler warnings that exit 0 stay visible despite the redirection; failing tracks additionally report their exit code.

Anchor CUBE_BUILD_TIME to the HEAD commit date instead of wall-clock so repeated builds on the same commit stay byte-identical and reuse the Go build cache and Rust target dirs, most importantly skipping a needless fat-LTO relink. Compress tarballs with pigz when available.

title: [Bug Report] 5-second regression in snapshot performance.
body:
## Summary

TLDR: #650 and #728 caused a 5-second regression in snapshot performance.

Snapshot creation latency regressed from approximately 50 ms to approximately 5.1 seconds after passfd IO became enabled by default, because the internal `envd --version` probe fails to start and then waits for a five-second cleanup timeout.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. run performance benchmark [4.1 Snapshot Creation vs Concurrency](https://cubesandbox.com/zh/blog/posts/2026-06-01-cubesandbox-perf-benchmark.html#_4-1-snapshot-%E5%88%B6%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%97%E6%97%B6%E4%B8%8E%E5%B9%B6%E5%8F%91%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB)

   ```bash
   cd examples/snapshot-rollback-clone
   python bench_snapshot_concurrency.py -c 1 -n 5
   ```

3. Observe that every snapshot takes approximately five seconds (wall_avg should be 50ms)

   ```bash
   $ python bench_snapshot_concurrency.py -c 1 -n 5
   concurrency  rounds    wall_avg    wall_min    wall_p95    wall_max     per_avg
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
             1       5      5138.0      5118.3      5185.3      5185.3      5138.0
   ```

3. check the CubeShim/Cubelet logs for the internal envd version probe failure.

## Expected Behavior

The internal `envd --version` probe should complete without materially affecting snapshot latency. With concurrency set to 1, snapshot creation should remain close to the previous baseline of approximately 50 ms rather than incurring a fixed five-second delay.

## Actual Behavior

The regression test on PVM reports approximately 5.1 seconds per snapshot:


The internal envd probe fails during `process.Start` with the following error:

```text
open stderr error: No such file or directory
```

After this immediate Start failure, snapshot completion is delayed until the five-second `envdVersionExecTimeout` expires.

## Additional Context

This appears to be an interaction between two pull requests:

- #728 enabled passfd IO by default after version 0.6.0. The envd probe requests terminal IO while also supplying a separate stderr stream. 
   https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/f252b982280735ec998e6c0b3eb8f8e7102b2d8e/Cubelet/services/cubebox/envd_version.go#L192-L197
   Containerd does not create a separate stderr FIFO for terminal IO, but CubeShim passfd setup attempts to open the non-empty stderr path synchronously.**The missing FIFO causes `process.Start` to fail consistently.**
- #650 added the synchronous `collectEnvdVersion` call to the successful `CommitSandbox` path. When `process.Start` fails, `abortProbe` kills the process and waits on `statusCh` for up to `envdVersionExecTimeout` (five seconds). This PR is included in version 0.6.0, but by itself did not cause the observed five-second snapshot latency.


so in summary, #650 introduced a potential path latency issue; #728 introduced a terminal/passfd compatibility bug that consistently triggered and exacerbated the potential issue from #650, ultimately resulting in a snapshot performance regression.

title: test(cube-bench): add all-in-one cubebench benchmark script
body:
Add tests/perf/cubebench.sh, a self-contained harness that benchmarks core CubeSandbox operations against a deployed single-host:

	bash tests/perf/cubebench.sh # --yes

It covers cold-start latency and concurrency scaling, single-host memory density, and the snapshot/rollback/clone/pause-resume operations. Each section is individually selectable and emits a markdown report capturing the test environment, sandbox spec, and measured results.

The script discovers the cluster through cubemastercli, resets sandboxes between sections for clean measurements, checks host.quota on startup and warns when it is too low, and surfaces hints for the two failures that dominate benchmark runs ("no more resource" and HTTP 408).

title: feat(webui): add interactive sandbox terminal
body:
## Summary

- add an xterm.js-based interactive terminal to running sandboxes in the WebUI
- bridge browser WebSocket traffic through CubeOps and CubeProxy to the envd PTY API
- add short-lived, sandbox-bound terminal tickets without exposing access JWTs in URLs
- configure Helm and one-click deployments for WebSocket proxying
- document usage, security controls, configuration, and troubleshooting in English and Chinese

## Security and reliability

- enforce same-origin WebSocket requests
- use 30-second sandbox-bound terminal tickets with replay protection
- limit sessions per user and per sandbox
- bound client frames and terminal dimensions
- enforce a 15-second opening timeout and a 30-minute inactivity timeout

title: fix(templatecenter): reclaim leaked loop devices instead of silently degrading ext4 builds
body:
## Problem

`createExt4ImageStreaming` (the loop-mount fast path from #472, hardened in #958) allocates a loop device, mounts it, and relies on two deferred cleanups to release it. Both cleanups discard their errors:

```go
_ = runCommand(cleanupCtx, "", "umount", "--", mountPoint)
...
_ = runCommand(cleanupCtx, "", "losetup", "--detach", "--", loopDevice)
```

They are also registered as two separate `defer`s — the umount first, the detach second — so LIFO ordering runs the **detach before the umount**. A detach attempted while the filesystem is still mounted fails with `EBUSY`, and nothing is logged. The consequences are permanent:

1. The loop device stays attached for the lifetime of the host.
2. If the backing `.ext4` is unlinked afterwards (the build's own failure cleanup does exactly that), the loop device keeps the inode alive and its disk space is never reclaimed — the same class of permanent disk leak as #822. `losetup -a` shows these as `... .ext4 (deleted)`.
3. Once enough devices have leaked, `losetup --find` fails and every subsequent build falls back to phase-1 behind a single WARN at `ext4.go:141`. The fast path never returns without operator intervention, and the only symptom is that template creation has become drastically slower.

Containerized deployments reach (3) far earlier than the kernel's loop limit would suggest. A container's `/dev` is a tmpfs whose node set is fixed when the container starts — typically `loop-control` plus `loop0..loop7` — while `LOOP_CTL_GET_FREE` hands out **node-global** indexes. As soon as it returns 8 or above, that node does not exist inside the container:

```
losetup: /.../rfs-XXXXXXXX.ext4: failed to set up loop device: No such file or directory
```

Observed in practice: 8 devices attached, none of them mounted, three with `(deleted)` backing files, and every template build after that point taking the slow path.

## Change

- The detach now runs from the *same* cleanup closure as the umount, immediately after it, so it can no longer be ordered before the umount and hit `EBUSY`. This is the primary fix.
- `umount` failure is logged and retried lazily (`umount -l`), so a busy mount point no longer cascades into a permanently pinned device.
- `losetup --detach` is retried briefly (5 attempts, 200 ms apart) before giving up, so a lazy umount that has not finished releasing the mount does not abandon the device, and the final failure is logged instead of discarded.
- A device that still could not be detached now **fails the build** instead of being reported as success. This is the one leak the backstop below cannot heal on its own: a successful build keeps its image, so the backing file is never unlinked and the device can never become a `(deleted)` reclaim candidate. Returning the error makes `BuildExt4` unlink the image (`ext4.go:141-143`) — turning the pinned device into a candidate for the next allocation failure — and rebuild via phase-1, so no image is lost. It also refuses an image whose `resize2fs -M` and pmem alignment would have run against a still-mounted filesystem (the stuck-mount case), which would otherwise serve an unshrunk, unaligned image that the microVM rejects with `PmemSizeNotAligned`.
- A detach that fails only because the device is *already gone* is not treated as a leak: before retrying, the code asks `losetup` what the device is backed by, and stops when it is no longer this build's image. Attaches with autoclear semantics are released by the umount itself, and without this check every such host would burn the whole backoff budget and then fail every build into phase-1. The check queries `losetup` rather than matching its error text, which is localized.
- As a backstop for devices already leaked (by an earlier build, or by a lazy umount that had not completed yet), `reclaimOrphanLoopDevices` runs when `losetup --find` fails and retries once, so exhaustion self-heals instead of permanently degrading every later build.

Reclaim is narrow by construction: a device is only detached when its backing file lives under the artifact store **and has already been unlinked** (`losetup --list` reports it as `(deleted)`). A build unlinks its image only after it has given up on it, so a build in flight elsewhere can never become a candidate — not even in the attach→mount window, where the device is not yet in the mount table and the kernel's `EBUSY` refusal would not protect it either. Devices that still cannot be detached are logged at debug level and skipped.

When the retry after a reclaim also fails, both errors are surfaced (`%w` on the original) so the reason allocation failed in the first place is not lost.

The happy path is unchanged — no additional command runs unless a cleanup fails or allocation is already exhausted.

## Note for containerized deployments

Even with zero leaks, a container that only has `loop0..loop7` can exhaust them with eight concurrent builds. Making more nodes available is a deployment concern (pre-create them, or share the host `/dev`) and is out of scope here; this change makes the failure recoverable and diagnosable rather than silent and permanent.

## Tests

New `disk_test.go`:

- Behaviour of the fix itself, driven through `createExt4ImageStreaming` with fake `losetup`/`mount`/`umount` on `PATH` that record their argv: the umount always precedes the detach (reverting the ordering fails this test), a busy detach is retried until it succeeds, the plain-umount-fails/lazy-umount-succeeds case releases the device on the retry, a mount point that survives even the lazy umount stops after one detach attempt instead of spending the whole budget, a failed `mount` still detaches the allocated device (which now happens only through the deferred cleanup), and an exhausted `losetup --find` is retried after the orphan reclaim frees a device — while an allocation failure with no orphan to reclaim returns the original error with no retry, and one whose retry fails too reports both failures.
- `losetup --list` parsing and store-prefix matching: the `(deleted)` suffix is required (a live backing file under the store is left alone), devices outside the store, sibling directories sharing a prefix (`storage-backup` vs `storage`), malformed and blank lines, a backing path containing spaces, and a `/` store dir (refused rather than detaching everything).

`gofmt`, `go build ./pkg/...`, `go vet ./pkg/templatecenter/image/` and the package tests (`-short`, as CI runs them) all pass.

title: [Feature Request] Support deferred configuration updates for paused sandboxes before resume
body:
## Motivation

We operate a warm pool of sandboxes in the **Paused** state. A request can claim a paused sandbox, but may need request-specific configuration before it is resumed:

- environment variables;
- persistent volume mounts (for example object storage, NFS, or other Volume plugins).

Today these settings are supplied at sandbox creation time. Resume restores the existing paused VM state, so a claimed warm-pool sandbox cannot safely receive a new request configuration without creating a new sandbox.

## Proposal

Introduce a control-plane operation that updates the **next-resume configuration** of a sandbox, valid only while it is in the `Paused` state. For example:

```http
PATCH /sandboxes/{sandboxID}/resume-config
```

The exact endpoint and field names are open for discussion. A possible payload could contain an optimistic-concurrency revision plus the supported deferred fields:

```json
{
  "expected_revision": 3,
  "env_vars": {
    "REQUEST_ID": "req-123",
    "TENANT": "acme"
  },
  "volume_mounts": [
    {"volume_id": "vol-abc", "path": "/workspace/data", "read_only": false}
  ]
}
```

`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxID}/resume` would then restore the VM using the saved next-resume configuration. Keeping configuration mutation separate from Resume makes retries and failure handling explicit.

## Required semantics

1. **State guard**: accept changes only in `Paused`; return a clear conflict for Running, Resuming, or terminal states.
2. **Atomicity / retries**: protect updates with a revision or idempotency key. A failed resume must not leave partially attached volumes or leaked plugin reference counts.
3. **Volume lifecycle**: current Volume Attach/Detach hooks are tied to sandbox create/destroy. Deferred `volume_mounts` need equivalent attach, detach, refcount, rollback, and Cubelet/virtiofs handling around Resume.
4. **Environment semantics**: changing a process environment inside a paused VM cannot retroactively modify already-running processes. The feature should document which subsequent execution paths observe the new values (for example command/PTY processes through envd) and preserve existing processes' behavior.
5. **Backward compatibility**: existing pause/resume behavior must remain unchanged when no deferred configuration is supplied.

## Suggested implementation order

1. Persist and apply deferred environment configuration on the resume path.
2. Add deferred Volume attach/detach with robust rollback and reconciliation.
3. Consider additional mutable fields only after their semantics are defined; CPU/memory/network policy should not be included implicitly in this proposal.

## Why this is useful

This enables low-latency, isolated warm pools while still allowing each request to receive its own storage and environment configuration. It also fits the existing E2B-compatible Volume direction without requiring applications to create a dedicated sandbox for every dynamic mount.

title: [Bugfix] Reopen CubeShim and VMM logs after rename-based rotation
body:
## Summary

Keep CubeShim and VMM log files bounded with host-side hourly rotation, retention, and periodic reopen without a service restart.

## Root cause

Both writers keep log files open. Host-side `rename + create` rotation replaces the pathname while the process still holds the old file descriptor, so each writer needs a safe reopen path that does not discard writes when the replacement is temporarily unavailable.

## Changes

- keep CubeShim's existing internal `Rotate` event and reopen both log files
- preserve the VMM's existing wall-clock-hour reopen on the first log write after the hour changes
- compare the VMM pathname and held descriptor by device/inode at most once per second, so rename-based rotation is detected on a subsequent write without waiting for the next hour
- let the VMM control thread own a monotonic `timerfd` and emit the existing `LOG_CTRL_REOPEN` control record once per hour
- keep the current descriptor usable when reopen fails; retry on later writes with a one-second cooldown
- open replacement files before swapping descriptors and let host-side `logrotate create` own replacement-file creation
- keep writer-created files subject to the process umask
- document an hourly `/etc/logrotate.d/cubesandbox` policy using `rename + create`, `delaycompress`, compression, and host-owned retention
- explicitly disallow `copytruncate`

The VMM timer is created and consumed by the VMM control thread after its VMM-specific seccomp filter is installed; it is not created from deferred logger initialization or a vCPU/API thread. The pathname/device/inode check remains a write-triggered fast path for arbitrary external rotations. This PR does not impose a fixed byte-size limit such as 100M; host-side rotation and retention remain the deployment policy.

Related to #1290
Related to #1136

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p logging --lib`
- `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p cube-hypervisor --lib`
- `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p containerd-shim-cube-rs --tests`

title: [Bug Report] CubeVmm and CubeShim logs need bounded rotation and safe reopen
body:
## Summary

CubeVmm and CubeShim write to long-lived shared host log files, but their current reopen paths do not provide a bounded rotation and retention contract. A normal rename-based logrotate job can leave one or more processes writing to the old inode until they explicitly reopen it; copytruncate is unsafe for concurrent writes.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: v0.6.0 / 8721dd151971ce3c2966482bbd32904ad98f378e
- Deployment mode: single-node
- Relevant components: CubeShim and hypervisor (CubeVmm)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run CubeSandbox with multiple live sandboxes and inspect:

   ~~~text
   /data/log/CubeShim/cube-shim-req.log
   /data/log/CubeShim/cube-shim-stat.log
   /data/log/CubeVmm/vmm.log
   ~~~

2. In CubeShim/shim/src/log/mod.rs, observe that LogType::Rotate only breaks the writer loop; the next loop opens the same active pathname and does not archive or enforce a size limit.
3. In hypervisor/logging/src/lib.rs, observe that PlainDecorator reopens on the time bucket changing, but does not detect that the active pathname was replaced by an external rotator.
4. Apply a standard size-based logrotate policy and rename the active file. With an already-open writer, subsequent writes can continue to the old inode until that process reopens.

## Expected Behavior

CubeVmm and CubeShim should have an explicit, documented rotation contract that keeps active files bounded, retains a configured number of archives, and safely reopens after rename-based rotation.

## Actual Behavior

The current code only reopens the same pathname. It does not perform archival, size checks, or retention, and there is no documented host-side configuration that is safe for all long-lived writers. On one v0.6.0 development node after about one month, vmm.log reached about 20.9 GiB and cube-shim-req.log about 6.6 GiB with no rotated archives.

## Proposed Fix

1. Make CubeShim and the VMM detect an active-file inode replacement and reopen the newly-created pathname.
2. Document and/or ship a logrotate policy using rename + create, compression, and retention; explicitly reject copytruncate.
3. Add focused tests that rename the active file, create a new active file, write again, and verify that the old and new records land in the expected files.

Related: #1136 proposes a broader per-Sandbox stdout/stderr log-source lifecycle. This issue is narrower: it covers the host-wide CubeShim request/stat files and the CubeVmm log.

title: [Bug Report] CubeMaster ignores file_size/file_num log rotation settings
body:
## Summary

The shipped CubeMaster configuration uses snake_case log rotation keys, but the Go config tags use camelCase. With yaml.v3, file_size and file_num are not unmarshaled into log.Conf, so the rotation writer receives zero values and the active log files grow without a bound.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: v0.6.0 / 8721dd151971ce3c2966482bbd32904ad98f378e
- Deployment mode: single-node
- Relevant component: CubeMaster

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start CubeMaster with the shipped configuration:

   ~~~yaml
   log:
     module: "cubemaster"
     path: "/data/log/CubeMaster"
     file_size: 100
     file_num: 10
     level: "info"
   ~~~

2. Inspect CubeMaster/pkg/base/log/Conf: the fields currently use yaml:"fileSize" and yaml:"fileNum".
3. Observe that FileSize and FileNum remain zero after unmarshaling the shipped keys.

## Expected Behavior

The shipped file_size and file_num settings should be honored. The active file should rotate at the configured size and retain the configured number of historical files.

## Actual Behavior

The rotation writer is constructed with zero size and file-count values. In a long-running node, the active files remain unrotated (for example, cubemaster-req.log grows while no .log.N files are created).

## Proposed Fix

Use yaml:"file_size" and yaml:"file_num" on log.Conf, and add a regression test that unmarshals the shipped keys. This matches the existing configs under CubeMaster/conf.yaml, configs/single-node/cubemaster.yaml, and the Kubernetes chart.

title: Enable GitHub workflow on arm64
body:
## Summary

Extend CI to run on arm64 in addition to amd64, and fix a CubeMaster
test that only failed on arm64. Together these give the project real
cross-architecture coverage and turn the arm64 legs green.

## Why

CI previously exercised amd64 runners only, so architecture-specific
breakage could reach master unnoticed. The Rust shim and hypervisor
carry `cfg(target_arch)` paths, and the test fix below is a concrete
case of a real arm64-only failure that amd64-only CI hid.

## Changes

**CI (`ci: run more workflows both on amd64 and arm64`)**
Add an arm64 leg (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`) alongside amd64 across build,
format, kubernetes-chart, migration, terraform, and unit-test
workflows, so every check runs on both architectures.

**Test fix (`test(cubemaster): assert commit response instead of
mocked arg on arm64`)**
`TestHandleSandboxCommitAction{AllowsMissingCreateRequest,
IgnoresProvidedTemplateID}` failed on arm64 with the captured
`templateID` coming back as garbage:

    expected: "tpl-49e22e5de1ab46c59a97a013"
    actual  : "\x90\v@\xf9\xffc0\xebi\x06\x00T..."

Root cause: gomonkey cannot read a patched function's 6th+ argument on
arm64. Under Go's register ABI the later arguments spill off the
register set and the trampoline forwards raw stack bytes. The handler
is correct; only the mock's view of the argument is corrupt. The tests
now assert the observable contract through the HTTP response rather
than the un-capturable mock argument.

## Test plan

- [ ] All workflows pass on both amd64 and arm64 legs
- [ ] `make cubemaster-test` (or the CubeMaster unit-test target) green
    on arm64

title: refactor(network): embed network-agent into Cubelet and simplify lifecycle
body:
Replace the standalone network-agent process with an in-process Cubelet network runtime so TAP lifecycle, CubeVS, CubeEgress, port mapping, and startup recovery no longer depend on a separate daemon, gRPC/HTTP, or fdserver transport.

- Add Cubelet/network/runtime as the NetworkController: TapPool (Ready/Active/Cleaning only), StateStore under /dev/shm, PortBinder, CubeVS/CubeEgress adapters, sync TapCleaner, StartupRecover, and a maintenance loop that retries durable cleanup once per tick.
- Wire CubeletNetworkPlugin Create/Destroy/CleanUp to EnsureNetwork / ReleaseNetwork; expose RegisterHTTP for CubeEgress policy dump and tap listing; hand shim TAP fds via GetTapFile one-shot duplicates over cubetap.sock (no plugin-side fd cache).
- Remove network-agent module, pkg/networkagentclient, enable_network_agent config, and related one-click / k8s / docs / CI deploy paths.
- Keep one-shot compatibility for old network-agent state files during upgrade recovery; restrict /v1/network/taps to loopback.
- Retain TAP fds across pool/active handoffs to remove create hot-path burst convoys; collapse PortBinder Reserve/Commit into allocate-as-owned with ReleaseOwnership; drop unused GetNetwork/ListNetworks APIs.
- Move CubeEgress loopback admin off :9090 to :9091 (configurable via `CUBE_EGRESS_ADMIN_PORT`) so it no longer collides with CubeProxy plaintext gRPC on 9090; wire the new default through one-click, Helm, and Cubelet `cube_egress_admin_url`.

title: Questions about template image: where it comes from, whether it's customizable, and preinstalling dev toolchains (Go/Java/Python3/Rust)
body: ### Question ## Context I'm looking at the "New Template" flow and the required `image` field (e.g. `registry.example.com/image:tag`). Before investing time in building custom images, I'd like to confirm a few things about how the `image` is sourced and used. ## What I've read so far - `docs/guide/tutorials/bring-your-own-image.md` - `docs/guide/tutorials/template-from-image.md` - Relevant code: `CubeMaster/pkg/templatecenter/template_image.go` My current understanding: CubeMaster runs `docker pull` on the master node, exports the container rootfs, packs it into an ext4 image, distributes it to Cubelet nodes, and registers it as a template; the sandbox runtime then uses the generated artifact ID (`rfs-...`) instead of the original image reference. ## Questions ### 1. Where does the image come from? - Is the `image` field simply a Docker/OCI registry reference (must be reachable from the cluster nodes)?
