title: fix(python-sdk): add user isolation support for commands and filesystem
body:
## Summary

Squash of 14 incremental commits into a single reviewable change that adds
per-user execution support to the Python SDK and rewires the SDK-compat e2e
suite to run on both `cubesandbox` and `e2b` backends.

### SDK (`sdk/python/cubesandbox`)
- `Commands.run` no longer takes an optional e2b dependency; gains a `user`
  parameter so the request honors the requested identity
- `_filesystem` propagates `user` to the envd RPC body so filesystem ops
  run as the requested user
- `_pty` minor adjustment to stay aligned with the Commands refactor

### e2e SDK-compat suite (`tests/e2e/sdk_compat`)
- All four adapters (`base`, `cubesandbox`, `e2b`, `tracing`) gain
  `make_dir / list_dir / file_exists / remove_file / rename_file`
- User-isolation tests renamed and de-duplicated by functionality
  (`test_command_user.py`, `test_filesystem_user.py`)
- `test_metadata_ops.py` rewritten to work on e2b: `stat` → `get_info`,
  accepts `EntryInfo` as well as dicts, drops the `user` kwarg where
  e2b does not accept it
- /tmp sticky-bit tests skipped on e2b (image-level difference)
- Permission-boundary tests rewritten to verify post-conditions via
  `run_command` instead of asserting on backend-specific stderr text
- `e2b` adapter passes `cwd=/` to `commands.run` so `user=nobody` does
  not trip on a missing `/nonexistent` home

### Docs
- `docs/dev/pending-envd-fixes.md` — new tracked-gap entry for the
  envd-side limitation around per-user filesystem RPCs
- `docs/dev/index.md` — link to the new tracked-gaps section

## Rebase & merge compatibility

Rebased onto latest `master` and resolved the overlap with the
`filesystem_extended` adapter methods that landed upstream in the meantime:

- The four adapters' filesystem metadata ops are unified onto a single
  signature set that keeps master's return-value semantics while adding an
  optional `user` keyword (default `"root"`, so existing no-user callers are
  unchanged): `list_files`/`stat_file`/`rename_file` still return
  `dict`/`list[dict]`, `file_exists` returns `bool`, `make_dir`/`remove_file`
  return `None`, `write_files` returns `int`, and the new `list_dir` returns
  `list[str]`. The duplicate method definitions left by the merge are removed.
- `test_sandbox.py` is updated for the `Commands` refactor: the dropped
  `_collect_process_events` / `_run_with_e2b_connect` helpers are no longer
  imported or patched (there is no e2b path to disable anymore), and the
  exit-code-from-status case now targets `_exit_code_from_status` directly.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest sdk/python/tests` — 261 passed, 4 skipped (skips need a live backend)
- [x] `pytest tests/e2e/sdk_compat/cases/commands/test_command_user.py` — passes on both backends (e2b only on the cases that map to its RPC surface)
- [x] `pytest tests/e2e/sdk_compat/cases/filesystem/test_filesystem_user.py` — passes; e2b variants for the /tmp sticky-bit cases are skipped per the new helper
- [x] `pytest tests/e2e/sdk_compat/cases/filesystem/test_metadata_ops.py` — passes on both backends
- [x] No more xfails; the previously xfailed `test_cross_user_filesystem_ops` was removed and replaced with post-condition tests, and the gap is tracked in `docs/dev/pending-envd-fixes.md`

## Follow-ups
- envd side: per-user filesystem RPCs — see `docs/dev/pending-envd-fixes.md`
  for the symptom, owner, and validation path

title: docs(troubleshooting): add WSL2 DNS troubleshooting for install preflight and sandbox data plane
body:
## What

Adds a bilingual troubleshooting page for two DNS problems that are specific to WSL2, requested by @fslongjin.

- `docs/guide/troubleshooting/wsl-dns.md`
- `docs/zh/guide/troubleshooting/wsl-dns.md`
- One index row in each language

`quickstart.md` lists WSL as a supported platform, and [#311](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/311) covers the XFS loopback workaround, but neither of the two DNS failures below is documented anywhere. Both were hit while bringing up v0.6.0 on WSL2 for [#644](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/issues/644).

## The two problems

**1. Preflight exits 3 before anything is downloaded**

`online-install.sh` requires `resolvectl` or a loaded `NetworkManager`. A default Ubuntu-on-WSL install has neither.

The generic prerequisite *is* documented in `self-build-deploy.md` ("DNS routing: `systemd-resolved` (preferred) or `NetworkManager + dnsmasq`"), so this is not a missing requirement — it is a discoverability gap:

- `quickstart.md` lists WSL as supported but its requirements table only mentions glibc and XFS.
- The error names the *command* `resolvectl`, while the command is shipped by the **`systemd-resolved` package**. `apt install resolvectl` does not exist, so the next step is not obvious.

Fix: `apt-get install -y systemd-resolved && systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved`.

**2. Install succeeds, sandbox is created, but `run_code` cannot resolve**

```
[1] sandbox created in 0.99s
    sandbox_id: 9e0b35c6183f4e969e1a6a8f6bdc5629     <- control plane OK
httpx.ConnectError: [Errno -2] Name or service not known   <- data plane fails
```

The control plane is fine because it goes through `127.0.0.1:3000`. The data plane needs wildcard resolution for `*.cube.app`, and WSL regenerates `/etc/resolv.conf` on every start, discarding the CoreDNS nameserver written by `dns-host-route-up.sh`.

This one is the more valuable of the two for a troubleshooting page: the error mentions neither DNS nor `cube.app`, and it can appear on a deployment that worked yesterday, because the trigger is a WSL restart rather than a config change.

Fix requires both steps — either alone does not survive a restart:

1. `/etc/wsl.conf` → `[network]` / `generateResolvConf = false`
2. `/etc/resolv.conf` is usually a symlink into `/run/...`, so `rm` it before writing; point the first nameserver at CoreDNS and keep an upstream resolver as a fallback (with only the CoreDNS address, `*.cube.app` resolves but general internet resolution breaks).

The page also notes which CoreDNS address applies to which backend (`169.254.254.53` on the `systemd-resolved` path, `127.0.0.54` on the `dnsmasq` fallback), points to the two DNS-free alternatives already in the repo (path-based access and `examples/e2b-dev-sidecar`), and lists the two pieces of state that do not survive `wsl --shutdown` (the loopback XFS mount and `resolv.conf`).

## Environment used for verification

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Cube Sandbox | v0.6.0 (`cubemastercli` `8721dd15`, built 2026-07-24) |
| Deployment | one-click, single node |
| Distro | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS on WSL2 |
| Host kernel | `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2` |
| glibc | 2.39 |
| `/data/cubelet` | loopback XFS, `reflink=1` |

Deployment screenshots and logs from that run are attached to [#1238](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1238) (14 systemd units active, template `READY`, guest kernel `6.6.1199` vs host `6.18.33.2`).

## Checklist

- [x] Both language files added with the same slug
- [x] Index row added in both `docs/guide/troubleshooting/index.md` and `docs/zh/guide/troubleshooting/index.md`
- [x] Follows `_template.md` section structure (Symptom / Environment / Root Cause / Resolution / References)
- [x] Frontmatter keys aligned across both files (`title`, `author`, `date`, `tags`, `lang`)
- [x] All six relative links verified to exist
- [x] The quoted `online-install.sh` snippet matches upstream (marked as an excerpt)
- [x] Files are LF-only; index diffs are one added line each
- [x] DCO signed off

Happy to adjust the wording, section split, or file placement if you would prefer this merged into `deployment.md` instead of a standalone page.

title: feat: add Web Terminal UI and one-click wiring
body: Closes #643 Depends on [#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258) ## Summary Adds the WebUI terminal experience and the minimum one-click deployment wiring required to reach it: xterm.js rendering with resize/fullscreen/font controls, i18n, target and container selection, bounded browser-side input, reconnect/resume with transient retries, a dedicated one-click nginx WebSocket route, and a root-only internal relay token shared only by CubeOps and CubeMaster. This PR is split out of [#1247](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1247). It builds on the second PR of the series, [#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258), which in turn builds on [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257): #1257 protocol/runtime, #1258 relay/gateway, #1259 UI + one-click wiring. ## Motivation The terminal backend (PR [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257)/[#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258)) is reachable only through authenticated WebSocket frames: the browser cannot connect to Cubelet or CubeMaster directly, and the gateway accepts only validated one-use grants. Reaching the feature from the Dashboard therefore needs three things this PR delivers: an interactive terminal UI, a same-origin WebSocket route through the one-click nginx that preserves the long-lived terminal stream, and a shared internal token that lets CubeOps and CubeMaster relay without reusing any existing credential. ## Live Demo https://cubedemo.1zero.me - Username: `admin` - Password: `admin` - This is a shared temporary environment; Password changes are disabled so the shared credentials remain stable. The deployment exercises the combined stack from [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257), [#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258), and [#1259](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259). It was developed from the final PR branch [feat/web-terminal-ui-one-click](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259), with a demo-only multi-container runtime patch layered in the separate branch [demo/issue643-multicontainer-runtime](https://github.com/1zero224/CubeSandbox/pull/12). The additional runtime patch provides a real sandbox with multiple containers so maintainers can verify container discovery, container selector switching, and independent terminal sessions. It is used only for the live demo. ## Changes | Area | What | |------|------| | WebUI | Terminal entry points on the sandbox list and detail pages; `TerminalDialog` with xterm.js rendering, resize/fullscreen/font controls, i18n (en/zh), and target/container selection | | WebUI | `TerminalSessionClient`: bounded input, transient resume retries, and reconnect state kept separate from user-initiated close; protocol constants generated from the shared manifest; deterministic browser storage for Vitest | | One-click | Dedicated exact `/opsapi/v1/terminal/ws` nginx location with WebSocket headers, 7200 s deadline, and request/response buffering disabled; the ordinary `/opsapi/` REST path keeps its existing 300 s timeout and buffering | | One-click | Internal relay token generated once, stored in a root-owned `0400`/`0600` file, preserved across upgrades/backups, loaded only by CubeMaster and CubeOps, and kept out of the shared `.one-click.env` | | Vite | `/opsapi` `ws: true` for local WebSocket development; the CubeOps Go configuration remains the single source of runtime defaults (deployment files pass only explicit administrator overrides) | | Docs | Bilingual `docs/guide/web-terminal.md` and `docs/zh/guide/web-terminal.md`: requirements, usage, security, troubleshooting, known limitations, and a 30-minute deploy-to-terminal reproduction | ## Session Lifecycle The browser keeps the reconnect path separate from user-initiated close: an abnormal transport close moves the session to `Detached`, where the UI retries a resume of the same session; only a user/terminal close or an exhausted resume grace reaches the terminal `Closed` state, which is never auto-reconnected. ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Opening Opening --> Attached: WebSocket and grant accepted Attached --> Detached: abnormal transport close Detached --> Attached: resume succeeds Detached --> Closed: grace exhausted Attached --> Closed: user close / terminal close Closed --> [*] ``` ## Security Model - CubeOps and CubeMaster share an independent internal terminal token; the value is never reused from the CubeOps JWT secret, the Cube Admin token, or any other existing credential. - The browser-facing route is same-origin and should be served over HTTPS/WSS. - Grants, authentication headers, internal tokens, and terminal payloads are not written to URLs, access logs, audit payloads, or committed configuration. - The one-click token file rejects symlinks, validates content, uses atomic `0600` writes, and is backed up with owner-only permissions. ## Validation Test plan: - [x] Frontend Vitest: 44 cases pass — wired into CI as a `web-test` job - [x] Web TypeScript lint passes - [x] Web production build passes (only the existing > 500 kB chunk warning) - [x] VitePress production build passes - [x] One-click terminal token generation, validation, upgrade preservation, redaction, and service-loading test passes - [x] One-click transport wiring test passes (dedicated nginx route, unchanged REST timeout, Vite WebSocket proxy, no duplicated deployment defaults) - [x] `bash -n` and CI-equivalent error-level shellcheck pass on the changed one-click scripts - [x] Diff gates: zero changes under Kubernetes/Helm, Terraform/TKE, evidence scripts, or architecture-evidence docs Real-cluster evidence: - Deployed topology: real WebUI/nginx → task HAProxy → CubeOps A or (via a cross-region TCP-22 SSH tunnel) CubeOps B → CubeMaster → real Cubelet PTY. Both replicas share CubeDB, Redis, CubeMaster, and the terminal internal token. - Functional: A-issued/B-consumed and B-issued/A-consumed grants both PASS; the same grant consumed concurrently across two backends yields one `HTTP 101/opened` and one `HTTP 401`; SIGTERM on B emitted `SERVER_DRAINING` and the client resumed the same session, shell PID, and exec; SSH tunnel restarts 0; DB/Cubelet reconciliation found no duplicate grant consumption, session, or exec. - Load (product limits unchanged): 20 sandboxes, 40 users, ≤ 3 sessions per user, ≤ 5 sessions per container, stepped concurrency 1 / 10 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 100. Every session awaited grant `HTTP 201` → WebSocket connect → `opened` status frame → a short fixed shell-ready marker over real stdout. - Result: 100/100 sessions succeeded, 0 failed, stdout observed on 100/100, exactly 100 sockets closed. HAProxy WebSocket `101`: node-a 52, node-b 48. Backend connection-error deltas 0; CubeOps B restarts 0; HAProxy restarts 0; SSH tunnel restarts 0. - 100-concurrency tier latency (p50/p95/p99; includes cross-region public-internet and SSH-tunnel overhead, so it is NOT production-equivalent): | Stage | p50 | p95 | p99 | |-------|-----|-----|-----| | Grant HTTP 201 | 269.1 ms | 726.0 ms | 734.2 ms | | WebSocket handshake | 732.5 ms | 913.7 ms | 980.4 ms | | Terminal `opened` | 927.6 ms | 1109.3 ms | 1161.0 ms | | Shell-ready stdout marker | 1375.0 ms | 1783.8 ms | 1900.2 ms | - CubeOps B resources over the 49 s load window: avg CPU 0.107 cores, peak sampled 0.889 cores, max MemoryCurrent 29,224,960 B (~30.2 MB peak), max Tasks 15, max fds 181, host min free memory 15,646,016 KiB, max load1 0.70; no OOM, no restarts, no backend errors — the workload stays far below the 8 vCPU / 16 GiB host, and no claim is made of reaching the host's limit (tested to 100 concurrent only). - Clock gate: 7 samples spanning 64.335 s (min 60 s required), max absolute A/B skew 0.208751 s, max observed RTT 1.032834 s, chrony Leap status Normal / 0 ppm; `timedatectl NTPSynchronized=no` disclosed — no public-NTP claim. - Post-load smoke: 1 real terminal open → shell-ready stdout → close, 1/1 passed. Manual interactive evidence — browser recordings/screenshots (UI-side behavior not covered by E3): - Reconnect UX: after ~5-10 s offline the UI shows a reconnecting state and resumes the same session (session/PID semantics per PR #1257); buffered output is replayed. - - Fullscreen layout: terminal text does not overlap buttons or the status bar in fullscreen. - Session tabs: a new session is an independent shell; closing one tab leaves the others running. - - Normal exit: `exit` or the close button does not auto-reconnect. - Paused sandbox: the terminal entry is disabled with a hint while the sandbox is paused. - Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-5.6-Sol Signed-off-by: Hong Cao

title: feat(cubeops): add Web Terminal grant gateway and CubeMaster relay
body:
Related to #643
Depends on [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257)

## Summary

Adds the CubeMaster relay and CubeOps grant/gateway layers of the Web Terminal feature. It connects the Cubelet Terminal RPC to an administrator-only WebSocket path, issues and validates short-lived single-use terminal grants, persists terminal grant/session state, records audit events, and hardens relay failure classification and stale-target resolution.

This PR is split out of [#1247](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1247). It builds on the first PR of the series, [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257), adding only relay, gateway, grant, configuration, and migration changes on top; the WebUI and one-click deployment wiring are delivered by the final PR, [#1259](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259).

## Motivation

After PR [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257), the Cubelet Terminal RPC is only reachable inside the cluster: there is no authorized, audited browser path, and browsers must never connect to Cubelet or CubeMaster directly. This PR introduces the two trust boundaries of the feature — CubeOps authenticates administrators, issues one-use grants, and terminates the browser WebSocket; CubeMaster relays typed terminal frames to Cubelet under shared internal credentials — so the terminal can be reached from the Dashboard without loosening the existing security model.

## Live Demo

https://cubedemo.1zero.me

- Username: `admin`
- Password: `admin`
- This is a shared temporary environment; Password changes are disabled so the shared credentials remain stable.

The deployment exercises the combined stack from [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257), [#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258), and [#1259](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259). It was developed from the final PR branch [feat/web-terminal-ui-one-click](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259), with a demo-only multi-container runtime patch layered in the separate branch [demo/issue643-multicontainer-runtime](https://github.com/1zero224/CubeSandbox/pull/12).

The additional runtime patch provides a real sandbox with multiple containers so maintainers can verify container discovery, container selector switching, and independent terminal sessions. It is used only for the live demo.

## Changes

| Area | What |
|------|------|
| CubeMaster | Relay bidirectional terminal frames between CubeOps and Cubelet (`httpservice/inner`); resolve terminal targets through the sandbox cache with a bounded 10 s stale-cache fallback |
| CubeMaster | Encode typed server status and close frames under the configured WebSocket write deadline; preserve resumability when an upstream transport write fails instead of misclassifying it as a Cubelet `SLOW_PRODUCER` |
| CubeOps | Issue short-lived, single-use terminal grants for authorized administrators; validate grant, Origin, target, session, and internal relay credentials before opening the WebSocket |
| CubeOps | Persist terminal grant/session state and record audit events without terminal payloads; remove an unreachable stdout-pending check (slow consumers are governed by write deadlines) |
| Config | Validated CubeOps and CubeMaster terminal relay settings; all CubeOps settings are environment-overridable, while CubeMaster exposes an environment override only for the shared internal token |
| DB | Additive `terminal_grants` / `terminal_sessions` migration for MySQL and PostgreSQL (same timestamp prefix) |

## Configuration

CubeOps `terminal.*` settings (env-overridable via `CUBE_TERMINAL_*`; defaults from `defaultTerminalConfig`):

| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `enabled` | true | Gateway and grant service on/off |
| `allowed_origins` | [] | Exact trusted WebUI origins; an empty list rejects every cross-origin request |
| `grant_ttl_seconds` | 60 | Grant lifetime (security maximum 60 s) |
| `handshake_timeout_seconds` | 10 | WebSocket handshake deadline |
| `ping_interval_seconds` | 20 | WebSocket ping interval |
| `pong_timeout_seconds` | 10 | WebSocket pong deadline |
| `write_deadline_seconds` | 10 | Write deadline for typed status/close frames |
| `reconnect_grace_seconds` | 30 | Matches the Cubelet detached-session grace |
| `max_frame_bytes` | 65536 | Maximum frame size (≤ 65536 enforced) |
| `max_sessions_per_user` | 5 | Concurrent terminal-session limit per user |
| `max_sessions_per_replica` | 200 | Active terminal WebSocket/relay limit per CubeOps replica |
| `drain_timeout_seconds` | 30 | Drain deadline for in-flight terminal relays |
| `internal_token` | "" | Shared relay credential (≥ 16 bytes); empty keeps the gateway fail-closed |

Settings mirrored for deployment visibility but enforced by the Cubelet session core (PR #1257): `idle_timeout_minutes` (30), `max_lifetime_hours` (8), `replay_buffer_bytes` (262144), `stdin_queue_frames` (8), and `stdout_pending_bytes` (262144). CubeOps validates these values locally, while deployment configuration must keep them aligned with Cubelet; authoritative enforcement remains in the terminal session runtime.

CubeMaster `terminal.*` settings:

| Key | Default | Environment override | Description |
|-----|---------|----------------------|-------------|
| `internal_token` | `""` | `CUBE_TERMINAL_INTERNAL_TOKEN` | Shared relay credential; when set, it must be at least 16 bytes |
| `max_frame_bytes` | 65536 | No | Maximum relay frame size; valid range is 1–65536 |
| `write_deadline_seconds` | 10 | No | Deadline for writing relay responses |
| `close_timeout_seconds` | 15 | No | Timeout for graceful relay-stream closure |

## Security Model

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Admin browser
    participant O as CubeOps
    participant M as CubeMaster
    participant L as Cubelet
    B->>O: request terminal grant
    O->>O: authorize admin and bind target
    O-->>B: one-use grant
    B->>O: WebSocket + grant + Origin
    O->>O: validate grant, Origin, session, token
    O->>M: relay with internal credentials
    M->>L: Terminal RPC
    L-->>M: opened/stdout/close frames
    M-->>O: typed relay frames
    O-->>B: terminal frames
```

- Grants are short-lived, single-use, and never placed in terminal payloads or long-lived URLs; tokens are stored only as hashes.
- Origin and internal-token checks remain at their respective trust boundaries; an empty internal token keeps the gateway fail-closed.
- No terminal payloads are written to CubeOps, CubeMaster, or audit logs.
- Transport failure is not treated as an authoritative Cubelet close reason.
- Missing/reused/forged grant → 401; non-admin → 403; non-running target → 409; forged Origin → 403; oversized frame → close code 1009.

## Validation

Test plan:

- [x] CubeOps unit tests: 27 passed (gateway, grants, store, service, config)
- [x] CubeMaster unit tests: 21 passed (relay, terminalprotocol, config)
- [x] Migration checks pass for both dialects (additive, same timestamp prefix, migration lock)
- [x] `git diff --check` passes; the branch contains PR #1257's base plus only relay/gateway/config/migration changes

Real-cluster evidence:

- Full-chain correlation reconciliation on a remote GCP KVM node: WebUI → CubeOps → CubeMaster → remote Cubelet session → remote Cubelet execID → database records, all bound to the remote node alias `node-c`.
- The full 401/403/409/1009 validation matrix from the Security Model was exercised and passed, including `409 TARGET_NOT_RUNNING` for a terminal open on a paused sandbox.
- Audit: grant/session tables record operator, time, and target; token stored as a hash only; no terminal content.
- The original failure and the independent correlation-recovery directory are both retained.
- Cross-backend semantics (E3, executed from the PR #1259 branch; full report in PR #1259): A↔B grant issuance/consumption both PASS; the same grant concurrently consumed across two backends yields one `101/opened` and one `401`; SIGTERM → `SERVER_DRAINING` → the client resumed the same session/PID/exec.

Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-5.6-Sol
Signed-off-by: Hong Cao <hongcao@u.nus.edu>

title: feat: add Web Terminal protocol and Cubelet runtime
body:
Related to #643

## Summary

Adds the protocol and Cubelet runtime layers of the Web Terminal feature. It introduces a bidirectional streaming `Terminal` RPC on the CubeboxMgr service, forwards PTY resize through CubeShim to the guest agent, and adds a Cubelet terminal session core with PTY lifecycle, bounded stdin/stdout, reconnect grace, idle timeout, maximum lifetime, deterministic close reasons, and replay journal recovery for resumable sessions.

This PR is split out of [#1247](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1247). It is scoped to protocol, CubeShim, and Cubelet runtime code; the CubeMaster relay, CubeOps grants/gateway, WebUI, and deployment wiring are delivered by the follow-up PRs [#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258) and [#1259](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259) of this series.

## Motivation

CubeSandbox offers unary command execution but no interactive shell into a running container. The unary `Exec` RPC is fire-and-forget: it cannot carry continuous stdin, incremental stdout, window resizes, TTY signal semantics, the asynchronous exit status, or resource reclamation after the caller disconnects. A Web Terminal (issue #643) needs a bidirectional, resumable session channel that survives transient transport loss.

The Web Terminal adds a governed bidirectional `Terminal` RPC instead of reusing either existing path, because neither can carry an authorized, per-container interactive stream:

- **Not the unary `Exec` RPC.** `Exec` is fire-and-forget with dummy IO (`exec.go` attaches `createDummyIO(req.Terminal, "", "", "")`, starts, and returns immediately; empty FIFO paths, no-op `Wait()`/`Close()`; the proto carries no stdin/stdout/resize fields) — it structurally cannot hold a live session.
- **Not the envd PTY path.** envd is a sandbox-internal service on port `49983` behind the guest-internal passwordless `Basic root:` credential — no platform-level per-user authorization; its PTY attaches to the sandbox **main environment**, not a chosen container; and a browser/CubeOps route to it would leave the ops plane (no Origin allowlist, rate limit, or audit hook) while depending on envd being baked into the guest image.
- **Reuse the same containerd `Task.Exec` engine instead.** That path is already proven streaming-TTY-capable in-repo (`envd_version.go` uses `cio.WithStreams` + `cio.WithTerminal`); the new RPC adds only a governed transport layer, so `Exec` and every existing caller stay untouched.

This satisfies issue #643 criterion 3 ("reuse the underlying execution capability") without leaving the ops plane, and keeps CubeAPI at zero diff (ops-only).

This PR provides that transport and session substrate. PR [#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258) adds the authorized browser-facing relay and gateway, and PR [#1259](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259) adds the WebUI entry points and deployment wiring that make the terminal reachable from the Dashboard.

## Live Demo

https://cubedemo.1zero.me

- Username: `admin`
- Password: `admin`
- This is a shared temporary environment; Password changes are disabled so the shared credentials remain stable.

The deployment exercises the combined stack from [#1257](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1257), [#1258](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1258), and [#1259](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259). It was developed from the final PR branch [feat/web-terminal-ui-one-click](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/1259), with a demo-only multi-container runtime patch layered in the separate branch [demo/issue643-multicontainer-runtime](https://github.com/1zero224/CubeSandbox/pull/12).

The additional runtime patch provides a real sandbox with multiple containers so maintainers can verify container discovery, container selector switching, and independent terminal sessions. It is used only for the live demo.

## Changes

| Area | What |
|------|------|
| Protocol | Bidirectional `Terminal` RPC on CubeboxMgr (cubebox v1); generated CubeMaster/Cubelet protobuf bindings; `protocol/terminal-v1.json` manifest; `tools/terminal-protocol-gen` generator with `make terminal-protocol-sync/check` wired into `fmt-check.yml` |
| CubeShim | Forward PTY resize to the guest agent, with containerd dimensions mapped to agent rows/columns |
| Cubelet | `terminalcore` session state machine: PTY lifecycle, bounded stdin/stdout, reconnect grace, idle timeout, maximum lifetime, deterministic close reasons (e.g. `SLOW_PRODUCER` for slow producers) |
| Cubelet | Fixed-capacity circular replay ring and journal records for resume/replay recovery; cleanup of admission fences and containerd wait/pipe resources on failure paths |
| Cubelet | `Terminal` service plumbing, `terminal_config.go` settings, open correlation logs, destroy/resume integration |

## Configuration

New Cubelet terminal settings (defaults from `defaultTerminalServicesConfig`, mirrored by the terminalcore `Config.Validate` checks):

| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `reconnect_grace_seconds` | 30 | A detached session may be resumed within this window |
| `replay_buffer_bytes` | 262144 | Fixed capacity of the resume replay ring |
| `max_frame_bytes` | 65536 | Maximum terminal frame size before rejection |
| `stdin_queue_frames` | 8 | Bounded stdin queue depth |
| `stdout_chunk_bytes` | 32768 | stdout chunk size |
| `stdout_pending_bytes` | 262144 | Bounded stdout pending budget |
| `max_sessions` | 100 | Node-wide session limit |
| `max_sessions_per_sandbox` | 10 | Per-sandbox session limit |
| `max_sessions_per_container` | 5 | Per-container session limit |
| `resize_coalesce_millis` | 100 | Resize coalescing window |
| `open_timeout_seconds` | 10 | Open handshake timeout |
| `idle_timeout_minutes` | 30 | Idle sessions are closed after this |
| `max_lifetime_hours` | 8 | Hard session lifetime |
| `cleanup_grace_seconds` | 2 | Post-close cleanup grace |
| `cleanup_timeout_seconds` | 10 | Cleanup deadline |
| `drain_timeout_seconds` | 15 | Drain deadline on sandbox pause |
| `reconcile_interval_seconds` | 300 | Detached-session reconciliation interval |

## Session Lifecycle

Reconnect is a deliberate design choice. On an abnormal transport close, the PTY stays alive locally for a 30 s grace period (`DetachedGrace`) and stdout is buffered into a 256 KiB ring with absolute offsets; a resume inside the window replays from the cursor and restores the same shell and PID, so the session survives a transient transport loss instead of being replaced. Because the grace window is enforced locally by the Cubelet, no dedicated broker is needed — which would add a new failure domain (persisted sensitive output, dual-writer fencing) — and the same resume benefit is achieved with bounded, per-node local state. Replay is cursor-incremental, stdin is fenced to a single attachment via generation counts, and slow consumers are never served under a held lock.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Opening
    Opening --> Attached: open accepted
    Attached --> Attached: stdin / resize / stdout activity
    Attached --> DetachedGrace: transport lost
    DetachedGrace --> Attached: resume before grace expiry
    DetachedGrace --> Closing: grace expires atomically
    Attached --> Closing: idle / lifetime / protocol / slow producer
    Closing --> Closed: cleanup complete
    Closed --> [*]
```

## Security And Limits

- Terminal payloads are bounded before entering the PTY path (frame size and queue limits).
- Replay data is retained only within the configured fixed capacity.
- Close reasons are sanitized against the protocol allowlist.
- Panic containment is installed in the independent receive goroutine so a malformed stream cannot unwind into the Cubelet process.
- No terminal payloads or credentials are written to logs.

## Validation

Test plan:

- [x] `Cubelet/services/cubebox/terminalcore` unit tests: 24 passed
- [x] `Cubelet/services/cubebox` handler tests: 8 passed, including backpressure close behavior
- [x] Cubelet integration tests: 2 passed on the cube runtime (real PTY lifecycle: ANSI output, Ctrl+C interrupt, `stty size` reflecting resize)
- [x] `make terminal-protocol-check` (generated-constant drift check) wired into CI
- [x] Go formatting and `git diff --check` pass

Real-cluster evidence:

- 10/10 scenario groups passed: discover, provision, core, security, grace-expiry, concurrency, idle, drain, audit, cleanup.
- Real xterm I/O: `ls --color`; `top`/`ping` interrupted via Ctrl+C — the same session stays open, no shell recreate; `top` renders fullscreen and exits via `q`; window resize reflected in `stty size`.
- Disconnect → resume restored the same session and shell PID within the grace window, replaying buffered output; `exit` closes the session normally without recreating a shell; idle timeout closes cleanly.
- Sessions isolated by sessionID under per-sandbox/container session limits; four sessions across two users did not interfere, and two sessions in one sandbox hold distinct shell PIDs — closing one leaves the other running.
- Non-running targets return `TARGET_NOT_RUNNING`, draining sandboxes `SANDBOX_TRANSITION`; pausing with a terminal open stops the old terminal.
- `terminal_opened` correlation logs and journal container binding (audit group pass).

Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-5.6-Sol
Signed-off-by: Hong Cao <hongcao@u.nus.edu>

title: one-click: make the CubeProxy admin port configurable
body:
## Problem

CubeProxy's `/admin/*` listener is pinned to `8082`. cube-proxy runs with host networking, so if anything else on the node already holds that port, nginx exits with:

```
nginx: [emerg] bind() to <node-ip>:8082 failed (98: Address in use)
```

`cube-sandbox-control.target` then fails to come up, and `install.sh` gives no indication of why. The public HTTP/HTTPS/gRPC ports have all been configurable for a while; the admin port was the gap.

Two checks made this worse rather than catching it:

- The pre-start conflict check in `up-cube-proxy.sh` covered `CUBE_PROXY_HTTP_PORT` / `HTTPS` / `GRPC`, but not the admin port.
- `cube-proxy-postcheck.sh` only probed HTTP and gRPC, so a failed admin bind left the unit looking healthy while every lifecycle operation (pause/resume via cube-lifecycle-manager) was dead.

## Fix

Adds `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT`, defaulting to `8082` so existing deployments are unaffected, and threads it through everything that referenced the port:

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| `up-cube-proxy.sh` | new var; `__CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT__` nginx placeholder; `CUBE_PROXY_ID` / `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_URL` |
| `up-cube-proxy.sh` preflight | admin port added to the existing conflict loop |
| `cube-proxy-postcheck.sh` | probes the admin listener |
| `build-release-bundle.sh` | emits the new placeholder |
| `create.sh` / `tke-addons.tf` / `variables.tf` | `cube_proxy_admin_port` variable across 5 sites |
| `env.example`, `README.md`, `README_zh.md` | documented, EN + ZH |

The Kubernetes chart already supported `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT` (`chart/files/cube-proxy/cube-proxy-entrypoint.sh`), so this brings the one-click and Terraform paths in line with naming that was already settled rather than inventing any.

## Worth a maintainer's eye

The Terraform `cube_proxy_admin_port` variable is the only piece here that adds new public surface rather than plumbing an existing value. The issue asked for Terraform coverage, so it is included — happy to drop it into a follow-up if you would rather keep this PR to the one-click path.

## Tests

Written test-first in `deploy/one-click/tests/test_package_layout.sh` (already run in CI by `terraform-validate.yml`). 8 assertions covering the default, the discovery URLs, the preflight loop, the postcheck, `env.example` and the bundle placeholder.

Plus a **round-trip test** that goes beyond static grepping: it renders the generated template with a deliberately non-default port and asserts the result is `listen 10.0.0.7:9082;`, with no `127.0.0.1:8082` binding left behind. Verified it actually bites by temporarily changing `CubeProxy/nginx.conf` to listen on `8085` — three assertions failed — then reverting.

## Verification

- `test_package_layout.sh` → `package layout tests OK`
- Full `deploy/one-click/tests/` suite → 9/10 pass
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive` → clean
- `terraform validate` → `Success! The configuration is valid.`
- `bash -n` clean on every modified script

The one failing suite file is `test_runtime_file_safety.sh`, which **fails identically on unmodified `master`** (an unrelated `cube-sandbox-webui.service` `After=` expectation) and is not run by CI. Untouched here.

Closes #945

title: cubeops,web: WebUI web terminal for running sandboxes (#643)
body: ## What this does Adds a **web terminal** to the WebUI: an interactive shell inside a running sandbox, opened from the dashboard with no SSH, SDK or CLI. Refs #643 ## Approach Terminals are an operations capability, so the endpoint lives in **CubeOps** and reuses the **envd `process.Process` PTY API** that the Python/Node/Go SDKs already drive through cube-proxy. **No new RPC is added to CubeMaster, Cubelet, CubeShim or the in-guest agent.** ``` Browser (xterm.js) │ wss:///opsapi/v1/terminal/ws?ticket= ▼ CubeOps :3010 ← JWT auth, ticket issuance, session registry, audit log │ Connect-JSON over HTTP (streaming Start/Connect + unary SendInput/Update/SendSignal) ▼ CubeProxy ──► envd :49983 inside the sandbox ``` Two paths were considered and rejected: - **Browser connecting straight to `/sandbox//49983/`** — that route has no authentication end to end, so anyone holding a sandbox ID gets a root shell, and the traffic never passes CubeOps so nothing can be audited. - **Cubelet Exec** — it is fire-and-forget with dummy IO: no streaming output, no attach semantics. It cannot carry an interactive session. ## Authentication Browsers cannot attach an `Authorization` header to a WebSocket handshake. Putting the login JWT in the query string would leak a long-lived credential into access logs and browser history, so instead: 1. `POST /api/v1/sdk/sandboxes/:id/terminal` — authenticated with the normal login JWT, on the existing authed route group. Verifies the sandbox exists and is `running`, then issues a **one-time ticket**: a 30-second JWT with its own audience (`cubeops:terminal`), consumed on first use. 2. `GET /api/v1/terminal/ws?ticket=…` — the upgrade. The ticket is the only credential, and it is useless against any other endpoint. ## Sessions - **Multiple terminals per sandbox**, each with its own PTY and PID. - **Closing the dialog kills the shell** — the client sends an explicit close frame and CubeOps sends `SIGKILL`. - **A dropped connection does not.** The session registry keeps the PTY, and the UI offers a reconnect that reattaches to the same PID via envd `Connect`, so foreground work survives a network blip. - **Idle sessions are reaped** after 30 minutes without input, configurable via `terminal_idle_timeout` / `CUBE_OPS_TERMINAL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`. ## Auditing `requestLogger()` records no identity, so the terminal writes its own lines to the CubeOps log (`/data/log/CubeOps/cubeops-req.log`). These are **real lines captured from the test cluster**, not illustrations — sandbox ID, username, client IP, PID, duration and the reason the session ended: One uninterrupted stretch of that log, covering two concurrent sessions, a drop-and-reconnect and both ways a session can end (sandbox ID abbreviated for width, everything else verbatim): ``` 22:59:40 terminal_session_start sessionID=931fffc8-f529-41ad-ba0c-a4ebc65eaa74 sandboxID=fe57331d… username=admin clientIP=127.0.0.1 pid=182 reconnect=false 23:00:02 terminal_session_start sessionID=75b6cdc4-aac8-435c-b763-1fdabf17ea75 sandboxID=fe57331d… username=admin clientIP=127.0.0.1 pid=192 reconnect=false 23:00:07 terminal_session_end sessionID=75b6cdc4-aac8-435c-b763-1fdabf17ea75 sandboxID=fe57331d… username=admin clientIP=127.0.0.1 pid=192 reason=detached durationMs=5007 23:00:08 terminal_session_start sessionID=75b6cdc4-aac8-435c-b763-1fdabf17ea75 sandboxID=fe57331d… username=admin clientIP=127.0.0.1 pid=192 reconnect=true 23:00:11 terminal_session_end sessionID=931fffc8-f529-41ad-ba0c-a4ebc65eaa74 sandboxID=fe57331d… username=admin clientIP=127.0.0.1 pid=182 reason=pty_exit durationMs=31174 23:00:11 terminal_session_end sessionID=75b6cdc4-aac8-435c-b763-1fdabf17ea75 sandboxID=fe57331d… username=admin clientIP=127.0.0.1 pid=192 reason=client_close durationMs=9602 ``` Reading it: two terminals run side by side on the same sandbox with distinct PIDs (182, 192); 192's socket drops abnormally at 23:00:07 and the reconnect a second later comes back on the **same session ID and the same PID**, so the shell was never killed; 182 ends because the user typed `exit`, 192 because the dialog was closed. Separately, the idle sweeper firing on a terminal left open and untouched for ~33 minutes: ``` 22:01:24 terminal_session_end sessionID=a82193f4-f5d1-4116-a018-18f579299bd5 sandboxID=fe57331d… username=admin clientIP=127.0.0.1 pid=94 reason=idle_timeout durationMs=1975625 ``` `reason` distinguishes `client_close`, `pty_exit`, `detached`, `idle_timeout`, `stream_error` and `reconnect_failed`. ## Deployment `/opsapi/` forwards no `Upgrade` header and caps reads at 300s, so the WebSocket path gets its own nginx location with the upgrade headers and the same 7206s timeout the `/sandbox/` proxy already uses. `vite.config.ts` sets `ws: true` on the dev proxy for the same reason. ## Testing **Go — 26 tests in `CubeOps/internal/terminal/`** (32 including table-driven subtests), passing under `-race`, with a fake envd HTTP server that speaks the Connect framing: - Streaming client: PID extraction, output decoding, the `-.` proxy Host, non-zero exit, interrupted transport, and that unary endpoints get plain `application/json` (envd answers 415 to a streaming content-type). - Tickets: issue/redeem, single use, expiry, foreign audience rejection, and that the consumed-ticket map is pruned. - WebSocket bridge: end-to-end through `httptest` + a gorilla client — input, resize, ping/pong, the requested initial window size, exit reporting, ticket replay rejection, two independent sessions, reconnect to a detached session, and rejection of a PID the registry does not know. - Registry: idle reaping, activity deferring it, detached sessions still reaped, and reattach requiring a sandbox+PID match. **Frontend — vitest + jsdom introduced** (`web/` had no test framework), 11 tests covering the socket state machine: ticket flow, UTF-8-safe base64, reconnect-by-PID, exit vs. drop, and the two races described below. **Real cluster** — verified against a running sandbox on a single-node KVM cluster (Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, nested virtualisation), driving the browser side of the protocol with a standalone WebSocket client: ``` === A. open a terminal and run commands [PASS] handshake upgraded to 101 — HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols [PASS] ready frame with pid — {'type': 'ready', 'pid': 197} [PASS] echo command executed [PASS] runs as root inside sandbox [PASS] sandbox is aarch64 === B. UTF-8 and ANSI colour [PASS] multi-byte UTF-8 round-trips [PASS] ANSI escape preserved === C. resize propagates to the PTY [PASS] stty reports the new size === D. ping/pong keepalive [PASS] pong received — [{'type': 'pong'}] === E. full-screen program (top) [PASS] top produced output === F. ticket is single-use [PASS] replayed ticket rejected — upgrade failed: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized === G. second concurrent terminal is independent [PASS] second session has a different pid — 197 vs 207 [PASS] second session runs its own shell [PASS] sessions do not cross-talk === H. reconnect after an abnormal drop [PASS] reattached to the same pid — {'type': 'ready', 'pid': 207} [PASS] shell survived the drop === I. shell exit is reported [PASS] exit frame received — [{'type': 'exit', 'exitCode': 0}] === J. explicit close kills the shell ALL CHECKS PASSED ``` The `top` case covers the issue's `ls` / `top` / `ping` acceptance criterion; the resize case asserts on `stty size` inside the PTY rather than on the UI alone. Browser verification found two real bugs, both fixed with regression tests: - **xterm never mounted.** Radix renders portal children on a second pass, so the ref was still null when the mount effect ran, and the effect never re-fired — the dialog was permanently blank. Fixed by tracking the node in state. - **One dialog leaked two PTYs.** A shared "closing" boolean was reset by a newer connect attempt while an older ticket request was still in flight, so the abandoned attempt opened a socket nobody owned. Confirmed in the backend log (two sessions, pids 59 and 60, for one dialog). Fixed with a per-attempt generation counter. A third issue surfaced from real calls: a deleted sandbox returned 502 instead of 404, because the CubeMaster business error code was not mapped. ## Screenshot An interactive session against a running sandbox on a real cluster — ANSI colour, UTF-8, the window size reported by `stty size` after a resize, and the sandbox's own process tree: ## Known limitations - **No container selector.** One sandbox is one MicroVM running one envd; the repo has no notion of a container list. Documented. - **Authorization is coarse.** Any authenticated dashboard user can open a root terminal into any sandbox — CubeOps has no per-sandbox ownership model today. This is pre-existing rather than introduced here, but the terminal makes it consequential, so it is called out in the docs with the recommendation to treat dashboard login as cluster-wide root. Happy to add an ownership check as a follow-up if maintainers want it. - **Scrollback lives in the browser**, capped at 5000 lines and lost on close. - **No file transfer** — the SDK filesystem API covers that. ## Docs `docs/guide/web-terminal.md` and `docs/zh/guide/web-terminal.md`, registered in both the EN "Operations" and ZH "安全与运维" sidebars.

title: cubeapi: accept e2b flattened autoPause/autoResume on sandbox create
body:
## Problem

The e2b Python SDK does not put `lifecycle` on the wire. `Sandbox.create(lifecycle={"on_timeout": "pause", "auto_resume": True})` is flattened client-side into top-level fields before `POST /sandboxes`:

```json
{ "templateID": "<id>", "timeout": 30, "autoPause": true, "autoResume": { "enabled": true } }
```

`NewSandbox` bound neither field, so serde dropped them silently. CubeAPI then resolved `lifecycle = None` and forwarded `auto_pause=false` to CubeMaster — the sandbox was **killed** at timeout instead of paused. The setting appeared to succeed at the SDK layer and did nothing.

## Fix

- `NewSandbox` binds `autoPause` and `autoResume`.
- New `SandboxAutoResume` untagged enum accepts both `{"enabled": true}` (current SDK) and bare `true` (older releases, hand-rolled clients) — same meaning, so no reason to 400 on shape.
- Lifecycle derivation extracted from the inline closure in `create_sandbox` into `resolve_lifecycle_flags()`, a pure function that unit tests can reach.

## Design decision worth reviewing

**When a request carries both `lifecycle` and the flattened fields, the nested `lifecycle` object wins.**

Reasoning: the e2b SDK never sends both, so this only disambiguates direct API callers — and an explicit `lifecycle` can only come from someone who meant it. Happy to invert this if maintainers prefer the flat fields taking precedence.

## Tests

7 lifecycle tests, 5 of them new, written test-first:

- `new_sandbox_deserializes_e2b_flat_lifecycle_fields` — the exact e2b wire body
- `new_sandbox_accepts_bare_bool_auto_resume`
- `flat_lifecycle_fields_enable_pause_and_resume`
- `nested_lifecycle_wins_over_flat_lifecycle_fields`
- `absent_lifecycle_fields_keep_kill_behaviour` — no behaviour change for callers that don't opt in

## Verification

Run in the project builder image (`rustc 1.89`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`):

- `make cube-api-test` → 108 passed, 0 failed
- `make cubeapi` → clean release build
- `cargo fmt --check` → clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` → warning set identical to the pre-change baseline; none in new code
- `cargo build --locked` passes — no dependency changes, `Cargo.lock` untouched

## Also updated

- `openapi.yml` — regenerated via `cube-api --export-openapi`, applying only the additive schema hunks so the hand-maintained license header and `servers:` block survive.
- `docs/guide/lifecycle.md` and `docs/zh/guide/lifecycle.md` — new "Wire format" section covering both accepted shapes and the precedence rule, EN and ZH in sync.

Closes #965

title: fix(templatecenter): fix snapshot-create request ID idempotency
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1105

`SubmitSandboxSnapshot` previously called `buildSnapshotRequests` before taking the snapshot write lock and passed an empty snapshot ID. `NormalizeRequest` filled that empty value with a random `tpl-*` ID. The first-time path later overwrote it with the generated snapshot ID, but the retry path compared a newly randomized request against the stored fingerprint, so an identical retry was rejected as payload drift.

This PR:

- Moves snapshot request construction inside the snapshot write lock.
- Rebuilds retry requests with the existing job's `TemplateID` before normalization.
- Generates the snapshot ID before request construction on the first-time path and uses that same ID throughout job and definition creation.
- Preserves the existing full-request fingerprint semantics, including the snapshot ID, and leaves the template COMMIT flow unchanged.
- Adds a regression test that exercises the real `SubmitSandboxSnapshot` retry matcher without patching it.

## Impact

An identical snapshot-create retry with the same `request_id` can reattach to the existing job or recover its stored result. Genuine request drift is still rejected, and no fingerprint fields are excluded.

## Test plan

The following tests passed in the repository-provided builder environment:

```bash
make builder-run BUILDER_CMD='cd /workspace/CubeMaster && go test -count=1 -v -run TestSubmitSandboxSnapshot ./pkg/templatecenter/'
make builder-run BUILDER_CMD='cd /workspace/CubeMaster && go test -count=1 -v -run TestBuildSnapshotRequestsUsesSnapshotID ./pkg/templatecenter/'
make builder-run BUILDER_CMD='cd /workspace/CubeMaster && go test -count=1 -v -run TestBuildCommitTemplateSpecFingerprintIgnoresRequestID ./pkg/templatecenter/'
```

title: fix(cubeproxy): invalidate deleted sandbox route cache
body:
## Motivation

CubeProxy should stop using stale local routes after a sandbox is deleted and expose a clear response when Redis confirms that no route metadata exists.

Scanning the entire shared cache during invalidation makes lifecycle operations proportional to the global cache size and blocks the Nginx worker performing the scan. After invalidation, a confirmed route miss and a Redis lookup failure also both return HTTP 503, so clients cannot distinguish missing metadata from a temporary metadata-store failure.

## What Changed

* Replace shared-cache scans with bounded invalidation of `meta_cached` and the fixed route metadata mirrored from Redis.
* Invalidate `meta_cached` first so new data-plane requests reload route metadata instead of immediately using stale per-port entries.
* Reuse the bounded helper for lifecycle deletion and explicit backend-cache invalidation without enumerating dynamic per-port keys.
* Return HTTP 404 when both supported Redis route lookups complete successfully and neither contains route metadata.
* Preserve HTTP 503 when any Redis route lookup fails and no valid route is found.
* Log confirmed route misses at warning level and add focused regression coverage.

## Validation

* `make -C CubeProxy test` passed with the target OpenResty LuaJIT runtime.
* Regression coverage confirms that invalidation never calls `get_keys()`, removes the cache-hit sentinel before the fixed route keys, leaves dynamic per-port entries to TTL cleanup, and does not affect other sandboxes.
* Route lookup coverage confirms HTTP 404 for authoritative misses and HTTP 503 for Redis failures and mixed miss/error outcomes.

## Scope

This PR keeps cache invalidation bounded to known per-sandbox keys. It intentionally does not scan or eagerly delete dynamic per-port entries; those entries cannot form an immediate cache hit after `meta_cached` is removed and remain subject to their existing TTL.

This PR does not add negative caching, change the lifecycle event protocol, or modify Redis route publication ordering. Requests for nonexistent sandbox IDs continue to perform the same Redis lookups as before.

## Note: E2B Compatibility

Official E2B's data-plane proxy returns HTTP 502 when the requested sandbox cannot be found, while this PR currently returns HTTP 404 for a confirmed missing sandbox route.

Maintainer confirmation is needed on whether CubeProxy should keep HTTP 404 or use HTTP 502 for closer E2B data-plane compatibility. Redis lookup failures remain HTTP 503 in either case.

title: fix(Node SDK): Add SetTimeout() to Node SDK
body:
## Summary

Fix the missing `Sandbox.setTimeout()` API in the Node SDK, allowing users to update a sandbox's idle TTL while it is running.

Closes #1250

## Changes

### Modified Files

- `sdk/node/src/config.ts` — Add the `NEVER_TIMEOUT = -1` constant.
- `sdk/node/src/index.ts` — Export `NEVER_TIMEOUT` from the Node SDK package entry point.
- `sdk/node/src/sandbox.ts` — Add `Sandbox.setTimeout(timeout)`, which calls `POST /sandboxes/:id/timeout`.
- `sdk/node/test/sandbox.test.ts` — Add regression coverage for timeout updates, boundary values, input validation, and error mapping.
- `sdk/node/README.md` — Document `sb.setTimeout(timeout)` in the API method table.

## API

```ts
async setTimeout(timeout: number): Promise<void>
```

## Behavior

- Positive integers update the sandbox idle TTL in seconds.
- `0` requests immediate expiry.
- `NEVER_TIMEOUT` (`-1`) disables the idle timeout.
- Positive fractional seconds are rounded up to whole seconds, matching the Go SDK's `time.Duration` semantics: `0.5` seconds is sent as `1` second.
- Other negative values, `NaN`, and `Infinity` are rejected before a request is sent.
- Reuses the Node SDK's existing control-plane error mapping; a 404 response results in `SandboxNotFoundError`.

## Testing

```
cd sdk/node
npm test -- sandbox.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

Test results:

- `npm test -- sandbox.test.ts`: passed, 45 tests.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm test`: passed, 186 tests passed and 1 integration test skipped.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Not in Scope

- No changes to CubeAPI, CubeMaster, Cubelet, or lifecycle services.
- No changes to existing sandbox URL path escaping behavior.
- Does not expose `POST /sandboxes/:id/refreshes`.

title: [Bug Report] Node SDK is missing Sandbox.setTimeout() for updating sandbox idle TTL
body:
## Summary

The Node SDK does not expose `Sandbox.setTimeout()`, preventing users from updating a sandbox's idle timeout (idle TTL) while it is running.

The server already implements `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxID}/timeout`; both the Python SDK (#743  ) and the Go SDK(#850 )provide corresponding wrappers. Only the Node SDK lacks this capability.

## Environment

- CubeSandbox version / commit: latest `master`
- Host OS and kernel version: N/A, SDK-only issue
- KVM info (`modinfo kvm`): N/A, SDK-only issue
- Deployment mode: N/A, SDK-only issue
- Relevant component: other / Node SDK (`sdk/node`, `@cubesandbox/sdk` 0.3.0)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a sandbox with the Node SDK:

   ```ts
   import { Sandbox } from "@cubesandbox/sdk";
   
   const sb = await Sandbox.create({ template: "tpl-test" });
   ```

2. Attempt to update the idle TTL while the sandbox is running:

   ```
   await sb.setTimeout(3600);
   ```

3. TypeScript compilation fails:

   ```
   error TS2339: Property 'setTimeout' does not exist on type 'Sandbox'.
   ```

## Expected Behavior

The Node SDK should expose the following method on `Sandbox` instances:

```
async setTimeout(timeout: number): Promise<void>
```

The method should call the already supported control-plane endpoint:

```
POST /sandboxes/{sandboxID}/timeout
Content-Type: application/json
```

Expected request body:

```
{
  "timeout": 3600
}
```

Expected `timeout` semantics:

```
await sb.setTimeout(3600);          // sends timeout: 3600
await sb.setTimeout(0.5);           // 500ms, sends timeout: 1
await sb.setTimeout(0);             // expires immediately
await sb.setTimeout(NEVER_TIMEOUT); // -1, disables idle timeout
```

The method should accept the server's `204 No Content` success response and reuse the SDK's existing error mapping: a 404 response should throw `SandboxNotFoundError`, while other non-success responses should map to the existing API error types.

## Actual Behavior

The Node SDK's `Sandbox` class has no `setTimeout()` method, and the package entry point does not export an equivalent `NEVER_TIMEOUT` constant.

Users must bypass the SDK and hand-roll the control-plane HTTP request:

```
await fetch(`${apiUrl}/sandboxes/${sb.sandboxId}/timeout`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ timeout: 3600 }),
});
```

This requires users to handle authentication, request timeouts, response status codes, and error mapping themselves, defeating the purpose of the SDK wrapper.

```
TypeScript users encounter TS2339 at compile time;
JavaScript users can only discover that this capability is unavailable at runtime.
```

## Additional Context

The server route, OpenAPI contract, and backend implementation already exist. This is therefore a missing client-side wrapper in the Node SDK, not missing backend functionality.

The Python SDK already provides:

```
sb.set_timeout(3600)
```

The Go SDK already provides:

```
err := sb.SetTimeout(ctx, time.Hour)
```

The Go SDK accepts `time.Duration`; positive fractional seconds are rounded up to whole seconds before being sent to the server. The Node SDK should follow the same semantics.

Suggested regression tests:

```
- setTimeout(positive integer) sends the correct POST path and JSON request body.
- setTimeout(0) preserves timeout: 0.
- setTimeout(0.5) sends timeout: 1.
- setTimeout(NEVER_TIMEOUT) sends timeout: -1 and verifies that the constant can be imported from the package entry point.
- -2, NaN, and Infinity are rejected before a request is sent.
- A server 404 response maps to SandboxNotFoundError.
```

title: cubelet: drop stale sched_core key from containerd config
body:
Closes #1153

## What

Removes the stale `sched_core = false` key from `[plugins."io.containerd.runtime.v2.task"]` in `Cubelet/config/config.toml`.

## Why

`sched_core` was a field of the runtime v2 task plugin config in containerd **v1.x**. In **v2.2.2** — the version Cubelet pins (`Cubelet/go.mod:175`) — that struct (`core/runtime/v2/task_manager.go`) carries only `platforms`:

```go
type Config struct {
	Platforms []string `toml:"platforms"`
}
```

containerd does ship a migration that rewrites `sched_core` into the shim plugin's `env` as `SCHED_CORE=1`, but it is guarded (`core/runtime/v2/shim_manager.go`):

```go
ConfigMigration: func(ctx context.Context, configVersion int, pluginConfigs map[string]interface{}) error {
	if configVersion >= version.ConfigVersion {
		return nil
	}
	...
	delete(src, "sched_core")
}
```

`Cubelet/config/config.toml:6` declares `version = 3`, and containerd v2.2.2 defines `ConfigVersion = 3`. Since `3 >= 3`, the migration returns early and never strips the key, so the strict-mode decode at plugin init reports it on every Cubelet start.

## Verification

Driven through the production path against real containerd v2.2.2 — `srvconfig.LoadConfig` followed by `Config.Decode("io.containerd.runtime.v2.task", ...)` — with a logrus hook counting warnings.

**Before** (current `master`):

```
LoadConfig OK (version=3, warnings so far=0)
cfg.Decode("io.containerd.runtime.v2.task", *TaskConfig)
  level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin"
    error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct"
    key=sched_core plugin=io.containerd.runtime.v2.task
decoded platforms = [linux/amd64 linux/arm64]
TOTAL WARNINGS = 1
```

**After** (this change):

```
LoadConfig OK (version=3, warnings so far=0)
cfg.Decode("io.containerd.runtime.v2.task", *TaskConfig)
decoded platforms = [linux/amd64 linux/arm64]
TOTAL WARNINGS = 0
```

`platforms` still decodes to `[linux/amd64 linux/arm64]`, so nothing else in the section regressed.

## Two corrections to the issue report

Both are minor but worth recording for anyone reading #1153 later:

1. The issue attributes the warning to `loadConfigFile` in `Cubelet/services/server/config/config.go`. I tested that directly — `LoadConfig` emits **zero** warnings even with `sched_core` present, because the top-level `plugins` field decodes as `map[string]interface{}` and tolerates unknown nested keys. The warning actually originates in `Config.Decode` at plugin-init time.
2. Consequently the real log line is `"Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin"` (containerd's), not `"Ignoring unknown key in TOML"` (Cubelet's) as quoted in the issue.

## Behavior impact

None. The value was `false`, and the migration only injects `SCHED_CORE=1` when it is `true`, so Linux core scheduling remains disabled either way.

For operators who *do* want core scheduling on a `version = 3` config, the supported form under containerd v2.x is:

```toml
[plugins."io.containerd.shim.v1.manager"]
  env = ["SCHED_CORE=1"]
```

## Testing notes

`Cubelet/cmd/cubelet` is Linux-only (cgroups, erofs, cgo `nsenter.c`) and could not be built or tested on the macOS host used here; the verification above was run against the `services/server/config` package, which builds natively. The one existing test that reads this file (`cmd/cubelet/main_test.go:32`) asserts only on the network plugin section and is unaffected by this change.

title: fix(templatecenter): restore snapshot-create request_id idempotency
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1105

`SubmitSandboxSnapshot` previously included the server-generated snapshot ID in the request fingerprint. When a client retried the same payload with the same `request_id`, rebuilding the request could produce a different generated ID, causing the fingerprint comparison to fail and preventing the retry from reusing the existing job.

This PR:

- Adds `marshalSnapshotFingerprintRequest` to exclude `CubeAnnotationAppSnapshotTemplateID` from the snapshot fingerprint input.
- Uses the new marshaller only for snapshot-create fingerprint generation.
- Keeps `marshalTemplateCommitJobRequest` unchanged so the template COMMIT serialization and deduplication behavior are unaffected.
- Adds two regression cases covering deterministic fingerprint rebuilding and matching an identical retry to the stored job.

## Impact

Identical snapshot-create retries using the same `request_id` can now reattach to the existing job or recover its stored result instead of being rejected as a payload mismatch.

The generated snapshot ID remains part of the stored request data; it is excluded only from the fingerprint input.

## Test plan

The following tests passed in the repository-provided builder environment:

- `TestBuildSnapshotRequestsUsesSnapshotID`
- `TestSubmitSandboxSnapshotReusesExistingRequest`
- `TestSubmitSandboxSnapshotResumesPendingExistingRequest`
- `TestSubmitSandboxSnapshotReturnsStoredFailureForExistingRequest`
- `TestSnapshotCreateRequestIDIdempotency`
- `TestBuildCommitTemplateSpecFingerprintIgnoresRequestID`

Each test was run with:

```bash
make builder-run BUILDER_CMD='cd /workspace/CubeMaster && go test -count=1 -v -run <test-name> ./pkg/templatecenter/'
```

## Notes

`make cubemaster-test` is not fully green locally because of pre-existing ARM64/gomonkey test failures that are reproducible on the unmodified `master` branch. The targeted snapshot-create and COMMIT regression tests listed above pass.

title: feat: add administrator-only interactive Web Terminal
body:
Closes #643 ## Summary This PR adds an administrator-only interactive Web Terminal to the existing CubeSandbox WebUI. The implementation uses xterm.js in the browser, one-time terminal grants in CubeOps, a stateless CubeMaster relay, and a Cubelet-owned PTY lifecycle backed by containerd `Task.Exec` through CubeShim. It supports real TTY input/output, resize, fullscreen, multiple independent terminal tabs, bounded replay, detached-session resume, session expiration, pause/drain handling, audit metadata, and production WebSocket routing. ```mermaid flowchart LR U["Admin browser (xterm.js)"] O["CubeOps
auth, one-time grant, Origin, audit"] M["CubeMaster
stateless WebSocket to gRPC relay"] L["Cubelet
terminalcore and PTY lifecycle owner"] C["containerd Task.Exec"] S["CubeShim"] V["Sandbox VM and target container"] U -->|"Authenticated grant POST"| O O -->|"Single-use grant"| U U -->|"cube-terminal.v1 WebSocket"| O O -->|"X-Cube-Internal-Token"| M M -->|"Bidirectional Terminal gRPC"| L L -->|"Create, Start, Resize, Wait, Kill, Delete"| C C --> S S --> V ``` ## Components ### Protocol - Adds the bidirectional `Terminal` RPC to the internal cubebox protocol. - Uses typed open, stdin, resize, close, opened, output, status, and exit frames. - Enforces a 64 KiB frame limit and strict channel/schema validation. - Does not expose runtime IDs, shell selection, or commands supplied by the browser. ### Cubelet - Owns the complete PTY and containerd exec lifecycle. - Resolves the trusted sandbox and container target server-side. - Registers `Wait` before `Start` so short-lived processes cannot lose exit events. - Implements bounded stdin and stdout queues. - Implements resize forwarding, idle/lifetime limits, cleanup aggregation, journal recovery, and per-sandbox drain. - Supports a 30-second detached grace period with bounded replay and generation fencing. - Prevents competing resume attachments from simultaneously owning one session. ### CubeMaster - Relays terminal streams without owning PTYs or durable session state. - Uses the existing Cubelet routing path. - Requires the shared internal transport token. - Propagates request/session correlation metadata. - Joins both relay directions on EOF, cancellation, or downstream failure. ### CubeOps - Requires an authenticated administrator. - Verifies that the sandbox and selected container are running. - Issues grants with a maximum 60-second lifetime. - Atomically consumes each grant once. - Checks the WebSocket Origin before accepting the upgrade. - Enforces user/replica connection limits and drain behavior. - Persists metadata-only grant/session audit records. - Never persists a raw grant or terminal payload. ### WebUI - Adds Terminal actions to the sandbox list and detail views. - Disables the action for non-running sandboxes with an explanatory tooltip. - Supports real xterm.js rendering, copy/paste, font size, fit/resize, and fullscreen. - Supports multiple independent terminal tabs. - Supports transport-loss resume with bounded exponential backoff. - Distinguishes normal close, runtime exit, sandbox transition, server drain, and lost-session states. - Provides synchronized English and Chinese UI text. ### Deployment And Documentation - Routes `/opsapi/v1/terminal/ws` through all three production nginx configurations. - Keeps the ordinary `/opsapi/` REST timeout unchanged. - Configures a 7200-second read timeout only for the terminal WebSocket route. - Preserves the existing `/sandbox/` WebSocket route. - Generates and reuses a shared internal token without placing it in process arguments. - Injects the same secret into CubeOps and CubeMaster through one-click, Helm, and Terraform deployments. - Adds Helm default/override render guards and one-click token/transport tests. - Adds synchronized English and Chinese Web Terminal documentation and VitePress navigation. ## Security Model ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant B as "Admin browser" participant O as "CubeOps" participant M as "CubeMaster" participant L as "Cubelet" participant R as "containerd and CubeShim" B->>O: "Authenticated POST terminal grant" O->>O: "Verify admin, running target, limits" O-->>B: "Single-use grant, session ID, same-origin WS URL" B->>O: "WebSocket with cube-terminal.v1 and grant subprotocol" O->>O: "Check Origin and atomically consume grant" O->>M: "Internal relay using shared service token" M->>L: "Terminal Open with trusted target metadata" L->>R: "Task.Exec with TTY" R-->>L: "Runtime process and PTY" L-->>M: "TerminalOpened" M-->>O: "TerminalOpened" O-->>B: "Opened status" ``` Security properties: - The raw grant appears only in the expected WebSocket subprotocol. - The grant is absent from URLs, query strings, DOM, browser storage, query caches, and committed artifacts. - JWT and Cookie credentials are not copied into the WebSocket URL or subprotocol. - CubeOps-to-CubeMaster authentication uses a separate shared internal token. - User authentication credentials are not forwarded to CubeMaster or Cubelet. - Raw grants are never stored; only a verifier hash is persisted. - Origin, missing, consumed, expired, and mismatched grants are rejected. - Terminal input/output is not written to audit tables or application logs. - `permessage-deflate` is not enabled. - Logs use server-derived error categories rather than peer-controlled terminal text. ## Session Lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Opening Opening --> Attached: "Runtime exec started" Opening --> Closed: "Open rejected or cleanup failed" Attached --> Detached: "Unexpected transport loss" Attached --> Closing: "User close, shell exit, pause, drain, timeout" Detached --> Attached: "Resume within grace period" Detached --> Closing: "Grace period expires" Closing --> Closed: "Kill, Wait, Delete and journal cleanup" Closed --> [*] ``` - A normal user close does not reconnect. - Shell/runtime exit reports the exit state and does not reconnect. - Unexpected transport loss enters the detached grace period. - Resume retains the same terminal session and shell process. - Output produced while detached is replayed from a bounded 256 KiB buffer. - Resume after grace expiry returns `SESSION_LOST`; a new session may then be opened. - Pausing an active sandbox produces `SANDBOX_TRANSITION` without blocking the pause operation. - CubeOps drain rejects new work, converges existing sessions, and recovers ordinary REST/WebUI health after restart. ## Confirmed Validation Completed gates include: - Web protocol/client/component tests: 34/34 PASS. - `npm run lint`: PASS. - `npm run build`: PASS. - `make web-test`: PASS. - `make web-lint`: PASS. - `make web-build`: PASS. - VitePress dependency install and production docs build: PASS. - Helm lint/template and repository workflow guards: PASS. - One-click token and transport wiring tests: PASS. - Terraform formatting, initialization without backend, validation, and shell checks: PASS. - Real nginx `nginx -t`: PASS. - Real WebSocket upgrade through nginx: HTTP 101. - Continuous terminal connection beyond the historical 300/305-second cutoff: PASS at 312 seconds. - Real PTY input/output before and after the long wait: PASS. - Rollback and redeployment verification: PASS. - Sensitive-pattern scans over bounded logs/browser artifacts: zero matches. - Exact task-owned sandbox/session/runtime cleanup: PASS for completed runs.
