title: feat(cubemaster): add CUBEMASTER_AUTO_MIGRATION switch to skip startup schema migration
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-out switch, `CUBEMASTER_AUTO_MIGRATION`, that lets a CubeMaster deployment skip the schema migration it runs at startup.

## Motivation

In a hardened deployment the CubeMaster **runtime** database account is granted DML only, no DDL. Such an account cannot run the startup migrator at all — even when the schema is already at HEAD, the fingerprint defence layer issues an unconditional `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, which fails with `ERROR 1142 (command denied)`. CubeMaster then refuses to boot.

The operational fix in these environments is to apply the schema **out-of-band** with a privileged account (CI job, DBA, etc.) and have CubeMaster boot without touching DDL. Today there is no way to tell CubeMaster to do that.

## Change

- New `migrate.AutoMigrationEnabled()` reads `CUBEMASTER_AUTO_MIGRATION`.
  - Defaults to **true** (migrate).
  - Returns **false** only for an explicit falsey value: `false` / `0` / `no` / `off` (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed).
  - Any unset, empty, or unrecognised value keeps the safe default, so a typo can never silently disable migration. (`strconv.ParseBool` is deliberately avoided because it rejects `no`/`off`.)
- `initDatabaseSchema` gates `dao.Migrate` behind the switch, between `dao.Open` and `dao.Migrate`. Because the gate sits at the top level it is dialect-agnostic (applies to both mysql and postgres).
- When the switch is off, CubeMaster logs a clear warning that DDL must be applied out-of-band.

No behaviour change for existing deployments: the default is unchanged (migrate on boot).

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` in both `CubeDB` and `CubeMaster` modules
- [x] `go vet` clean on the changed packages
- [x] New table-driven unit test `TestAutoMigrationEnabled` covering unset / empty / true / 1 / True / on / yes / garbage (→ enabled) and false / 0 / no / off / FALSE / whitespace-wrapped (→ disabled); 14/14 pass

## Summary

This PR improves the SDK compatibility E2E suite by expanding lifecycle and
network coverage, tightening framework behavior, and reorganizing bilingual
documentation.

Key changes:

- Add per-test/per-module `sandbox_template_id(...)` support so selected cases
  can use a dedicated template without changing the global `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID`.
- Extend network public access coverage for `network.allow_public_traffic=false`:

  - invalid token is rejected with 403;
  - `e2b-traffic-access-token` works with the correct token;
  - `cube-traffic-access-token` works with the correct token.
- Add adapter-level support for public URL and traffic token access through
  `get_host()` and `traffic_access_token()`.
- Keep traffic tokens out of trace output; tracing only records whether a token
  is present.
- Adjust lifecycle tests so data-plane failures after `running` are exposed as
  backend regressions instead of being hidden by extra readiness polling.
- Add comments to creation smoke tests to document their validation points.
- Improve cleanup documentation and add TODO context for paused sandbox cleanup.
- Expand `env.example` and README documentation for E2E configuration,
  failure sandbox retention, public access endpoint expectations, and template
  selection.
- Reorganize E2E docs so English docs live under `docs/` and Chinese docs live
  under `docs/zh/`.

`platform_lifecycle` remains gated by backend capability. The current framework
does not enable it for E2B until lifecycle create-parameter compatibility is

title: [Feature Request] Restore a sandbox's writable layer from an existing disk artifact (backup / restore / migration)

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Impacts the cube-agent which runs in the guest VM

body:
## Problem / Motivation

We are building an agent sandbox platform on CubeSandbox. Our needs center on **backup, restore, and migration** — we do **not** need sandboxes to drift between nodes dynamically:

- **Backup**: periodically export a sandbox's filesystem state to object storage, keeping historical versions;
- **Restore**: rebuild a sandbox from a given historical version (rollback after a bad change, data corruption, rebuild after node failure);
- **Migration**: move a sandbox's state to another node and start it there (node retirement, scaling, datacenter moves) — **infrequent and planned**, not real-time failover.

Today a sandbox's writable layer can come from only two sources (`Cubelet/storage/local.go`, `prepareDefaultMedium`): cloned from a template rootfs snapshot, or a freshly created empty volume. **There is no entry point for "use an existing writable-layer artifact as the initial content of a new sandbox's writable layer"**, so none of the flows above are possible without pulling in templates or memory snapshots.

## Proposed Solution

Add a third source for the writable layer at create time: **initialize the new volume's content from an existing disk artifact on the node**.

With that entry point in place, the full flow works like this:

- **Export**: freeze the writable-layer volume (`pause` → FICLONE → `resume`) and store incremental diffs in object storage as a chain, using our open-source [cowdiff](https://github.com/lf4096/cowdiff) (reflink-aware incremental binary diff).
- **Restore / migrate**: materialize the chain into a writable-layer file on any node, create a sandbox with it as the initial content, and cold-boot.

Restore semantics are **cold only** (disk state, no memory), which is sufficient for all three scenarios. It also requires **no shared storage** — the chain lives in object storage and is materialized locally on the target node.

## Relationship to planned work

We're aware of several related plans; this proposal is **orthogonal** to them:

- **volumes** (#855 / #997, and the plan mentioned in #578): persistent **directory** volumes, decoupling workspace data from the sandbox lifecycle. They do not restore the rootfs writable layer itself, and offer no historical versions / point-in-time rollback. Our state lives in the unified rootfs writable layer.
- **Cross-node pause/resume + tiered snapshot storage** (#921, #578): keeping a *running* sandbox alive across nodes (including memory artifacts), serving real-time drift / failover. **We don't need that** — our migrations are planned and infrequent, and a cold boot is perfectly acceptable. Memory artifacts would be a liability for us (largest artifact, incrementals lose most of their value over long intervals, and they couple tightly to the guest image version).
- Per the discussion in #578, those capabilities assume **user-provided shared storage (NFS / object storage)**. This proposal introduces no shared-storage assumption: restore only needs the target node to fetch the artifact and materialize it locally.

In short: the planned work optimizes **how a running sandbox survives across nodes**; this proposal fills in **how a sandbox's disk state is backed up, restored to a specific version, and moved on demand**. The two can coexist — and the latter is exactly the building block #578's *Sandbox Failover Controller* refers to as "fallback to **restore from backup artifacts** when local replicas are missing".

## Questions before we go further

1. Does this capability (restoring a sandbox's writable layer from an existing disk artifact, then cold-booting) fit CubeSandbox's direction? Would you be open to a PR for it?
2. If so, how would you like it expressed in product terms — a new volume source, or folded into the existing snapshot / template concepts? We're happy to implement it your way.
3. #578 is already assigned — is there in-flight design or implementation that would overlap with this? We'd rather not duplicate work.

## Status

We have a working implementation (consumed in cubelet, field passed through in CubeMaster; **no changes to the cubecow engine**), validated on a two-node PoC: after same-node and cross-node restore, in-guest `md5sum` matches byte-for-byte; invalid inputs are rejected with no resource leaks. Once the direction is confirmed, we'll clean it up into a PR linked to this issue.

Related: #578 (node reliability / restore-from-backup scenario), #855 / #997 (persistent volumes — adjacent but orthogonal), #921 (cross-node snapshot plans).

title: feat(web,api): add interactive Web Terminal for sandboxes
body:
## What

Adds an interactive **Web Terminal** to the WebUI so operators can open a shell into a running sandbox from the console, instead of stitching together CLI/SDK calls. Closes the feature requested in #643.

## Backend — `CubeAPI`

- New route `GET /sandboxes/:sandboxID/terminal` (`handlers/terminal.rs`) that upgrades to a WebSocket and bridges the browser to the sandbox's interactive PTY.
- **Reuses the existing exec path**: the PTY is driven by envd's `process.Process` Connect-JSON RPC (`Start` / `SendInput` / `Update` / `SendSignal`) over the same sandbox proxy (`AGENTHUB_SANDBOX_PROXY_URL` + `Host: 49983-<id>.<domain>`) that `run_envd_command` and the SDKs already use. No new execution mechanism.
- Full-duplex bridge: base64 input (keystrokes/paste), PTY output, **TTY window resize sync**, ping/pong keep-alive, **idle timeout**, and **PTY reaping on disconnect** so closed tabs don't leak shells. Raw binary frames are also accepted for the input hot path.
- **Auth in the handler** (browsers can't set headers on a WS upgrade): honors the `auth_callback_url` gate and the WebUI session store, accepting credentials from headers *or* query params, mirroring `middleware::auth::unified_auth`. Sandbox id + guest user are validated to prevent proxy `Host`-header smuggling.
- **Access control + audit**: rejects non-running sandboxes (HTTP 409) and unauthorized users (401); writes `terminal.session.started` / `terminal.session.closed` audit events (operator, target instance, reason, duration). Idle timeout configurable via `CUBE_API_TERMINAL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 15 min).

## Frontend — `web`

- `SandboxTerminalDialog` renders an **xterm.js** terminal (fit addon, fullscreen toggle, reconnect, live status dot) wired to the WebSocket channel; UTF-8-safe base64 framing.
- `SandboxDetail` gains a **Terminal** action, enabled only while the sandbox is running (disabled with a tooltip otherwise); multiple concurrent sessions are supported.
- New i18n strings in the `en` and `zh` `sandboxDetail` bundles.
- Vite dev proxy set to `ws: true` so the terminal works under `npm run dev` too.

## Docs

`docs/guide/webui.md` and `docs/zh/guide/webui.md` document the terminal entry point, session management, permission/audit model, and the reuse of the envd PTY.

## Acceptance criteria mapping

| # | Criterion | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | "Open Terminal" entry for running instances | `SandboxDetail.tsx` |
| 2 | Interactive shell, ANSI/cursor, resize | xterm.js + `Update` resize RPC |
| 3 | Concurrent sessions, no interference | per-connection session, integration test |
| 4 | Unauthorized blocked; disabled when not running | `authorize()` + 409 guard, button `disabled` |
| 5 | Active disconnect + idle timeout + clear prompts | `CloseReason`, idle sweep, status/reconnect UI |
| 6 | Access audit log | `terminal.session.*` events |
| 7 | Reuse existing container exec/attach; WSS transport | envd `process.Process` over the sandbox proxy |
| 8 | Tests + code-quality checks | see below |

## Testing

Run in Docker on Ubuntu (no host toolchain), against the committed (LF) tree:

- **CubeAPI** (`rust:1.85`): `cargo fmt -- --check` clean; `cargo test` → **100 passed**, including 11 new terminal tests: Connect-frame decoder across chunk boundaries, wire-message parsing, sandbox-id/guest-user validation, session-token precedence, and end-to-end WS↔envd bridge + auth-callback enforcement against mock envd/CubeMaster servers.
- **web** (`node:22`): `npm ci` + `npx prettier --check .` → *All matched files use Prettier code style*; `npm run build` (`tsc -b --noEmit && vite build`) succeeds with `@xterm/*` added.

title: test(cubemaster): resolve unit test debt in builder CI
body:
## Motivation

The change-aware unit-test workflow introduced in #833 initially omitted CubeMaster because its suite did not run reliably in the shared builder CI environment.

CubeMaster declares Go 1.25.7, while the builder image currently uses Go 1.24.8. Letting the older Go command auto-download the module-required toolchain caused coverage collection to fail with `go: no such tool "covdata"`. The suite also contained configuration-path assumptions, root-owned OCI fixtures, inline-sensitive runtime patches, vet-invalid formatting calls, and positive scoring tests that did not exercise non-zero results.

This PR resolves those CubeMaster-specific blockers and then adds the component to the existing unit-test workflow.

## What Changed

- Update the builder image to Go 1.25.7, matching `CubeMaster/go.mod`, while preserving the existing `go list ./...` coverage enumeration.
- Make test configuration deterministic by using the correct component configuration path or an isolated temporary configuration file.
- Use the current test UID/GID for OCI layer fixtures where ownership is not part of the behavior under test.
- Replace inline-sensitive runtime monkey patches with package-local test seams whose default production paths remain unchanged.
- Serialize local-cache data through a detached snapshot instead of mutating the live LRU cache representation.
- Strengthen image-score tests with non-zero lookup results and assertions for lookup IDs, aggregation, threshold conversion, and weighted combinations.
- Update the CubeMaster CLI template-summary assertion to expect the `alias` label introduced by #749 instead of the former `display_name` label.
- Correct stale fixtures and vet-invalid formatting calls without changing the production scoring algorithm.
- Add CubeMaster path detection, manual dispatch, and the `cubemaster-test` target to the change-aware unit-test workflow.

## Review Focus

This PR updates several existing tests and includes a small production fix exposed by the suite. Please pay particular attention to whether:

- The refreshed assertions preserve the original behavior contracts instead of accommodating incorrect behavior.
- The local-cache snapshot fix preserves the live cache representation while retaining the persisted value format.
- The package-level test seams leave the default production paths unchanged.
- The OCI ownership changes only remove unprivileged-builder assumptions from tests where ownership is not under test.

## Validation

The complete CubeMaster unit target passed in the Linux builder:

```bash
cd CubeMaster
make test
```

- `Test CubeMaster` passed in 9m59s with the original coverage-package loop and no `covdata` failure.
- The amd64 and arm64 builder image checks passed with Go 1.25.7.
- Build checks passed for CubeAPI, CubeMaster, Cubelet, CubeShim, agent, and network-agent.
- Code Format Check, DCO Check, and the existing Network Agent unit test passed.

Fork validation: https://github.com/zyl1121/CubeSandbox/pull/7

## Scope

This PR changes:

- `CubeMaster/**`
- `docker/Dockerfile.builder`
- CubeMaster-only entries in `.github/workflows/unit-test-check.yml`

The workflow change does not add a Cubelet mapping or test job. Because the builder Dockerfile is shared infrastructure, its change intentionally revalidates the existing component builds and unit-test targets; those checks passed in the fork validation PR.

Follow-up to #833.

title: fix(fmt): add formatting coverage for CubeNet, CLM, and web frontend
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes missing formatting coverage in the CI pipeline for several components that were not being formatted by `make fmt` or checked in CI.

## What was missing

The root `Makefile` fmt target and the `.github/workflows/fmt-check.yml` CI workflow did not cover the following components:

- **CubeNet** and **CubeNet/cubevs** — had no Makefile with a fmt target, so `make fmt` skipped them entirely
- **cube-lifecycle-manager (CLM)** — had a Makefile but was not wired into the root `make fmt` target
- **sdk/go** — had no Makefile with fmt target
- **examples/cube-bench** — had a Makefile but was not wired into root `make fmt`
- **web frontend** — had no Makefile with fmt target, no prettier config, and was not covered by `make fmt` or CI

## Changes

1. **Added Makefiles** with fmt targets for: `CubeNet/`, `sdk/go/`, `web/`
2. **Added prettier config** (`.prettierrc.json`, `.prettierignore`) for the web frontend
3. **Wired all missing components** into the root `Makefile` fmt target, including a graceful skip for web when npm is not available
4. **Updated CI workflow** (`.github/workflows/fmt-check.yml`) to:
   - Set up Node.js 22 and run prettier formatting check on web sources
   - Add trigger paths for all newly-covered components
5. **Applied formatting** to fix existing style violations in:
   - `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/` Go packages
   - `cubecow/examples/go-test/` Go files
   - `sdk/go/template.go`
   - All web TypeScript/TSX/CSS/JSON files (prettier)

## Verification

- `make fmt` now covers all components end-to-end
- CI will enforce formatting for the entire project on relevant PRs

title: refactor(proto): unify shared proto definitions into a standalone proto/ Go module (#1023 phase1)
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #1023: Unify shared protobuf definitions to eliminate duplication between CubeMaster and Cubelet.

- **Created `proto/` shared Go module** (`github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/proto`) containing the canonical protobuf definitions for `cubebox`, `errorcode`, `images`, and `types`
- **Removed duplicated proto files** from `CubeMaster/api/` (entirely) and `Cubelet/api/` (shared protos only; Cubelet-specific protos like `nbi`, `cubehost`, `multimetadb`, `version` remain)
- **Migrated ~200 Go files** across both CubeMaster and Cubelet to import from the shared module
- **Extracted CRI conversion functions** from `Cubelet/api/types/v1/cri.go` into `Cubelet/pkg/critypes/convert.go` as standalone functions with nil guards, avoiding `k8s.io/cri-api` dependency pollution in the shared module
- **Added table-driven unit tests** for all CRI conversion functions (v1 and v1alpha2), including nil input and edge cases
- **Updated Makefiles** for the new proto generation layout (`proto/Makefile` for shared protos, both CubeMaster and Cubelet delegate to it)
- **Fixed `PROTOBUF_INCLUDE_DIR` detection** to prefer system dirs over `gogo/protobuf`, avoiding CI failures
- **Removed gRPC v1.67.1 pin** from Cubelet to align versions with the shared module

### Before
```
CubeMaster/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto  ← duplicate
Cubelet/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto      ← duplicate
(same for errorcode, images, types)
```

### After
```
proto/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto            ← single source of truth
proto/services/errorcode/v1/errorcode.proto
proto/services/images/v1/images.proto
proto/types/v1/images.proto
proto/types/v1/descriptor.proto
```

## Test plan

- [x] `proto/` module: `go build ./...` passes
- [x] CubeMaster: `GOOS=linux` cross-compilation passes (all packages)
- [x] Cubelet: `GOOS=linux` cross-compilation passes (excluding CGO-only `cubemnt`/`nsenter`)
- [x] Cubelet CRI conversion unit tests: 20/20 pass (including nil guards and v1alpha2 edge cases)
- [x] CI: all builds pass (CubeMaster, Cubelet, CubeShim, CubeAPI, agent, network-agent)
- [x] CI: Code Format Check pass
- [x] CI: DCO check pass

Refs: #1023

## Summary

Phase 1 of #1023: Unify shared protobuf definitions to eliminate duplication between CubeMaster and Cubelet.

- **Created `api/` shared Go module** (`github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/api`) containing the canonical protobuf definitions for `cubebox`, `errorcode`, `images`, and `types`
- **Removed duplicated proto files** from `CubeMaster/api/` (entirely) and `Cubelet/api/` (shared protos only; Cubelet-specific protos like `nbi`, `cubehost`, `multimetadb`, `version` remain)
- **Migrated ~200 Go files** across both CubeMaster and Cubelet to import from the shared module
- **Extracted CRI conversion functions** from `Cubelet/api/types/v1/cri.go` into `Cubelet/pkg/critypes/convert.go` as standalone functions, avoiding `k8s.io/cri-api` dependency pollution in the shared module
- **Updated Makefiles** for the new proto generation layout (`api/Makefile` for shared protos, Cubelet uses `-I=..` to reference them)

### Before
```
CubeMaster/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto  ← duplicate
Cubelet/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto      ← duplicate
(same for errorcode, images, types)
```

### After
```
api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto              ← single source of truth
api/services/errorcode/v1/errorcode.proto
api/services/images/v1/images.proto
api/types/v1/images.proto
```

title: [Feature Request] Refactor control plane API architecture: unify protocol definitions, eliminate redundant types, centralize validation

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

labels.name: rust
labels.description: Pull requests that update rust code

body:
## Background

The CubeSandbox control plane (CubeAPI → CubeMaster → Cubelet) currently suffers from significant architectural redundancy in protocol definitions, type management, serialization/deserialization, and parameter validation. This leads to an unnecessarily large blast radius for every API change and frequent inconsistencies.

## Goals

1. **Single protocol definition** — Proto as the Single Source of Truth
2. **Unified communication protocols** — CubeAPI→CubeMaster via RESTful HTTP, CubeMaster→Cubelet via gRPC
3. **Unified full-chain type definitions** — Eliminate intermediate type layers and manual type conversions
4. **Minimal API change blast radius** — Adding/removing a field should touch as few places as possible
5. **Minimize manual serialization/deserialization** — Leverage `protojson` for automatic handling
6. **Centralized parameter validation** — Declare validation rules in proto using `protovalidate`

---

## Current State Analysis

### Quadruple Type Redundancy

The same concept (e.g., "create sandbox") is defined **4 times** across the chain, with manual type conversion at every boundary:

| Layer | File | Type Name | Language |
|---|---|---|---|
| CubeAPI external API | `CubeAPI/src/models/mod.rs` | `NewSandbox` | Rust |
| CubeAPI→Master wire | `CubeAPI/src/cubemaster/mod.rs` | `CreateSandboxRequest` | Rust |
| CubeMaster HTTP | `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/types/types.go` | `CreateCubeSandboxReq` | Go |
| CubeMaster→Cubelet gRPC | `CubeMaster/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto` | `RunCubeSandboxRequest` | Protobuf |

### Duplicated Proto Files

The same proto files exist in both `CubeMaster/api/` and `Cubelet/api/` with identical semantic content, differing only in `go_package`. This means every proto change must be synchronized in two places.

| Proto File | CubeMaster Path | Cubelet Path |
|---|---|---|
| cubebox.proto | `CubeMaster/api/services/cubebox/v1/` | `Cubelet/api/services/cubebox/v1/` |
| images.proto | `CubeMaster/api/services/images/v1/` | `Cubelet/api/services/images/v1/` |
| errorcode.proto | `CubeMaster/api/services/errorcode/v1/` | `Cubelet/api/services/errorcode/v1/` |
| images.proto (types) | `CubeMaster/api/types/v1/` | `Cubelet/api/types/v1/` |
| descriptor.proto | **does not exist** | `Cubelet/api/types/v1/` |

### Inconsistent Naming Conventions

| Concept | CubeAPI External | CubeAPI Wire | CubeMaster HTTP | Proto |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sandbox ID | `sandboxID` (camelCase) | `sandbox_id` | `sandbox_id` or `sandboxID` | `sandbox_id` |
| Request ID | — | `requestID` | `requestID` or `request_id` | `request_id` |
| Instance Type | — | `instance_type` | `instance_type` or `instanceType` | `instance_type` |

Even within the same file (`types/types.go`), `SetTimeoutRequest` uses camelCase while `CreateCubeSandboxReq` uses snake_case.

### Validation Logic Scattered Across Three Layers

| Layer | Mechanism | Location | Actual Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| CubeAPI (Rust) | `validator` crate derive macros + hand-written functions | `models/mod.rs`, `services/*.rs` | **Active** |
| CubeMaster types | `v:"required"` struct tags | `types/types.go` | **Dead code** (no `validate.Struct()` call exists) |
| CubeMaster service | Hand-written `checkXxx()` functions (~15) | `util.go` | **Active**, but interleaved with type conversion |

The `v:"required"` tags in `types/types.go` are never enforced. Real validation lives in `util.go`'s 15 `checkAndGet*` functions, tightly coupled with type mapping code. Some validations (e.g., domain/deny_out mutual exclusion) are independently implemented in both CubeAPI and CubeMaster.

### Manual Serialization/Deserialization

The full chain involves 4 manual serialization/deserialization steps. Only the gRPC step is automatic:

```
CubeAPI:    serde::Deserialize → Rust struct (models)                ← manual
            serde::Serialize   → Rust struct (cubemaster wire)       ← manual
CubeMaster: jsoniter.Unmarshal → Go struct (types)                   ← manual
            hand-written field-by-field copy → Go proto struct       ← manual
            proto auto-serialize → gRPC binary                       ← automatic
Cubelet:    proto auto-deserialize → Go proto struct                 ← automatic
```

### Current API Change Blast Radius

Adding a single field (e.g., `gpu_count`) requires changes in **7-8 places**:

| # | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CubeMaster/api/.../cubebox.proto` | Add proto field |
| 2 | `Cubelet/api/.../cubebox.proto` | Sync proto field |
| 3 | `CubeMaster/api/` make proto | Regenerate .pb.go |
| 4 | `Cubelet/api/` make proto | Regenerate .pb.go |
| 5 | `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/types/types.go` | Add JSON struct field |
| 6 | `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/util.go` | Add manual mapping |
| 7 | `CubeAPI/src/cubemaster/mod.rs` | Add Rust wire struct field |
| 8 | `CubeAPI/src/models/mod.rs` + `services/*.rs` | Add external API field + conversion |

---

## Proposed Solution

### Target Architecture

```
Before (4 type layers + 2 proto copies):
  SDK → [Rust models] → [Rust wire] → HTTP → [Go JSON types]
      → manual mapping → [Go proto types ×2] → gRPC

After (2 type layers + 1 proto copy):
  SDK → [Rust models] → HTTP/protojson → [Go proto types ×1] → gRPC
```

### Target Validation Model

```
CubeAPI (Rust)
  │ validator crate: External API-specific validation (E2B compat, env var safety)
  ↓
CubeMaster (Go)
  │ protojson.Unmarshal: Auto-deserialize to proto message
  │ protovalidate.Validate(msg): Auto-validate all proto-declared constraints
  │ Business logic: CubeMaster-specific rules (resource quotas, scheduling affinity)
  ↓
Cubelet (Go)
  │ protovalidate.Validate(msg): Optional defensive re-validation
```

### Validation Responsibility Assignment

| Validation Type | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Structural (required/type/range/length) | Proto definition | `buf.validate` annotation |
| Cross-field constraints (domain+deny_out) | Proto definition | `buf.validate.message` CEL expression |
| Business validation (resource quotas, scheduling) | CubeMaster service layer | Go code operating on proto message |
| External API validation (E2B constraints, env var safety) | CubeAPI handler layer | Rust `validator` crate |
| Defensive re-validation (optional) | Cubelet entry point | `protovalidate.Validate(msg)` |

### Post-Refactor API Change Blast Radius

| # | Action | Where | Manual/Auto |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add proto field + validate annotation | `api/.../cubebox.proto` | Manual (2 lines) |
| 2 | `make proto` | `api/` | Automatic |
| 3 | CubeMaster business logic consumes new field | Service layer | Manual (if needed) |
| 4 | CubeAPI external API adds field | `models/mod.rs` + `cubemaster/...` | Manual (if needed) |

Reduced from **7-8 places** to **2-4 places**, with step 2 fully automatic.

---

## Phased Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Create Shared `api/` Module (Eliminate Duplicate Protos)

**Goal**: Maintain proto in one place; CubeMaster and Cubelet share the same generated code.

- Create `api/` as an independent Go module at repo root (`module github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/api`)
- Unify `go_package` to `github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/api/...`
- Both CubeMaster and Cubelet add `require` + `replace ../api`
- Delete `CubeMaster/api/` entirely
- Delete shared protos from `Cubelet/api/` (keep Cubelet-only: `nbi`, `version`, `multimetadb`, `cubehost`)
- Move `Cubelet/api/types/v1/cri.go` to `Cubelet/pkg/critypes/`
- Global find-and-replace import paths

**Risk**: Low (only import path changes, no runtime behavior change)

### Phase 2: Introduce protovalidate in Proto Definitions

**Goal**: Validation rules declared alongside type definitions; one line of code for all parameter validation.

- Add `buf/validate/validate.proto` imports and `buf.validate` annotations to proto messages
- Add `protovalidate-go` dependency to `api/go.mod`
- Cover structural validations: `required`, `min_len`, `min_items`, `gte/lte`, etc.
- Cover cross-field constraints via CEL expressions (e.g., domain allow_out requires deny_out 0.0.0.0/0)
- Retain CubeMaster-specific business validations in Go code (resource quotas, host path security, scheduling)

**Risk**: Low (proto annotations are additive, do not affect existing serialization)

### Phase 3: CubeMaster Handler Layer Refactoring

**Goal**: CubeMaster HTTP handlers use proto types directly; eliminate `types/types.go` and manual mapping in `util.go`.

- Replace `jsoniter.Unmarshal → types struct` with `protojson.Unmarshal → proto message`
- Replace `ConstructCubeletReq()` manual mapping with direct proto message pass-through
- Replace `common.WriteAPI()` with `protojson.Marshal` for responses
- Define HTTP response envelopes in proto (e.g., `CreateSandboxHTTPResponse`, `ListSandboxHTTPResponse`)
- Retain CubeMaster business logic (`applyDefaults`, `mergeTemplate`, `injectHostDirMounts`, etc.) but refactor to operate on proto messages directly
- Delete ~1500 lines: redundant types from `types/types.go`, `checkAndGet*` functions from `util.go`, scattered handler-local types
- Migrate API-by-API: List/Info → Delete/Update/Exec → Create → Snapshot/Template

**Risk**: Medium (protojson serialization behavior differs subtly from jsoniter; requires per-API compatibility verification)

### Phase 4: CubeAPI Rust-Side Optimization

**Goal**: Reduce manual maintenance of CubeMaster wire types in Rust.

- **Short-term**: Align `cubemaster/mod.rs` struct fields with protojson output (snake_case with `UseProtoNames: true`)
- **Long-term**: Use `prost-build` + `prost-serde` to auto-generate Rust structs from proto, eliminating ~2000 lines of hand-written wire structs
- Keep `models/mod.rs` (external API types) as-is — it serves E2B compatibility, OpenAPI generation, and camelCase JSON

**Risk**: Short-term low; long-term medium (requires adding prost toolchain to Rust build)

### Phase 5: Unify Naming Conventions

**Goal**: Consistent naming across the full chain.

| Layer | Convention | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Proto field | snake_case | Proto standard |
| Go struct field | PascalCase | Go standard (auto-generated by proto) |
| HTTP JSON wire | snake_case | `protojson` with `UseProtoNames: true` |
| CubeAPI→Master wire | snake_case | Consistent with CubeMaster HTTP |
| CubeAPI external API | camelCase | E2B compatibility, frontend-friendly |

**Risk**: High (client-facing API compatibility). Mitigated by protojson accepting both camelCase and snake_case on input.

---

## Estimated Code Reduction

| Source | What Gets Deleted | ~Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `CubeMaster/api/` | Duplicate proto + generated code | ~10,000 |
| `Cubelet/api/` (shared portion) | Duplicate proto + generated code | ~9,000 |
| `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/types/` | Redundant type definitions (~30 types) | ~600 |
| `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/util.go` | `checkAndGet*` + `ConstructCubeletReq` | ~600 |
| CubeMaster handler-local types | Scattered request/response structs | ~200 |
| `CubeAPI/src/cubemaster/mod.rs` (long-term) | Hand-written wire structs | ~2,000 |
| **Total** | | **~22,000** |

---

## Key Dependencies & Tooling

| Tool/Library | Purpose | Introduced In |
|---|---|---|
| `protojson` (Go stdlib) | Automatic JSON ↔ proto serialization | Phase 3 |
| `protovalidate-go` (buf) | Proto annotation validation runtime | Phase 2 |
| `buf/validate` proto | Proto validation annotation declarations | Phase 2 |
| `prost-build` (Rust, optional) | Proto → Rust struct auto-generation | Phase 4 |
| `prost-serde` (Rust, optional) | JSON support for proto Rust structs | Phase 4 |

---

## Priority & Milestones

| Phase | Content | Risk | Benefit | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Create shared `api/` module | Low | Medium | P0 |
| 2 | Introduce protovalidate | Low | High | P0 |
| 3 | CubeMaster handler refactoring | Medium | High | P1 |
| 4 | CubeAPI Rust-side optimization | Medium | Medium | P2 |
| 5 | Unify naming conventions | High | Medium | P3 |

Phases 1 and 2 can proceed in parallel (no dependency). Phase 3 delivers the largest benefit and should be executed API-by-API to control risk.

title: feat(metrics): add real-time metrics for a single sandbox
body:
## Summary

Related to #1021 

This PR implements the sandbox metrics API requested in the issue by adding `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxID}/metrics`, with optional `start` and `end` Unix timestamps in seconds. The endpoint returns an E2B-compatible JSON array containing the sample time, CPU allocation and utilization, memory usage, and disk usage for the requested sandbox.

This API gives users a standard way to inspect sandbox resource usage. It supports performance analysis, CPU and memory bottleneck detection, disk capacity monitoring, operational troubleshooting, sandbox health monitoring, and resource quota evaluation.

## Changes

The request flows through the following components:

```text
Client
  -> CubeAPI: GET /sandboxes/{sandboxID}/metrics
  -> CubeMaster: GET /cube/sandbox/metrics
  -> Cubelet: gRPC GetSandboxMetrics
  -> envd: GET http://<sandbox-ip>:49983/metrics
```

CubeAPI registers the public route, validates the optional time range, calls CubeMaster, maps internal errors to public API errors, and converts the response to the E2B-compatible JSON format. The related files are:

- `CubeAPI/src/routes.rs`
- `CubeAPI/src/handlers/sandboxes.rs`
- `CubeAPI/src/models/mod.rs`
- `CubeAPI/src/cubemaster/mod.rs`
- `CubeAPI/src/services/sandboxes.rs`

CubeMaster registers the internal HTTP endpoint, resolves the Cubelet that owns the sandbox, verifies that the node is available, calls Cubelet with the inherited request context, filters the current sample using `start` and `end`, and returns empty results as `[]`. The related files are:

- `CubeMaster/pkg/cubelet/actions.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/server/server_test.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/service/httpservice/cube/cube.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/service/httpservice/cube/routes.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/service/httpservice/cube/sandbox_metrics.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/service/httpservice/cube/sandbox_metrics_test.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/sandbox_metrics.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/sandbox_metrics_test.go`
- `CubeMaster/pkg/service/sandbox/types/types.go`

Cubelet adds the `GetSandboxMetrics` gRPC method, requests the current metrics from envd, and falls back to CubeBox resource metadata when envd is unavailable or does not provide a value. The protobuf definitions and generated Go files are updated on both the CubeMaster and Cubelet sides. The related files are:

- `CubeMaster/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto`
- `CubeMaster/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.pb.go`
- `CubeMaster/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox_grpc.pb.go`
- `Cubelet/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.proto`
- `Cubelet/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox.pb.go`
- `Cubelet/api/services/cubebox/v1/cubebox_grpc.pb.go`
- `Cubelet/services/cubebox/sandbox_metrics.go`
- `Cubelet/services/cubebox/sandbox_metrics_test.go`
- `Cubelet/doc/cubelet-api.md`

## Limitations and TODO

This PR provides a real-time metrics snapshot and does not persist metrics. The optional `start` and `end` parameters only determine whether the current sample falls within the requested range; they do not query historical samples.

The remaining work is split into three follow-up PRs, in priority order:

1. Add periodic metrics collection and persistence, and implement E2B-compatible historical range queries so `start` and `end` return all samples within the requested time window.
2. Replace the MVP collector with HA-safe, node-batched metrics collection for multi-node and multi-CubeMaster deployments.
3. Improve query and storage scalability with dynamic downsampling, query protection, retention hardening, and complete observability.

title: [Feature Request] Add E2B-compatible sandbox metrics API

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem / Motivation

CubeSandbox does not currently provide users with an E2B-compatible API for retrieving sandbox resource metrics. This API helps users analyze sandbox performance, identify CPU, memory, or disk bottlenecks, troubleshoot slow tasks and resource exhaustion, monitor sandbox health, and evaluate resource quotas.

## Proposed Solution

Add `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxID}/metrics`, compatible with E2B's Get Sandbox Metrics API. The `sandboxID` path parameter identifies the sandbox to query, while the optional `start` and `end` query parameters are Unix timestamps in seconds that define the requested time range. A successful response is a JSON array in which each item represents one metrics sample and includes its collection time (`timestamp` and `timestampUnix`), allocated CPU cores (`cpuCount`), CPU utilization (`cpuUsedPct`), memory usage in bytes (`memUsed`, `memTotal`, and `memCache`), and disk usage in bytes (`diskUsed` and `diskTotal`).



## Additional Context

E2B API reference: https://e2b.dev/docs/api-reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox-metrics

title: feat(version): upgrade component version inventory with component-json source and incomplete-report handling
body:
## Background

Refs: #954 

In one-click deployment, all components are installed and upgraded together as a single atomic operation. Cubelet collects and reports node component versions from a single `version.json` file under cubetoolbox, which works because the entire toolbox is replaced at once.

In Kubernetes deployment, however, components can be rolled out independently via separate DaemonSets (installer, bootstrap, node, etc.), each carrying its own image. The old single-source design could not correctly report per-component versions during or after independent upgrades — a cube-shim upgrade would either be invisible or would look like a wholesale regression of every other component.

This PR redesigns version collection to handle independently-rolling components while remaining compatible with the one-click layout.

## Summary

Introduce a multi-source version collection report (`CollectReport`) with an `Incomplete` flag that prevents transient collection gaps from wiping persisted version data in CubeMaster.

### Key changes

**New `component-json` source**
- Reads per-component `version.json` under the staging layout as the primary version source (replaces release-manifest.json as the primary)
- Per-directory allowlist ensures only authorized keys are accepted

**`CollectReport` with `InventoryIncomplete` propagation**
- Collector now returns `CollectReport{Versions, Incomplete}` instead of raw `[]ComponentVersion`
- Register and heartbeat requests propagate `InventoryIncomplete` to CubeMaster
- Mid-stage nodes (`.staging-*` markers or staged sentinel with missing directory) are flagged as incomplete

**Upsert-only persistence for incomplete reports**
- CubeMaster `persistVersions` merges incomplete reports with the previous snapshot (upsert-only, no DELETE of absent keys)
- Skips the DB write when the effective inventory is unchanged (content-hash compare)
- `mergeComponentVersions` deduplicates by component name so prior entries survive

**Kernel variant tracking (bm|pvm)**
- `Variant` field added to `ComponentVersion`
- Kernel version resolved from `version.json` variants, not from the manifest
- Active variant determined from `bootstrap-state/vmlinux-active` with fallback to artifact symlink

**CubeEgress version.json publishing**
- Best-effort `version.json` write into toolbox for inventory discovery

**Chart documentation updates**
- Rewritten guest-kernel selection narrative: effective-pvm first, keep-what-is-running for upgrades, Chart default is first-install intent only
- Added FAQ D6 for turning off PVM per node
- Updated ARCHITECTURE sentinel table and installer bootstrap flow

### Tests
All collector and service tests updated to cover incomplete-report merging, writer signature changes, and per-node mutation lock behavior.

title: [Feature Request] Go SDK Commands.Run buffers unbounded stdout and stderr

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

body:
## Problem

With `github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/sdk/go v0.0.0-20260717090631-002e4049fff0`, `Sandbox.Commands().Run` has no output limit or streaming callback. `parseProcessStartStream` appends every decoded stdout/stderr event to two `strings.Builder` values and returns only after the process ends.

A command controlled by untrusted input can therefore make the Go client allocate memory proportional to remote output before an application can truncate the returned strings. Limiting the final `CommandResult` is too late.

Relevant code: `sdk/go/envd.go`, `parseProcessStartStream`, currently around lines 245-313.

## Expected API

Please provide one of:

- bounded command output options with a fail/truncate policy; or
- a streaming command API with stdout/stderr callbacks/readers and an explicit maximum frame/output size.

The decoder should reject oversized Connect envelopes before allocating their declared payload.

## Current workaround

We still use the official SDK for client/sandbox lifecycle, PTY, files and snapshots, but had to bypass `Commands.Run` with a small application-owned decoder for the same `/process.Process/Start` Connect protocol:

- maximum Connect event: 1 MiB, checked before allocation;
- maximum combined decoded stdout+stderr: 512 KiB;
- compressed/end/error/exit-code events handled explicitly;
- oversized output leaves a mutating command in an unknown/recoverable state;
- no fork, `replace` directive or patched SDK is used.

We also wrap remaining SDK responses with bounded transports because several unary helpers decode directly from response bodies.

This workaround is intentionally temporary and duplicates private wire types because the public command API cannot enforce a memory bound.

title: Feat/opencode sandbox integration （Refs #644)
body: ## feat(examples): add OpenCode integration guide and examples（Refs #644 ） Refs #644 ## Problem CubeSandbox has integration examples for Claude Code but lacked an OpenCode reference. OpenCode is a terminal-native, open-source AI coding agent with a different plugin model (JS/Bun hooks instead of Claude's PreToolUse Python hook). Users otherwise need to assemble templates, credential injection, egress policy, session persistence, MCP tools, and Bash isolation themselves. ## Solution Add bilingual guides and one runnable example covering four execution modes: 1. **One-shot headless run** — `run_opencode.py` spins up a short-lived sandbox, forwards the prompt, and exits. 2. **Session persistence** — `resume_opencode.py` uses `sandbox.pause()` / `Sandbox.connect()` to retain OpenCode's data dir across turns. 3. **Credential vault** — `network_policy.py` applies default-deny egress and CubeEgress key injection so the provider token never enters the VM. 4. **Bash routing via OpenCode plugin** — `hooks/` ships a JS plugin (`tool.execute.before`) that intercepts `bash` calls and transparently forwards them through a reusable sandbox; `install.sh` copies only allowlisted `CUBE_*` settings into the installed config. Additionally, two generic execution paths that do not require the OpenCode agent itself: 5. **`sandbox_exec.py`** — host-side CLI for `--code` / `--file` / `--cmd` / `--pip` with UID-scoped session file for cross-process sandbox reuse. 6. **`mcp_server.py`** — JSON-RPC stdio MCP server exposing 5 sandbox tools (`run_code`, `run_command`, `write_file`, `read_file`, `reset`) so any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, …) can run untrusted code in the sandbox. ## Changes - Add English and Chinese integration guides and index entries. - Add `examples/opencode-integration/` with Dockerfile, one-shot, resume, network policy, standalone executor, MCP server, and hook examples. - Scope host state by UID, use owner-only permissions, atomically update state, and serialize each hook session. - Keep optional host mounts read-only and document co-location/shared-path requirements. - Copy only allowlisted `CUBE_*` values into installed hook configuration; provider credentials are excluded. - Use the MCP stdio transport's newline-delimited JSON-RPC framing. - Preserve command exit codes plus stdout and stderr in MCP tool results and set `isError` for failures. - Destroy the cached MCP sandbox on reset, stdin EOF, and process exit. - Support OpenCode's provider inference (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, etc.) through `*_BASE_URL` or explicit `OPENCODE_PROVIDER`. - `run_command` unifies `CommandExitException` handling so callers can branch uniformly on `exit_code` without catching at every call site. ## Security boundaries - This PR adds examples and documentation only; it does not change CubeSandbox runtime or API behavior. - The hook covers Bash. OpenCode Read, Write, and Edit tools still run on the host. - Hook failures block Bash execution. - The optional project mount is read-only; if the mount cannot be created, Bash remains isolated in a sandbox without the shared file view. - Real provider credentials are injected at egress and are not stored in the sandbox or installed hook configuration. ## Verification ```text cd examples/opencode-integration python3 -m pytest tests/ -q 133 passed in 0.29s python3 -m py_compile sandbox_exec.py mcp_server.py _opencode_common.py \ env_utils.py run_opencode.py resume_opencode.py network_policy.py passed bash -n hooks/install.sh passed ruff check examples/opencode-integration passed Assisted-by: Cursor:composer-2.5-fast Signed-off-by: YanxuanLiu [3205348955@qq.com](mailto:3205348955@qq.com)

title: feat(kubernetes): split PVM host bootstrap into dedicated DaemonSet
body:
Introduce a separate **cube-node-pvm** DaemonSet to decouple PVM host kernel installation from the general node bootstrap flow.

## Summary of changes

- **New `node-pvm-daemonset.yaml`**: DaemonSet gated by `placement.pvm` (`allow-pvm-bootstrap`), installs PVM host kernel and writes `pvm-host-ready` fingerprint. Non-PVM compute nodes skip this workload entirely.
- **New `wait-pvm-host.sh`**: Sidecar script that waits for `pvm-host-ready` before `cube-node-bootstrap` proceeds.
- **Refactored `node-prep-lib.sh`**: Extracted reusable helper functions for kernel pattern matching, status checking, and file readiness.
- **Simplified `cube-node-bootstrap`**: Replaced inline PVM kernel prep with `wait-pvm-host` initContainer; streamlined `pvm-host-bootstrap.sh`.
- **Updated `values.yaml`**: Added `placement.pvm` configuration block.
- **Updated chart docs**: README, ARCHITECTURE, FAQ, QUICKSTART, UPGRADE, and NOTES.txt now reflect the four-DaemonSet compute plane shape.
- **Updated image build scripts and Dockerfiles** for the new entrypoint.

title: [Feature Request] Go SDK nested module is not installable from release tags

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

body:
## Problem

The Go SDK declares a nested module:

```text
module github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/sdk/go
```

However, the current root release tag `v0.5.1` is not usable for that module. Go applies nested-module tag semantics and looks for `sdk/go/v0.5.1`:

```console
$ go list -m github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/sdk/go@v0.5.1
go: github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/sdk/go@v0.5.1: invalid version: unknown revision sdk/go/v0.5.1
```

The root `v0.5.1` snapshot also predates the PTY API currently present in `sdk/go`, so pinning the root release would not cover the documented lifecycle, command, file, snapshot, clone/rollback, egress, and PTY integration surface.

## Current workaround

After validating the official SDK against a full local control/data-plane protocol suite, restart recovery, race tests, and a built-binary PTY E2E, we had to pin the exact commit as an immutable pseudo-version:

```go
require github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/sdk/go v0.0.0-20260717090631-002e4049fff0
```

We are not using a fork, `replace` directive, or floating branch. This works, but it is a temporary workaround rather than a normal consumable SDK release.

## Request

Please publish a semantic version tag for the nested Go module (for example `sdk/go/v0.5.2`, following Go nested-module conventions), including the current PTY API and recent SDK fixes. It would also help to document whether root releases and Go SDK releases are intended to share a version or move independently.

Environment: Go 1.26.5 on Linux.

title: fix(cubelet): skip capacity admission for delete-triggered auto-resume
body:
## Summary

- When `paused_resource_release_ratio > 0` and a node is overcommitted, deleting a paused sandbox was blocked by the same `admitResume` capacity check used for user-initiated resume, creating a deadlock: the user wants to free resources by deleting, but the delete is blocked because the node lacks resources.
- Add a `skipAdmission` flag to `resumeOptions` so that `resumePausedSandboxForDestroy` bypasses the capacity check. The resume is a transient step before immediate destruction, so the brief overcommit is bounded by the destroy deadline.
- User-initiated resume (`UpdateWithResume`) remains subject to the full capacity admission check.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `Cubelet/services/cubebox/update.go` | Add `skipAdmission bool` to `resumeOptions`; guard `admitResume` call with `!opts.skipAdmission` |
| `Cubelet/services/cubebox/delete_resume.go` | Set `skipAdmission: true` in `resumePausedSandboxForDestroy` |
| `Cubelet/services/cubebox/destroy_auto_resume_test.go` | Integration test: delete succeeds under capacity pressure |
| `Cubelet/services/cubebox/release_paused_resources_test.go` | Unit tests: `admitResume` rejects when exceeded; `resumeLocked` bypasses with flag; `resumeLocked` rejects without flag |

## Test plan

- [x] `TestDestroyPausedSandboxSucceedsWhenCapacityWouldRejectResume` — end-to-end: delete of a paused sandbox succeeds even when node quota would reject a normal resume
- [x] `TestAdmitResumeRejectsWhenCapacityExceeded` — confirms `admitResume` correctly rejects when post-resume demand exceeds quota
- [x] `TestResumeLockedSkipsAdmissionWhenFlagSet` — `skipAdmission: true` bypasses admission and resume succeeds
- [x] `TestResumeLockedRejectsWithoutSkipAdmissionUnderCapacityPressure` — `skipAdmission: false` (user resume path) still rejected under capacity pressure
- [x] All existing `destroy_auto_resume_test.go` and `delete_resume_test.go` tests remain passing
- [x] `GOOS=linux go test -c` compilation verified

title: network-agent: fix stale tap-pool assertions in reuse test
body:
## Summary
Fixes the deterministically-failing test `TestEnsureReleaseEnsureReusesTapFromPool` in `network-agent/internal/service`. Closes #1013.

## Problem
After a successful `ReleaseNetwork`, the test asserted the recycled tap is deferred into `abnormalTapPool` (empty `tapPool`) "before async preparation," then promoted by `handleAbnormalTaps()`. But `releaseState → prepareAndStageTapForPool` stages the tap synchronously into `tapPool` on success and only defers to `abnormalTapPool` on a preparation *failure* — the path `TestReleaseNetworkQueuesTapWhenPoolPrepareFails` covers by injecting an error. With only success mocks installed, the assertion failed 10/10.

## Fix
Test-only: assert the synchronous outcome (`tapPool==1`, `abnormalTapPool==0`) and drop the `handleAbnormalTaps()` step. Production code is unchanged.

## Verification
- Before: `go test ./internal/service/ -run '^TestEnsureReleaseEnsureReusesTapFromPool$'` → 10/10 FAIL
- After: 50/50 PASS; sibling `TestReleaseNetworkQueuesTapWhenPoolPrepareFails` still passes; `go vet ./internal/service/` clean.

title: [Bug Report] network-agent: TestEnsureReleaseEnsureReusesTapFromPool fails (stale async tap-pool assertions)
body:
## Environment
- CubeSandbox commit: master @ `002e404`
- Relevant component: `network-agent` (`internal/service`)

## Problem
`TestEnsureReleaseEnsureReusesTapFromPool` fails deterministically. After a successful `ReleaseNetwork` it asserts the recycled tap is empty in `tapPool` and pending in `abnormalTapPool` ("before async preparation"), but the tap is already in `tapPool`.

## Steps to Reproduce
```
cd network-agent && go test ./internal/service/ -run '^TestEnsureReleaseEnsureReusesTapFromPool$'
```

## Actual Behavior
```
local_service_test.go:588: tapPool len=1, want 0 before async preparation
--- FAIL: TestEnsureReleaseEnsureReusesTapFromPool
```
Deterministic (10/10) — the test builds `localService` as a struct literal with success mocks and no maintenance goroutine, so there is no timing element.

## Root cause
With only success mocks installed (`cubevsPrepareTAPPolicy` → nil, etc.), `releaseState` → `prepareAndStageTapForPool` runs synchronously and stages the tap straight into `tapPool` via `stageTapForPoolLocked`. Deferral into `abnormalTapPool` happens only when preparation *fails* — exactly what the sibling test `TestReleaseNetworkQueuesTapWhenPoolPrepareFails` exercises by injecting a `prepare boom` error. The assertions in `TestEnsureReleaseEnsureReusesTapFromPool` appear to predate the switch to synchronous-on-success staging and were left stale.

## Expected Behavior
On the success path the recycled tap is staged synchronously into `tapPool` (`tapPool==1`, `abnormalTapPool==0`).

## Proposed fix
Test-only: assert the synchronous outcome and drop the `handleAbnormalTaps()` step. Production code is unchanged; the intended behavior is already covered by the failure-path sibling test. Verified 50/50 pass after the change, `internal/service` package green. A PR follows.

title: feat(proxy): customize Host header forwarded to sandbox services
body:
Add E2B-compatible network.maskRequestHost so create-time config can control the Host CubeProxy sends to user services (for example localhost:${PORT}), without changing the public URL, DNS, or TLS SNI.

CubeAPI accepts camelCase/snake_case and validates the value as a host or host:port authority; only ${PORT} is supported as a placeholder. CubeMaster merges the field from templates, keeps it in sandboxspec / snapshots, and stores the unexpanded template on the sandbox proxy Redis hash. It is not forwarded to Cubelet.

CubeProxy expands ${PORT} per request after routing, rewrites upstream Host through $cube_upstream_host, and sets X-Forwarded-Host when masking applies. Envd port 49983 is exempt. Host, path, and streaming routes share the same path. Optional local-cache metadata uses a false negative sentinel so a missing MaskRequestHost key reloads from Redis instead of failing open.

Also wire the option through Go/Node/Python SDKs, docs, and a quickstart example. Redis key docs additionally list the existing AllowPublicTraffic and TrafficAccessToken fields.

title: fix(cubebox): allow deleting paused sandboxes via shim binary delete
body:
## Problem

Deleting a **paused** sandbox fails and the sandbox becomes undeletable.

`DELETE /sandboxes/<id>` on a paused sandbox returns HTTP 500:

```
CubeMaster error 130593 -> delete paused sandbox failed
  -> shim ttrpc: Others("sandbox not in normal state")
```

A paused VM cannot serve its runtime (ttrpc) API, so the shim's per-container task-delete handler rejects the request with `sandbox not in normal state`. Retries fail identically. The GC / `CleanUp` path is affected the same way: `stopTask` fails on the guard and the reconcile loops forever on `shim process still Exists`, so a paused sandbox is never reclaimed.

This is issue #219. Two earlier attempts did not land:

- #317 removed the `sb.paused()` guard in the shim's task-delete handler. Review raised state-consistency concerns (sandbox state vs container state, the `delete_exec` path).
- #480 force-deleted from Cubelet with a hand-rolled `syscall.Kill` + `/proc` PID check. In review, @fslongjin requested changes (2026-06-16): Cubelet should not reimplement the shim's teardown; the cube shim already has `delete_shim()` which SIGKILLs the shim and reclaims resources, and containerd already has a standard binary-delete flow for an unresponsive shim. The manual kill also skipped the pause-snapshot and ivshmem cleanup that `delete_shim()` does. That PR was closed without the rework.

## Approach

This PR follows @fslongjin's suggested direction: reuse the shim's own binary delete instead of any custom kill logic in Cubelet.

For a paused sandbox, `destroyPausedSandbox` runs the shim's `delete` subcommand the same way containerd reaps a dead shim — via `pkg/shim.Command` against the bundle from `l.shims.Get(id).Bundle()`:

```
containerd-shim-cube-rs -namespace <ns> -id <id> -bundle <bundle> ... delete
```

The containerd-shim framework dispatches this to the shim's `delete_shim()`, which SIGKILLs the original shim process (reaping the in-process cube-hypervisor VMM) and reclaims the VM workdir, pause snapshot, and ivshmem file through `clean_sandbox_resource`. Cubelet then detaches the shim from the runtime manager with `l.shims.Delete`. Both `Destroy` and `CleanUp` take this path when the sandbox is paused, so GC reclaims paused sandboxes instead of looping.

How this addresses the earlier review:

- **No custom kill logic in Cubelet** — the SIGKILL and all resource cleanup stay owned by the shim's `delete_shim()` / `clean_sandbox_resource`; the earlier `syscall.Kill` + `/proc` PID verification is gone.
- **Pause snapshot and ivshmem are reclaimed** — because `delete_shim()` runs, not just a bare kill.
- **Standard mechanism** — `pkg/shim.Command` with the bundle path is exactly what containerd's own `binary.Delete` builds; the bundle comes from `ShimInstance.Bundle()`, not a hand-reconstructed path.
- The addresses passed to the shim are read from the same `PropertyGRPCAddress` / `PropertyTTRPCAddress` init properties that `ShimManager` itself uses to start shims.

Detaching after the kill is best-effort: the shim and VMM are already reaped by the `delete` subcommand, so a hiccup while removing the bundle dir is logged rather than failing the delete (a leftover bundle is reconciled by GC / on restart), matching the existing `CleanUp` behavior.

## Files

- `Cubelet/services/cubebox/destroy.go` — `destroyPausedSandbox` helper; the paused branch of `Destroy` now force-deletes and cleans up the cubestore container records.
- `Cubelet/services/cubebox/local.go` — capture the containerd grpc/ttrpc addresses at plugin init; `CleanUp` takes the same force-delete path when paused.

## Testing

Verified end-to-end on a two-node cluster (both nodes on this build).

Before: `create -> pause -> DELETE` returns 500 (`sandbox not in normal state`), retries fail identically.

After, `create -> pause -> DELETE`:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| DELETE (Destroy path) | 200/204 (was 500) |
| shim process + in-process VMM | reaped |
| pause snapshot dir (`root/pausevm/<id>`) | reclaimed |
| runtime bundle (`state/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/.../<id>`) | reclaimed |
| cubecow writable-layer volume | reclaimed |
| residual process | none |
| sandbox detail API | 404 |

GC / `CleanUp` path (exercised via a delete that routes to `engine.CleanUp`):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| result | success |
| shim / VMM / pause snapshot / bundle / volume | all reclaimed |
| log | takes the `CleanUp` force-delete branch, no `shim process still Exists` loop |

A previously stuck paused sandbox (undeletable before) also deletes cleanly once this build is running, with the same full reclamation.

title: network-agent: durable live update of a sandbox's L7 egress rule
body:
This adds a durable, live update path for a single L7 egress rule on a running sandbox, at the `network-agent` source-of-truth layer. A colocated caller can refresh an injected credential — e.g. a rotated short-lived OAuth token — without recreating the sandbox, and unlike a raw CubeEgress admin PATCH the change survives a CubeEgress or `network-agent` restart. I wrote this up in #1009 and that issue could be closed when this change is accepted and merged.

## Motivation

See #1009 for the full write-up. In short: injected credentials are effectively create-time today, and there is no way to swap the injected secret on a live sandbox that also persists. A direct `PATCH /admin/v1/policies/{ip}` updates the live data plane but is ephemeral, because CubeEgress re-bootstraps from `network-agent`'s `GET /v1/policies/dump` on restart and `network-agent` is the source of truth.

## What this changes

Scoped entirely to `network-agent`, split into three focused commits:

- **types** — add `UpdateEgressRuleRequest` / `UpdateEgressRuleResponse`.
- **service** — add `UpdateEgressRule` to `localService` (plus a noop stub). It upserts the rule into the sandbox's persisted `CubeNetworkConfig` by name (replaced in place when the name already exists, with order preserved; appended otherwise), calls `store.Save` **before** pushing, then re-pushes to CubeEgress via the same best-effort dispatcher `EnsureNetwork` already uses.
- **server** — expose `POST /v1/egress/update` alongside the existing `ensure` / `release` / `reconcile` / `get` / `list` routes on the loopback surface.

## Behavior

- **Live:** the rule applies on the next request with no restart, the same as the admin PATCH.
- **Durable:** persisted before the push, so it survives a CubeEgress restart (it is now part of the `/v1/policies/dump` bootstrap) and a `network-agent` restart (it is on disk).
- **Resilient:** a transient push failure does not fail the call — the rule is still persisted and `pending: true` is returned, so the existing maintenance retry loop lands it.

```jsonc
// POST /v1/egress/update
{
  "sandboxID": "sb-123",
  "rule": {
    "name": "gitlab_token",            // upsert key
    "match":  { "path": "/api/*" },
    "action": { "allow": true, "inject": [
      { "header": "Authorization", "secret": "…", "format": "Bearer %s" }
    ]}
  }
}
// -> { "sandboxID": "sb-123", "sandboxIP": "…", "applied": true, "ruleCount": 2 }
```

## Testing

- New `cubeegress_update_test.go` covers: append, in-place replace with order preserved, persist-before-push on a transient push failure, lookup by network handle, and input validation. The tests are hermetic — a real on-disk store plus a fake CubeEgress client, no netns or privileges required.
- `go vet ./internal/service/` is clean.
- Run locally: `cd network-agent && go test ./internal/service/ -run UpdateEgress -v`.

## Scope / follow-ups

- Deliberately scoped to the `network-agent` source-of-truth layer, which is where durability is decided. Threading the update up to an authenticated SDK / CubeAPI edge is a natural follow-up and can be a separate PR if that's wanted.
- The endpoint name and request/response shape are open to whatever the maintainers prefer before merge.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits are focused and atomic (one component each)
- [x] All commits are DCO signed-off
- [x] Tests added for the new behavior
- [ ] Docs — none needed for an internal loopback endpoint; happy to add a note to the `network-agent` docs if preferred

title: [Feature Request] network-agent: durable live update of a sandbox's L7 egress rule
body:
## Problem / Motivation

CubeEgress can inject credentials into a sandbox's egress traffic via the L7 egress rules supplied in `Sandbox.create` (`cubeNetworkConfig.rules[].action.inject`). This is great for handing a sandbox a credential it can _use_ but never _read_.

The gap is refreshing that credential on a **running** sandbox. Our use case is injecting a short-lived per-user OAuth token (≈2h TTL) for git/API egress: when the token rotates we need to swap the injected secret without tearing down the sandbox and losing its state.

Today there is no durable path to do this:

- The rules are only read from the `Sandbox.create` request, so they are effectively create-time on the SDK/API surface.
- `network-agent` exposes `ensure` / `release` / `reconcile` / `get` / `list`, but none of them updates a single rule on a live sandbox. `reconcile` in particular does not re-push egress policy (it converges CubeVS/tap state only), so it can't be used to land a rule-only change.
- CubeEgress's admin API (`PATCH /admin/v1/policies/{sandbox_ip}`) _does_ replace a rule on the live data plane with no restart — but the change is ephemeral. On a CubeEgress restart it re-bootstraps from `network-agent`'s `GET /v1/policies/dump`, so any rule not reflected in `network-agent`'s persisted `CubeNetworkConfig` is lost. `network-agent` is the source of truth; a direct admin PATCH bypasses it.

## Proposed Solution

Add an update path at the source-of-truth layer — `network-agent` — so the change is both **live** and **durable**.

- New service method `UpdateEgressRule(sandboxID | networkHandle, rule)` that upserts a single rule into the sandbox's persisted `CubeNetworkConfig` (replace-by-name in place when the name already exists, append otherwise), saves state to disk **before** re-pushing, then re-pushes via the same best-effort dispatcher `EnsureNetwork` already uses.
- Exposed as `POST /v1/egress/update` alongside the existing network routes.

Because it persists first, a refreshed credential survives a CubeEgress restart (it's now part of the `/v1/policies/dump` bootstrap) as well as a `network-agent` restart — unlike a raw admin PATCH.

Sketch of the request/response:

```jsonc
// POST /v1/egress/update
{
  "sandboxID": "sb-123",
  "rule": {
    "name": "gitlab_token", // upsert key
    "match": { "path": "/api/*" },
    "action": {
      "allow": true,
      "inject": [
        { "header": "Authorization", "secret": "…", "format": "Bearer %s" },
      ],
    },
  },
}
// -> { "sandboxID": "sb-123", "sandboxIP": "…", "applied": true, "ruleCount": 2 }
```

`applied` reports whether the live CubeEgress push landed immediately; if the push transiently fails the rule is still persisted and `pending` is returned so the existing maintenance retry loop lands it.

**A PR implementing this will be opened shortly.** It's scoped to `network-agent` (new types, the service method + a noop stub, the HTTP route) with focused unit tests (append, in-place replace with order preserved, persist-before-push on a transient failure, lookup by network handle, and validation). Happy to adjust the endpoint name/shape to whatever the maintainers prefer before merge.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Recreate the sandbox with new rules.** Correct but disruptive — it discards the running sandbox and any in-memory state, which defeats the "refresh a live credential" goal.
- **Call the CubeEgress admin PATCH directly.** Works on the live data plane with no restart, but is ephemeral (reverts on CubeEgress restart / next bootstrap from `network-agent`), so it can't be the durable mechanism on its own.
- **Thread the update all the way up to the SDK / CubeAPI.** Reasonable as a follow-up for an authenticated external edge, but this proposal deliberately starts at the `network-agent` source-of-truth layer, which is where durability is decided. The loopback endpoint is enough for a colocated caller today.

## Additional Context

- Concrete use case: a colocated dispatcher refreshes a rotated per-user OAuth token injected for `git.*`/API egress, at kickoff/attach/resume time, without recreating the sandbox.
- Relevant code: `network-agent/internal/service/local_service.go` (state, `pushEgressForState`), `network-agent/internal/service/state_store.go` (persistence), `network-agent/internal/httpserver/server.go` (routes), `CubeEgress/lua/admin.lua` + `bootstrap.lua` (live replace + bootstrap pull).

title: feat(cubelet): refactor state tmpfs mount with safer resize logic
body:
## Background

Some machines have larger specifications and can create a very high number of sandboxes. The existing default 500Mi state tmpfs is insufficient to hold the metadata for all those sandboxes.

To address this, the following adjustments were made:

1. Bump the default state tmpfs size from 500Mi to 1Gi.
2. Add automatic remount logic so that after users manually adjust the size configuration, the tmpfs is resized automatically on next startup without requiring a manual remount.

## Summary

Refactor cubelet's state tmpfs mount logic to be safer and more robust.

## Changes

- Extract `mountTmpfsDir` from `main.go` into dedicated `state_tmpfs.go`
- Add remount-on-start support for existing tmpfs mounts without wiping state data
- Add shrink guard: refuse to shrink tmpfs when used bytes exceed the target size
- Add kernel size-option parsing (k/m/g suffixes, percent-of-RAM rejection)
- Add page-size-aware equality check to avoid unnecessary remount churn
- Bump default `state-tmpfs-size` from 500Mi → 1024Mi

## Test

- Unit tests cover size parsing, equality checks, skip-non-tmpfs, noop-when-size-matches, and shrink-refusal scenarios

title: fix(CubeMaster/templatecenter): make artifact GC advisory-lock cleanup cancellation-safe
feat(examples): add crash recovery worker
body:
## Summary This PR adds a long-running, stateful crash-recovery Worker example backed by CubeSandbox checkpoints. This example runs a deterministic transfer workload across multiple recovery epochs. Ever epoch: 1. commits and verifies several transfers. 2. creates a stable checkpoint. 3. commits additional post-checkpoint work. 4. aborts the Worker halfway through another transfer. 5. rolls the same sandbox back. 6. verifies exact process-memory and writable-workspace restoration. 7. replays the lost work and verifies idempotent retry behavior. Related to #645. ## Motivation Several existing examples demonstrate the capabilities of CubeSandbox. For instance, `code-sandbox-quickstart` covers basic sandbox creation, command execution, file access, and lifecycle APIs, while `snapshot-rollback-clone` focuses on snapshot, clone, and rollback operations. Snapshot and rollback are core capabilities of CubeSandbox, but successfully invoking these APIs is only the first level of validation. For a long-running stateful workload, the more important question is whether rollback restores a coherent checkpoint across all in-sandbox state: process memory and the writable filesystem must return to the same logical point, and application-level invariants must continue to hold. This example wants to fill the gap with a worker that intentionally crashes in the middle of a state transition. ## Implementation - A Rust worker maintains account balances, pending transfers, a committed ledger, seen request IDs, and operation counters. - State transitions are mirrored to `/workspace/crash-recovery/audit.json` through atomic file replacement. - `run_demo.py` generates reproducible legal transfers from a fixed seed and the default workload runs three checkpoint, fault, rollback, and reply epochs. ## Intermittent post-rollback stall ***This example may intermittently pause for several minutes after a rollback while waiting for the first post-rollback data-plane request.*** The behavior is tracked in #992. During this example, the delay usually appears between `Fault verified` and `Rollback verified`. title: fix(one-click): expose CubeProxy logs on the host
body:
## Motivation

The one-click CubeProxy container writes OpenResty access, error, and sidecar
logs under `/data/log/cube-proxy`.

Previously, this directory only existed inside the container filesystem, which
made host-side diagnostics harder and caused logs to be lost when the container
was recreated.

This PR exposes the existing CubeProxy log directory on the host while keeping
the current container paths and log behavior unchanged.

## What Changed

* Bind-mount the host `/data/log/cube-proxy` directory into the CubeProxy
  container at the same path.
* Create the host log directory before CubeProxy starts.
* Update `collect-logs.sh` to collect CubeProxy logs directly from the host
  directory instead of using `docker exec`.
* Add package-layout regression coverage for:

  * compose log mount wiring
  * log directory creation
  * host-side log collection wiring
* Update English and Chinese operator documentation for CubeProxy log locations.

## Scope

This PR only exposes the existing CubeProxy log directory on the host and
updates diagnostics/documentation to use the host path.

It does not:

* change CubeProxy `nginx.conf`
* change the existing log rotation behavior

## Validation

Validated on a Linux one-click control node:

* The rendered compose file contains:

  ```text
  /data/log/cube-proxy:/data/log/cube-proxy
  ```

* `docker inspect cube-proxy` confirmed the active host bind mount.

* Host and container `access.log` paths reported the same device and inode,
  confirming both paths reference the same file.

* `collect-logs.sh --module cube-proxy --lines 200` successfully collected
  `access.log` and `error.log` from the host directory.

* `bash deploy/one-click/tests/test_package_layout.sh` passed:

  ```text
  package layout tests OK
  ```

title: cubemaster: resolve sandbox request for template commit
body:
## Motivation

`cubemastercli tpl commit` required both a sandbox ID and the original `CreateCubeSandboxReq` JSON file.

This required users to keep and provide the original request file when committing a sandbox. The sandbox create request is already associated with the sandbox in the control plane, so users should not need to preserve and resubmit it just to commit the sandbox as a template.

CubeMaster's snapshot path already restores the canonical sandbox create request from `sandboxspec`, with an origin-template fallback for legacy sandboxes. Template commit should use the same source of truth.

## What Changed

* Allow `/cube/sandbox/commit` to omit `create_request`.
* Resolve the sandbox request inside CubeMaster using the existing snapshot resolver:

  * prefer the canonical `sandboxspec` record
  * fall back to the sandbox's origin template request for legacy sandboxes
* Keep an explicitly supplied `create_request` as a complete override.
* Simplify `cubemastercli tpl commit` so the default path sends only `sandbox_id`.
* Keep `--file` as the optional complete request override.
* Keep network override flags file-based; they still require `--file`.
* Log full template commit failures in CubeMaster while returning stable,
  sanitized error messages to clients.
* Preserve output `tpl-...` generation, host resolution, and the asynchronous `build_id` flow.
* Document the behavior and default progress-watching flow in English and Chinese.

CubeAPI is unchanged because it does not call `/cube/sandbox/commit`.

## Validation

Added focused tests for:

* The default `tpl commit --sandbox-id ...` flow, where the CLI sends only the sandbox ID and CubeMaster accepts the request without `create_request`.
* Sandbox request restoration through the shared resolver, including existing HTTP error handling for resolver failures.
* The explicit `create_request` override, which remains a complete replacement.
* The `--file` flow, including successful network flag merging and the
  requirement that network override flags be used with `--file`.
* Existing request ID validation and template commit error mapping.
* Sanitization of wrapped resolver, template, and database errors before they
  are returned in `RetMsg`.

The focused CLI, HTTP handler, and template commit tests pass. Both `cubemaster` and `cubemastercli` also build successfully.

The default flow was verified end to end against a running sandbox:

```bash
cubemastercli tpl commit --sandbox-id <sandbox-id>
```

The command completed successfully, and the generated template reached `READY` without `--file` or the original create request.

A broader test run passed the CLI and HTTP handler packages. `pkg/templatecenter` still has an unrelated nil-pointer failure in the unmodified `TestRefreshSnapshotStorageMetricsRetriesCachedUnknown` test.

## Summary

Introduce a top-level `persistence.storageClassName` convenience key for the Helm chart, allowing users to pin all three control-plane PVCs (CubeMaster / MySQL / Redis) to a single StorageClass with one setting.

## Changes

- **New helper**: `cube.persistenceStorageClassName` template with clear three-tier precedence (component-level → top-level `persistence.storageClassName` → omit for cluster default)
- **New example file**: `runtime-values.example.yaml` as a documented starting point with inline guidance
- **PVC templates**: `master-pvc`, `mysql`, `redis` now use the new helper instead of reading component-level `storageClassName` directly
- **Documentation**: Updated README, ARCHITECTURE, FAQ, and QUICKSTART to reflect the new persistence model, clarify StorageClass creation vs PVC binding, and improve troubleshooting guidance
- **NOTES.txt**: Shows persistence mode on `helm install`

## Use case

Before, users had to set `storageClassName` on each component individually:

```yaml
controlPlane.master.persistence.storageClassName: gp3
mysql.persistence.storageClassName: gp3
redis.persistence.storageClassName: gp3
```

Now, a single key covers all three:

```yaml
persistence.storageClassName: gp3
```

Component-level settings still take precedence when different SCs are needed per component.
